body.text:
(PB 1.1.1) oṃ mahan me voco bhargo me voco yaśo me vocaḥ stomaṃ me voco bhuktiṃ me vocaḥ sarvaṃ me vocas tan māvatu tan māviśatu tena bhukṣiṣīya
(PB 1.1.2) devo devam etu somaḥ somam etv ṛtasya pathā
(PB 1.1.3) vihāya dauṣkṛtyam
(PB 1.1.4) badvā nāmasi sṛtiḥ somasaraṇī somaṃ gameyam
(PB 1.1.5) pitaro bhūḥ pitaro bhūḥ pitaro bhūḥ
(PB 1.1.6) nṛmaṇa ūrdhvabharasaṃ tvordhvabharā dṛśeyam
(PB 1.1.7) mṛdā śithirā devānāṃ tīrthaṃ vedir asi mā mā hiṃsīḥ
(PB 1.1.8) viṣṇoḥ śiro 'si yaśodhā yaśo mayi dhehi
(PB 1.1.9) iṣa ūrja āyuṣe varcase ca
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.1.1) Oṃ. Speak to me of greatness, speak to me of splendor, speak to me of glory, speak to me of the <s>stoma</s> (hymn of praise), speak to me of enjoyment, speak to me of everything — may that protect me, may that enter me, may I partake of that.
(PB 1.1.2) May the god go to the god, may <s>Soma</s> go to <s>Soma</s>, by the path of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order).
(PB 1.1.3) Having left behind wrongdoing,
(PB 1.1.4) you are named 'Badva,' the path, the course of <s>Soma</s> — may I go to <s>Soma</s>.
(PB 1.1.5) O Fathers, hail! O Fathers, hail! O Fathers, hail!
(PB 1.1.6) O manly-minded one, may I see you bearing upward, bearing upward.
(PB 1.1.7) O soft and loose one, you are the altar, the ford of the gods — do not harm me!
(PB 1.1.8) You are the head of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bestower of glory — place glory in me.
(PB 1.1.9) For nourishment, sustenance, life, and vigor.

body.text:
(PB 1.2.1) yunajmi te pṛthivīm agninā saha yunajmi vācaṃ saha sūryeṇa yukto vāto 'ntarikṣeṇa te saha yuktās tisro vimṛjaḥ sūryasya
(PB 1.2.2) ṛtasya sadane sīdāmi
(PB 1.2.3) ṛtapātram asi
(PB 1.2.4) vānaspatyo 'si bārhaspatyo 'si prājāpatyo 'si prajāpater mūrdhāsy atyāyupātram asīdam ahaṃ māṃ prāñcaṃ prohāmi tejase brahmavarcasāya
(PB 1.2.5) maruto napāto 'pāṅkṣayāḥ parvatānāṅkakubhaḥ śyenā ajirā endraṃ vagnunā vahata ghoṣeṇāmīvāṃ cātayadhvaṃ yuktāstha vahata
(PB 1.2.6) idam aham amuṃ yajamānaṃ paśuṣv adhy ūhāmi paśuṣu ca māṃ brahmavarcase ca
(PB 1.2.7) vasavas tvā gāyatreṇa chandasā saṃ mṛjantu rudrās tvā traiṣṭubhena chandasā saṃ mṛjantv ādityās tvā jāgatena chandasā saṃ mṛjantu
(PB 1.2.8) pavitraṃ te vitataṃ brahmaṇaspate prabhur gātrāṇi pary eṣi viśvato 'taptatanūr na tad āmo aśnute śṛtāsa id vahantaḥ saṃ tad āśataḥ
(PB 1.2.9) praśukraitu devīmanīṣāsmad rathaḥ sutaṣṭo na vājy āyuṣe me pacasva varcase me pavasva viduḥ pṛthivyā divo janitrāc chṛṇvantv āpo 'dhaḥ kṣarantīḥ somehodgāya mām āyuṣe mama brahmavarcasāya yajamānasyarddhyā amuṣya rājyāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.2.1) I yoke for you the earth together with <s>Agni</s> (fire), I yoke speech together with <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun); <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is yoked together with the atmosphere for you; yoked are the three purifications of <s>Sūrya</s>.
(PB 1.2.2) I sit in the seat of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order).
(PB 1.2.3) You are the vessel of <s>Ṛta</s>.
(PB 1.2.4) You belong to the lord of the forest, you belong to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>; you are the head of <s>Prajāpati</s>; you are the vessel that transcends life. I propel myself forward for radiance and for the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 1.2.5) O <s>Maruts</s>, kinsmen of <s>Napāt</s>, dwellers on the heights, hawks of the mountain-peaks, swift eagles — carry <s>Indra</s> with the cry of praise, drive away disease with the shout! You are yoked — carry!
(PB 1.2.6) I now convey this sacrificer into cattle, and myself into cattle and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 1.2.7) May the <s>Vasus</s> (divine beings) purify you with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, may the <s>Rudras</s> purify you with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, may the <s>Ādityas</s> purify you with the <s>Jagatī</s> meter.
(PB 1.2.8) Your purifier is spread wide, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> (Lord of Prayer); mighty, you pass through all the limbs. The one whose body is not heated cannot attain that; only those who are cooked carry it and partake of it.
(PB 1.2.9) Let the divine thought shine forth brightly; like a well-fashioned chariot seeking the prize — cook for my life, purify for my vigor. Let the waters flowing below hear, from the birthplace of earth and heaven. O <s>Soma</s>, sing the <s>Udgītha</s> for my life, for my splendor of <s>Brahman</s>, for the prosperity of the sacrificer, for the sovereignty of that one.

body.text:
(PB 1.3.1) vekurānāmāsi juṣṭā devebhyo namo vāce namo vācas pataye devi vāg yat te vāco madhumat tasmin mā dhāḥ sarasvatyai svāhā
(PB 1.3.2) sūryo mā divyābhyo nāṣṭrābhyaḥ pātu vāyur antarikṣābhyo 'gniḥ pārthivābhyaḥ svāhā
(PB 1.3.3) yo 'dya saumyo vadho 'ghāyūnām udīrate viṣūkuhasya dhanvanāpa tān varuṇo 'pa dhamatu
(PB 1.3.4) yo ma ātmā yā me prajā ye me paśavas tair ahaṃ mano vācaṃ pra sīdāmi
(PB 1.3.5) agnes tejasendrasyendriyeṇa sūryasya varcasā bṛhaspatis tvā yunaktu devebhyaḥ prāṇāyāgnir yunaktu tapasā somaṃ yajñāya voḍhave dadhātv indra indriyaṃ satyāḥ kāmā yajamānasya santu
(PB 1.3.6) annaṃ kariṣyāmy annaṃ praviṣyāmy annaṃ janayiṣyāmi
(PB 1.3.7) annam akaram annam abhūd annam ajījanam
(PB 1.3.8) śyeno 'si gāyatracchandā anu tvā rabhe svasti mā saṃ pārayā mā stotrasya stotraṃ gamyād indravanto vanemahi bhakṣīmahi prajām iṣam
(PB 1.3.9) saṃ varcasā payasā saṃ tapobhir aganmahi manasā saṃ śivena saṃ vijñānena manasaś ca satyair yathā vo 'haṃ cārutamaṃ vadānīndro vo dṛśe bhūyāsaṃ sūryaś cakṣuṣe vātaḥ prāṇāya somo gandhāya brahma kṣatrāya
(PB 1.3.10) namo gandharvāya viṣvag vādine varcodhā asi varco mayi dhehi
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.3.1) You are named 'Vekura,' favored by the gods. Homage to Speech, homage to the lord of Speech! O divine <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), whatever of your speech is sweet, place me in that. To <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
(PB 1.3.2) May <s>Sūrya</s> protect me from the celestial dangers, <s>Vāyu</s> from the atmospheric ones, <s>Agni</s> from the terrestrial ones. <s>Svāhā</s>!
(PB 1.3.3) Whatever deadly weapon of <s>Soma</s> is raised today against those of evil intent, may <s>Varuṇa</s> blow away those of <s>Viṣūkuha</s> (the crooked-armed) with his bow.
(PB 1.3.4) Whatever is my self, whatever is my offspring, whatever are my cattle — with them I settle my mind and speech.
(PB 1.3.5) With the radiance of <s>Agni</s>, the power of <s>Indra</s>, the splendor of <s>Sūrya</s>, may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> yoke you for the gods. May <s>Agni</s> yoke <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>Soma</s> to carry the sacrifice. May <s>Indra</s> bestow <s>indriya</s> (power). May the desires of the sacrificer be true.
(PB 1.3.6) I shall make food, I shall enter into food, I shall generate food.
(PB 1.3.7) I have made food, food has come into being, I have generated food.
(PB 1.3.8) You are the eagle, of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. I hold fast to you — carry me safely across. May the <s>stoma</s> (hymn) reach its <s>stoma</s>. Possessing <s>Indra</s>'s favor, may we conquer; may we partake of offspring and nourishment.
(PB 1.3.9) With splendor, with the milk-offering, with austerities we have come together, with auspicious mind, with knowledge and with the truths of the mind — that I may speak most charmingly to you. May <s>Indra</s> be present for your sight, <s>Sūrya</s> for your vision, <s>Vāyu</s> for your breath, <s>Soma</s> for your fragrance, <s>Brahman</s> for <s>kṣatra</s> (sovereign power).
(PB 1.3.10) Homage to the <s>Gandharva</s> who speaks in all directions! You are a bestower of splendor — place splendor in me.

body.text:
(PB 1.4.1) adhvanām adhvapate svasti me 'dyāsmin devayāne pathi bhūyāt
(PB 1.4.2) samrāḍ asi kṛśānuḥ
(PB 1.4.3) tutho 'si janadhāyo nabho 'si pratakvāsaṃmṛṣṭo 'si havyasūdanaḥ
(PB 1.4.4) vibur asi pravāhaṇaḥ
(PB 1.4.5) vahnir asi havyavāhanaḥ
(PB 1.4.6) śvātro 'si pracetāḥ
(PB 1.4.7) tutho 'si viśvavedā uśig asi kavir aṅghārir asi bambhārir avasyur asi duvasvān
(PB 1.4.8) śundhyur asi mārjālīyaḥ
(PB 1.4.9) ṛtadhāmāsi svarjyotiḥ
(PB 1.4.10) samudro 'si viśvavyacāḥ
(PB 1.4.11) ahir asi budhnyaḥ
(PB 1.4.12) ajo 'sy ekapāt
(PB 1.4.13) sagarā asi budhnyaḥ
(PB 1.4.14) kavyo 'si kavyavāhanaḥ
(PB 1.4.15) pāta māgnayo raudreṇānīkena piṣṭata mā namo vo 'stu mā mā hiṃsiṣṭa
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.4.1) O lord of paths, protector of the paths, may there be well-being for me today on this path of divine travel.
(PB 1.4.2) You are the sovereign ruler, <s>Kṛśānu</s> (the divine archer).
(PB 1.4.3) You are the powerful one, nourisher of people; you are the cloud, wiped clean; you are the purifier of oblations.
(PB 1.4.4) You are the mighty one, the one who carries forward.
(PB 1.4.5) You are the carrier, the conveyor of oblations.
(PB 1.4.6) You are the swift one, the wise one.
(PB 1.4.7) You are the powerful one, the all-knowing; you are the desirer, the sage; you are <s>Aṅghāri</s>, you are <s>Bambhāri</s>; you are the helper, the bountiful one.
(PB 1.4.8) You are the purifier, the cleanser.
(PB 1.4.9) You are the upholder of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the light of heaven.
(PB 1.4.10) You are the ocean, all-pervading.
(PB 1.4.11) You are <s>Ahi Budhnya</s> (the Serpent of the Deep).
(PB 1.4.12) You are <s>Aja Ekapād</s> (the One-footed Goat).
(PB 1.4.13) You are <s>Sagara</s> (the Ocean), dwelling in the depths.
(PB 1.4.14) You are the sage, the conveyor of oblations to the ancestors.
(PB 1.4.15) Protect me, O <s>Agnis</s> (fires), with your fierce <s>Rudra</s>-like front! Be ground to dust! Homage be to you! Do not harm me!

body.text:
(PB 1.5.1) ṛtasya dvārau stho mā mā saṃ tāptam
(PB 1.5.2) namaḥ sakhibhyaḥ pūrvasadbhyo namo parasadbhyaḥ
(PB 1.5.3) śyeno nṛcakṣā agneṣ ṭvā cakṣuṣāva paśyāmi
(PB 1.5.4) indav indrapītasya ta indriyāvato gāyatracchandasaḥ sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.5.5) ūrdhvaḥ sapta ṛṣīn upa tiṣṭhasvendrapīto vācas pate saptartvijo 'bhyuc chrayasva juṣasva lokam mārvāg ava gāḥ
(PB 1.5.6) soma rārandhi no hṛdi pitā no 'si mama tan mā mā hiṃsīḥ
(PB 1.5.7) soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayaṃ vardhayāmo vācovidaḥ sumṛḍīko na ā viśa
(PB 1.5.8) ā pyāyasva sam etu te viśvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam / bhavā vājasya saṃgathe
(PB 1.5.9) avamais ta ūrdhvais te kāvyais te pitṛbhir bhakṣitasya madhumato nārāśaṃsasya sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.5.10) dīkṣāyai varṇena tapaso rūpeṇa manaso mahimnā vāco vibhūtyā prajāpatis tvā yunaktu prajābhyo 'pānāya
(PB 1.5.11) vāyur yunaktu manasā stomaṃ yajñāya voḍhave dadhātv indra indriyaṃ satyāḥ kāmā yajamānasya santu
(PB 1.5.12) vṛṣako 'si triṣṭupchandā anu tvā rabhe svasti mā saṃ pārayā mā stotrasya stotraṃ gamyād indravanto vanemahi bhakṣīmahi prajām iṣam
(PB 1.5.13) indav indrapītasya ta indriyāvato triṣṭupchandasaḥ sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.5.14) sūryo yunaktu vācā stomaṃ yajñāya voḍhave dadhātv indra indriyaṃ satyāḥ kāmā yajamānasya santu
(PB 1.5.15) svaro 'si gayo 'si jagacchandā anu tvā rabhe svasti mā saṃ pārayā mā stotrasya stotraṃ gamyād indravanto vanemahi bhakṣīmahi prajām iṣam
(PB 1.5.16) indav indrapītasya ta indriyāvato triṣṭupchandasaḥ sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.5.17) āyur me prāṇo mano 'si me prāṇa āyupatnyām ṛci yan me mano yamaṃ gataṃ yad vā me aparāgataṃ rājñā somena tad vayaṃ punar asmāsu dadhnasi
(PB 1.5.18) yan me yamaṃ vaivasvataṃ mano jagāma dūragās tan ma āvartayā punar jīvātave na martave 'tho ariṣṭatātaye
(PB 1.5.19) yenāhy ājim ajayad vicakṣya yena śyenaṃ śakunaṃ suparṇaṃ yad āhuś cakṣur aditāv anantaṃ somo nṛcakṣā mayi tad dadhātu
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.5.1) You are the two doors of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) — do not scorch me.
(PB 1.5.2) Homage to the companions who sat before, homage to those who sit after.
(PB 1.5.3) O eagle, beholder of men — with the eye of <s>Agni</s>, I behold you.
(PB 1.5.4) O drop of <s>Soma</s>, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, possessing <s>Indra</s>'s power, of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, of all the hosts, invoked among all hosts — I partake of you, the invoked one.
(PB 1.5.5) Rise upward, attend upon the seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), O one drunk by <s>Indra</s>, lord of speech! Rise up over the seven officiants! Enjoy your station — do not descend downward.
(PB 1.5.6) O <s>Soma</s>, delight our hearts! You are our father — therefore do not harm me.
(PB 1.5.7) O <s>Soma</s>, we augment you with songs, we who know speech. Enter us graciously.
(PB 1.5.8) Swell up, let virile strength come to you from all sides, O <s>Soma</s>; be present at the attainment of the prize.
(PB 1.5.9) Of the sweet, praiseworthy <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (portion), partaken of by your lowest, highest, and ancestral sages, of all the hosts, invoked among all hosts — I partake of you, the invoked one.
(PB 1.5.10) With the hue of <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration), with the form of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), with the greatness of the mind, with the power of speech — may <s>Prajāpati</s> yoke you for offspring, for the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath).
(PB 1.5.11) May <s>Vāyu</s> yoke the <s>stoma</s> (hymn) with the mind, to carry the sacrifice. May <s>Indra</s> bestow <s>indriya</s> (power). May the desires of the sacrificer be true.
(PB 1.5.12) You are the bull, of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. I hold fast to you — carry me safely across. May the <s>stoma</s> reach its <s>stoma</s>. Possessing <s>Indra</s>'s favor, may we conquer; may we partake of offspring and nourishment.
(PB 1.5.13) O drop of <s>Soma</s>, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, possessing <s>Indra</s>'s power, of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, of all the hosts, invoked among all hosts — I partake of you, the invoked one.
(PB 1.5.14) May <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun) yoke the <s>stoma</s> (hymn) with speech, to carry the sacrifice. May <s>Indra</s> bestow <s>indriya</s> (power). May the desires of the sacrificer be true.
(PB 1.5.15) You are the resonant one, you are the melodious one, of the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. I hold fast to you — carry me safely across. May the <s>stoma</s> reach its <s>stoma</s>. Possessing <s>Indra</s>'s favor, may we conquer; may we partake of offspring and nourishment.
(PB 1.5.16) O drop of <s>Soma</s>, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, possessing <s>Indra</s>'s power, of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, of all the hosts, invoked among all hosts — I partake of you, the invoked one.
(PB 1.5.17) My life, my breath — you are my breath, my life, my wife. In the <s>ṛc</s> (verse), whatever of my mind has gone to <s>Yama</s>, or whatever has gone away from me — with King <s>Soma</s>, may we place that back in ourselves.
(PB 1.5.18) Whatever of my mind has gone far away to <s>Yama Vaivasvata</s> (son of the Sun) — turn that back to me, for living, not for dying, and for freedom from harm.
(PB 1.5.19) By which he won the contest with clear sight, by which he won the eagle, the bird <s>Suparṇa</s> — that which they call the eye, infinite in <s>Aditi</s> — may <s>Soma</s>, beholder of men, place that in me.

body.text:
(PB 1.6.1) aindraṃ saho 'sarji tasya ta indav indrapītasyendriyāvato 'nuṣṭupchandaso harivataḥ sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.6.2) indav indrapītasya ta indriyāvato 'nuṣṭupchandasaḥ sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.6.3) stutasya stutam asy ūrjasvat payasvad ā mā stotrasya strotraṃ. gamyād indravanto vanemahi bhakṣīmahi prajām iṣam
(PB 1.6.4) iṣṭayajuṣas te deva soma stutastomasya śastokthasya tirohnyasya yo 'śvasanir gosanir bhakṣas tasyopahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.6.5) ṛtasya tvā deva stomapade viṣṇor dhāmāni vi muñcāmy etat tvaṃ deva stomān avakaram agann aśīmahi vayaṃ pratiṣṭhām
(PB 1.6.6) somehānu mehi soma saha sadasa indriyeṇa
(PB 1.6.7) subhūr asi śreṣṭho raśmir devānāṃ saṃsad devānāṃ yātur yayā tanvā brahma jinvasi tayā mā jinva tayā mā janaya prakāśaṃ mā kuru
(PB 1.6.8) apāṃ puṣpam asy oṣadhīnāṃ rasa indrasya priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāhā
(PB 1.6.9) hāriyojanasya te deva someṣṭayajuṣaḥ stutastomasya śastokthasya yo 'śvasanir gosanir bhakṣas tasyopahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 1.6.10) devakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi pitṛkṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi manuṣyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asy asmatkṛtasyainaso 'vayajanam asi yad divā ca naktaṃ cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asi yat svapantaś ca jāgrataś cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asi yad vidvāṃsaś cāvidvāṃsaś cainaś cakṛma tasyāvayajanam asy enasa-enasāvayajanam asi
(PB 1.6.11) apsu ghautasya te deva soma nṛbhiḥ sutasya
(PB 1.6.12) madhumantaṃ bhakṣaṃ karomi
(PB 1.6.13) sam adbhya oṣadhībhyaḥ
(PB 1.6.14) kāmakāmaṃ ma ā vartaya
(PB 1.6.15) ūrg asy ūrjam mayi dhehi
(PB 1.6.16) prāṇa somapīthe me jāgṛhi
(PB 1.6.17) dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣaṃ jiṣṇor aśvasya vājinaḥ / surabhi no mukhā karat pra na āyūṃṣi tāriṣat
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.6.1) The <s>Aindra</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s>) vigor has been released; of that, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma drop), drunk by <s>Indra</s>, possessed of <s>Indra</s>'s power, of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter, possessing the bay horses, of all hosts, O all hosts, invoked, of the invoked, I partake.
(PB 1.6.2) O <s>Indu</s>, of that which is drunk by <s>Indra</s>, of yours possessed of <s>Indra</s>'s power, of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter, of all hosts, O all hosts, invoked, of the invoked, I partake.
(PB 1.6.3) You are the praised of the praised, full of vigor, full of milk — may the praise of the <s>stotra</s> come to me. May we win those endowed with <s>Indra</s>; may we partake; may we consume progeny and nourishment.
(PB 1.6.4) Of you, O divine <s>Soma</s>, who have been offered with the desired <s>yajus</s> formulas, of the praised <s>stoma</s>, of the recited <s>uktha</s>, of the hidden one, who are the horse-winning, cattle-winning portion — of that, invoked, of the invoked, I partake.
(PB 1.6.5) At the chanting-station of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), O divine one, I release you to the abodes of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. You, O divine one, have entered the <s>stomas</s> as residue. May we consume stability.
(PB 1.6.6) O <s>Soma</s>, come along with me; O <s>Soma</s>, together with the assembly, with <s>Indra</s>'s power.
(PB 1.6.7) You are the well-born one, the best ray of the <s>devas</s>, the assembly of the <s>devas</s>, the course of the <s>devas</s>. With that body by which you invigorate <s>Brahman</s>, by that invigorate me, by that generate me, make me radiant.
(PB 1.6.8) You are the flower of the waters, the essence of the herbs, the dearest oblation of <s>Indra</s>. <s>Svāhā</s>!
(PB 1.6.9) Of you, O divine <s>Soma</s>, of the <s>Hāriyojana</s> (yoked with bay horses), who have been offered with the desired <s>yajus</s> formulas, of the praised <s>stoma</s>, of the recited <s>uktha</s>, who are the horse-winning, cattle-winning portion — of that, invoked, of the invoked, I partake.
(PB 1.6.10) You are the expiation of sin committed by the <s>devas</s>; you are the expiation of sin committed by the ancestors; you are the expiation of sin committed by humans; you are the expiation of sin committed by us. Whatever sin we committed by day and by night, you are its expiation; whatever sin we committed while sleeping and while waking, you are its expiation; whatever sin we committed knowingly and unknowingly, you are its expiation. You are the expiation of sin after sin.
(PB 1.6.11) O divine <s>Soma</s>, of you who were washed in the waters, pressed by men,
(PB 1.6.12) I make a honey-sweet drink.
(PB 1.6.13) Together with the waters and herbs,
(PB 1.6.14) Turn desire after desire toward me.
(PB 1.6.15) You are vigor; place vigor in me.
(PB 1.6.16) O <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath), be wakeful at the <s>Soma</s>-drinking.
(PB 1.6.17) I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>, the victorious swift horse. May he make our mouths fragrant; may he extend our lifespans.

body.text:
(PB 1.7.1) aśvo 'sy atyo 'si mayo 'si hayo 'si vājy asi saptir arvāg si vṛṣāsi
(PB 1.7.2) ādityānāṃ patmānv ihi namas te 'stu mā mā hiṃsīḥ
(PB 1.7.3) vāyoṣ ṭvā tejasā prati gṛhṇāmi nakṣatrāṇāṃ tvāṃ rūpeṇa prati gṛhṇāmi sūryasya tvā varcasā prati gṛhṇāmi
(PB 1.7.4) rathantaram asi vāmadevyam asi bṛhad asi
(PB 1.7.5) aṅkānyaṅkū abhito rathaṃ yau dhvāntaṃ vātāgram abhisaṃcaratau dūre hetir indriyavān patatrī te no 'gnayaḥ paprayaḥ pārayantu
(PB 1.7.6) vaiśvānaraḥ pratnathā nākam ā ruha divaḥ pṛṣṭhe mandamānaḥ sumanmabhiḥ sapūrvavaj jantave dhanāḥ samānam ayman pary eti jāgṛviḥ
(PB 1.7.7) gidaiṣa te ratha eṣa vām aśvinā ratho 'riṣṭo viśvabheṣajaḥ
(PB 1.7.8) kṛśāno savyān ā yaccha
(PB 1.7.9) dāsāno dakṣiṇān ava gṛhāṇa
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.7.1) You are a horse, you are a racer, you are a whinnyer, you are a steed, you are a prize-winner, you are a swift one, you are a stallion.
(PB 1.7.2) Follow the paths of the <s>Ādityas</s>. Homage to you; do not harm me.
(PB 1.7.3) I receive you with the brilliance of <s>Vāyu</s>; I receive you with the form of the <s>Nakṣatras</s> (constellations); I receive you with the radiance of <s>Sūrya</s>.
(PB 1.7.4) You are the <s>Rathantara</s>, you are the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, you are the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 1.7.5) Two hooks on either side of the chariot, which move together toward the dark wind-front — far-reaching is the missile, winged and powerful. May our fires carry us across to the far shore.
(PB 1.7.6) <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire), in the ancient way, ascended to heaven, rejoicing on the ridge of the sky with beautiful hymns. Like the former ones, he goes around providing wealth to mortals, the same one, ever wakeful.
(PB 1.7.7) Take it — this is your chariot, this chariot of yours, O <s>Aśvins</s>, unharmed, a remedy for all.
(PB 1.7.8) O <s>Kṛśānu</s>, extend the left ones.
(PB 1.7.9) O <s>Dāsāna</s>, take hold of the right ones.

body.text:
(PB 1.8.1) devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prati gṛhṇāmi
(PB 1.8.2) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe varuṇāyāśvaṃ tenāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.3) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe rudrāya gāṃ tayāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.4) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe 'gnaye 'jam
(PB 1.8.5) agnaye hiraṇyam
(PB 1.8.6) agnīṣomābhyām ajān mayāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.7) annasyānnapatiḥ prādād anamīvasya śuṣmiṇo namo viśvajanasya kṣāmāya bhuñjati mā mā hiṃsīḥ
(PB 1.8.8) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe tvaṣṭre 'viṃ tayāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.9) gnās tvā 'kṛntann apaso 'tanvata vayitryo 'vayan
(PB 1.8.10) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe bṛhaspataye vāsas tenāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigṛhītre
(PB 1.8.11) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe uttānāyāṅgirasāyāprāṇat tenāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.12) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe pūṣṇa uṣṭram
(PB 1.8.13) vāyave mṛgaṃ tenāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.14) jāpataye hastinaṃ prajāpataye varāhaṃ prajāpataye vrīhiyavāṃs tair amṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.15) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe kṣetrapataye tilamāṣās tair amṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.16) varuṇas tvā nayatu devi dakṣiṇe savitre 'śvataraṃ vāśvatarīṃ vā tayāmṛtatvam aśīya vayo dātre bhūyān mayo mahyaṃ pratigrahītre
(PB 1.8.17) ka idaṃ kasmā adāt kāmaḥ kāmāyādāt kāmo dātā kāmaḥ pratigrahītā kāmaḥ samudram āviśat kāmena tvā prati gṛhṇāmi kāmaitat te
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.8.1) At the impulse of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I receive you.
(PB 1.8.2) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial gift). A horse for <s>Varuṇa</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.3) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A cow for <s>Rudra</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.4) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A goat for <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 1.8.5) Gold for <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 1.8.6) Goats for <s>Agnīṣomau</s> (Agni and Soma together) — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.7) The lord of food has given food — of the vigorous and disease-free. Homage to the ground of all people. He who eats — do not harm me.
(PB 1.8.8) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A sheep for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.9) The divine women cut you; the workers wove; the weavers wove.
(PB 1.8.10) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A garment for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.11) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. To <s>Uttānā Āṅgirasī</s>, who breathed forth — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.12) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A camel for <s>Pūṣan</s>.
(PB 1.8.13) A wild animal for <s>Vāyu</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.14) An elephant for <s>Prajāpati</s>; a boar for <s>Prajāpati</s>; rice and barley for <s>Prajāpati</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.15) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. Sesame and beans for <s>Kṣetrapati</s> (lord of the field) — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.16) May <s>Varuṇa</s> lead you, O divine <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. A mule or a she-mule for <s>Savitṛ</s> — thereby may I attain immortality; may there be vitality for the giver, and delight for me the receiver.
(PB 1.8.17) Who gave this and to whom? <s>Kāma</s> (Desire) gave to <s>Kāma</s>. <s>Kāma</s> is the giver, <s>Kāma</s> the receiver. <s>Kāma</s> entered the ocean. By <s>Kāma</s> I receive you. This is yours, O <s>Kāma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 1.9.1) raśmir asi kṣayāya tvā kṣayaṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.2) pretir asi dharmaṇe tvā dharmaṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.3) anvitir asi dive tvā divaṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.4) saṃdhir asy antarikṣāya tvāntarikṣaṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.5) pratidhir asi pṛthivyai tvā pṛthivīṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.6) viṣṭambho 'si vṛṣṭyai tvā vṛṣṭiṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.7) prāco 'sy ahne tvāhar jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.8) anvāsi rātryai rātriṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.9) uśig asi vasubhyas tvā vasūn jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.10) praketo 'si rudrebhyas tvā rudrān jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.11) sudītir asy ādityebhyas tvādityān jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.9.12) ojo 'si pitṛbhyas tvā pitṝn jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.9.1) You are a ray; for dwelling, invigorate dwelling — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.2) You are advancement; for <s>dharma</s>, invigorate <s>dharma</s> — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.3) You are a following; for heaven, invigorate heaven — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.4) You are a junction; for the atmosphere, invigorate the atmosphere — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.5) You are a support; for the earth, invigorate the earth — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.6) You are a pillar; for rain, invigorate rain — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.7) You are the eastern one; for day, invigorate day — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.8) You are the follower; for night, invigorate night — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.9) You are the eager one; for the <s>Vasus</s>, invigorate the <s>Vasus</s> — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.10) You are the herald; for the <s>Rudras</s>, invigorate the <s>Rudras</s> — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.11) You are the well-shining one; for the <s>Ādityas</s>, invigorate the <s>Ādityas</s> — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.9.12) You are vigor; for the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>), invigorate the ancestors — impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

body.text:
(PB 1.10.1) tantur asi prajābhyas tvā prajā jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.2) rodasy asy oṣadhībhyas tvauṣadhīr jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.3) pṛtanāṣāḍ asi paśubhyas tvā paśūn jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.4) abhijid asi yuktagrāvendrāya tvendraṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.5) adhipatir asi prāṇāya tvā prāṇān jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.6) dharuṇo 'sy apānāya tvāpānān jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.7) saṃsarpo 'si cakṣuṣe tvā cakṣur jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.8) vayodhā asi kṣetrāya tvā kṣetraṃ jinva savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.9) trivṛd asi trivṛte tvā savṛd asi savṛte tvā pravṛd asi pravṛte tvānuvṛd asy anuvṛte tvā savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.10) niroho 'si nirohāya tvā saṃroho 'si saṃrohāya tvā praroho 'si prarohāya tvānuroho 'sy anurohāya tvā savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.11) vasuko 'si vasyaṣṭir asi veṣaśrīr asi savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
(PB 1.10.12) ākramo 'sy ākramāya tvā saṃkramo 'si saṃkramāya tvotkramo 'sy utkramāya tvotkrāntir asy utkrāntyai tvā savitṛprasūtā bṛhaspataye stuta
body.translated_text:
(PB 1.10.1) You are the warp; for offspring I enliven you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.2) You are the two worlds (heaven and earth); for herbs I enliven you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.3) You are the conqueror of armies; for cattle I enliven you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.4) You are the victorious one with pressed Soma stones; for <s>Indra</s> I enliven you, enliven <s>Indra</s>. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.5) You are the overlord; for the in-breath I enliven you, I enliven the vital breaths. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.6) You are the support; for the out-breath I enliven you, I enliven the out-breaths. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.7) You are the creeping one; for the eye I enliven you, I enliven the eye. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.8) You are the giver of vitality; for the field I enliven you, I enliven the field. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.9) You are the threefold; for the threefold I dedicate you. You are the well-turning; for the well-turning I dedicate you. You are the forward-turning; for the forward-turning I dedicate you. You are the following-turning; for the following-turning I dedicate you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.10) You are the sprouting down; for sprouting down I dedicate you. You are the sprouting together; for sprouting together I dedicate you. You are the sprouting forth; for sprouting forth I dedicate you. You are the sprouting after; for sprouting after I dedicate you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.11) You are the giver of wealth; you are the rod of wealth; you are the splendor of adornment. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
(PB 1.10.12) You are the step forward; for stepping forward I dedicate you. You are the step across; for stepping across I dedicate you. You are the step upward; for stepping upward I dedicate you. You are the ascent; for ascending I dedicate you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

body.text:
(PB 2.1.1) tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa prathamayā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa madhyamayā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa uttamayodyatī trivṛto viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.1.2) jyeṣṭho jyaiṣṭhineya stuvīta
(PB 2.1.3) agrād agraṃ rohaty abhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāmantyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
(PB 2.1.4) pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtir vipāpmanā vartate ya etayā stute nāvagato 'pa rudhyate nāparuddho 'va gacchati / na śreyāṃsaṃ pāpīyān abhyā rohati na janatā janatām abhy eti nānyo 'nyasya prajā ā dadate yathākṣetraṃ kalpante / avarṣukas tu parjanyo bhavatīme hi lokās tṛcas tān hiṅkāreṇa vy eti
(PB 2.1.5) eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā trivṛto viṣṭutiḥ prati tiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.1.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> (the syllable 'hiṅ') over three verses — that is the first. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three — that is the middle. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three — that is the last. The ascending <s>viṣṭuti</s> (hymn-arrangement) of the <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold <s>stoma</s>).
(PB 2.1.2) The eldest, the son of the eldest, should chant it.
(PB 2.1.3) It rises from beginning to beginning; it is an advancing <s>viṣṭuti</s>. By advancing, indeed by what has been advanced, the sacrifice succeeds. Therefore one should chant with this — for prosperity indeed.
(PB 2.1.4) The <s>vidhṛti</s> (separation) of those whose garments are worse; one moves free from evil by it. He who is praised with this is not cut off if he falls down, nor does he fall down if he is cut off. The worse does not rise above the better, nor does one people overpower another people, nor does one take away the offspring of another — they are arranged according to their fields. But <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) does not send rain, for these worlds are <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three verses) — he separates them by the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
(PB 2.1.5) This is the established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trivṛt</s>. He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 2.2.1) tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhis tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhis tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhiḥ parivartinī triviṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.2.2) praparīvartam āpnoti ya etayā stute saṃtatā viṣṭutiḥ prāṇo 'pāno vyānas ta ṛcas tān hiṅkāreṇa saṃ tanoti / sarvam āyur eti na purāyuṣaḥ pra mīyate ya etayā stute varṣukaḥ parjanyo bhavatīme hi lokās tṛcas tān hiṅkāreṇa saṃ dadhāti
(PB 2.2.3) ślakṣṇeva tu vā īśvarā paśūn nirmṛjaḥ saiṣā ca parācota śreyān bhavaty uta yādṛṅ eva tādṛṅ net tu pāpīyān
(PB 2.2.4) tām etāṃ bhāllavaya upāsate tasmāt te pratigṛṇantaḥ parīvartān na cyavante
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.2.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three verses in reverse order; he makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three in reverse order; he makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three in reverse order. This is the revolving <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trivṛt</s>.
(PB 2.2.2) He who is praised with this attains a complete revolution. The <s>viṣṭuti</s> is continuous. <s>Prāṇa</s> (in-breath), <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) — these are the <s>ṛcas</s> (verses); he weaves them together by the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. He lives the full life-span; he does not die before his time, he who is praised with this. <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) sends rain, for these worlds are <s>tṛcas</s> — he binds them together by the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
(PB 2.2.3) But like a smooth surface, this one has the power to wipe away cattle. With this one turns away — either one becomes better or remains as one is, but never becomes worse.
(PB 2.2.4) The <s>Bhāllavas</s> practice this. Therefore they, receiving gifts, do not fall from their revolutions.

body.text:
(PB 2.3.1) tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhis tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti yā madhyamā sā prathamā yottamā sā madhyamā yā prathamā sottamā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti yottamā sā prathamā yā prathamā sā madhyamā yā madhyamā sottamā kulāyinī trivṛto viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.3.2) prajākāmo vā paśukāmo vā stuvīta vai kulānāyapaśavaḥ kulāyaṃ-kulāyam eva bhavati
(PB 2.3.3) etām evānujāvarāya kuryād etāsām evāgraṃ pariyatīnāṃ prajānā[m] agraṃ pary eti
(PB 2.3.4) etām eva bahubhyo yajamānebhyaḥ kuryāt yat sarvā agriyā bhavanti sarvā madhye sarvā uttamāḥ sarvān evainān samāvadbhājaḥ karoti nānyo 'nyam apa ghnate sarve samāvadindriyā bhavanti
(PB 2.3.5) varṣukaḥ parjanyo bhavatīme hi lokās tṛcas tān hiṅkāreṇa vyati ṣajati
(PB 2.3.6) pāpavasīyasaṃ tu bhavati
(PB 2.3.7) adharottaram apāvagato rudhyateva gacchaty aparuddhaḥ pāpīyān śreyāṃsam abhyā rohati janatā janatām abhy ety anyo 'nyasya prajā ā dadate na yathākṣetraṃ kalpante
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.3.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three in reverse order; he makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three — that which is the middle becomes the first, that which is the last becomes the middle, that which is the first becomes the last; he makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three — that which is the last becomes the first, that which is the first becomes the middle, that which is the middle becomes the last. This is the nest-like <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trivṛt</s>.
(PB 2.3.2) One desiring offspring or one desiring cattle should chant it. Indeed, cattle are in the nest — one becomes a nest, as it were.
(PB 2.3.3) One should perform this for one whose offspring fails. It goes to the beginning of those who have gone around — one goes to the beginning of offspring.
(PB 2.3.4) One should perform this for many sacrificers. Since all become first, all become middle, all become last — it makes them all equal sharers. One does not strike down the other; all become equal in vital powers.
(PB 2.3.5) <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) sends rain, for these worlds are <s>tṛcas</s> — he interweaves them by the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
(PB 2.3.6) But it tends toward worse garments.
(PB 2.3.7) It causes inversion of higher and lower — one who has fallen down is cut off, one goes as if obstructed even when unobstructed. The worse rises above the better, one people overpowers another people, one takes away the offspring of another — they are not arranged according to their fields.

body.text:
(PB 2.4.1) pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa ekayā pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ pañcapañcinī pañcapañcadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.4.2) pāṅktaḥ puruṣaḥ pāṅktāt paśavas tayā puruṣaṃ ca paśūṃś cāpnoti vajro vai pancapaśo yat pañca-pañca vyūhati vajram eva tad vy ūhati śāntyā eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā pañcadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ prati tiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.4.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — three, then one, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — one, then three, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — one, then one, then three. This is the five-by-five <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold <s>stoma</s>).
(PB 2.4.2) Man is fivefold; cattle are born from the fivefold. By this one obtains both man and cattle. The <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) is indeed fivefold — since one arranges in groups of five, one thereby arranges the <s>vajra</s>. For pacification — this is the established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>pañcadaśa</s>. He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 2.5.1) pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhiḥ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhis
(PB 2.5.2) trīn stomān prativihitā brahmavarcasakāmaḥ stuvīta
(PB 2.5.3) pañcabhiḥ pañcadaśaṃ tisṛbhis trivṛtaṃ saptabhiḥ saptadaśam
(PB 2.5.4) vīryaṃ vai stomā vīryam eva tad ekadhā samūhate brahmavarcasyāvaruddhyai tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.5.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — three, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three in reverse order. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over seven — one, then three, then three.
(PB 2.5.2) It is arranged against three <s>stomas</s> (hymn forms). One desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge should chant it.
(PB 2.5.3) With five it makes the <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold), with three the <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold), with seven the <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold).
(PB 2.5.4) The <s>stomas</s> are indeed vigor — it gathers vigor together in one way for the attainment of the splendor of sacred knowledge. He who is praised with this becomes radiant with the splendor of sacred knowledge.

body.text:
(PB 2.6.1) tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhiḥ pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir udyatī pañcadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.6.2) etayā vai devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyan svargakāmaḥ stuvīta svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 2.6.3) abhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāmantyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.6.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over three in reverse order. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — one, then three, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over seven — one, then three, then three. This is the ascending <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>pañcadaśa</s>.
(PB 2.6.2) By this the gods went to the heavenly world. One desiring heaven should chant it, for the attainment of the heavenly world. He who has chanted does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 2.6.3) It is an advancing <s>viṣṭuti</s>. By advancing, indeed by what has been advanced, the sacrifice succeeds. Therefore one should chant with this — for prosperity indeed.

body.text:
(PB 2.7.1) pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa ekayā pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir daśasaptā saptadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.7.2) etayā vai devā asurān aty akrāmann ati pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ krāmati ya etayā stute
(PB 2.7.3) abhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāmantyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
(PB 2.7.4) garbhiṇī viṣṭutiḥ pa prajayā pra paśubhir jāyate ya etayā stute
(PB 2.7.5) viḍ vai saptadaśas tasyā rājā garbho viśa eva tad rājānaṃ garbhaṃ karoti
(PB 2.7.6) nāvagato 'pa rudhyate nāparuddho 'va gacchati
(PB 2.7.7) annaṃ vai saptadaśo yat sapta madhye bhavanti pañca-pañcābhito 'nnam eva tan madhyato dhīyate 'naśanāyuko yajamāno bhavaty anaśanāyukāḥ prajāḥ
(PB 2.7.8) vairājo vai puruṣaḥ sapta grāmyāḥ paśavo yad daśapūrvā bhavanti saptottamā yajamānam eva tat paśuṣu prati ṣṭhāpayati
(PB 2.7.9) eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā saptadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ prati tiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.7.1) He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — three, then one, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over five — one, then three, then one. He makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over seven — one, then three, then three. The ten-and-seven — this is the <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold <s>stoma</s>).
(PB 2.7.2) By this the gods surpassed the <s>Asuras</s>. He who is praised with this surpasses evil and the hostile rival.
(PB 2.7.3) It is an advancing <s>viṣṭuti</s>. By advancing, indeed by what has been advanced, the sacrifice succeeds. Therefore one should chant with this — for prosperity indeed.
(PB 2.7.4) It is a pregnant <s>viṣṭuti</s>. He who is praised with this prospers with offspring and with cattle.
(PB 2.7.5) The <s>viś</s> (people) is indeed the <s>saptadaśa</s>; its king is the embryo. It thus makes the king the embryo of the people.
(PB 2.7.6) He who has fallen is not cut off; he who is cut off does not fall.
(PB 2.7.7) Food is indeed the <s>saptadaśa</s>. Since seven are in the middle and five-and-five on either side, food is placed in the middle. The sacrificer becomes free from hunger; his offspring become free from hunger.
(PB 2.7.8) Man is the <s>Virāj</s> (cosmic meter); seven are the domestic animals. Since ten are first and seven are last, it establishes the sacrificer among his cattle.
(PB 2.7.9) This is the established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>saptadaśa</s>. He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 2.8.1) eṣa eva vyūhaḥ saptaikamadhyā
(PB 2.8.2) brahmaṇo vā āyatanaṃ prathamā kṣatrasya madhyamā viśa uttamā yat prathamā bhūyiṣṭhā bhājayati brahmaṇy eva tad ojo vīryaṃ dadhāti brahmaṇa eva tat kṣatraṃ ca viśaṃ cānuge karoti kṣatrasyāsya prakāśo bhavati ya etayā stute
(PB 2.8.3) tām etāṃ trikharvā upāsate tasmāt te spardhamānā na vlīyante
(PB 2.9.1) saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti parācībhiḥ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ saptāsthitā
(PB 2.9.2) bhrātṛvyaṃ stuvīta yathā saptāsthitena matyena samī karoty evaṃ pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ pra rujati
(PB 2.9.3) etām eva bahubhyo yajamānebhyaḥ kuryād yaḥ prathamo hiṅkāraḥ sa prathamāyā yattāṃ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti tena sā sapta bhajate yat saptaiva madhye sapadyante tena sā sapta bhajate ya uttamo hiṅkāraḥ sa uttamayā yattāṃ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti tena sā sapta bhajate sarvān evainān samāvadbhājaḥ karoti nānyo 'nyam apa ghnate samāvadindriyā bhavanti
(PB 2.9.4) tām etām abhipratāriṇa upāsate tasmāt ta ojiṣṭhāsvānām
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.8.1) This is the arrangement (<s>vyūha</s>): seven with one in the middle.
(PB 2.8.2) The first [group] belongs to <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly order), the middle to <s>Kṣatra</s> (the warrior order), the last to <s>Viś</s> (the commoners). Because the first group is the most numerous in the distribution, thereby one places vigor and vitality in <s>Brahman</s>. Thereby one makes <s>Kṣatra</s> and <s>Viś</s> subordinate to <s>Brahman</s>. Brilliance belongs to his <s>Kṣatra</s>, for him who chants with this.
(PB 2.8.3) This [is to be arranged] in three sections,

body.text:
(PB 2.10.1) eṣa eva vyūha ubhayaḥ saptaikamadhyā nirmadhyā
(PB 2.10.2) ānujāvara stuvītāloko vā eṣa yad ānujāvaro yat saptaprathamāḥ saptottamās tisro madhye tryakṣaraḥ puruṣo lokam evāsmai tan madhyataḥ karoti tasmiṃl loke prati tiṣṭhati
(PB 2.10.3) etām eva prajākāmāya kuryān madhyato vā eṣa saṃrūḍho yaḥ prajāṃ na vindate lokam evāsmai taṃ madhyataḥ karoti taṃ lokaṃ prajayā ca paśubhiś cānu pra jāyate
(PB 2.10.4) etām evāparuddharājanyāya kuryād viḍ vai saptadaśas tasyā rājā garbho viśa eva tad rājānaṃ nir hanty apāvagato 'pa rudhyate 'va gacchaty aparuddhaḥ
(PB 2.10.5) etām evābhicaryamāṇāya kuryāt prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajāpatim eva madhyattaḥ pra viśanty astṛtyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.10.1) This is the arrangement, both ways: seven with one in the middle, and without a middle.
(PB 2.10.2) One should chant with the <s>ānujāvara</s> (progressive) pattern. This <s>ānujāvara</s> is indeed light. Because the first seven and the last seven have three in the middle — the person has three syllables — thereby one establishes the world for him from the center; in that world he stands firm.
(PB 2.10.3) One should perform this for one desiring offspring. From the center, indeed, this one is formed,

body.text:
(PB 2.11.1) pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa ekayā tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhir navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 2.11.2) caturastomān prativihitā brahmavarcasakāmāḥ stuvīta pañcabhiḥ pañcadaśaṃ tisṛbhis trivṛtaṃ navabhis triṇavaṃ svayaṃ saptadaśaḥ sampanno vīryaṃ vai stomā vīryam eva tad ekadhā samūhate brahmavarcasyāvaruddhyai tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.11.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over three, then over one, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over three. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine in reverse order, then over three, then over three, then over three.
(PB 2.11.2) These are arranged upon the four <s>stomas</s> (chant patterns). One desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmic splendor) should chant: with five the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold), with three the <s>Trivṛt</s> (three-fold), with nine the <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold); he himself becomes the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold), thus accomplished.

body.text:
(PB 2.12.1) tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhiḥ pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir udyatīsaptadaśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.12.2) etayā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan svargakāmaḥ stuvīta svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvāno 'bhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāntyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.12.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over three in reverse order. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over one, then over three, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over three, then over three, ascending. This is the <s>viṣṭuti</s> (chant-arrangement) of the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold).
(PB 2.12.2) By this, indeed, the gods ascended to the heavenly world. One desiring heaven should chant with this, for the attainment of the heavenly world. He does not fall from the heavenly world.

body.text:
(PB 2.13.1) saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa ekayā sa tisṛbhir bhastrāvācīnabilā
(PB 2.13.2) yaṃ dviṣyāt tasya kuryād yathāvācīnabilayā bhastrayā pradhūnuyād evaṃ yajamānasya paśūn pradhūnoty apakrāmantī viṣṭutis tayā yajamānasya paśavo 'pakrāmanti pāpīyān bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.13.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over three, then over three, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over one, then over three, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over one, then over one, then over three. This is [called] 'the bellows with the opening downward.'
(PB 2.13.2) One should perform this against one whom one hates. Just as one would blow away [chaff] with a bellows having the opening downward, so does it blow away the cattle of the sacrificer's [enemy].

body.text:
(PB 2.14.1) saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ saptasaptiny ekaviṃśasya viṣsṭutiḥ
(PB 2.14.2) sapta grāmyāḥ paśavas tān etayā spṛṇoti sapta śirasi prāṇāḥ prāṇā indriyāṇīndriyāṇy evaitayāpnoti
(PB 2.14.3) eṣā vai pratiṣthitaikaviṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.14.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over three, then over three, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over one, then over three, then over three. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over three, then over one, then over three. This is the <s>viṣṭuti</s> (chant-arrangement) of the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold), arranged in sevens.
(PB 2.14.2) There are seven domestic animals; by this one wins them. There are seven vital breaths in the head. The vital breaths are the sense faculties; the sense faculties,

body.text:
(PB 2.15.1) pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa ekayā saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir udyaty ekaviṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.15.2) etayā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan svargakāmaḥ stuvīta svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvāno 'bhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāntyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
(PB 2.15.3) saiṣā trivṛt prāyaṇā trivṛd udayanā yat trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ bhavati navaitā ekaviṃśasyottamā bhavanti prāṇā vai trivṛt prāṇān eva tad ubhayato dadhāti tasmād ayam ardhabhāgavāk (?) prāṇa uttareṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ sarvam āyur eti na purāyuṣaḥ pramīyate ya etayā stute
(PB 2.15.4) tām etāṃ kradviṣa upāsate tasmāt te sarvam āyur yanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.15.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over three, then over one, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over one, then over three, then over three. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over three, then over three, ascending. This is the <s>viṣṭuti</s> (chant-arrangement) of the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold).
(PB 2.15.2) By this, indeed, the gods ascended to the heavenly world. One desiring heaven should chant with this, for the attainment of the heavenly world, for the attainment of heaven.

body.text:
(PB 2.16.1) navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ pañcabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ pratiṣṭutiḥ
(PB 2.16.2) navabhis trivṛtaṃ pratiṣṭauti pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcadaśaṃ saptabhiḥ saptadaśaṃ svayam ekaviṃśaḥ saṃpannaḥ
(PB 2.16.3) sa eva stomā yajñaṃ vahanti tān uttame stotre saṃtarpayati yathānaḍuho vāśvān vāśvatarān vohuṣaḥ saṃtarpayed evam etad uttame stotre stomān saṃtarpayati tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir ya etayā stute
(PB 2.16.4) etām eva purodhākāmāya kuryād brahma vai trivṛt kṣatram ekaviṃśo yat trivṛtaikaviṃśaṃ pratipadyate brahma tat kṣatrasya purastān nidadhāti gacchati purodhāṃ na purodhāyāś cyavate ya etayā stute
(PB 2.16.5) tām etāṃ prāvāhaṇya upāsate tasmāt te purodhāyā na cyavanta
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.16.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over three, then over three. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over five, then over one, then over three, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over seven, then over three, then over one, then over three. This is the counter-chant (<s>pratiṣṭuti</s>).
(PB 2.16.2) With nine he counter-establishes the <s>Trivṛt</s> (three-fold), with five the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold), with seven the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold); he himself becomes the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold), thus accomplished.

body.text:
(PB 2.17.1) navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhis tisṛbhyo hiṅ karoti sa parācībhir navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sūrmy ubhayata ādīptā
(PB 2.17.2) brahmavarcasakāmaḥ stuvīta tejo vai trivṛt tryakṣaraḥ puruṣo yat trivṛtāv abhito bhavatas tisro madhye yathā hi hiraṇyaṃ niṣṭaped evam enaṃ trivṛtau niṣṭapatas tejase brahmavarcasāya
(PB 2.17.3) apaśavy eva tu vā īśvarā paśūn nirdahaḥ kilāsattvān nūbhayamati hi niṣṭapataḥ
(PB 2.17.4) etām evābhiśasyamānāya kuryāc chamalaṃ vā etam ṛcchati yam aślīlā vāg ṛcchati yaivainam asāv aślīlaṃ vāg vadati tām asya trivṛtau niṣṭapatas tejasvī bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 2.17.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over three, then over three. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over three in reverse order. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over three, then over three. This is [called] 'the wave blazing on both sides.'
(PB 2.17.2) One desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmic splendor) should chant with this. The <s>Trivṛt</s> (three-fold) is indeed radiance. The person has three syllables. Because the <s>Trivṛt</s> patterns are on both sides with three in the middle, just as

body.text:
(PB 3.1.1) navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhiḥ sa ekayā navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhir navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa pañcabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.1.2) vajro vai triṇavo vajram eva tad vyūhati śāntyai
(PB 3.1.3) pañcabhir vihitaikā paricarā pāṅktāḥ paśavo yajamānaḥ paricarā yat pañcabhir vidadhāty ekā paricarā bhavati yajamānam eva tat paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayaty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā triṇavasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.1.1) He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over three, then over five, then over one. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over one, then over three, then over five. He makes the <s>hiṃ</s> sound over nine, then over five, then over one, then over three.
(PB 3.1.2) The <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold) is indeed the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>). Thereby one arranges the thunderbolt, for the sake of pacification.
(PB 3.1.3) Arranged with five, one is the attendant. The animals are related to the <s>Pāṅkta</s> (five-fold meter). The sacrificer

body.text:
(PB 3.2.1) saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa pañcabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir udyatī triṇavasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 3.2.2) etayā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan svargakāmaḥ stuvīta svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvāno 'bhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāntyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.2.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over seven verses: three of them, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over nine: one of them, then three, then five — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: five of them, then three, then three. This is the ascending <s>viṣṭuti</s> (arrangement of praise-verses) of the <s>triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-versed stoma).
(PB 3.2.2) By this indeed the gods ascended to the heavenly world. One who desires heaven should praise with it, for the attainment of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world. This is a progressive <s>viṣṭuti</s>; through progression indeed, for by what has progressed the sacrifice prospers. Therefore one should praise with this — for prosperity indeed.

body.text:
(PB 3.3.1) ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayaikādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.3.2) anto vai trayastriṃśaḥ paramo vai trayastriṃśa stomānāṃ saptabhir vihitaikā paricarā sapta grāmyāḥ paśavo yajamānaḥ paricarā yat saptabhir vidadhāty ekā paricarā bhavati yajamānam eva tad antataḥ paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayaty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā trayastriṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.3.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: three of them, then seven, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: one of them, then three, then seven — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: seven of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.3.2) Thirty-three is indeed the final and supreme among <s>stomas</s> (praise-configurations). It is arranged with seven; one serves as attendant. Seven are the domestic animals; the sacrificer is the attendant. When he arranges with seven, one becomes the attendant — thereby he establishes the sacrificer among animals at the very end. This is indeed the firmly established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-versed stoma). He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 3.4.1) ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhiḥ sa tisṛbhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa pañcabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir nedīyaḥsaṃkramā
(PB 3.4.2) anto vai trayastriṃśo yathā mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ sṛptvā nedīyaḥsaṃkramāt saṃkrāmaty evam etan nedīyaḥsaṃkramayā nedīyaḥsaṃkramāt saṃkrāmati
(PB 3.4.3) pañcabhir vihitās tisraḥ paricarāḥ pāṅktāḥ paśava etāvān puruṣo yadātmā prajā jāyā yat pañcabhir vidadhāti tisraḥ paricarā bhavanti yajamānam eva tat paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati paśumān bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.4.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: three of them, then five, then three — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: three of them, then three, then five — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: five of them, then three, then three. This is the 'near-crossing' (<s>nedīyaḥsaṃkramā</s>).
(PB 3.4.2) Thirty-three is indeed the final. Just as one who has climbed to the top of a great tree crosses over by a nearby bridge, even so by the 'near-crossing' one crosses over from the nearest crossing.
(PB 3.4.3) It is arranged with five; three serve as attendants. Animals belong to the group of five; a man is as much as this: himself, his offspring, and his wife. When he arranges with five, three become attendants — thereby he establishes the sacrificer among animals. He who is praised with this becomes possessed of animals.

body.text:
(PB 3.5.1) navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhiḥ sa ekayaikādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhis trayodaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa saptabhiḥ sa tisṛbhir udyatī trayastriṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 3.5.2) etayā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan svargakāmaḥ stuvīta svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvāno 'grād agraṃ rohaty abhikrāmantī viṣṭutir abhikrāntyā evābhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti tasmād etayā stotavyam ṛddhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.5.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over nine: three of them, then five, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: one of them, then three, then seven — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over thirteen: seven of them, then three. This is the ascending <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-versed stoma).
(PB 3.5.2) By this indeed the gods ascended to the heavenly world. One who desires heaven should praise with it, for the attainment of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world. He ascends from summit to summit. This is a progressive <s>viṣṭuti</s>; through progression indeed, for by what has progressed the sacrifice prospers. Therefore one should praise with this — for prosperity indeed.

body.text:
(PB 3.6.1) trayodaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhiḥ sa pañcabhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa pañcabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir navabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ pratyavarohiṇītrayastriṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ
(PB 3.6.2) yathā mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ sṛptvā śākhāyāḥ śākhām ālambham upāvarohed evam etayemaṃ lokam upāvarohati pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 3.6.3) trivṛtā praiti trivṛtodeti prāṇā vai trivṛt prāṇenaiva praiti prāṇam abhyudeti sarvam āyur eti na purāyuṣaḥ pramīyate ya etayā stute
(PB 3.6.4) tām etāṃ karadviṣa upāsate tasmāt te sarvam āyur yanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.6.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over thirteen: three of them, then five, then five — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: five of them, then three, then three — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over nine: three of them, then three, then three. This is the descending (<s>pratyavarohiṇī</s>) <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>trayastriṃśa</s>.
(PB 3.6.2) Just as one who has climbed to the top of a great tree descends by grasping branch after branch, even so by this one descends to this world — for firm establishment.
(PB 3.6.3) It proceeds with the <s>trivṛt</s> (three-fold), it rises with the <s>trivṛt</s>. The <s>trivṛt</s> is indeed <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath). By <s>prāṇa</s> alone he proceeds; he rises up to <s>prāṇa</s>. He lives his full lifespan; he does not die before his time — he who is praised with this.
(PB 3.6.4) The <s>Karadviṣas</s> practice this; therefore they live their full lifespan.

body.text:
(PB 3.7.1) pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa pañcabhir ekādaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa pañcabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ saptabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.7.2) yo vai trayastriṃśam ekaviṃśe pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśaḥ stomānāṃ yad etāḥ sapta trayastriṃśasyottamā bhavanti saptavidhaikaviṃśasya viṣṭutir ekaviṃśa eva tat trayastriṃśaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.7.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: three of them, then five — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eleven: five of them, then three, then three — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over seven: three of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.7.2) He who knows the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-versed stoma) as established in the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-versed stoma) becomes firmly established. The <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is indeed the firm foundation among <s>stomas</s>. When these seven become the final portion of the <s>trayastriṃśa</s>, it is the seven-fold <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>ekaviṃśa</s>. Thereby he establishes the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> in the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> itself. He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 3.8.1) aṣṭābhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa catasṛbhiḥ sa ekayāṣṭābhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa catasṛbhir aṣṭābhyo hiṅ karoti sa catasṛbhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.8.2) paśavo vai chandogā yad aṣṭābhyo-'ṣṭābhyo hiṅ karoti aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśas tat paśūn āpnoti
(PB 3.8.3) catasṛbhir vihitaikā paricarā catuṣpādāḥ paśavo yajamānaḥ paricarā yac catasṛbhir vidadhāty ekā paricarā bhavati yajamānam eva tat paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayaty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā caturviṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.8.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eight: three of them, then four, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eight: one of them, then three, then four — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eight: four of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.8.2) Animals are indeed the chanters (<s>chandogas</s>). When he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over eight after eight, animals have eight-part hooves — thereby he obtains animals, hoof by hoof.
(PB 3.8.3) It is arranged with four; one serves as attendant. Animals are four-footed; the sacrificer is the attendant. When he arranges with four, one becomes the attendant — thereby he establishes the sacrificer among animals at the very end. This is indeed the firmly established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-versed stoma). He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 3.9.1) pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekādaśabhiḥ sa ekayā caturdaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa daśabhiḥ pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekādaśabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.9.2) brahmaṇo vā āyatanaṃ prathamā kṣatrasya madhyamā viśa uttamā yat pañcadaśinyau pūrve bhavataś caturdaśottamā brahmaṇi caiva tat kṣatre caujo vīryaṃ dadhāti brahmaṇe caiva tat kṣatrāya ca viśam anugāṃ karoti kṣatrasyevāsya prakāśo bhavati ya etayā stute
(PB 3.9.3) astomā vā ete yac chandogā ayujo hi stomā yugmanti chandāṃsi yad eṣā yujinī catuścatvāriṃśasya viṣṭutis tenāstomāḥ
(PB 3.9.4) eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā catuścatvāriṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhait ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.9.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: three of them, then eleven, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fourteen: one of them, then three, then ten — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: eleven of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.9.2) The first triplet is the domain of <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly order), the middle one of <s>Kṣatra</s> (the warrior order), and the last of <s>Viś</s> (the common people). When the two sets of fifteen come first and the fourteen comes last, he thereby places vigor and power in both <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Kṣatra</s>, and makes the <s>Viś</s> subservient to <s>Kṣatra</s>. The brilliance of <s>Kṣatra</s> becomes his — he who is praised with this.
(PB 3.9.3) These chanters (<s>chandogas</s>) are indeed '<s>stoma</s>-less' (<s>astomā</s>), for <s>stomas</s> are odd-numbered while meters are even-numbered. Since this is the even-numbered <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>catuścatvāriṃśa</s> (forty-four-versed stoma), therefore they are '<s>stoma</s>-less.'
(PB 3.9.4) This is indeed the firmly established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>catuścatvāriṃśa</s>. He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 3.10.1) caturdaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa daśabhiḥ sa ekayā pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekādaśabhiḥ pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekādaśabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhir nirmadhyā
(PB 3.10.2) astīva vā ayaṃ loko 'stīvāsau chidram ivedam antarikṣaṃ yad eṣā nirmadhyā bhavatīmān eva lokān anu prajāyate pra prajayā pra paśubhir jāyate ya etayā stute
(PB 3.11.1) pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekādaśabhiḥ sa ekayā pañcadaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa ekādaśabhiḥ caturdaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa daśabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.11.2) ājyānāṃ prathamā pṛṣṭhānāṃ dvitīyokthānāṃ tṛtīyā
(PB 3.11.3) yājyānāṃ sā hotur yā pṛṣṭhānāṃ sā maitrāvaruṇasya yokthānāṃ sā brāhmaṇācchaṃsino yaiva hotuḥ sācchāvākasya yā pṛṣṭhānāṃ sahotur yokthānāṃ sā maitrāvaruṇasya yājyānāṃ sā brāhmaṇācchaṃsino yaiva hotuḥ sācchāvākasya yokthānāṃ sā hotur yājyānāṃ sā maitrāvaruṇasya yā pṛṣṭhānāṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsino yaiva hotuḥ sācchāvākasya sarvā ājyeṣu sarvāḥ pṛṣtheṣu sarvā uktheṣu
(PB 3.11.4) paśavo vai samīṣantī yad eṣā sarvāṇi savanāny anusaṃcaraty anusavanam evainaṃ paśubhiḥ samardhayati paśuman bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.10.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fourteen: three of them, then ten, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: one of them, then three, then eleven — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: eleven of them, then one, then three. This is the 'without-middle' (<s>nirmadhyā</s>).
(PB 3.10.2) This world exists, as it were, and that world exists, as it were — this intermediate space is like a gap. When this arrangement is 'without-middle,' he is born in accordance with these very worlds. He prospers in offspring and in animals — he who is praised with this.
(PB 3.11.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: three of them, then eleven, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fifteen: one of them, then three, then eleven — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over fourteen: ten of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.11.2) The first is for the <s>ājya</s> (ghee offerings), the second for the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back chants), the third for the <s>uktha</s> (recitations).
(PB 3.11.3) That which is for the <s>yājyā</s> (offering formulas) belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest); that which is for the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest of Mitra-Varuṇa); that which is for the <s>uktha</s> belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> (praising priest); that which belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s> also belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s> (calling priest). That which is for the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> together with the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s, and that which is for the <s>uktha</s> belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; that which is for the <s>yājyā</s> belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; that which belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s> also belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. That which is for the <s>uktha</s> belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; that which is for the <s>yājyā</s> belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; that which is for the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; that which belongs to the <s>Hotṛ</s> also belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. All of them apply in the <s>ājya</s> offerings, all in the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants, all in the <s>uktha</s> recitations.
(PB 3.11.4) The <s>samīṣantī</s> (traversing) arrangement indeed pertains to animals. Since this traverses all <s>savanas</s> (pressings of Soma), it enriches him with animals at each pressing. He who is praised with this becomes possessed of animals.

body.text:
(PB 3.12.1) ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa dvadaśabhiḥ sa ekayā ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa dvādaśabhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa dvādaśabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ
(PB 3.12.2) anto vā aṣṭācatvāriṃśaḥ paśavaś chandogā yat ṣoḍaśabhyaḥ-ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti ṣoḍaśakalāḥ paśavaḥ kalāśas tat paśūn āpnoti
(PB 3.12.3) dvādaśabhir vihitaikā paricarā dvādaśamāsās saṃvvatsaro yajamānaḥ paricarā yad dvādaśabhir vidadhāty ekā paricarā bhavati yajamānam eva tad antatas saṃvvatsare paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayaty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitāṣṭācatvāriṃśasya viṣṭutiḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.12.1) He chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over sixteen: three of them, then twelve, then one — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over sixteen: one of them, then three, then twelve — he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over sixteen: twelve of them, then one, then three.
(PB 3.12.2) Forty-eight is indeed the final. Animals are the chanters (<s>chandogas</s>). When he chants the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over sixteen after sixteen, animals have sixteen parts — thereby he obtains animals, part by part.
(PB 3.12.3) It is arranged with twelve; one serves as attendant. Twelve months make the year; the sacrificer is the attendant. When he arranges with twelve, one becomes the attendant — thereby he establishes the sacrificer among animals at the very end within the year. This is indeed the firmly established <s>viṣṭuti</s> of the <s>aṣṭācatvāriṃśa</s> (forty-eight-versed stoma). He who is praised with this becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 3.13.1) ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa daśabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa daśabhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhyo hiṅ karoti sa daśabhiḥ sa tisṛbhiḥ sa tisṛbhir nedīyaḥsaṃkramā
(PB 3.13.2) anto vā aṣṭācatvāriṃśo yathā mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ sṛptvā nedīyaḥsaṃkramāt saṃkrāmaty evam etan nedīyaḥsaṃkramayā nedīyaḥsaṃkramāt saṃkrāmati
(PB 3.13.3) daśabhir vihitā tisraḥ paricarā daśākṣarā virāḍ etāvān puruṣo yad ātmā prajā jāyā yad daśabhir vidadhātt tisraḥ paricarā bhavanti yajamānam eva tad virājy annādye 'ntataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayaty annādo bhavati ya etayā stute
body.translated_text:
(PB 3.13.1) He utters the <s>hiṅkāra</s> to the sixteen: with three, with ten, with three. He utters the <s>hiṅkāra</s> to the sixteen: with three, with three, with ten. He utters the <s>hiṅkāra</s> to the sixteen: with ten, with three, with three. These are the nearest crossings.
(PB 3.13.2) The limit is indeed forty-eight. Just as one, having climbed to the top of a great tree, crosses over by the nearest crossing, so indeed one crosses over from the nearest crossing by the nearest crossing.
(PB 3.13.3) Distributed among the ten, the three are attendant portions. The ten-syllabled <s>Virāj</s> (meter) — such is the person: what is the self, the offspring, the wife. When he distributes among the ten, the three become the attendant portions. He thus establishes the sacrificer at the end in the <s>Virāj</s> for the eating of food. He who is praised with this becomes an eater of food.

body.text:
(PB 4.1.1) gāvo vā etat sattram āsata tāsāṃ daśasu māssu śṛṅgaṇy ajāyanta tā abruvannarāḥ smottiṣṭhāmopaśā no 'jñateti tā udatiṣṭhan
(PB 4.1.2) tāsāṃ tv evābruvann āsāmahā evemau dvādaśau māsau saṃsaṃvvatsaram āpayāmeti tāsāṃ dvādaśasu māḥsu śṛṅgāṇi prāvartanta tāḥ sarvam annādyam āpnuvaṃs tā etās tūparās tasmāt tāḥ sarvān dvādaśamāsaḥ prerate sarvaṃ hi tā annādyam āpnuvan
(PB 4.1.3) sarvam annādyam āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 4.1.4) prajāpatir vā idam eka āsīt so 'kāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa etam atirātram apaśyat tam āharat tenāhorātre prājanayat
(PB 4.1.5) yad eṣo 'tirātro bhavaty ahorātre eva prajanayanty ahorātrayoḥ pratitiṣṭhanty etāvān vāva saṃvvatsaro yad ahas ca rātriś cāhorātrābhyām eva tat saṃvvatsaram āpnuvanti
(PB 4.1.6) yaj jyotiṣṭomo bhavati yajñamukhaṃ tad ṛdhnuvanti yad uktho yajñakrator anantarayāya yad rātriḥ sarvasyāptyai
(PB 4.1.7) sa etān stomān apaśyat jyotir gaur aur itīme vai lokā ete stomā ayam eva jyotir ayaṃ madhyamo gaur asāv uttama āyuḥ
(PB 4.1.8) yad ete stomā bhavantīmān eva lokān prajanayanty eṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.1.9) sa etaṃ tryahaṃ punaḥ prāyauṅkta tena ṣaḍahena ṣaṭkratūn prājanayat
(PB 4.1.10) yad eṣa ṣaḍaho bhavati ṛtūn eva prajanayanti ṛtuṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.1.11) sa etaṃ ṣaḍahaṃ punaḥ prāyuṅkta tābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ ṣaḍahābhyāṃ dvādaśamasaḥ prājanayat
(PB 4.1.12) yad etau ṣaḍahau bhavato māsān eva prajanayanti māseṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.1.13) sa etau dvau ṣaḍahau punaḥ prayuṅkta taiś caturbhiḥ ṣaḍahaiś caturviṃśatim ardhamāsān prājanayat
(PB 4.1.14) yad ete catvāraḥ ṣaḍahā bhavanty ardhamāsān eva prajanayanty ardhamāseṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.1.15) sa idaṃ bhuvanaṃ prajanayitva pṛṣṭhyena ṣaḍahena vīryam ātmany adhatta
(PB 4.1.16) yad eṣaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho bhavati vīrya evāntataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.1.17) tena māsān saṃvvatsaraṃ prājanayad yad eṣa māso bhavati saṃvvatsaram eva prajanayanti saṃvvatsare pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.1.1) Cows once performed this <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session). In ten months their horns grew. They said: 'We are not flourishing — let us stand up! Our ropes have become known.' They stood up.
(PB 4.1.2) But they said among themselves: 'Let us sit and complete these twelve months to achieve the full year.' In twelve months their horns developed fully. They obtained all food. These are the <s>tūpara</s> cows. Therefore they give birth throughout all twelve months, for they obtained all food.
(PB 4.1.3) He who knows this obtains all food.
(PB 4.1.4) <s>Prajāpati</s> was indeed alone in the beginning. He desired: 'May I become many, may I propagate.' He perceived this <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite). He brought it forth. With it he generated day and night.
(PB 4.1.5) When this <s>Atirātra</s> takes place, they generate day and night and become established in day and night. The year is indeed just this much — what is day and what is night. Through day and night they obtain the year.
(PB 4.1.6) When there is a <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> (light-praise rite), they accomplish the opening of the sacrifice. When there is an <s>Uktha</s> (recitation rite), it is for the uninterrupted performance of the sacrifice. When there is the night rite, it is for the obtainment of everything.
(PB 4.1.7) He perceived these <s>stomas</s> (hymn-forms): <s>Jyotis</s> (light), <s>Gaus</s> (cow), <s>Āyus</s> (life). These are indeed the worlds, these <s>stomas</s>. This world is <s>Jyotis</s>, the middle world is <s>Gaus</s>, that highest world is <s>Āyus</s>.
(PB 4.1.8) When these <s>stomas</s> occur, they generate these very worlds and become established in these worlds.
(PB 4.1.9) He employed this three-day period again. With that six-day period he generated six rites.
(PB 4.1.10) When this six-day period occurs, they generate the seasons and become established in the seasons.
(PB 4.1.11) He employed this six-day period again. With those two six-day periods he generated the twelve months.
(PB 4.1.12) When these two six-day periods occur, they generate the months and become established in the months.
(PB 4.1.13) He employed those two six-day periods again. With those four six-day periods he generated twenty-four half-months.
(PB 4.1.14) When these four six-day periods occur, they generate the half-months and become established in the half-months.
(PB 4.1.15) Having generated this world, he placed vigor in himself with the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day period.
(PB 4.1.16) When this <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day period occurs, they become established in vigor at the end.
(PB 4.1.17) With that he generated the months and the year. When this month occurs, they generate the year and become established in the year.

body.text:
(PB 4.2.1) prāyaṇīyam etad ahar bhavati
(PB 4.2.2) prāyaṇīyena vā ahnā devāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāyan yat prāyaṃs tat prāyaṇīyasya prāyaṇīyatvam
(PB 4.2.3) tasmāt prāyaṇīyasyāhna ṛtvijā bhavitavyam etad dhi svargasya lokasya nediṣṭhaṃ ya etasyartviṅ na bhavati hīyate svargāl lokāt
(PB 4.2.4) caturviṃśaṃ bhavati
(PB 4.2.5) caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam ārabhya prayanti
(PB 4.2.6) caturviṃśaṃ bhavati caturviṃśo vai saṃvvatsaraḥ sākṣād eva saṃvvatsaram ārabhante
(PB 4.2.7) yāvatyaś caturviṃśasyokthasya stotrīyās tāvatyaḥ saṃvvatsarasya rātrayaḥ stotrīyābhir eva tat saṃvvatsaram āpnuvanti
(PB 4.2.8) pañcadaśastotrāṇi bhavanti pañcadaśārdhamāsasya rātrayo 'rdhamāsaśa eva tat saṃvvatsaram āpnuvanti
(PB 4.2.9) pañcadaśa stotrāṇi pañcadaśaśastrāṇi samāso māsaśa eva tat saṃvvatsaram āpnuvanti
(PB 4.2.10) tad āhur īrma iva vā eṣā hotrā yad acchāvākyā yad acchāvākam anusaṃtiṣṭhata īśvarermā bhavitor iti yady ukthaṃ smātraikakubhañcodvaṃśīyañcāntataḥ pratiṣṭhāpye vīryaṃ vā ete samanī vīrya evāntataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.2.11) atho khalv āhur agniṣṭomam eva kāryam eṣa vai yajñaḥ svargyo yad agniṣṭoma ūrdhvo hi hotāram anusaṃtiṣṭhate
(PB 4.2.12) dvādaśastotrāṇy agniṣṭomo dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvvatsaras tena saṃvvatsarasaṃmito dvādaśa stotraṇi dvādaśa śastrāṇi tac caturviṃśatiś caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvvatsaras tena saṃvvatsarasaṃmitaḥ
(PB 4.2.13) atho khalv āhur uktham eva kāryam ahnaḥ samṛddhyai
(PB 4.2.14) sarvāṇi rūpāṇi kriyante sarvaṃ hy etāhnāpyate
(PB 4.2.15) pavante vājasātaye somāḥ sahasrapājasa iti sahasravatī pratipat kāryā
