(PB 4.2.16) saṃvvatsarasya rūpaṃ sarvan evainān etayā punāti sarvān abhivadati
(PB 4.2.17) atho khalv āhuḥ pavasva vāco agriya ity eva kāryā mukhaṃ vā etat saṃvvatsarasya yad vāco 'graṃ mukhata eva tat saṃvvatsaram ārabhante
(PB 4.2.18) mithunam iva vā eṣā vyāhṛtiḥ pavasveti puṃso rūpaṃ vāca iti striyāḥ someti puṃso rūpaṃ citrābhir iti striyā mithunam evaibhyo yajñamukhe dadhāti prajananāya
(PB 4.2.19) agne yuṅkṣvā hi ye taveti jarābodhīyam agniṣṭoma sāma kāryaṃ yuktenaiva saṃvvatsareṇa prayanti caturviṃśatyakṣarāsu bhavati caturviṃśasya rūpam
(PB 4.2.20) atho khalv āhur yajñāyajñīyam eva kāryam
(PB 4.2.21) panthā vai yajñāyajñīyaṃ patha eva tan na yanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.2.1) This is the opening day (<s>prāyaṇīya</s>).
(PB 4.2.2) By the opening day the gods went to the heavenly world. Because they went forth (<s>prāyan</s>), that is the character of the opening day as 'opening.'
(PB 4.2.3) Therefore one should be an officiant on the opening day, for this is nearest to the heavenly world. He who is not an officiant on this day is excluded from the heavenly world.
(PB 4.2.4) It is a twenty-four-fold (<s>caturviṃśa</s>) rite.
(PB 4.2.5) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is radiance and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>. They set forth having taken hold of radiance and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 4.2.6) It is twenty-four-fold. The year is indeed twenty-four (half-months). They directly take hold of the year.
(PB 4.2.7) As many as are the <s>stotrīya</s> (praise verses) of the twenty-four-fold <s>uktha</s>, so many are the nights of the year. Through the <s>stotrīya</s> verses they obtain the year.
(PB 4.2.8) There are fifteen <s>stotras</s> (praise chants). Fifteen are the nights of the half-month. By the half-months they obtain the year.
(PB 4.2.9) Fifteen <s>stotras</s>, fifteen <s>śastras</s> (recitations) — together that is thirty. By the months they obtain the year.
(PB 4.2.10) On this they say: 'The <s>Acchāvāka</s> (calling priest) recitation is like a pillar for this <s>hotra</s> (priestly function). If one follows the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, there is possibility of becoming a pillar.' If it is an <s>Uktha</s>, one should establish the <s>Aikakubha</s> and <s>Audvaṃśīya</s> at the end. These are indeed powers — they become established in power at the end.
(PB 4.2.11) Now they also say: 'One should perform just the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. This is indeed the sacrifice that leads to heaven — the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> — for the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) rises upward following it.'
(PB 4.2.12) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has twelve <s>stotras</s>. Twelve are the months of the year. Therefore it is measured by the year. Twelve <s>stotras</s> and twelve <s>śastras</s> — that is twenty-four. Twenty-four are the half-months of the year. Therefore it is measured by the year.
(PB 4.2.13) Now they also say: 'One should perform just the <s>Uktha</s> rite, for the completion of the day.'
(PB 4.2.14) All forms of the rite are performed, for everything is obtained by this day.
(PB 4.2.15) 'The <s>Soma</s> juices purify themselves for the winning of the prize, those of thousand-fold power' — the opening verse (<s>pratipat</s>) should contain the word 'thousand.'
(PB 4.2.16) This is the form of the year. He purifies all of them with this, he addresses all of them.
(PB 4.2.17) Now they also say: 'One should use the verse "Purify yourself, O foremost of speech." For the foremost part of speech is the mouth of the year. They take hold of the year from its very mouth.'
(PB 4.2.18) This utterance is like a pair — 'purify' is the masculine form, 'of speech' is the feminine; '<s>Soma</s>' is the masculine form, 'with the brilliant ones' is the feminine. He thus establishes a pair at the mouth of the sacrifice for procreation.
(PB 4.2.19) 'O <s>Agni</s>, yoke those that are yours' — the <s>Jarābodha</s> <s>Sāman</s> (chant) of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> should be used. They set forth with the year already yoked. It occurs in twenty-four syllables — that is the form of the twenty-four-fold rite.
(PB 4.2.20) Now they also say: 'One should use the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> (chant).'
(PB 4.2.21) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is indeed a path. By that path they go forth.

body.text:
(PB 4.3.1) abhīvarto brahmasāma bhavati
(PB 4.3.2) abhīvartena vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokam abhyavartanta yad abhīvarto brahmasāma bhavati svargasya lokasyābhivṛttyai
(PB 4.3.3) ekākṣaraṇidhano bhavaty ekākṣarā vai vāg vācaiva tad ārabhya svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti
(PB 4.3.4) sāmneto yanty ṛcā punar āyanti
(PB 4.3.5) sāma vai asau loka ṛg ayaṃ yad itaḥ sāmnā yanti svargaṃ lokam ārabhya yanti yad ṛcā punar āyanty asmin loke pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.3.6) yat sāmāvasṛjeyur ava svargāl lokāt padyeran yad ṛcam anusṛjeyur naśyeyur asmāl lokāt
(PB 4.3.7) samānaṃ sāma bhavaty anyo-'nyaḥ pragātho 'nyad-anyad dhi citram adhvānam avagacchann eti
(PB 4.3.8) vṛṣā vā eṣa retodhā yad abhīvartaḥ pragātheṣu reto dadhad eti yad itaḥ samānaṃ sāma bhavaty anyo-'nyaḥ pragātho reta eva tad dadhati yat parastāt samānaḥ pragātho bhavaty anyad-anyat sāma reta eva tad dhitaṃ prajanayanti
(PB 4.3.9) sāmnetaḥ pragāthāṃ dugdhe pragāthena parastāt sāmāni dugdhe salomatvāya
(PB 4.3.10) yo vā adhvānaṃ punar nivartayanti nainaṃ te gacchanti ye 'punar nivartaṃ yanti te gacchati
(PB 4.3.11) ya āstutaṃ kurvate yathā dugdhām upasīded evaṃ tat
(PB 4.3.12) ye nāstutaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayante tam abhyaśnuvate
(PB 4.3.13) brahmavādino vadanti yātayāmāḥ saṃvvatsarā3 ayātayāmā3 iti te nāyātayāmeti vaktavyaṃ punar anyāni stotrāṇi nivartanta ūrdhvam eva brahmasāmaiti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.3.1) The <s>Abhīvarta</s> becomes the <s>Brahmasāman</s> (the chant of the <s>Brahman</s> priest).
(PB 4.3.2) By the <s>Abhīvarta</s>, the gods turned toward the heavenly world. Since the <s>Abhīvarta</s> becomes the <s>Brahmasāman</s>, it is for turning toward the heavenly world.
(PB 4.3.3) It has a single-syllable <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). Speech is indeed single-syllabled. By speech they go, having attained the heavenly world.
(PB 4.3.4) By the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) they go from here; by the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse) they return.
(PB 4.3.5) The <s>Sāman</s> is indeed that world (heaven); the <s>Ṛc</s> is this world. Since they go from here by the <s>Sāman</s>, they go having attained the heavenly world. Since they return by the <s>Ṛc</s>, they become established in this world.
(PB 4.3.6) If they were to abandon the <s>Sāman</s>, they would fall from the heavenly world. If they were to abandon the <s>Ṛc</s>, they would perish from this world.
(PB 4.3.7) The <s>Sāman</s> is the same, but the <s>pragāthas</s> (strophes) are different from one another; for one goes along a wonderful path encountering different things.
(PB 4.3.8) This <s>Abhīvarta</s> is indeed a bull, a depositor of seed. Going among the <s>pragāthas</s>, it deposits seed. Since from this side the <s>Sāman</s> is the same and the <s>pragāthas</s> are different, it deposits seed. Since beyond that the <s>pragātha</s> is the same and the <s>Sāmans</s> are different, they bring forth from that deposited seed.
(PB 4.3.9) From this side, with the <s>Sāman</s> it milks the <s>pragātha</s>; beyond, with the <s>pragātha</s> it milks the <s>Sāmans</s> — for smoothness.
(PB 4.3.10) Those who turn the path back do not reach it. Those who go without turning back reach it.
(PB 4.3.11) Those who make it into a praised chant — that is like sitting down by a milked cow.
(PB 4.3.12) Those who do not make it into a praised chant — whatever desire they desire, they attain it.
(PB 4.3.13) The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'The years are exhausted' or 'not exhausted.' They should be told 'not exhausted.' The other <s>stotras</s> (praise songs) turn back, but the <s>Brahmasāman</s> goes only upward.

body.text:
(PB 4.4.1) pañcasu māḥsu bārhatāḥ pragāthā āpyante
(PB 4.4.2) teṣv āpteṣu chandasī saṃyujyaitavyam
(PB 4.4.3) tisra uṣṇihaḥ syur ekā gāyatrī tās tisro bṛhatyo bhavanti
(PB 4.4.4) tad āhuḥ saṃśara iva vā eṣa cchandasāṃ yad dve chandasī saṃyuñjantīti
(PB 4.4.5) catur uttarair eva cchandobhir etavyam
(PB 4.4.6) paśavo vai caturuttarāṇi cchandasāṃsi paśubhir eva tat svargaṃ lokam ākramam ānayanti
(PB 4.4.7) ekaṃ gāyatrīm ekāham upeyur ekāmuṣṇiham ekāham ekām anuṣṭubham ekāhaṃ bṛhatyā pañcamāsa iyuḥ paṅktim ekāham upeyus triṣṭubhā ṣaṣṭhaṃ māsam īyuḥ śvo viṣuvān bhaviteti jagatīm upeyuḥ
(PB 4.4.8) tad āhur anavakḷptāni vā etāni cchandāṃsi madhyandine bṛhatyā caiva triṣṭubhā caitavyam
(PB 4.4.9) ete vai chandasī vīryavatī ete pratyakṣaṃ madhyandinasya rūpam
(PB 4.4.10) rathantare 'hani bṛhatī kāryaitad vai rathantarasya svam āyatanaṃ yad bṛhatī sva eva tad āyatane rathantaraṃ pratitiṣṭhati bārhate 'hani triṣṭup kāryaitad vai bṛhataḥ svam āyatanaṃ yat triṣṭup sva eva tad āyatane bṛhadrathantare pratitiṣṭhantī itaḥ
(PB 4.4.11) trayastriṃśatā pragāthair etavyaṃ trayastriṃśad devatā devatāsv eva pratitiṣṭhanto yanti caturviṃśatyaitavyaṃ caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ saṃvvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhanto yanti dvādaśabhir etavyaṃ dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ saṃvvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ṣaḍbhir etavyaṃ ṣaḍ ṛtava ṛtuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanto yanti caturbhir etavyaṃ catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanto yanti tribhir etavyaṃ traya ime lokā eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanto yanti dvābhyām etavyaṃ dvipād yajamānaḥ svargasya lokasyākrāntyā anyenānyena hi padā puruṣaḥ pratitiṣṭhann eti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.4.1) In five months, the <s>Bārhatī</s> <s>pragāthas</s> (strophes in the <s>Bṛhatī</s> meter) are completed.
(PB 4.4.2) When they are completed, one should proceed by joining the meters.
(PB 4.4.3) There should be three <s>Uṣṇih</s> verses and one <s>Gāyatrī</s>; those become three <s>Bṛhatīs</s>.
(PB 4.4.4) They say about this: 'This is indeed a confusion of meters, that they join two meters together.'
(PB 4.4.5) One should proceed with meters each increasing by four.
(PB 4.4.6) Cattle are the meters increasing by four. By cattle they bring about the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 4.4.7) They approached one <s>Gāyatrī</s> for one day; one <s>Uṣṇih</s> for one day; one <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> for one day; with the <s>Bṛhatī</s> they went through the fifth month; they approached one <s>Paṅkti</s> for one day; with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> they went through the sixth month. 'Tomorrow will be the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day)' — they approached the <s>Jagatī</s>.
(PB 4.4.8) They say about this: 'These meters are not properly arranged. At midday one should proceed with the <s>Bṛhatī</s> and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.'
(PB 4.4.9) These two meters are powerful; these are the manifest form of the midday pressing.
(PB 4.4.10) On the <s>Rathantara</s> day, the <s>Bṛhatī</s> should be employed — this is the own seat of the <s>Rathantara</s>, namely the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. Thus the <s>Rathantara</s> becomes established in its own seat. On the <s>Bārhata</s> day, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> should be employed — this is the own seat of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, namely the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Thus from here the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> become established in their seats.
(PB 4.4.11) One should proceed with thirty-three <s>pragāthas</s> — there are thirty-three gods; establishing themselves among the gods, they go. One should proceed with twenty-four — there are twenty-four half-months in a year; establishing themselves in the year, they go. One should proceed with twelve — there are twelve months in a year; establishing themselves in the year, they go. One should proceed with six — there are six seasons; establishing themselves in the seasons, they go. One should proceed with four — cattle are four-footed; establishing themselves among cattle, they go. One should proceed with three — there are three worlds; establishing themselves in these worlds, they go. One should proceed with two — the sacrificer is two-footed; for the attainment of the heavenly world, for a man goes on becoming established by one foot after another.

body.text:
(PB 4.5.1) svarasāmāna ete bhavante
(PB 4.5.2) svarbhānur vā āsur ādityaṃ tamasāvidhyat taṃ devāḥ svarair aspṛṇvan yat svarasāmāno bhavanty ādityasya spṛtyai
(PB 4.5.3) parair vai devā ādityaṃ svargaṃ lokam apārayan yad aparayaṃs tat parāṇāṃ paratvaṃ
(PB 4.5.4) pārayanty enaṃ parāṇi ya evaṃv veda
(PB 4.5.5) saptadaśā bhavanti
(PB 4.5.6) prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajāpatim evopayanti
(PB 4.5.7) anuṣṭup chandaso bhavanty ānuṣṭubho vai prajāpatiḥ sākṣād eva prajāpatim ārabhante
(PB 4.5.8) trayaḥ purastāt trayaḥ parastād bhavanti
(PB 4.5.9) devā vā ādityasya svargāl lokād avapādād abibhayus tam etaiḥ stomaiḥ saptadaśair adṛṃhan yad ete stomābhavanty ādityasya dhṛtyai
(PB 4.5.10) catustriṃśā bhavanti varṣma vai catustriṃśo varṣmaṇaivainaṃ saṃmimate
(PB 4.5.11) tasya parācīnātipādād abibhayus taṃ sarvaiḥ stomaiḥ +paryārṣan viśvajidabhijidbhyāṃ vīryaṃ vā etau stomau vīryeṇaiva tad ādityaṃ paryuṣanti dhṛtyai
(PB 4.5.12) anavapādāyānatipādāya
(PB 4.5.13) tad āhuḥ kartapraskanda iva vā eṣa yat trayastriṃśata+ḥ saptadaśam upayantīti pṛṣṭhyo 'ntaraḥ kāryaḥ
(PB 4.5.14) tasya yat saptadaśam ahas tad uttamaṃ kāryaṃ salomatvāya
(PB 4.5.15) tad āhur udaraṃ vā eṣa stomānāṃ yat saptadaśo yat saptadaśaṃ madhyato nirhareyur aśanāyavaḥ prajāḥ syur aśanāyavaḥ sattriṇaḥ
(PB 4.5.16) trayastriṃśād eva saptadaśa upetyo varṣma vai trayastriṃśo varṣma saptadaśo varṣmaṇa eva tad varṣmābhisaṃkrāmanti
(PB 4.5.17) nānāhur ukthāḥ kāryā3 iti yady ukthāḥ syuḥ
(PB 4.5.18) paśavo vā ukthāni śāntiḥ paśavaḥ śāntenaiva tad viṣuvantam upayanti
(PB 4.5.19) tad āhur vivīvadham iva vā etad yad agniṣṭomo viṣuvān agniṣṭomau viśvajidabhijitāv athetara ukthāḥ syur iti
(PB 4.5.20) agniṣṭomā eva sarve kāryāḥ
(PB 4.5.21) vīryaṃ vā agniṣṭomo vīrya eva madhyataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti nava saṃstutā bhavanti nava prāṇāḥ praṇeṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.5.1) These become <s>Svarasāmans</s> (chants characterized by tonal accents).
(PB 4.5.2) <s>Svarbhānu</s> the <s>Asura</s> pierced the sun with darkness. The gods freed him with the <s>svaras</s> (tones). Since they become <s>Svarasāmans</s>, it is for freeing the sun.
(PB 4.5.3) By the <s>paras</s> (far-going chants) the gods carried the sun across to the heavenly world. Since they carried across, that is the far-going nature of the <s>paras</s>.
(PB 4.5.4) The <s>paras</s> carry across one who knows thus.
(PB 4.5.5) They are seventeenfold (<s>saptadaśa</s>).
(PB 4.5.6) <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the seventeenfold. They thereby approach <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 4.5.7) They are in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. <s>Prajāpati</s> is of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. They directly take hold of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 4.5.8) Three are on this side, three are on the far side.
(PB 4.5.9) The gods were afraid of the sun falling from the heavenly world. They strengthened him with these seventeenfold <s>stomas</s>. Since these <s>stomas</s> exist, it is for the support of the sun.
(PB 4.5.10) They are thirty-four. The stature is thirty-four. They measure him out by his stature.
(PB 4.5.11) They were afraid of his toppling over on the far side. They surrounded him with all the <s>stomas</s>, with the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s> days. These two <s>stomas</s> are vigor. They surround the sun with vigor for support.
(PB 4.5.12) So that he neither falls down nor topples over.
(PB 4.5.13) They say about this: 'This is like a jump into a pit, that from the thirty-three they approach the seventeenfold.' A <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> day should be made in between.
(PB 4.5.14) That seventeenfold day should be made the last — for smoothness.
(PB 4.5.15) They say: 'The belly of the <s>stomas</s> is the <s>saptadaśa</s>. If they were to remove the <s>saptadaśa</s> from the middle, the offspring would be hungry, the <s>sattrins</s> (session-performers) would be hungry.'
(PB 4.5.16) From the thirty-three itself one should approach the seventeenfold. The stature is the thirty-three; the stature is the seventeenfold. They cross from stature to stature.
(PB 4.5.17) They say: 'The <s>Uktha</s> days should be made' — if they were <s>Uktha</s> days.
(PB 4.5.18) Cattle are the <s>Uktha</s> chants; pacification is cattle. By pacification they approach the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day).
(PB 4.5.19) They say: 'This is like a tearing apart, that the <s>Viṣuvat</s> is an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, and the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s> are <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>, while the others would be <s>Uktha</s> days.'
(PB 4.5.20) All should be made <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>.
(PB 4.5.21) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is indeed vigor. They become established in vigor at the center. There are nine chanted praises. There are nine vital breaths. They become established in the vital breaths.

body.text:
(PB 4.6.1) viṣuvān eṣa bhavati
(PB 4.6.2) devaloko vā eṣa yad viṣuvān devaokam eva tad abhyārohanti
(PB 4.6.3) ekaviṃśo bhavaty ekaviṃśo vā asya bhuvanasyāditya ādityalokam eva tad abhyārohanti
(PB 4.6.4) dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavas traya ime lokā asāv āditya ekaviṃśaḥ
(PB 4.6.5) madhyata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.6.6) vāyo śukro ayāmi ta iti śukravatī pratipad bhavaty ādityasya rūpam
(PB 4.6.7) vāyur vā etaṃ devatānām ānaśe 'nuṣṭup chandasaṃ yad ato 'nyā pratipat syāt pradahet
(PB 4.6.8) yanti vā ete prāṇādityāhur ye gāyatryāḥ pratipado yantīti yad vayavyā bhavanti tena prāṇān na yanti prāṇo hi vāyuḥ
(PB 4.6.9) atho śamayanty evainam etayā śantir hi vāyuḥ
(PB 4.6.10) ā yāhi somapītaya iti saumī pāvamānī
(PB 4.6.11) niyutvatī bhavati paśavo vai niyutaḥ śāntiḥ paśavaḥ śāntenaiva tad ādityam upayanti
(PB 4.6.12) divākīrtyasāmā bhavati
(PB 4.6.13) svarbhānur vā āsur ādityaṃ tamasāvidhyat tasya devā divākīrtyais tamo 'pāghnan yad divākīrtyāni bhavanti tama evāsmād apaghnanti raśmayo vā eta ādityasya yad divākīrtyāni raśmibhir eva tad ādityaṃ sākṣād ārabhante
(PB 4.6.14) bhrājābhrāje pavamānamukhe bhavato mukhata evāsya tābhyāṃ tamo 'paghnanti
(PB 4.6.15) mahādivākīrtyaṃ ca vikarṇaṃ ca madhyato bhavato madhyata evāsya tābhyāṃ tamo 'paghnanti bhāsam antato bhavati patta evāsya tena tamo 'paghnanti
(PB 4.6.16) daśastobhaṃ bhavti daśākṣarā virāḍ virājy eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.6.17) yat tv ity āhuḥ ṣaḍbhir ito māsair adhvānaṃ yanti ṣaḍbhiḥ punar āyanti kva tarhi svargo loko yasya kāmāya sattram āsata iti
(PB 4.6.18) mūrdhānaṃ diva iti svargaṃ lokam ārabhante
(PB 4.6.19) aratiṃ pṛthivyā ity asmiṃ loke pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.6.20) vaiśvānaram ṛta ājātam agnim iti viṣuvata eva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 4.6.21) kaviṃ samrājam atitihiṃ janānām ity annādyam evopayanti
(PB 4.6.22) āsan nāpātraṃ janayanta devā iti jāyanta eva
(PB 4.6.23) tat triṣṭub jagatīṣu bhavati traiṣṭubhjāgato vā ādityo yad ato 'nyāsu syād ava svargāl lokāt padyeran
(PB 4.6.24) samrāḍvatīṣu bhavati sāmrājyaṃ vai svargo lokaḥ svarga eva loke pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.6.1) This becomes the <s>Viṣuvān</s> (solstice day).
(PB 4.6.2) The <s>Viṣuvān</s> is indeed the world of the <s>devas</s>; thereby they ascend to the abode of the <s>devas</s>.
(PB 4.6.3) It is twenty-one-fold, for the sun is the twenty-first of this world; thereby they ascend to the world of the sun.
(PB 4.6.4) Twelve months, five seasons, these three worlds, and yonder sun — that is twenty-one.
(PB 4.6.5) They establish themselves at the very center of the sacrifice.
(PB 4.6.6) 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, the bright one, I come to you' — the opening verse contains the word 'bright' (<s>śukra</s>); it is the form of the sun (<s>Āditya</s>).
(PB 4.6.7) <s>Vāyu</s> indeed obtained this one among the deities; <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> among the meters. If the opening verse were any other, it would burn.
(PB 4.6.8) They say, 'Those who have <s>Gāyatrī</s> opening verses go away from the vital breaths and the sun.' Because they are addressed to <s>Vāyu</s>, they do not depart from the vital breaths, for <s>Vāyu</s> is breath.
(PB 4.6.9) Moreover, they pacify him with this, for <s>Vāyu</s> is peace.
(PB 4.6.10) 'Come to the <s>Soma</s>-drinking' — this is a <s>Pāvamānī</s> verse belonging to <s>Soma</s>.
(PB 4.6.11) It contains the word <s>niyut</s> (team of horses); <s>niyuts</s> are cattle; cattle are peace. With peace they approach the sun.
(PB 4.6.12) The <s>sāman</s> of the <s>Divākīrtya</s> type is used.
(PB 4.6.13) <s>Svarbhānu</s>, the <s>Asura</s>, struck the sun with darkness. The <s>devas</s> drove away its darkness with the <s>Divākīrtya</s> chants. When the <s>Divākīrtya</s> chants are employed, they drive away darkness from it. The <s>Divākīrtya</s> chants are indeed the rays of the sun; with rays they directly take hold of the sun.
(PB 4.6.14) The <s>Bhrāja</s> and <s>Abhrāja</s> chants are at the beginning of the <s>Pavamāna</s> chant; thereby they drive away darkness from its front.
(PB 4.6.15) The <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s> and <s>Vikarṇa</s> are in the middle; thereby they drive away darkness from its middle. The <s>Bhāsa</s> is at the end; thereby they drive away darkness from its rear.
(PB 4.6.16) It is ten-syllabled with <s>stobhas</s> (exclamatory syllables). The <s>Virāj</s> meter has ten syllables; thus they are established in the <s>Virāj</s>.
(PB 4.6.17) Now they say: 'With six months they travel the path from here, and with six they return — where then is the heavenly world for whose sake they undertook the <s>sattra</s> (session)?'
(PB 4.6.18) With 'The summit of heaven' they take hold of the heavenly world.
(PB 4.6.19) With 'The delight of the earth' they establish themselves in this world.
(PB 4.6.20) With '<s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, born in the cosmic order (<s>Ṛta</s>),' the very form of the <s>Viṣuvān</s> is made.
(PB 4.6.21) With 'The poet, the sovereign, the guest of the people,' they attain the consumption of food.
(PB 4.6.22) With 'The <s>devas</s> begot one who was not a vessel,' they are indeed born.
(PB 4.6.23) These are in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s> meters. The sun is of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>-<s>Jagatī</s> nature. If they were in other meters, they would fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 4.6.24) They are in verses containing the word 'sovereign' (<s>samrāj</s>). Sovereignty is the heavenly world; thus they are established in the heavenly world.

body.text:
(PB 4.7.1) ātmā vā eṣa saṃvvatsarasya yad viṣuvān pakṣāv etāv abhito bhavato yena ceto 'bhīvartena yanti yaś ca parasmāt pragātho bhavati tāv ubhau viṣuvati kāryau pakṣāv eva tad yajñasyātman pratidadhati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 4.7.2) indra kratuṃ na ābhareti pragātho bhavati
(PB 4.7.3) vasiṣṭho vā etaṃ putrahato 'paśyat sa prajayā paśubhiḥ prājāyata yad eṣa pragātho bhavati prajātyai
(PB 4.7.4) jīvā jyotir aśīmahīti ye vai svasti saṃvvatsaraṃ saṃtaranti te jīvā jyotir aśnuvate
(PB 4.7.5) māno ajñātā vṛjanā durādhyo māśivāso 'vakramur iti ye vai stenā ripavas te durādhyas tān eva tad atikrāmati
(PB 4.7.6) tvayā vyayaṃ pravataḥ śaśvatīr apo 'ti śūra tarāma so 'tisaṃvvatsaro vai pravataḥ śaśvatīr apas tam eva tat taranti
(PB 4.7.7) adyādyāśvaḥ śvas tvām idā hyo naro vayam enam idā hya iti saṃtanayaḥ pragāthā bhavanti teṣām ekaḥ kāryaḥ salomatvāya śvastanam evābhisaṃtanvanti
(PB 4.7.8) atho khalv āhur indra kratuṃ na ābharety eva kāryaṃ samṛddhyai
(PB 4.7.9) pratyavarohiṇo māsā bhavanti
(PB 4.7.10) yathā vā ito vṛkṣaṃ rohanty evam enaṃ pratyavarohanti svargam eva lokaṃ rūḍhvāsmiṃl loke pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 4.7.1) The <s>Viṣuvān</s> is the self (<s>ātman</s>) of the year. The two wings are on either side of it. The <s>pragātha</s> (chant) by which they go with the <s>abhīvarta</s> (turning-toward) hymn, and the one that comes from the other side — both these should be performed at the <s>Viṣuvān</s>. Thus they place the wings at the self of the sacrifice, for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 4.7.2) '<s>Indra</s>, bring us wisdom' — this becomes the <s>pragātha</s> (chant-pair).
(PB 4.7.3) <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, when his son was slain, beheld this; he was then blessed with progeny and cattle. This <s>pragātha</s> serves for the gaining of progeny.
(PB 4.7.4) 'Living, may we enjoy the light' — those who safely cross the year attain the light of the living.
(PB 4.7.5) 'May the unknown, hostile, evil-scheming ones not overwhelm us, nor the malicious ones attack' — those who are thieves and deceivers are the evil-schemers; thereby one surpasses them.
(PB 4.7.6) 'With you, O hero, may we cross the perpetual waters of the steep descent' — the year is indeed the perpetual waters of the steep descent; thereby they cross it.
(PB 4.7.7) 'Today, today; tomorrow, tomorrow; now, yesterday — O men, we now, yesterday' — these are <s>pragāthas</s> of continuation. One of them should be performed for the sake of continuity; they extend to the next day.
(PB 4.7.8) Moreover, they say: '<s>Indra</s>, bring us wisdom' should indeed be performed for the sake of success.
(PB 4.7.9) The months are the descending ones.
(PB 4.7.10) Just as they climb a tree from this side, so they descend from it. Having ascended to the heavenly world, they establish themselves in this world.

body.text:
(PB 4.8.1) gauś cāyuś ca stomau bhavataḥ
(PB 4.8.2) dvipād yajamānaḥ pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 4.8.3) ūnātiriktau bhavata ūnātiriktaṃ vā anu prajāḥ prajāyante prajātyai
(PB 4.8.4) vairājau bhavato 'nnaṃ virāḍ annādya eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.8.5) dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni bhavanti
(PB 4.8.6) virāḍ vā eṣā samṛddhā yad daśāhāni virājy eva samṛddhāyāṃ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.8.7) pṛṣthāni bhavanti vīryaṃ vai pṛṣṭhāni vīrya eva pratitiṣṭhanti cchandomā bhavanti paśavo vai cchandomāḥ paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanty athaitad daśamam ahar āptastomam āptacchanda āptavibhaktikam aniruktaṃ prājāpatyam
(PB 4.8.8) yad adhyāhur ati tad recayanti tasmān na vyucyam
(PB 4.8.9) parokṣam anuṣṭubham upayanti prajāpatir vā anuṣṭub yat pratyakṣam upeyuḥ prajāpatim ṛccheyuḥ
(PB 4.8.10) yo vai sattrasya sad veda sad bhavati vāmadevyaṃ vai sāmnāṃ sad agnir devatānāṃ virāṭ chandasāṃ trayastriṃśaḥ stomānāṃ tāny eva tad ekadhā saṃbhṛtyottiṣṭhanti
(PB 4.8.11) brahmavādino vadanti yataḥ sattrād udasthātā3sthitā3d iti

(PB 4.9.1) patnīḥ saṃyājya prāñca udetyāyaṃ sahasramānava ity aticchandasāhavanīyam upatiṣṭhante

(PB 4.8.1) The <s>Gaus</s> and the <s>Āyus</s> are the two <s>stomas</s> (chant patterns).
(PB 4.8.2) The sacrificer is two-footed — for firm establishment.
(PB 4.8.3) They are deficient and excessive. Offspring are born in conformity with what is deficient and excessive — for the sake of procreation.
(PB 4.8.4) They belong to <s>Virāj</s>. <s>Virāj</s> is food. Through food they become firmly established.
(PB 4.8.5) The twelve-day rite has ten days.
(PB 4.8.6) This is indeed <s>Virāj</s>, fully accomplished,

(PB 4.10.1) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata so 'ricyata so 'padyata taṃ devā abhisamagacchanta te 'bruvan mahad asmai vrataṃ saṃbharāma yad imaṃ dhinavad iti tasmai yat saṃvvatsaram annaṃ pacyate tat samabharaṃs tad asmai prāyacchaṃs tad avrajayat tad enam adhinon mahan maryā vrataṃ yad imam adhinvīd iti tan mahāvratasya mahāvratatvam
(PB 4.10.2) prajāpatir vāva mahāṃs tasyaitad vratam annam eva

body.translated_text: (PB 4.10.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. He was depleted. He fell ill. The gods came together to him. They said: 'Let us prepare a great observance (<s>vrata</s>) for him, so that we may nourish him.' They gathered together whatever food ripens in the course of a year and offered it to him. He undertook the observance. That nourished him. 'Great is the observance of the warrior who nourished him' — thus

body.text:
(PB 5.1.1) vāmadevyaṃ mahāvrataṃ kāryam
(PB 5.1.2) trivṛc chiro bhavati
(PB 5.1.3) trivṛd dhy eva śiro loma tvag asthi
(PB 5.1.4) pāṅkta itara ātmā loma tvaṅ māṃsam asthi majjā
(PB 5.1.5) sakṛd dhiṅkṛtena śirasā pārācā stuvate
(PB 5.1.6) tasmāc chiro 'ṅgāni medyanti nānumedyati na kṛśyanty anukṛśyati
(PB 5.1.7) punar abhyāvartam itareṇātmanā stuvate tasmād itara ātmā medyati ca kṛśyati ca
(PB 5.1.8) arkavatīṣu gāyatrīṣu śiro bhavati
(PB 5.1.9) annaṃ vā arko brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatry annādyaṃ caivaibhyo brahmavarcasaṃ ca mukhato dadhāti
(PB 5.1.10) pañcadaśasaptadaśau pakṣau bhavataḥ prakṣābhyāṃ vai yajamāno vayo bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam eti
(PB 5.1.11) tāv āhuḥ samau kāryau pañcadaśau vā saptadaśau vā savīvadhatvāya
(PB 5.1.12) tad v āhur yat samau bhavata ekavīryau tarhi bhavata iti pañcadaśasaptadaśāv eva kāryau sācīva vai vayaḥ pakṣau kṛtvāpatīyaḥ patati
(PB 5.1.13) dakṣiṇato bṛhat kāryaṃ dakṣiṇo vā ardha ātmano vīryavattaraḥ
(PB 5.1.14) atho khalv āhur uttarata eva kāryaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsino 'rdhāt traiṣṭubhaṃ vai bṛhat traiṣṭubho vai brāhmaṇācchaṃsī traiṣṭubhaḥ pañcadaśastomaḥ
(PB 5.1.15) dakṣiṇato rathantaraṃ kāryaṃ maitrāvaruṇasyārdhād gāyatraṃ vai rathantaraṃ gāyatro maitrāvaruṇo gāyatraḥ saptadaśastomaḥ
(PB 5.1.16) ekaviṃśaṃ pucchaṃ bhavati
(PB 5.1.17) ekaviṃśo vai stomānāṃ pratiṣṭhā tasmād vayaḥ pucchena pratiṣṭhāyotpatati pucchena pratiṣṭhāya niṣīdati
(PB 5.1.18) yajñāyajñīyaṃ pucchaṃ kāryaṃ yajñāyajñīyaṃ hy eva mahāvratasya puccham
(PB 5.1.19) atho khalv āhur atiśayaṃ vai dvipadāṃ yajñāyajñīyaṃ bhadram kāryaṃ samṛddhyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.1.1) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance) is to be performed.
(PB 5.1.2) The <s>Trivṛt</s> (three-fold) is the head.
(PB 5.1.3) For the <s>Trivṛt</s> is indeed the head: hair, skin, bone.
(PB 5.1.4) The <s>Pāṅkta</s> (five-fold) is the rest of the body: hair, skin, flesh, bone, marrow.
(PB 5.1.5) With the head, which receives the <s>hiṃ</s> sound once, they chant in the reverse direction.
(PB 5.1.6) Therefore, when the head fattens, the limbs also fatten; they do not fatten independently. They do not grow thin independently.

body.text:
(PB 5.2.1) vāmadevyaṃ mahāvrataṃ kāryaṃ tasya gāyatraṃ śiro bṛhadrathantare pakṣau yajñāyajñīyaṃ puccham
(PB 5.2.2) yo vai mahāvrate sahasraṃ protaṃ veda pra sahasraṃ paśūn āpnoti
(PB 5.2.3) tasya prācī dik śiras tac chandobhiḥ sahasram asāv anyataraḥ pakṣaḥ sanakṣattraiḥ sāhasro 'yam anyataraḥ pakṣaḥ sa oṣadhibhiś ca vanaspatibhiś ca sāhasro 'ntarikṣam ātmā tad vayobhiḥ sāhasraṃ pratīcī dik pucchaṃ tad agnibhiś ca raśmibhiś ca sāhasraṃ pra sasasraṃ paśūn āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 5.2.4) tad āhur apṛṣṭhaṃ vai vāmadevyam anidhanaṃ hīti
(PB 5.2.5) anāyatanaṃ vā etat sāma yad anidhanam
(PB 5.2.6) rājanaṃ mahāvrataṃ kāryam
(PB 5.2.7) etad vai sākṣād annaṃ yad rājanaṃ pañcavidhaṃ bhavati pāṅktaṃ hy annam
(PB 5.2.8) hiṅkāravad bhavati tena vāmadevyasya rūpam
(PB 5.2.9) nidhanavad bhavati tena prṣṭhasya rūpam
(PB 5.2.10) aticchandaḥsu pañcanidhanaṃ vāmadevyaṃ brahmasāma kāryam
(PB 5.2.11) ati vā eṣānyāni cchandāṃsi yad aticchandā aty etad anyāny ahāny ahar yan mahāvratam
(PB 5.2.12) brahmasāmnaiva tad anyāny ahāny atimedayati
(PB 5.2.13) pañcanidhanaṃ bhavati pāṅktaṃ hy annam
(PB 5.3.1) ilāndam agniṣṭomasāma kāryam
(PB 5.3.2) etad vai sākṣād annaṃ yad ilāndam irānnaṃ etad irāyām evānnādye 'ntataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 5.3.3) samudro vā etac chandaḥ salilaṃ lomaśaṃ samudra iva khalu vai sa bhavati salila iva lomaśa iva yo bhavati
(PB 5.3.4) tasmād etāsu kāryaṃ samṛddhyai
(PB 5.3.5) vratam iti nidhanaṃ bhavati mahāvratasyaiva tad rūpaṃ kriyate svar iti bhavati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai śakuna iti bhavati śakuna iva vai yajamāno vayo bhūtvā svargaṃl lokam eti
(PB 5.3.6) yajñāyajñīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryam
(PB 5.3.7) yad vā anyā vāṅ nātivadet tad agniṣṭomasāma kāryaṃ na vai vāg vācam ativadati vāg yajñāyajñīyaṃ vācy evāntataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 5.3.8) vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryam
(PB 5.3.9) agnir vā idaṃ vaiśvānaro 'dahan naitasmād devā abibhayus taṃ varaṇaśākhayāvārayanta yad avārayanta tasmād vāravantīyam
(PB 5.3.10) tasmād varaṇo bhiṣajya etena hi devā ātmānam atrāyanta
(PB 5.3.11) tasmād brāhmaṇo vāraṇena na pibed vaiśvānaraṃ necchamayā iti
(PB 5.3.12) paśavo vai vāravantīyaṃ śāntiḥ paśavaḥ śāntād eva tat saṃvvatsarād uttiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.2.1) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> (sāman) should be performed at the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance). Its head is the <s>Gāyatra</s>, its two wings are the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, and its tail is the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>.
(PB 5.2.2) He who knows the thousand woven into the <s>Mahāvrata</s> obtains a thousand animals.
(PB 5.2.3) Its head is the eastern direction — that together with the meters constitutes a thousand. One wing is the yonder world — that together with the constellations constitutes a thousand. The other wing is this world — that together with herbs and trees constitutes a thousand. The body is the atmosphere — that together with birds constitutes a thousand. The tail is the western direction — that together with fires and rays constitutes a thousand. He obtains a thousand animals — he who knows thus.
(PB 5.2.4) They say: 'The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is indeed without a <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), for it has no <s>nidhana</s> (concluding phrase).'
(PB 5.2.5) That <s>Sāman</s> which has no <s>nidhana</s> is indeed without a foundation.
(PB 5.2.6) The <s>Rājana</s> should be performed at the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
(PB 5.2.7) The <s>Rājana</s> is indeed food directly, for it is fivefold, and food belongs to the group of five.
(PB 5.2.8) It has a <s>hiṅkāra</s> — thereby it has the form of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
(PB 5.2.9) It has a <s>nidhana</s> — thereby it has the form of a <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chant.
(PB 5.2.10) In the <s>Atichandas</s> (hyper-metric) days, the <s>Vāmadevya</s> with five <s>nidhanas</s> should be made the <s>Brahma-sāman</s>.
(PB 5.2.11) The <s>Atichandas</s> days indeed surpass other meters; this day, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, surpasses other days.
(PB 5.2.12) By the <s>Brahma-sāman</s> itself it outshines the other days.
(PB 5.2.13) It has five <s>nidhanas</s>, for food belongs to the group of five.
(PB 5.3.1) The <s>Ilānda</s> should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>.
(PB 5.3.2) The <s>Ilānda</s> is indeed food directly — it is refreshment-food. Thereby they become firmly established in refreshment and food-eating at the very end.
(PB 5.3.3) This meter is like the ocean — watery and hairy. He indeed becomes like the ocean, like water, like one who is hairy.
(PB 5.3.4) Therefore it should be performed on these days, for prosperity.
(PB 5.3.5) The <s>nidhana</s> is '<s>vratam</s>' (observance) — thereby the very form of the <s>Mahāvrata</s> is produced. It becomes '<s>svar</s>' (heaven) — for the attainment of the heavenly world. It becomes '<s>śakuna</s>' (bird) — for the sacrificer, like a bird, having become winged, goes to the heavenly world.
(PB 5.3.6) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>.
(PB 5.3.7) When no other speech would outspeak it, that should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>. Indeed, speech does not outspeak speech. The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is speech — thereby they become firmly established in speech at the very end.
(PB 5.3.8) The <s>Vāravantīya</s> should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>.
(PB 5.3.9) <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire) was burning this world. The gods did not fear him. They warded him off with a branch of the <s>varaṇa</s> tree. Because they warded him off (<s>avārayanta</s>), therefore it is called <s>Vāravantīya</s>.
(PB 5.3.10) Therefore the <s>varaṇa</s> tree is healing, for by this the gods protected themselves from harm.
(PB 5.3.11) Therefore a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not drink from a <s>varaṇa</s> vessel, lest he incur displeasure from <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
(PB 5.3.12) Animals are indeed the <s>Vāravantīya</s>; peace is animals. From peace itself they arise at the end of the year.

body.text:
(PB 5.4.1) prāṇena purastād āhavanīyam upatiṣṭhante prāṇam eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.2) apānena paścāt puccham upatiṣṭhante apānam eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.3) vratapakṣābhyāṃ pakṣāv upatiṣṭhante diśa eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.4) prajāpater hṛdayenāpikakṣam upatiṣṭhante jyaiṣṭhyam eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.5) vasiṣṭhasya nihavena cātvālam upatiṣṭhante svargam eva tal lokam āotvā śriyaṃ vadante
(PB 5.4.6) vaiśvadevyām ṛci bhavati viśvarūpaṃ vai paśūnāṃ rūpaṃ paśūn eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.7) sattrasyarddhyāgnīdhram upatiṣṭhanta ṛddhāv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 5.4.8) caturakṣarāṇidhanaṃ bhavati catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 5.4.9) ātamitor nidhanam upayanty āyur eva sarvam āpnuvanti
(PB 5.4.10) ślokānuślokābhyāṃ havirdhāne upatiṣṭhante kīrtim eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.11) yāmena mārjālīyam upatiṣṭhante pitṛlokam eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.4.12) āyurṇavastobhābhyāṃ sada upatiṣṭhante brahma caiva tat kṣatraṃ ca jayanti
(PB 5.4.13) ṛśyasya sāmnā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhante
(PB 5.4.14) indraṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny astuvaṃs tasyarśya ekam aṅgam astutam acāyat tad asyaitenāstaut tenāsya priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat priyam evāsyaitena dhāmopagacchanti
(PB 5.4.15) yat paro'kṣaṃ nidhanam upeyur hrītamukhaṃ pratimuñceran pratyakṣam upayanti hrītamukham evāpajayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.4.1) They attend the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) from the front with <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) — thereby they win <s>prāṇa</s> itself.
(PB 5.4.2) They attend the tail from behind with <s>apāna</s> (in-breath) — thereby they win <s>apāna</s> itself.
(PB 5.4.3) They attend the two wings with the two <s>vrata</s>-wings (observance-wings) — thereby they win the directions themselves.
(PB 5.4.4) They attend the <s>apikakṣa</s> (armpit area) with the heart of <s>Prajāpati</s> — thereby they win supremacy itself.
(PB 5.4.5) They attend the <s>cātvāla</s> (ritual pit) with the <s>nihava</s> (invocation) of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> — thereby, having won the heavenly world, they declare glory.
(PB 5.4.6) It is set to a <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (pertaining to the All-Gods) verse. The form of animals is indeed manifold — thereby they win animals themselves.
(PB 5.4.7) They attend the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's shed) for the prosperity of the <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) — thereby they become firmly established in prosperity.
(PB 5.4.8) The <s>nidhana</s> has four syllables. Animals are four-footed — thereby they become firmly established in animals.
(PB 5.4.9) They approach the <s>nidhana</s> 'from the <s>Ātamita</s>' — thereby they obtain the entire lifespan.
(PB 5.4.10) They attend the two <s>Havirdhāna</s> sheds (carts for Soma vessels) with the <s>Śloka</s> and <s>Anuśloka</s> — thereby they win fame itself.
(PB 5.4.11) They attend the <s>Mārjālīya</s> (purification shed) with the <s>Yāma</s> — thereby they win the world of the ancestors.
(PB 5.4.12) They attend the <s>Sadas</s> (assembly hall) with the <s>Āyus</s> and <s>Navastobha</s> — thereby they win both <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly power) and <s>Kṣatra</s> (the ruling power).
(PB 5.4.13) They attend the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (householder's fire) with the <s>Sāman</s> of <s>Ṛśya</s>.
(PB 5.4.14) All beings praised <s>Indra</s>; <s>Ṛśya</s> sang one limb of his that was unpraised. Thereby he attained <s>Indra</s>'s beloved abode. By this they attain his beloved abode.
(PB 5.4.15) If they were to approach the <s>nidhana</s> in a concealed manner, they would put on a mask of shame. They approach openly — thereby they overcome the mask of shame.

body.text:
(PB 5.5.1) āsandīm āruhyodgāyati devasākṣya eva tad upariṣadyaṃ jayati
(PB 5.5.2) audumbarī bhavaty ūrg udumbara ūrjam evāvarunddhe
