(PB 5.5.6) sarveṇātmanā samuddhṛtyodgeyam eṣu lokeṣu ned vyāhito 'sānīti
(PB 5.5.7) ekasyāṃ stotrīyāyām astutāyāṃ pādāv upāharati
(PB 5.5.8) saha nidhanena pratiṣṭhām upayanty eṣeṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhante
(PB 5.5.9) preṅkhām āruhya hotā śaṃsati mahasa eva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 5.5.10) yadā vai prajā maha āviśati preṅkhās tarhy ārohanti
(PB 5.5.11) phalakam āruhyādhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti
(PB 5.5.12) kūrcān itare 'dhyāsata ūrdhvā eva tad utkrāmanto yanti
(PB 5.5.13) abhigarāpagarau bhavato nindaty enān anyaḥ prānyaḥ śaṃsati ya enān nindati pāpmānam eṣāṃ so 'pahanti yaḥ praśaṃsati yad evaiṣāṃ suṣṭutaṃ suśastaṃ tat so 'bhigṛṇāti
(PB 5.5.14) śūdrāryau carmaṇi vyāyacchete tayor āryaṃ varṇam ujjāpayanti
(PB 5.5.15) devāś ca vā asurāś cāditye vyāyacchantas taṃ devā abhyajayaṃs tato devā abhavan / parāsurā abhavann ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 5.5.16) yadāryaṃ varṇam ujjāpayanty ātmānam eva tad ujjāpayanti
(PB 5.5.17) parimaṇḍalaṃ carma bhavaty ādityasyaiva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 5.5.18) sarvāsu sraktiṣu dundubhayo vadanti yā vanaspatiṣu vāk tām eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.5.19) bhūmidundubhir bhavati yā pṛthivyāṃ vāk tām eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.5.20) sarvā vāco vadanti yeṣu lokeṣu vāk tām eva taj jayanti
(PB 5.5.21) saṃnaddhāḥ kavacinaḥ pariyantīndriyasyaiva tad rūpaṃ kriyate 'tho mahāvratam eva mahayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.5.1) He mounts the seat and sings the <s>Udgītha</s>. He wins the upper seat in the sight of the gods.
(PB 5.5.2) It is made of <s>udumbara</s> (fig) wood. <s>Udumbara</s> is vital sap — thereby he obtains vital sap.
(PB 5.5.3) It is a span in height — so as not to uproot this world.
(PB 5.5.4) He ascends by the meters — thereby he ascends to the heavenly world.
(PB 5.5.5) He descends by the meters — thereby he becomes firmly established in this world.
(PB 5.5.6) Having raised himself up with his whole body, one should sing, thinking: 'May I not be confounded in these worlds.'
(PB 5.5.7) When one <s>stotrīya</s> (praise-verse) has not been sung, he draws up his feet.
(PB 5.5.8) Together with the <s>nidhana</s> they attain firm establishment — thereby they become firmly established in these very worlds.
(PB 5.5.9) The <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) recites while mounting the swing — thereby the form of greatness is produced.
(PB 5.5.10) When festive joy enters the people, then they mount the swings.
(PB 5.5.11) The <s>Adhvaryu</s> (performing priest) responds while mounting a plank.
(PB 5.5.12) The others sit upon bundles of grass — thereby they go upward, ascending.
(PB 5.5.13) There are the censurer and the praiser. One censures them, the other praises them. He who censures them removes their evil. He who praises — whatever of theirs was well-sung and well-recited, that he extols.
(PB 5.5.14) A <s>Śūdra</s> and an <s>Ārya</s> pull at a hide. They cause the <s>Ārya</s> color to triumph.
(PB 5.5.15) The gods and the <s>asuras</s> contended over the sun. The gods conquered it. Thereupon the gods prevailed; the <s>asuras</s> were defeated. His rival is defeated by his own self — he who knows thus.
(PB 5.5.16) When they cause the <s>Ārya</s> color to triumph, they cause their own self to triumph.
(PB 5.5.17) The hide is circular — thereby the very form of the sun is produced.
(PB 5.5.18) Drums sound at all the corners — whatever speech resides in the trees, that they win.
(PB 5.5.19) There is an earth-drum — whatever speech resides in the earth, that they win.
(PB 5.5.20) They utter all kinds of speech — whatever speech resides in whatever worlds, that they win.
(PB 5.5.21) They go around armored and wearing cuirasses — thereby the very form of <s>Indra</s>'s power is produced. And thereby they magnify the <s>Mahāvrata</s> itself.

body.text:
(PB 5.6.1) sarve sahartvijo mahāvratena stuvīran
(PB 5.6.2) adhvaryuḥ śirasodgāyan maitrāvaruṇo dakṣiṇena pakṣeṇa brāhmaṇācchaṃsy uttareṇa gṛhapatiḥ pucchenodgātātmanā
(PB 5.6.3) tad yady evaṃ kuryur ekaikayā stotrīyayāstutayodgātāram abhisameyuḥ
(PB 5.6.4) tisṛbhir udgātātmana udgīyātha yā śirasaḥ stotrīyā tāṃ dadhyād aparābhis tisṛbhir udgīyātha yā dakṣiṇasya pakṣasya stotrīyā tāṃ dadhyād aparābhis tisṛbhir udgīyātha yottarasya pakṣasya stotrīyā tāṃ dadhyāt tisṛbhir vaikayā vā stutaṃ syād atha yā pucchasya stotrīyā tāṃ dadhyāt
(PB 5.6.5) ātmany eva tad aṅgāni pratidadhati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 5.6.6) atho khalv āhuḥ katham adhvaryur bahvṛcaḥ sāma gāyed ity udgātaiva sarveṇodgāyet tad eva samṛddhaṃ samṛddhāv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 5.6.7) havirdhāne śirasā stutvā saṃrabdhāḥ pratyañca eyus te dakṣiṇena dhiṣṇyān parītya paścān maitrāvaruṇasya dhiṣṇyasyopaviśya rathantareṇa pañcadaśena stuvīraṃs ta udañcaḥ saṃsarpeyur jaghanena hotur dhiṣṇyaṃ paścād brāhmaṇācchaṃsino dhiṣṇyasyopaviśya bṛhatā saptadaśena stuvīraṃs te yenaiva prasarpeyus tena punar niḥsṛpyottareṇāgnīdhraṃ parītya paścād gārhapatyasyopaviśya pucchenaikaviṃśena stuvīraṃs te yenaiva niḥsarpeyus tena punaḥ prasṛpya yathāyatanam upaviśyāsandīm āruhyodgātātmanodgāyati
(PB 5.6.8) taṃ patnyo 'paghāṭilābhir upagāyanty ārtvijyam eva tat patnyaḥ kurvanti saha svargaṃl lokam ayāmeti
(PB 5.6.9) kule-kule 'nnaṃ kriyate tad yat pṛccheyuḥ kim idaṃ kurvantītīme yajamānā annam atsyantīti brūyuḥ
(PB 5.6.10) yo vai dīkṣitānāṃ pāpaṃ kīrtayati tṛtīyam evāṃśaṃ pāpmano haraty annādas tṛtīyaṃ pipīlikās tṛtīyam
(PB 5.6.11) parimādbhiś caranti tvak ca vā etal loma ca mahāvratasya yat parimādas tvacaṃ caiva tal loma ca mahāvratasyāptvāvarundhate
(PB 5.6.12) vāṇaṃ vitanvanty anto vai vāṇo 'nto mahāvratam antenaiva tad antam abhivādayanti
(PB 5.6.13) śatatantrīko bhavati śatāyur vai puruṣaḥ śatavīryaḥ
(PB 5.6.14) tam ullikhet prāṇāya tvāpānāya tvā vyānāya tveti prāṇāpānavyānān eva tad āptvāvarundhate
(PB 5.6.15) pari kumbhinyo mārjālīyaṃ yantīdaṃ madhv idaṃ madhv iti saghoṣā eva tad vayo bhūtvā saha svargaṃl lokaṃ yanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.6.1) All the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) together should chant with the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
(PB 5.6.2) The <s>Adhvaryu</s> [chants] with the head, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> [chants], the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> with the right wing, the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> with the left, the <s>Gṛhapati</s> with the tail, and the <s>Udgātṛ</s> with the body.
(PB 5.6.3) If they were to do it thus, they would meet the <s>Udgātṛ</s> with each individual <s>stotrīyā</s> (chant verse) that has been chanted.
(PB 5.6.4) The <s>Udgātṛ</s> sings with three as the body; then those that belong to the head,

body.text:
(PB 5.7.1) devā vai vācaṃ vyabhajanta tasyā yo raso 'tyaricyata tad gaurīvitam abhavad anuṣṭubham anu pariplavate vāg anuṣṭub vāco raso gaurīvitam
(PB 5.7.2) yad gaurīvitenānvahaṃs stuvate vācy eva tad vācā rasaṃ dadhati
(PB 5.7.3) rasavad vācā vadati ya evaṃv vedeti
(PB 5.7.4) dvyudāsaṃ bhavati svargasya vā etau lokasyāvasānadeśau pūrveṇaiva pūrvam ahaḥ saṃsthāpayanty uttareṇottaram ahar abhyativadanti
(PB 5.7.5) etad vai yajñasya śvastanaṃ yad gaurīvitaṃ yad gaurīvitam anusṛjeyur aśvastanā aprajasaḥ syuḥ
(PB 5.7.6) saṃ vā anyo yajñas tiṣṭhata ity āhur vāg eva na saṃtiṣṭhata iti yad gaurīvitam anvahaṃ bhavati vācam eva tat punaḥ prayuñjate
(PB 5.7.7) svarṇidhanam anvahaṃ bhavati
(PB 5.7.8) devakṣetraṃ vā ete 'bhyārohanti ye svarṇidhanam upayanti sa u vai sattriṇaḥ sattram upanayed ity āhur ya enān devakṣetram abhyārohed iti na vai devakṣetra āsīna ārtim ārchati yat svarṇidhanam anvahaṃ bhavati naiva kāṃ canārtim ārchanti
(PB 5.7.9) cyavante vā ete 'smāl lokād ity āhur ye svarṇidhanam upayantīti yad ṛcā svarūpaṃ yanty asmiṃ loke pratitiṣṭhanti yad ekāro 'tarikṣe yat sāmnāmuṣmint sarveṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti svarṇidhanena tuṣṭuvānāḥ
(PB 5.7.10) sujñānaṃ bhavati
(PB 5.7.11) devā vai svargaṃl lokaṃ yanto 'jñātād abibhayus ta etat saṃjñānam apaśyaṃs tena jñātram agacchan yat sujñānam anvahaṃ bhavati jñātram eva gacchanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.7.1) The gods divided <s>Vāc</s> (speech). The essence that was left over from her became the <s>Gaurīvita</s> (chant). It flows around the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (meter). <s>Vāc</s> is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; the essence of <s>Vāc</s> is the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 5.7.2) When one chants daily with the <s>Gaurīvita</s>, one places essence in speech through speech.
(PB 5.7.3) 'He speaks with essence through speech, who knows thus.'
(PB 5.7.4) It has two <s>udāsa</s> (exhalations),

body.text:
(PB 5.8.1) ye vai vācam annam ādayanty annādā bhavanti ye vitarṣayanti rukṣā bhavanti
(PB 5.8.2) gaurīvitaṃ śyāvāśvaṃ nihava etāni vai sāmāni vāco 'nnam eteṣāṃ vāg annaṃ yad etāni na cyavante vācam eva tad annam ādayanti tena sarve 'nnādā bhavanti
(PB 5.8.3) abhikrāntāpakrāntāni bhavanty abhikrāntāpakrāntaṃ vai vāco rūpam
(PB 5.8.4) plavo 'nvahaṃ bhavati
(PB 5.8.5) samudraṃ vā ete prasnānti ye saṃvvatsaram upayanti yo vā aplavaḥ samudraṃ prasnāti na sa tata udeti yat plavo bhavati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 5.8.6) ati viśvāni duritā taremeti yad evaiṣāṃ duṣṭutaṃ duḥśastaṃ tad etena taranti
(PB 5.8.7) okonidhanaṃ ṣaḍahamukhe bhavati
(PB 5.8.8) parāṃ vā ete parāvataṃ gacchanti ye ṣaḍahasyāntaṃ gacchanti yadokonidhanaṃ ṣaḍahamukhe bhavati prajñātyai
(PB 5.8.9) yadā vai puruṣaḥ svam oka āgacchati sarvaṃ tarhi prajānāti sarvam asmai divā bhavati
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.8.1) Those who extract food from speech become eaters of food; those who let it dry up become parched.
(PB 5.8.2) The <s>Gaurīvita</s>, the <s>Śyāvāśva</s>, and the <s>Nihava</s> — these indeed are the <s>sāmans</s> (chants) that are the food of speech. Speech is the food of these. Because these do not fall away, thereby one extracts food from speech; therefore all become eaters of food.
(PB 5.8.3) They are with approach and departure,

body.text:
(PB 5.9.1) ekāṣṭakāyāṃ dīkṣeran
(PB 5.9.2) eṣā vai saṃvvatsarasya patnī yad ekāṣṭakaitasyāṃ vā gatāṃ rātriṃ vasati sākṣād eva tat saṃvvatsaram ārabhya dīkṣante
(PB 5.9.3) tasya sāniryā yad apo' nabhinandanto 'bhyavayanti
(PB 5.9.4) vicchinnaṃ vā ete saṃvvatsarasyābhidīkṣante ya ekāṣṭakāyāṃ dīkṣante 'ntanāmānāv ṛtū bhavete
(PB 5.9.5) ārtaṃ vā ete saṃvvatsarasyābhidīkṣante ye 'ntanāmānāv ṛtū abhidīkṣante
(PB 5.9.6) tasmād ekāṣṭakāyāṃ na dīkṣyam
(PB 5.9.7) phālgune dīkṣeran
(PB 5.9.8) mukhaṃ vā etat saṃvvatsarasya yat phālguno mukhata eva tat saṃvvatsaram ārabhya dīkṣante
(PB 5.9.9) tasya sāniryā yat saṃmeghe viṣuvān saṃpadyate
(PB 5.9.10) citrāpūrṇamāse dīkṣeran
(PB 5.9.11) cakṣur vā etat saṃvvatsarasya yac citrāpūrṇamāso mukhato vai cakṣur mukhata eva tat saṃvvatsaram ārabhya dīkṣante tasya na niryāsti
(PB 5.9.12) caturahe purastāt paurṇamāsyā dīkṣeran
(PB 5.9.13) teṣām akāṣṭakāyāṃ krayaḥ saṃpadyate tenaikāṣṭakāṃ na saṃbaṭ kurvanti
(PB 5.9.14) teṣāṃ pūrvapakṣe sutyā saṃpadyate pūrvapakṣe māsāḥ saṃtiṣṭhamānā yanti pūrvapakṣa uttiṣṭhanti tān uttiṣṭhataḥ paśava oṣadhayo 'nūttiṣṭhanti tān kalyāṇī vāg abhivadary arātsur ime sattriṇa iti te rādhnuvanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.9.1) They should undergo consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> (eighth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha).
(PB 5.9.2) This <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> is indeed the wife of the year. On this night when it has passed, they undergo consecration, taking hold of the year directly.
(PB 5.9.3) The departure from it is that they partake of water without rejoicing.
(PB 5.9.4) Those who undergo consecration on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> consecrate themselves at a break in the year.

body.text:
(PB 5.10.1) ā vā ete saṃvvatsaraṃ pyāyayanti ya utsṛjanti
(PB 5.10.2) yathā vai dṛtir ādhmāta evaṃ saṃvvatsaro 'nutsṛṣṭo yan notsṛjeyur amehena pramāyukāḥ syuḥ
(PB 5.10.3) prāṇo vai saṃvvatsara udānā māsā yad utsṛjanti prāṇa evodānān dadhati yo dīkṣitaḥ pramīyate yā saṃvvatsarasyānutsṛṣṭasya śuk sā tam ṛcchati
(PB 5.10.4) tad āhur utsṛjyā3ṃ notsṛjyā3m iti
(PB 5.10.5) yady utsṛjeyur ukthāny utsṛjeyus tad evotsṛṣṭaṃ tad anutsṛṣṭam
(PB 5.10.6) atho khalv āhur ekatrikaṃ kāryaṃ tad eva sākṣād utsṛṣṭam abhyutṣuṇvanti
(PB 5.10.7) chidro vā eteṣāṃ saṃvvatsara ity āhur ye stomam utsṛjantīti
(PB 5.10.8) paśum ālabhante stomam eva tad ālabhante stomo hi paśuḥ
(PB 5.10.9) śva utsṛṣṭāḥ sma iti vatsān apākurvanti prātaḥ paśum ālabhante tasya vapayā pracaranti tatas savanīyenāṣṭākapālena tata āgneyenāṣṭākapālena tato dadhnaindreṇa tataś caruṇā vaiśvadevena tat prātaḥsavanaṃ saṃtiṣṭhante
(PB 5.10.10) tataḥ paśupuroḍāśenaikādaśakapālena tataḥ savanīyenaikādaśakapālena tato marutvatīyenaikādaśakapālena tataś caruṇaindreṇa tan mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saṃtiṣṭhante
(PB 5.10.11) paśunā pracaranti tataḥ savanīyena dvādaśakapālena tato vaiśvadevena dvādaśakapālena tataś caruṇāgnimārutena tat tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ saṃtiṣṭhante
(PB 5.10.12) pṛṣadājyena pracarya patnīs saṃyājayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 5.10.1) Those who release [the stoma] indeed cause the year to swell.
(PB 5.10.2) Just as a leather bag when inflated, so is the year when not released. If they did not release it, they would die of urinary disease.
(PB 5.10.3) The year is indeed the inbreath (prāṇa), and the months are the outbreaths (udāna). When they release, they place the outbreaths in the inbreath. He who dies while consecrated (dīkṣita) — the grief of the unreleased year afflicts him.
(PB 5.10.4) Thereupon they say: 'Shall we release or not release?'
(PB 5.10.5) If they release, they should release the <s>ukthas</s> (recitations); that is both released and unreleased.
(PB 5.10.6) Moreover, they say: 'The <s>ekatrika</s> (one-out-of-three) should be performed' — thereby they directly press over what has been released.
(PB 5.10.7) 'The year of those who release the <s>stoma</s> is perforated,' they say.
(PB 5.10.8) They offer an animal; thereby they take hold of the <s>stoma</s>, for the <s>stoma</s> is the animal.
(PB 5.10.9) Saying 'Tomorrow the release begins,' they separate the calves. In the morning they slaughter the animal. They proceed with its omentum (<s>vapā</s>), then with the <s>savanīya</s> cake on eight potsherds, then with the <s>āgneya</s> cake on eight potsherds, then with the <s>aindra</s> curd offering, then with the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> porridge. Thus the morning pressing is completed.
(PB 5.10.10) Then with the <s>paśupuroḍāśa</s> (animal cake-offering) on eleven potsherds, then with the <s>savanīya</s> on eleven potsherds, then with the <s>mārutvatīya</s> on eleven potsherds, then with the <s>aindra</s> porridge. Thus the midday pressing is completed.
(PB 5.10.11) They proceed with an animal, then with the <s>savanīya</s> on twelve potsherds, then with the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> on twelve potsherds, then with the <s>āgnimāruta</s> porridge. Thus the third pressing is completed.
(PB 5.10.12) Having proceeded with curd mixed with ghee (<s>pṛṣadājya</s>), they make the wives offer.

body.text:
(PB 6.1.1) prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa etam agniṣṭomam apaśyat tam āharat tenemāḥ prajā asṛjata
(PB 6.1.2) ekādaśena ca vai satā stotreṇāgniṣṭomasyāsṛjataikādaśena ca māsā saṃvvatsarasya tā dvādaśena ca stotreṇāgniṣṭomasya paryagṛhṇād dvādaśena ca māsā saṃvvatsarasya
(PB 6.1.3) tasmāt prajā daśamāso garbhaṃ bhṛtvaikādaśam anu prajāyante tasmād dvādaśaṃ nābhyatiharanti dvādaśena hi parigṛhītās tad ya evaṃv veda pari jātāḥ prajā gṛhṇāti pra jātā janayanti
(PB 6.1.4) tāsāṃ parigṛhītānām aśvatary atyakrāmat tasyā anuhāya reta ādattā tad vaḍavāyāṃ nyamāḍ yasmād vaḍavā dviretās tasmād aśvatary aprajā āttaretā hi
(PB 6.1.5) tasmād v adakṣiṇīyāti hi sā yajñam aricyatātiriktasya dakṣiṇā syāt salomatvāya ṣoḍaśinaḥ stotredeyātirikto vai ṣoḍaśy atirikta evātiriktāṃ dadāti
(PB 6.1.6) so 'kāmayata yajñaṃ sṛjeyeti sa mukhata eva trivṛtam asṛjata taṃ gāyatrī cchando 'nyasṛjyatāgnir devatā brāhmaṇo manuṣyo vasanta ṛtus tasmāt trivṛt stomānāṃ mukhaṃ gāyatrī cchandasām agnir devatānāṃ brāhmaṇo manuṣyāṇāṃ vasanta ṛtūnāṃ tasmād brāhmaṇo mukhena vīryaṃ karoti mukhato hi sṛṣṭaḥ
(PB 6.1.7) karoti mukhena vīryaṃ ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.1.8) sa urasta eva bāhubhyāṃ pañcadaśam asṛjata taṃ triṣṭup chando 'nvasṛjyatendro devatā rājanyo manuṣyo grīṣma ṛtus tasmād rājanyasya pañcadaśa stomas triṣṭup chanda indro devatā grīṣma ṛtus tasmād u bāhuvīryo bāhubhyāṃ hi sṛṣṭaḥ
(PB 6.1.9) karoti bāhubhyāṃ vīryaṃ ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.1.10) sa madhyata eva prajananāt saptadaśam asṛjata taṃ jagatī cchando 'nvasṛjyata viśve devā devatā vaiśyo manuṣyo varṣā ṛtus tasmād vaiśyo 'dyamāno na kṣīyate prajananād dhi sṛṣṭas tasmād u bahupaśur vaiśvadevo hi jāgato varṣā hy asyartus tasmād brāhmaṇasya ca rājanyasya cādyo 'dharo hi sṛṣṭaḥ
(PB 6.1.11) sa patta eva pratiṣṭhāyā ekaviṃśam asṛjata tam anuṣṭup chando 'nvasṛjyata na kā cana devatā śūdro manuṣyas tasmāc chūdra uta bahupaśur ayajñiyo videvo hi na hi taṃ kā cana devatā 'nvasṛjyata tasmāt pādāv anejyaṃ nāti vardhate patto hi sṛṣṭas tasmād ekaviṃśastomānāṃ pratiṣṭhā pratiṣṭhāyā hi sṛṣṭas tasmād anuṣṭubhaṃ chandāṃsi nānu vyūhanti
(PB 6.1.12) pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtyai
(PB 6.1.13) vidhṛtiḥ pāpavasīyaso bhavati ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.1.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I become many, may I procreate.' He beheld this <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> (fire-praise sacrifice). He took it up. With it he created these creatures.
(PB 6.1.2) He created with the eleven-fold and the hundred-fold <s>stotra</s> (chant) of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, and with the eleven months of the year. He encompassed them with the twelve-fold <s>stotra</s> of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and with the twelve months of the year.
(PB 6.1.3) Therefore creatures carry the embryo for ten months and are born in the eleventh. Therefore they do not exceed the twelfth, for they are encompassed by the twelfth. He who knows thus encompasses his born offspring; his born offspring multiply.
(PB 6.1.4) Among those encompassed ones, a she-mule ran out. Having pursued her, he took her seed and placed it in a mare. That is why a mare is double-seeded; therefore a she-mule is barren, for her seed was taken.
(PB 6.1.5) Therefore she is not fit for a sacrificial fee, for she exceeded the sacrifice. The fee should be for the surplus — for the sake of consistency, it should be given at the <s>stotra</s> of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> (the sixteenth), for the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is the surplus; thus one gives the surplus to the surplus.
(PB 6.1.6) He desired: 'May I create the sacrifice.' From his mouth he created the nine-fold (<s>trivṛt</s>). The <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter followed it, <s>Agni</s> the deity, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> among humans, spring among the seasons. Therefore the nine-fold is the mouth of the <s>stomas</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of the meters, <s>Agni</s> of the deities, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of humans, spring of the seasons. Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> performs his power through the mouth, for he was created from the mouth.
(PB 6.1.7) He performs power through the mouth who knows thus.
(PB 6.1.8) From his chest and arms he created the fifteen-fold. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter followed it, <s>Indra</s> the deity, the <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior) among humans, summer among the seasons. Therefore the <s>Rājanya</s>'s <s>stoma</s> is the fifteen-fold, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> his meter, <s>Indra</s> his deity, summer his season. Therefore he is mighty in arms, for he was created from the arms.
(PB 6.1.9) He performs power through the arms who knows thus.
(PB 6.1.10) From his middle, from the organ of generation, he created the seventeen-fold. The <s>Jagatī</s> meter followed it, the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All Gods) the deity, the <s>Vaiśya</s> among humans, the rainy season among the seasons. Therefore the <s>Vaiśya</s>, though consumed, does not diminish, for he was created from the organ of generation. Therefore he is rich in cattle, for he belongs to the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> and the <s>Jagatī</s>, and the rains are his season. Therefore he is the food of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>Rājanya</s>, for he was created below.
(PB 6.1.11) From his feet, from his foundation, he created the twenty-one-fold. The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter followed it, no particular deity, the <s>Śūdra</s> among humans. Therefore the <s>Śūdra</s>, though having many cattle, is unfit for sacrifice, devoid of deity, for no deity followed him. Therefore his feet are not to be washed, and he does not greatly prosper, for he was created from the feet. Therefore the twenty-one-fold is the foundation of the <s>stomas</s>, for it was created from the foundation. Therefore the meters do not arrange the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> in a special sequence.
(PB 6.1.12) For the restraint of the worst.
(PB 6.1.13) He becomes the restrainer of the worst who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 6.2.1) yo vai stomān upadeśanavato vedopadeśanavān bhavati
(PB 6.2.2) prāṇo vai trivṛd ardhamāsaḥ pañcadaśaḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ saptadaśa āditya ekaviṃśa ete vai stomā upadeśanavanta upadeśanavān bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.2.3) ime vai lokās triṇavas triṇavasya vai brāhmaṇeneme lokās triṣ punar navā bhavanti
(PB 6.2.4) eṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.2.5) devatā vāva trayastriṃśo 'ṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiś ca vaṣaṭkāraś ca trayastriṃśau
(PB 6.2.6) sa devena yajñena yajate ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.2.7) yo vā adhipatiṃ vedādhipatir bhavati trayastriṃśo vai stomānam adhipatiḥ puruṣaḥ paśumān
(PB 6.2.8) tasmān nyañco 'nye paśavo 'danty ūrdhvaḥ puruṣo 'dhipatir hi saḥ
(PB 6.2.9) adhipatiḥ samānānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.2.1) He who knows the <s>stomas</s> with their correspondence (<s>upadeśana</s>) becomes one who has correspondences.
(PB 6.2.2) Breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is the nine-fold, the half-month is the fifteen-fold, the year is the seventeen-fold, the sun is the twenty-one-fold. These are the <s>stomas</s> with their correspondences. He who knows thus has correspondences.
(PB 6.2.3) These worlds are the twenty-seven-fold (<s>triṇava</s>). Through the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Triṇava</s>, these worlds become three times nine.
(PB 6.2.4) He is established in these worlds who knows thus.
(PB 6.2.5) The thirty-three-fold represents the deities: eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> call — that is thirty-three.
(PB 6.2.6) He sacrifices with the divine sacrifice who knows thus.
(PB 6.2.7) He who knows the overlord becomes the overlord. The thirty-three-fold is the overlord of the <s>stomas</s>; the human (<s>puruṣa</s>) possesses cattle.
(PB 6.2.8) Therefore other animals eat with their faces downward, while the human faces upward, for he is the overlord.
(PB 6.2.9) He becomes the overlord among his equals who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 6.3.1) eṣa vāva yajño yad agniṣṭomaḥ
(PB 6.3.2) ekasmā anyo yajñaḥ kāmāyāhriyate sarvebhyo 'gniṣṭomaḥ
(PB 6.3.3) dvādaśa stotrāṇy agniṣṭomo dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ saṃvvatsaraṃ paśavo 'nu prajāyante tena paśavyaḥ samṛddhaḥ
(PB 6.3.4) dvādaśa stotrāṇi dvādaśa śastrāṇi tac caturviṃśatiś caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ saṃvvatsaraṃ paśavo 'nuprajāyante tena paśavyaḥ samṛddhaḥ
(PB 6.3.5) agnau stotram agnau śastraṃ pratitiṣṭhati tena brahmavarcasasya
(PB 6.3.6) kiṃ jyotiṣṭomasya jyotiṣṭomatvam ity āhur virājaṃ saṃstutaḥ saṃpadyate virāḍ vai cchandasāṃ jyotiḥ
(PB 6.3.7) jyotiḥ samānānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.3.8) jyeṣṭhayajño vā eṣa yad agniṣṭomaḥ
(PB 6.3.9) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā asmai śraiṣṭhyāya nātiṣṭhanta sa etam agniṣṭomam apaśyat tam āharat tato 'smai prajāḥ śraiṣṭhyāyātiṣṭhanta
(PB 6.3.10) tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śraiṣṭhyāya ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.3.11) yat tv ity āhur gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ kva tarhi turīyaṃ cchando 'nuṣṭub iti
(PB 6.3.12) chandasāṃ vā anvavaluptiṃ yajamāno 'nvavalupyate
(PB 6.3.13) aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī hiṅkāro navama ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub dvādaśākṣarā jagatī cchandobhirevānuṣṭubham āpnoti yajamānasyānavalopāya
(PB 6.3.14) yo vā anuṣṭubhaṃ sarvatrāpiṃ savanāny anvāyattāṃ veda sarvatrāsyāpir bhavaty eṣā vā anuṣṭup sarvatrāpiḥ savanāny anvāyattā tad ya evaṃ vveda sarvatrāpir bhavati
(PB 6.3.15) yad vai rājāno 'dhvānaṃ dhāvayanti ye 'śvānāṃv vīryavattamās tān yuñjate trivṛt pañcadaśa ekaviṃśa ete vai stomānāṃv vīryavattamās tān eva yuṅkte svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 6.3.16) catuṣṭomo bhavati pratiṣṭhā vai catuṣṭomaḥ pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.3.1) This sacrifice is indeed the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
(PB 6.3.2) Other sacrifices are performed for the sake of one desire; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is for all.
(PB 6.3.3) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has twelve <s>stotras</s>; twelve are the months of the year. Animals reproduce following the year; therefore it is productive of cattle and prosperous.
(PB 6.3.4) Twelve <s>stotras</s> and twelve <s>śastras</s> (recitations) — that makes twenty-four. Twenty-four are the half-months of the year. Animals reproduce following the year; therefore it is productive of cattle and prosperous.
(PB 6.3.5) The <s>stotra</s> is established in <s>Agni</s>, the <s>śastra</s> in <s>Agni</s>; therefore it gives <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance).
(PB 6.3.6) 'What makes the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> a <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> (praise of light)?' they ask. When fully praised, it becomes the <s>Virāj</s> meter. The <s>Virāj</s> is the light (<s>jyotis</s>) of the meters.
(PB 6.3.7) He becomes the light among his equals who knows thus.
(PB 6.3.8) This <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is indeed the eldest sacrifice.
(PB 6.3.9) <s>Prajāpati</s> created the creatures, but they did not acknowledge his supremacy. He beheld this <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and took it up. Then the creatures acknowledged his supremacy.
(PB 6.3.10) His equals acknowledge his supremacy who knows thus.
(PB 6.3.11) Now they say: 'The morning pressing has the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the midday pressing the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the third pressing the <s>Jagatī</s> — where then is the fourth meter, the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>?'
(PB 6.3.12) The sacrificer follows the remnant of the meters.
(PB 6.3.13) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has eight syllables — the <s>hiṅkāra</s> (humming syllable) makes nine; the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> has eleven syllables; the <s>Jagatī</s> has twelve syllables. Thus through the meters themselves one reaches the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — so that the sacrificer is not deprived.
(PB 6.3.14) He who knows the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> as pervading everywhere, dependent on all the pressings — he has pervasion everywhere. This <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is indeed all-pervading and dependent on the pressings. He who knows thus has pervasion everywhere.
(PB 6.3.15) Just as when kings run a race they yoke the most vigorous of horses, so the nine-fold, fifteen-fold, and twenty-one-fold are the most vigorous of the <s>stomas</s>. One yokes them for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 6.3.16) It becomes four-<s>stoma</s>-fold. The four-<s>stoma</s>-fold is a foundation; for the sake of firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 6.4.1) prajāpatir devebhya ūrjaṃ vyabhajat tata udumbaraḥ samabhavat prājāpatyo vā udumbaraḥ prājāpatya udgātā yad udgātaudumbarīṃ prathamena karmaṇānvārabhate svayaiva tad devatayātmānam ārtvijyāya vṛṇīte
(PB 6.4.2) tām ucchrayati dyutānas tvā māruta ucchrayatūd divaṃ stabhānāntarikṣaṃ pṛṇa dṛṃha pṛthivīm
(PB 6.4.3) tām anvārabhata āyoṣ ṭvā sadane sādayāmy avataś chāyāyāṃ samudrasya hṛdaya iti
(PB 6.4.4) yajño vā āyus tasya tat sadanaṃ kriyate
(PB 6.4.5) yajño vā avati tasya sā cchāyā kriyate
(PB 6.4.6) madhyato vā ātmano hṛdayaṃ tasmān madhye sadasa audumbarī mīyate
(PB 6.4.7) namaḥ samudrāya namaḥ samudrasya cakṣuṣa ity āha vāg vai samudro manaḥ samudrasya cakṣus tābhyām eva tan namas karoti
(PB 6.4.8) sāmā yūnarvāhāsīd ity āha sāma vai yūnarvā sāmna eva tan namaskaroty ārtvijyaṃ kariṣyan
(PB 6.4.9) yo vā evaṃ sāmne namaskṛtya sāmnārtvijyaṃ karoti na sāmno hīyate nainaṃ sāmāpahate
(PB 6.4.10) ya enam anuvyāharati sa ārtim ārchati
(PB 6.4.11) ūrg asy ūrjodā ūrjaṃ me dehy ūrjaṃ me dhehy annaṃ me dehy annaṃ me dhehi prajāpater vā etad udaraṃ yat sada ūrg udumbaro yad audumbarī madhye sadaso mīyate madhyata eva tat prajābhyo 'nnam ūrjaṃ dadhāti
(PB 6.4.12) tasmād yatraiṣā yātayāmā kriyate tat prajā aśanāyavo bhavanti
(PB 6.4.13) sāma devānām annaṃ sāmany eva tad devebhyo 'nna ūrhaṃ dadhāti sa eva tad ūrji śritaḥ prajābhya ūrjaṃ vibhajati
(PB 6.4.14) udaṅṅ āsīna udgāyaty udīcīṃ tādṛśam ūrjā bhājayati pratyaṅṅ āsīnaḥ prastauti pratīcīṃ tādṛśam ūrjā bhājayati dakṣiṇāsīnaḥ pratiharati dakṣiṇāṃ tādṛśam ūrjā bhājayati prāñco 'nya ṛtvija ārtvijyaṃ kurvanti tasmād eṣā diśāṃ vīryavattamaitāṃ hi bhūyiṣṭhāḥ prīṇanti
(PB 6.4.15) brahmavādino vadanti kasmāt satyāt prāñco 'nya ṛtvija ārtvijyaṃ kurvantīti viparikramyodgātāra iti diśām abhīṣṭyai diśām abhiprītyā iti brūyāt tasmāt sarvāsu dikṣv annaṃv vidyate sarvā hy abhīṣṭāḥ prītāḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.4.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> distributed nourishment (<s>ūrj</s>) to the gods. From that the <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree) came into being. The <s>udumbara</s> belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. The <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest) belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. When the <s>Udgātṛ</s> takes hold of the <s>audumbarī</s> (udumbara post) at the first rite, by that very deity he chooses himself for the priestly office.
(PB 6.4.2) He raises it up: 'May the shining <s>Māruta</s> (wind god) raise you up! Prop up the sky, fill the atmosphere, make firm the earth.'
(PB 6.4.3) He takes hold of it: 'I seat you in the seat of life, in the shade of the water-pool, in the heart of the ocean.'
(PB 6.4.4) The sacrifice is indeed life; its seat is thus made.
(PB 6.4.5) The sacrifice indeed protects; its shade is thus made.
(PB 6.4.6) The heart is in the middle of the self; therefore the <s>audumbarī</s> post is measured in the middle of the sacrificial hall.
(PB 6.4.7) He says: 'Homage to the ocean, homage to the eye of the ocean.' Speech is indeed the ocean; the mind is the eye of the ocean. To these two he thus makes his homage.
(PB 6.4.8) He says: 'The <s>Sāman</s> (chant) was <s>Yūnarvā</s>.' The <s>Sāman</s> is indeed <s>Yūnarvā</s>. He thus pays homage to the <s>Sāman</s>, being about to perform the priestly office.
(PB 6.4.9) He who, having thus paid homage to the <s>Sāman</s>, performs the priestly office with the <s>Sāman</s>, is not separated from the <s>Sāman</s>, nor does the <s>Sāman</s> harm him.
(PB 6.4.10) He who speaks against him falls into distress.
(PB 6.4.11) 'You are nourishment, giver of nourishment — give me nourishment, place nourishment in me, give me food, place food in me.' The sacrificial hall is indeed the belly of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Nourishment is the <s>udumbara</s>. When the <s>audumbarī</s> is measured in the middle of the sacrificial hall, he places food and nourishment for creatures from the very center.
(PB 6.4.12) Therefore wherever this is made stale, there the creatures become hungry.
(PB 6.4.13) The <s>Sāman</s> is the food of the gods. In the <s>Sāman</s> he thus places food and nourishment for the gods. He who is established in nourishment distributes nourishment to creatures.
(PB 6.4.14) Sitting facing north, he sings the <s>Udgītha</s> — he causes the northern direction to share in such nourishment. Sitting facing west, he performs the <s>Prastāva</s> (introductory chant) — he causes the western direction to share in such nourishment. Sitting facing south, he performs the <s>Pratihāra</s> (response) — he causes the southern direction to share in such nourishment. The other priests perform their priestly functions facing east. Therefore this is the most vigorous of the directions, for the greatest number please it.
(PB 6.4.15) The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'For what reason do the other priests face east in performing their priestly functions?' One should say: 'By going around the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests, for the conquest of the directions, for the gratification of the directions.' Therefore food is found in all directions, for all are conquered and gratified.

body.text:
(PB 6.5.1) prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti so 'śocat tasya śocata ādityo mūrdhno 'sṛjyata so 'sya mūrdhānam udahan sa droṇakalaśo 'bhavat tasmin devāḥ śukram agṛhṇata tāṃ vai sa āyuṣārtim atyajīvat
(PB 6.5.2) āyuṣārtim atijīvati ya evaṃv veda /
(PB 6.5.3) raṃ prohed vānaspatyo 'si bārhaspatyo 'si prājāpatyo 'si prajāpater mūrdhāsy atyāyupātram asīdam ahaṃ māṃ prāñcaṃ prohāmi tejase brahmavarcasāyeti
(PB 6.5.4) yad āha vānaspatya iti satyenaivainaṃ tat prohati
(PB 6.5.5) yad āha bārhaspatya iti bṛhaspatir vai devānām udgātā tam eva tad yunakti
(PB 6.5.6) yad āha prājāpatya iti prājāpatyo hy eṣa devatāyā yad droṇakalaśo yad āha prajāpater mūrdheti prajāpater hy eṣa mūrdhna udahanyata
(PB 6.5.7) yad āhātyāyupātram ity ati hy etad anyāni pātrāṇi yad droṇakalaśo devapātraṃ droṇakalaśaḥ
(PB 6.5.8) devapātrī bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.5.9) brāhmaṇaṃ pātre na mīmāṃseta yaṃ brāhmaṇam iva manyate pra devapātram āpnoti na manuṣyapātrāc chidyate
(PB 6.5.10) vāg vai devebhyo 'pakrāmat sāpaḥ prāviśat tāṃ devāḥ punar ayācaṃs tā abruvan yat punar dadyāma kiṃ nas tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayadhva ity abruvaṃs tā abruvan yad evāsmāsu manuṣyā apūtaṃ praveśayāṃs tenāsaṃsṛṣṭā asāmeti
(PB 6.5.11) śuddhā asmā āpaḥ pūtā bhavanti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.5.12) sā punartātyakrāmat sā vanaspatīn prāviśat tān devāḥ punar ayācaṃs tāṃ na punar adadus tān aśapan svena vaḥ kiṣkuṇā vajreṇa vṛścān iti tasmād vanaspatīn svena kiṣkuṇā vajreṇa vṛścanti devaśaptā hi
(PB 6.5.13) tāṃv vanaspatayaś caturdhā vācaṃv vinyadadhur dundubhau vīṇāyām akṣe tūṇave tasmād eṣā vadiṣṭhaiṣā valgutamā vāg vā vanaspatīnāṃ devānāṃ hy eṣā vāg āsīt
(PB 6.5.14) adho-'dho 'kṣaṃ droṇakalaśaṃ prohanti tasyā vāco 'varudhyā upary-upary akṣaṃ pavitraṃ prayacchanty ubhayata eva vācaṃ parigṛhṇanti
(PB 6.5.15) yasya kāmayetāsuryam asya yajñaṃ kuryāṃv vācaṃv vṛñjīyeti droṇakalaśaṃ prohan bāhubhyām akṣan upaspṛśed asuryam asya yajñaṃ karoti vācaṃv vṛṅkte yo 'sya priyaḥ syād anupaspṛśann akṣaṃ prohet prāṇā vai droṇakalaśaḥ prāṇān evāsya kalpayati
(PB 6.5.16) yan nv ity āhur vācānyān ṛtvijo vṛṇate kasmād udgātāro vṛtā ārtvijyaṃ kurvantīti
(PB 6.5.17) yad droṇakalaśam upasīdanti tenodgātāro vṛtāḥ
(PB 6.5.18) prājāpatyā vā udgātāraḥ prājāpatyo droṇakalaśo droṇakalaśa evainām ārtvijyāya vṛṇīte
(PB 6.5.19) prāñca upasīdanti prāñco yajñasyāgre karavāmeti
(PB 6.5.20) anabhijitā vā eṣodgātṝṇāṃ dig yat prācī yad droṇakalaśaṃ prāñcaṃ prohanti diśo 'bhijityai
(PB 6.5.21) yan nv ity āhur antarāśvaḥ prāsevau yujyate 'ntarā śamya anaḍvān ka udgātṝṇāṃ yoga iti yad droṇakalaśam upasīdanti sa eṣāṃ yogas tasmād yuktair evopasadyaṃ na hy ayukto vahati
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.5.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I become many, may I propagate.' He grieved. From him as he grieved, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) was emitted from his head. That burned his head. It became the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> (the large Soma vessel). In it the gods collected the bright <s>Soma</s>. He survived that affliction through life.
(PB 6.5.2) He survives the affliction through life, who knows this.
(PB 6.5.3) Let him push forward: 'You belong to the lord of the forest, you belong to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>. You are the head of <s>Prajāpati</s>. You are the vessel that transcends life. I propel myself forward for radiance and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.'
(PB 6.5.4) When he says 'belonging to the lord of the forest,' he pushes it forward with truth.
(PB 6.5.5) When he says 'belonging to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,' — <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is indeed the <s>Udgātṛ</s> of the gods — he thus yokes him.
(PB 6.5.6) When he says 'belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>' — for the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s> as its deity. When he says 'the head of <s>Prajāpati</s>' — for it was burned from the head of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 6.5.7) When he says 'the vessel that transcends life' — for this <s>droṇakalaśa</s> surpasses other vessels. The <s>droṇakalaśa</s> is the divine vessel.
(PB 6.5.8) He becomes the possessor of the divine vessel, who knows this.
(PB 6.5.9) One should not examine a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in the vessel. He whom one considers to be like a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> obtains the divine vessel; he is not cut off from the human vessel.
(PB 6.5.10) Speech indeed departed from the gods. She entered the waters. The gods asked her back. The waters said: 'If we give her back, what will be ours from that?' The gods said: 'Whatever you desire.' The waters said: 'Let us be unmingled with whatever impure thing humans may introduce into us.'
(PB 6.5.11) The waters become pure and clean for him who knows this.
(PB 6.5.12) She departed again. She entered the trees. The gods asked them for her back. They did not return her. The gods cursed them: 'With your own trunk as a thunderbolt, they shall cut you!' Therefore they cut trees with their own trunk as a thunderbolt, for they are cursed by the gods.
(PB 6.5.13) The trees distributed Speech in four ways: in the drum, in the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), in the axle, and in the quiver. Therefore this is the most eloquent, the most melodious speech — for it was the speech of the gods among the trees.
(PB 6.5.14) They push the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> lower and lower along the axle — for the purpose of confining that speech. They place the purifier higher and higher on the axle — thus they grasp speech from both sides.
(PB 6.5.15) If one desires: 'I shall make his sacrifice demonic, I shall rob him of speech' — while pushing the <s>droṇakalaśa</s>, he should touch the axle with his arms. He makes his sacrifice demonic and robs him of speech. For one who is dear to him, he should push without touching the axle. The <s>droṇakalaśa</s> is indeed the vital breaths — he thus restores his vital breaths.
(PB 6.5.16) Now they say: 'Other priests are chosen by speech — why do the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests perform their office as if chosen?'
(PB 6.5.17) When they approach the <s>droṇakalaśa</s>, by that the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests are chosen.
(PB 6.5.18) The <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. The <s>droṇakalaśa</s> itself chooses them for the priestly office.
(PB 6.5.19) They approach facing east: 'Let us be at the forefront of the sacrifice.'
(PB 6.5.20) The eastern direction is indeed the unconquered direction of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests. When they push the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> eastward, it is for the conquest of the direction.
(PB 6.5.21) Now they say: 'A horse is yoked between the two side-poles, an ox between the two pegs — what is the yoking of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priests?' When they approach the <s>droṇakalaśa</s>, that is their yoking. Therefore one should approach when yoked, for an unyoked one does not carry.

body.text:
(PB 6.6.1) grāvṇaḥ saṃsādya droṇakalaśam adhyūhanti viḍ vai grāvāṇo 'nnaṃ somo rāṣṭraṃ droṇakalaśo yad grāvasu droṇakalaśam adhyūhanti viśy eva tad rāṣṭram adhyūhanti
(PB 6.6.2) yaṃ dviṣyād vimukhān grāvṇaḥ kṛtvedam aham amum amuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram amuṣyā viśo 'muṣmād annādyān nirūhāmīti nirūhed viśa evainam annādyān nirūhati
(PB 6.6.3) yo 'sya priyaḥ syāt saṃmukhān grāvṇaḥ kṛtvedam aham amuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram amuṣyāṃ viśy amuṣinn annādye 'dhyūhāmīty adhyūhed viśy evainam annādye 'dhyūhati
(PB 6.6.4) atho tad ubhayam anādṛtyedam ahaṃ māṃ tejasi brahmavarcasse 'dhyūhāmīty adhyūhet tejasy eva brahmavarcasa ātmānam adhyūhati
(PB 6.6.5) yaḥ kāmayeta viśā rāṣṭraṃ hanyām iti vyūhya grāvṇo 'dho droṇakalaśaṃ sādayitvopāṃśusavanam upariṣṭād abhinidadhyād idam aham amuyā viśā 'do rāṣṭraṃ hanmīti viśaiva tad rāṣṭraṃ hanti
(PB 6.6.6) yo vai daivāni pavitrāṇi veda pūto yajñiyo bhavati cchandāṃsi vai daivāni pavitrāṇi tair droṇakalaśaṃ pāvayanti
(PB 6.6.7) vasavas tvā gāyatreṇa cchandasā punantu rudrās tvā traiṣṭubhena cchandasā punantv ādityās tvā jāgatena cchandasā punantv etāni vai daivāni pavitrāṇi pūto yajñiyo bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.6.8) svarbhānur vā āsura ādityaṃ tamasāvidhyat taṃ devā na vyajānaṃs te 'trim upādhāvaṃs tasyātrir bhāsena tamo 'pāhan yat prathamam apāhan sā kṛṣṇāvir abhavad yad dvitīyaṃ sā rajatā yat tṛtīyaṃ sā lohinī yayā varṇam abhyatṛṇat sā śuklāsīt
(PB 6.6.9) tasmāc chuklaṃ pavitraṃ śukraḥ somaḥ sa śukratvāya
(PB 6.6.10) yaṃ dviṣyāt tasyaiteṣāṃ varṇānām api pavitre kuryāt pāpmanaivainaṃ tamasā vidhyati kṛṣṇam iva hi tamo yo 'sya priyaḥ syād āsaktiśuklaṃ kuryāj jyotir vai hiraṇyaṃ jyotir evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 6.6.11) tasmād ātreyaṃ candreṇecchanty atrir hi tasya jyotiḥ
(PB 6.6.12) abhyatṛṇat pavitraṃv vigṛhṇanti hastakāryam eva tad yajñasya kriyata etad vā udgātṝṇāṃ hastakāryaṃ yat pavitrasya vigrahaṇam
(PB 6.6.13) na hastaveṣyān nir ṛcchati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.6.14) yo 'pi na vigṛhṇāti prāṇād enam antaryanti
(PB 6.6.15) taṃ brūyād vepamānaḥ prameṣyasa iti vepamāna eva pramīyate
(PB 6.6.16) pra śukraitu devī manīṣāsmad rathaḥ sutaṣṭo na vājīty udgātā dhārām anumantrayate
(PB 6.6.17) āyuṣe me pavasva varcase me pavasva viduḥ pṛthivyā divo janitrāc chṛṇvantv āpo 'dhaḥ kṣarantīḥ somehodgāyety āha mahyaṃ tejase brahmavarcasāyeti
(PB 6.6.18) eṣa vai somasyodgītho yat pavate somodgītham eva sāma gāyati
(PB 6.6.19) ācchinnaṃ pāvayanti yajñaṃ caiva prāṇāṃś ca saṃtanvanti saṃtataṃ pāvayanti yajñasya saṃtatyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.6.1) Having set down the pressing stones, they raise up the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> (wooden vessel) over them. The pressing stones are indeed the <s>Viś</s> (commoners); food is <s>Soma</s>; sovereignty is the <s>droṇakalaśa</s>. When they raise up the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> over the pressing stones, thereby they raise up sovereignty over the commoners.
(PB 6.6.2) Against one whom one hates, one should turn the pressing stones face-away and pronounce: 'I hereby remove from so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of such a woman, from his people and from his food-sovereignty' — thus one should remove it.

body.text:
(PB 6.7.1) bṛhaspatir vai devānām udagāyat taṃ rakṣāṃsy ajighāṃsan sa ya eṣāṃ lokānām adhipatayas tān bhāgadheyenopādhāvat
(PB 6.7.2) sūryo mā divābhyo nāṣṭrābhyaḥ pātu vāyur antarikṣābhyo 'gniḥ pārthivābhyaḥ svāheti juhoti
(PB 6.7.3) ete vā eṣāṃ lokānām adhipatayas tān bhāgadheyenopāsarat
(PB 6.7.4) karoti vācā vīryaṃ na sadasyām ārtim ārcchati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.7.5) vāg vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat tāṃ devā anvamantrayanta sā 'bravīd abhāgāsmi bhāgadheyaṃ me 'stv iti kas te bhāgadheyaṃ kuryād ity udgātāra ity abravīd udgātāro vai vāce bhāgadheyaṃ kurvanti
(PB 6.7.6) tasyai juhuyād bekurānāmāsi juṣṭā devebhyo namo vāce namo vācas pataye devi vāg yat te vāco madhumat tasmin mā dhāḥ sarasvatyai svāheti
(PB 6.7.7) vāh vai sarasvatī tām eva tad bhāgadheyenārabhate
(PB 6.7.8) yaṃ dviṣyāt tasyaitām āhutiṃ juhuyād vācaṃ manasā dhyāyed vācam evāsya vṛṅkte
(PB 6.7.9) bahiṣpavamānaṃ sarpanti svargam eva tal lokaṃ sarpanti
(PB 6.7.10) prakvāṇā iva sarpanti pratikūlam iva hītaḥ svargo lokaḥ tsaranta iva sarpanti mṛgadharmo vai yajño yajñasya śāntyā apratrāsāya
(PB 6.7.11) vācaṃ yacchanti yajñam eva tad yacchanti yad vyavavadeyur yajñaṃ nirbrūyus tasmān na vyavavadyam
(PB 6.7.12) pañcartvijaḥ saṃrabdhāḥ sarpanti pā-nkto yajño yāvān yajñas tam eva saṃtanvanti
(PB 6.7.13) yadi prastotāvacchidyate yajñasya śiraś chidyate brahmaṇe varaṃ dattvā sa eva punar vartavyaś chinnam eva tat pratidadhāti
(PB 6.7.14) yady udgātāvacchidyate yajñena yajamāno vyṛdhyate 'dakṣiṇaḥ sa yajñakratuḥ saṃsthāpyo 'thānya āhṛtyas tasmin deyaṃ yāvad dāsyan syāt
(PB 6.7.15) yadi pratihartā 'vacchidyate paśubhir yajamāno vyṛdhyate paśavo vai pratihartā sarvavedasaṃ deyaṃ yadi sarvavedasaṃ na dadāti sarvajyāniṃ jīyate
(PB 6.7.16) adhvaryuḥ prastaraṃ harati
(PB 6.7.17) yajamāno vai prastaro yajamānam eva tat svargaṃl lokaṃ harati
(PB 6.7.18) yajño vai devebhyo 'śvo bhūtvāpākrāmat taṃ devāḥ prastareṇāsamayaṃs tasmād aśvaḥ prastareṇa saṃmṛjyamāna upāvarabhate yad adhvaryuḥ prastaraṃ harati yajñasya śāntyā apratrāsāya
(PB 6.7.19) prajāpatiḥ paśun asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā aśanāyanto 'pākrāmaṃs tebhyaḥ prastaram annaṃ prāyacchat enam upāvartanta tasmād adhvaryuṇā prastara īṣad iva vidhūyo vidhūtim iva hi tṛṇaṃ paśava upāvartante
(PB 6.7.20) upainaṃ paśava āvartante ya evaṃv veda
(PB 6.7.21) prastaram āsadyodgāyed dhaviṣo 'skandāya
(PB 6.7.22) yajamānaṃ tu svargāl lokā avagṛhṇāti
(PB 6.7.23) aṣṭhīvatopaspṛśatodgeyaṃ tenāsya havir askannaṃ bhavati na yajamānaṃ svargāl lokād avagṛhṇāti
(PB 6.7.24) cātvālam avekṣya bahiṣpavamānaṃ stuvanty atra vā asāv āditya āsīt ta devā bahiṣpavamānena svargaṃl lokam aharan yac cātvālam avekṣya bahiṣpavamānaṃ stuvanti yajamānam eva tat svargaṃl lokaṃ haranti
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.7.1) <s>Bṛhaspati</s> indeed chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> (sacred chant) for the gods. The <s>rakṣas</s> (demons) sought to harm him. He sought refuge with the lords of these worlds, offering them a share.
(PB 6.7.2) 'May <s>Sūrya</s> protect me from the [demons] of the day, from those of the night; may <s>Vāyu</s> [protect me] from those of the atmosphere; may <s>Agni</s> from those of the earth — <s>svāhā</s>!' — thus he makes the offering.
(PB 6.7.3) These indeed are the lords of these worlds. He approached them with a share of the offering.
(PB 6.7.4)

body.text:
(PB 6.8.1) sa tu vai yajñena yajetety āhur yasya virājaṃ yajñamukhe dadhyur iti
(PB 6.8.2) navabhiḥ stuvanti hiṅkāro daśamo daśākṣarā virāḍ virājam evāsya yajñamukhe dadhāti
(PB 6.8.3) navabhiḥ stuvanti prāṇāḥ prāṇair evainaṃ samarddhayanti hiṅkāro daśamas tasmān nābhir anavatṛṇṇā daśamī prāṇānām
(PB 6.8.4) navabhiḥ stuvanti navādhvaryuḥ prātaḥsavane grahān gṛhṇāti tān eva tat pāvayanti teṣāṃ prāṇān utsṛjanti
(PB 6.8.5) prajāpatir vai hiṅkāras trayo bahiṣpavamānyo yad dhiṅkṛtya prastauti mithunam evāsyā yajñamukhe dadhāti prajananāya
(PB 6.8.6) eṣa vai stomasya yogo yad dhiṅkāro yad dhiṅkṛtya prastauti yuktenaiva stomena prastauti
(PB 6.8.7) eṣa vai sāmnāṃ raso yad dhiṅkāro yad dhiṅkṛtya prastauti rasenaivaitā abhyudya prastauti
(PB 6.8.8) āraṇyebhyo vā etat paśubhyaḥ stuvanti yad bahiṣpavamānam ekārūpābhiḥ stuvanti tasmād ekarūpā āraṇyāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 6.8.9) parācībhiḥ stuvanti tasmāt parāñcaḥ prajāyante parāñco vitiṣṭhante
(PB 6.8.10) apariśrite stuvanti tasmād aparigṛhītā āraṇyāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 6.8.11) bahiḥ stuvanty antar anuśaṃsanti tasmād grāmam āhṛtair bhuñjate
(PB 6.8.12) grāmebhyo vā etat paśubhyaḥ stuvanti yad ājyair nānārūpaiḥ stuvanti tasmān nānārūpā grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 6.8.13) punarabhyāvartaṃ stuvanti tasmāt pretvaryaḥ pretya punar āyanti
(PB 6.8.14) pariśrite stuvanti tasmāt parigṛhītā grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 6.8.15) amuṣmai vā etal lokāya stuvanti yad bahiṣpavamānaṃ sakṛd dhiṅkṛtābhiḥ parācībhiḥ stuvanti sakṛd dhīto 'sau parāṅ lokaḥ
(PB 6.8.16) asmai vā etal lokāya stuvanti yad ājyaiḥ punarabhyāvartaṃ stuvanti tasmād ayaṃl lokaḥ punaḥ-punaḥ prajāyate
(PB 6.8.17) parāñco vā eteṣāṃ prāṇā bahvantīty āhur ye parācībhir bahiṣpavamānībhiḥ stuvata ity āvatīm uttamāṃ gāyet prāṇānāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 6.8.18) cyavante vā ete 'smāl lokād ity āhur ye parācībhir bahiṣpavamānībhiḥ stuvata iti rathantaravarṇam uttamāṃ gāyed iyaṃ vai rathantaram asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.8.1) 'He should sacrifice with the sacrifice,' they say, 'in whose sacrifice-mouth they place the <s>Virāj</s> (cosmic meter).'
(PB 6.8.2) They praise with nine; the <s>hiṅkāra</s> is the tenth. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables. He thus places the <s>Virāj</s> at the mouth of his sacrifice.
(PB 6.8.3) They praise with nine — the vital breaths are nine. With the vital breaths they bring him to fullness. The <s>hiṅkāra</s> is the tenth. Therefore the navel is the tenth of the vital breaths, uncut.
(PB 6.8.4) They praise with nine. The <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) draws nine cups at the morning pressing. They thereby purify those and release their vital breaths.
(PB 6.8.5) <s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. The three <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> chants — since he begins the chant after making the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, he places a productive pair at the mouth of his sacrifice, for procreation.
(PB 6.8.6) This yoking of the <s>stoma</s> is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Since he begins the chant after making the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, he begins the chant with the <s>stoma</s> already yoked.
(PB 6.8.7) This essence of the <s>Sāmans</s> is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. Since he begins the chant after making the <s>hiṅkāra</s>, he begins the chant having risen with the essence.
(PB 6.8.8) They praise for the wild animals when they praise the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> with verses of uniform appearance. Therefore wild animals are of uniform appearance.
(PB 6.8.9) They praise with reversed verses. Therefore they are born going away and they stand going away.
(PB 6.8.10) They praise in the unclosed space. Therefore wild animals are uncaptured.
(PB 6.8.11) They praise outside; they recite inside. Therefore they enjoy the things brought to the village.
(PB 6.8.12) They praise for the domestic animals when they praise with the <s>Ājya</s> chants of various forms. Therefore domestic animals are of various forms.
(PB 6.8.13) They praise with returning. Therefore the departed, having departed, return again.
(PB 6.8.14) They praise in the enclosed space. Therefore domestic animals are captured.
(PB 6.8.15) They praise for yonder world when they praise the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> with reversed verses preceded by a single <s>hiṅkāra</s>. That world, preceded by a single <s>hiṅkāra</s>, is turned away.
(PB 6.8.16) They praise for this world when they praise with the <s>Ājya</s> chants with returning. Therefore this world reproduces again and again.
(PB 6.8.17) 'The vital breaths of those who praise the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> with reversed verses turn away,' they say. One should sing the last verse with the <s>Āvatī</s> melody — for the support of the vital breaths.
(PB 6.8.18) 'Those who praise the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> with reversed verses fall from this world,' they say. One should sing the last verse with the color of the <s>Rathantara</s>. This world is the <s>Rathantara</s>. He thereby becomes established in this world.

body.text:
(PB 6.9.1) upāsmai gāyata nara iti grāmakāmāyapratipadaṃ kuryāt
(PB 6.9.2) naro vai devānāṃ grāmo grāmam evāsmā upākaḥ
(PB 6.9.3) upa vā annam-annam evāsmā upākaḥ
(PB 6.9.4) upoṣu jātam apturam iti prajākāmāya pratipadaṃ kuryāt
(PB 6.9.5) upa vai prajā tāṃ jātam ity evājījanat
(PB 6.9.6) sa naḥ pasvasya śaṃ gava iti pratipadaṃ kuryāt
(PB 6.9.7) yāṃ samāṃ mahādevaḥ paśūn hanyāt sa naḥ pavasva śaṃ gava iti catuṣpade bheṣajaṃ karoti
(PB 6.9.8) śaṃ janāyeti dvipade śam arvata ity ekaśaphāya
(PB 6.9.9) viṣeṇa vai tāṃ samām oṣadhayo 'ktā bhavanti yāṃ samāṃ mahādevaḥ paśūn hanti yac chaṃ rājann oṣadhībhya ity āhauṣadhīr evāsmai svadayaty ubhayyo 'smai svaditāḥ pacyante 'kṛṣṭapacyāś ca kṛṣṭapacyāś ca
(PB 6.9.10) pavasva vāco agriya iti pratipadaṃ kuryād yaṃ kāmayeta samānānāṃ śīreṣṭhaḥ syād iti
(PB 6.9.11) pavasva vāco agriya ity agram evainaṃ pariṇayati
(PB 6.9.12) śrīr vai vāco 'graṃ śriyam evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 6.9.13) ete asṛgram indava iti bahubhyaḥ pratipadaṃ kuryāt
(PB 6.9.14) eta iti sarvān evainān ṛddhyai bhūtyā abhivadati
(PB 6.9.15) eta iti vai prajāpatir devān asṛjatāsṛgram iti manuṣyān indava iti pitṝṃs tiraḥ pavitra iti grahān āśava iti stotraṃv viśvānīti śastram abhi saubhagety anyāḥ prajāḥ
(PB 6.9.16) yad eta iti tasmād yāvanta evāgre devās tāvanta idānīm
(PB 6.9.17) sarvān vṛddhim ārdhnuvaṃ sthiteva hy eṣā vyāhṛtiḥ
(PB 6.9.18) yad asṛgram iti tasmān manuṣyāḥ śvaḥ-śvaḥ sṛjyante
(PB 6.9.19) yad indava itīndava iva hi pitaraḥ
(PB 6.9.20) mana iva
(PB 6.9.21) yāntāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭā ṛddhim ārdhnuvaṃs tām ṛdhnuvanti yeṣām evaṃv vidvān etāṃ pratipadaṃ karoti
(PB 6.9.22) chandāṃsi vai somam āharaṃs taṃ gandharvo viśvāvasuḥ paryamuṣṇāt. tenāpaḥ prāviśat taṃ devatā anvaicchaṃs taṃ viṣṇur apsu paryapaśyat sa vyakāṅkṣad ayaṃ nū3 nā3 iti taṃ padā prāsphurat tasmāt pṛthag indavo 'sṛjyanta sa devatābhyo 'bhitas tiṣṭhantībhya ete asṛgram indava iti prābravīd bahiṣpavamānena vai yajñaḥ sṛjyate yad ete asṛgram indava iti prastauti yajñam eva tat sṛṣṭaṃ devatābhyaḥ prāha
(PB 6.9.23) vyṛddhaṃ vā etad apaśavyaṃ yat prātaḥsavanam aniḍaṃ hi yad iḍām asmabhyaṃ saṃyatam ity āha prātaḥsavanam eva tad iḍāvat paśumat karoti
(PB 6.9.24) davidyūtatyā ruceti vrātāya pratipadaṃ kuryāt
(PB 6.9.25) davidyūtatyā receti vai gāyatryā rūpaṃ pariṣṭobhantyeti triṣṭubhaḥ kṛpety anuṣṭubhaḥ somāḥ śukrā gavāśira iti jagatyāḥ sarveṣāṃ vā eṣā cchandasāṃ rūpaṃ cchandāṃsīva khalu vai vratopadeṣā pratipad bhavati svenaivaināṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 6.9.26) vṛddhā vā eta indriyeṇa vīryeṇa yad vrāta indriyaṃ vīryaṃ chandāṃsīndriyeṇaivainān vīryeṇa samardhayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 6.9.1) 'Sing up for him, O men' — one should make this the opening verse for one desiring a village.
(PB 6.9.2) Men are the village of the gods. He thus brings a village near to him.
(PB 6.9.3) Or 'near' means food — he brings food near to him.
(PB 6.9.4) 'The newly born, the fit one, has risen' — one should make this the opening verse for one desiring offspring.
(PB 6.9.5) 'Near' means offspring. 'Born' — thus he causes offspring to be born.
(PB 6.9.6) 'Purify yourself for our benefit, O giver of cattle' — one should make this the opening verse.
(PB 6.9.7) In the year when <s>Mahādeva</s> (the Great God) kills cattle, 'Purify yourself for our benefit, O giver of cattle' — he makes a remedy for four-footed animals.
(PB 6.9.8) 'Welfare to people' — for two-footed. 'Welfare to the horse' — for the single-hoofed.
(PB 6.9.9) In that year when <s>Mahādeva</s> kills cattle, the herbs are smeared with poison. Since he says 'Welfare, O king, to the herbs,' he makes the herbs sweet for him. Both kinds ripen for him: the uncultivated and the cultivated.
(PB 6.9.10) 'Purify yourself, O foremost of speech' — one should make this the opening verse for one whom one wishes to be the chief among his equals.
(PB 6.9.11) 'Purify yourself, O foremost of speech' — he leads him to the forefront.
(PB 6.9.12) <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) is the forefront of speech. He places <s>Śrī</s> in him.
(PB 6.9.13) 'These drops have flowed forth' — one should make this the opening verse for many.
(PB 6.9.14) By 'these,' he addresses them all with prosperity and abundance.
(PB 6.9.15) By 'these' <s>Prajāpati</s> created the gods; by 'they flowed forth' the humans; by 'drops' the ancestors; by 'through the filter' the cups; by 'the swift ones' the <s>stotra</s> (praise chant); by 'all' the <s>śastra</s> (recitation); by 'toward good fortune' the other creatures.
(PB 6.9.16) Because he says 'these,' therefore as many gods as there were in the beginning, so many are there now.
(PB 6.9.17) All have prospered. This utterance is like something standing firm.
(PB 6.9.18) Because he says 'they flowed forth,' therefore humans are created day after day.
(PB 6.9.19) Because he says 'drops' — for the ancestors are like drops.
(PB 6.9.20) Like mind.
(PB 6.9.21) The creatures that were created prospered. They prosper for whom a knower of this makes this the opening verse.
(PB 6.9.22) The meters carried <s>Soma</s> hither. The <s>Gandharva</s> <s>Viśvāvasu</s> stole him away. He entered the waters with him. The gods searched for him. <s>Viṣṇu</s> perceived him in the waters. He yearned: 'This one, now, now!' He kicked him with his foot. Therefore the drops were released separately. He announced to the gods standing on all sides: 'These drops have flowed forth.' By the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> the sacrifice is released. When he begins the chant with 'These drops have flowed forth,' he announces the released sacrifice to the gods.
(PB 6.9.23) The morning pressing is indeed defective, without cattle-increase, for it is without the <s>Iḍā</s> (consecrated portion). When he says 'The <s>Iḍā</s> has been directed to us,' he makes the morning pressing endowed with the <s>Iḍā</s> and with cattle.
(PB 6.9.24) 'With the flashing <s>ruc</s> (brightness)' — one should make this the opening verse for a <s>vrātya</s> (outcast who returns to Vedic fold).
(PB 6.9.25) 'With the flashing' is the form of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; '<s>rec</s>' is the embellishment of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; '<s>kṛp</s>' is of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; 'the bright <s>Soma</s> juices mixed with milk' is of the <s>Jagatī</s>. This is the form of all meters. Meters indeed are the means of instruction for the <s>vrātya</s> rite. By their own form he brings them to fullness.
(PB 6.9.26) The <s>vrātyas</s> have grown in vital power and vigor. The meters are vital power. He brings them to fullness with vital power and vigor.

(PB 6.10.1) 'O <s>Agni</s>, purify our life-spans' — one should make this the opening verse when one of the consecrated [sacrificers] dies.

body.translated_text:
(PB 7.1.1) These worlds are the <s>Gāyatra</s> (chant). It should be sung with the three-fold repetition, for these worlds are three. When one sings with the three-fold repetition, one measures it out with these very worlds.
(PB 7.1.2) One should bellow twice and make the <s>hiṃ</s> sound the third time.
(PB 7.1.3) If one bellows three times, one extends the <s>Gāyatra</s> too far.
(PB 7.1.4) He who chants with the <s>Gāyatra</s> without the proper response becomes unestablished. The <s>hiṃkāra</s> is indeed the <s>Gāyatra's</s>

(PB 7.2.1) <s>Prajāpati</s>, having made himself the sacrifice, offered himself to the gods. They did not stand aside for one another for the sake of precedence. He said to them: 'Race for it!' They raced. Because they raced (<s>ājim āyan</s>), that is the origin of the <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblation) chants' name.
(PB 7.2.2) <s>Indra</s> knew: '<s>Agni</s> will be the first to win this.' He said: 'Whichever of us two wins first, let that be ours together.' <s>Agni</s> won first.

(PB 7.3.1) etāvatā vāva mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ pupuve

(PB 7.3.4) etāvanti vāva sarvāṇi sāmāni yāvanti mādhyandine pavamāne

(PB 7.3.14) aiḍena bṛhatīm ārabhante
(PB 7.3.15) paśavo vā iḍā paśavo bṛhatī paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti
(PB 7.3.16) bṛhatyāṃ bhūyiṣṭhāni sāmāni bhavanti
(PB 7.3.17) tatrāpi triṇidhanam
(PB 7.3.18) abaliṣṭha iva vā ayaṃ madhyami lokas tasyaiva tad āyatanaṃ kriyate
