(PB 7.3.28) prāṇo vai gāyatraṃ prāṇaḥ svaraḥ prāṇān evatad ubhayato dadhāti tasmād ubhayataḥ prāṇāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 7.3.29) yad gāyatraṃ purastād bhavati svāram antataḥ prāṇair eva praity apāne pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.3.1) By this much indeed the midday pressing (<s>mādhyandina savana</s>) was purified.
(PB 7.3.2) By three meters and five <s>sāmans</s>.
(PB 7.3.3) When they praise with the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> (the purifying chant), they thereby purify the midday pressing itself.
(PB 7.3.4) All the <s>sāmans</s> are indeed as many as those in the midday <s>Pavamāna</s>.
(PB 7.3.5) The <s>Gāyatra</s> with <s>nidhana</s> (concluding phrase), without <s>nidhana</s>, and the <s>Aiḍa</s>.
(PB 7.3.6) When they praise with the midday <s>Pavamāna</s>, they praise with all the <s>sāmans</s> indeed.
(PB 7.3.7) The <s>Pavamāna</s> is indeed the self of the sacrifice. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the mouth; <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) is the <s>Gāyatra</s>. When they praise with the <s>Gāyatra</s> on the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, they thereby place the vital breaths at the mouth.
(PB 7.3.8) These meters are indeed the <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (in-breath): the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>, the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath), the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is <s>apāna</s>. When they praise with these meters, it is for the non-interruption of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(PB 7.3.9) These worlds are indeed these meters: the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is this world, the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is the middle world, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is the highest world. When they praise with these meters joined together, it is for the non-interruption of these worlds.
(PB 7.3.10) If another meter were to intervene between them, it would sever these worlds.
(PB 7.3.11) Having praised with the <s>Gāyatra</s>, they praise with one having a <s>nidhana</s>. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is this world — thereby a foundation is established in this very world.
(PB 7.3.12) If they were to praise first with one without a <s>nidhana</s>, the sacrificer would be without a foundation.
(PB 7.3.13) They praise with one having a <s>nidhana</s>. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed vigor; the <s>nidhana</s> is vigor — thereby they strengthen vigor with vigor.
(PB 7.3.14) They begin the <s>Bṛhatī</s> with the <s>Aiḍa</s>.
(PB 7.3.15) <s>Iḍā</s> is animals; the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is animals — thereby they place animals among animals.
(PB 7.3.16) The most numerous <s>sāmans</s> are on the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(PB 7.3.17) And there too it has a triple <s>nidhana</s>.
(PB 7.3.18) This middle world is, as it were, the weakest — thereby a foundation is made for it.
(PB 7.3.19) It has a triple <s>nidhana</s>. There are three gaps in the pressings — those are closed up by it.
(PB 7.3.20) It has a triple <s>nidhana</s>. These are the three worlds — thereby one becomes firmly established in these very worlds.
(PB 7.3.21) It has a triple <s>nidhana</s>. By this indeed the midday pressing is established. If it did not have a triple <s>nidhana</s>, the midday pressing would be without a firm foundation.
(PB 7.3.22) The <s>nidhanas</s> have two syllables. The sacrificer is two-footed — thereby he establishes the sacrificer in the sacrifice and among animals.
(PB 7.3.23) The last one is without a <s>nidhana</s> — so as not to overstep the heavenly world.
(PB 7.3.24) If it had a <s>nidhana</s>, it would cast the sacrificer out of the heavenly world.
(PB 7.3.25) It has the <s>svāra</s> (tonal accent).
(PB 7.3.26) By the <s>svāra</s> indeed, food-eating is given to the gods at the very end — thereby he gives food-eating to the gods at the very end by the <s>svāra</s>.
(PB 7.3.27) The <s>Gāyatra</s> comes first; the <s>svāra</s> comes last.
(PB 7.3.28) <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatra</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>svāra</s>. Thereby he places the vital breaths on both sides. Therefore the animals that are <s>prāṇas</s> are on both sides.
(PB 7.3.29) When the <s>Gāyatra</s> comes first and the <s>svāra</s> comes last, he proceeds by the vital breaths and becomes firmly established in the <s>apāna</s>.

body.text:
(PB 7.4.1) etad vai yajñasya svargyaṃ yan mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ mādhyandinasya pavamānaḥ pavamānasya bṛhatī yad bṛhatyāḥ stotre dakṣiṇā dīyante svargasyaiva tal lokasyāyatane dīyante
(PB 7.4.2) devā vai cchandāṃsy abruvan yuṣmābhiḥ svargyaṃl lokam ayāmeti te gāyatrīṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvaṃs triṣṭubhaṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvañ jagatīṃ prāyuñjata tayā na vyāpnuvann anuṣṭubhaṃ prāyuñjata tayālpakādi na vyāpnuvaṃs ta āsāṃ diśāṃ rasān prabṛhya catvāry akṣarāṇy upādadhuḥ sā bṛhaty abhavat tayemāṃl lokān vyāpnuvan
(PB 7.4.3) bṛhatī maryā yayemāṃl lokān vyāpāmeti tad bṛhatyā bṛhattvam
(PB 7.4.4) paśūn vā asyāntān upādadhuḥ paśavo vai bṛhatī yad bṛhatyāḥ stotre dakṣiṇā dīyante sva eva tad āyatane dīyante
(PB 7.4.5) yan nv ity āhur anyāni cchandāṃsi varṣīyāṃsi kasmād bṛhaty ucyata eṣā hīmāṃl lokān vyāpnon nānyac chandaḥ kiṃ cana yāni sapta caturuttarāṇi cchandāṃsi tāni bṛhatīm abhisaṃpadyante tasmād bṛhaty ucyate
(PB 7.4.6) yan nv ity āhur gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ kasmād bṛhatyā madhyandine stuvantīti
(PB 7.4.7) bahiṣpavamānena vai devā ādityaṃ svargaṃl lokam aharan sa nādhriyata taṃ bṛhatyā madhyandine 'stabhnuvaṃs tasmād bṛhatyā madhyandinaṃ stuvanty ādityaṃ hy eṣā madhyandine dādhāra
(PB 7.4.8) yair u kaiś ca cchandobhir madhyandine stuvanti tāni triṣṭubham abhi saṃpadyante tasmāt triṣṭubho nayanti mādhyandināt savanāt
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.4.1) This indeed is the heavenly part of the sacrifice: the midday pressing. Of the midday pressing, the <s>Pavamāna</s>; of the <s>Pavamāna</s>, the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. When at the <s>Bṛhatī</s> <s>stotra</s> (chant) the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are given, they are given at the very foundation of the heavenly world.
(PB 7.4.2) The gods said to the meters: 'By you we will go to the heavenly world.' They employed the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — by it they did not reach it. They employed the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> — by it they did not reach it. They employed the <s>Jagatī</s> — by it they did not reach it. They employed the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — by it, being of little extent, they did not reach it. They extracted the essences of these directions and took up four syllables. That became the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. By it they encompassed these worlds.
(PB 7.4.3) The <s>Bṛhatī</s> is the boundary by which they encompassed these worlds — that is the greatness (<s>bṛhattva</s>) of the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(PB 7.4.4) They took up animals at her ends. Animals are the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. When at the <s>Bṛhatī</s> <s>stotra</s> the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> are given, they are given at their own proper foundation.
(PB 7.4.5) Now they ask: 'Other meters are larger; why is the <s>Bṛhatī</s> called great?' Because this one encompassed these worlds, while no other meter could — the seven meters with four additional syllables come to equal the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. Therefore the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is called great.
(PB 7.4.6) Now they ask: 'The morning pressing is of the <s>Gāyatra</s>, the midday pressing is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the third pressing is of the <s>Jagatī</s>. Why do they praise with the <s>Bṛhatī</s> at midday?'
(PB 7.4.7) By the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (outer purification chant) the gods carried the sun to the heavenly world. He did not hold firm. They propped him up with the <s>Bṛhatī</s> at midday. Therefore they praise with the <s>Bṛhatī</s> at midday, for she upheld the sun at midday.
(PB 7.4.8) Whatever meters they praise with at midday, those come to equal the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Therefore they lead the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> from the midday pressing.

body.text:
(PB 7.5.1) prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa śocann amahīyamāno 'tiṣṭhat sa etad āmahīyavam apaśyat tenemāḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā amahīyanta yad amahīyanta tasmād āmahīyavam
(PB 7.5.2) tā asmāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tāsāṃ divi sad bhūmy ādada iti prāṇān ādatta tā enaṃ prāṇeṣv ātteṣu punar upāvartanta tābhya ugraṃ śarma mahi śrava iti punaḥ prāṇān prāyacchat tā asmād ud evāyodhaṃs tāsāṃ stauṣa iti manyūn avāśṛṇāt tato vai tasmai tāḥ śraiṣṭhyāyātiṣṭhanta
(PB 7.5.3) tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śraiṣṭhyāya ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.5.4) prajānāṃ ca vā eṣā sṛṣṭiḥ pāpavasīyaś ca vidhṛtir yad āmahīyavam
(PB 7.5.5) vidhṛtiḥ pāpavasīyaso bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.5.6) devā vai yaśaskāmāḥ sattram āsatāgnir indro vāyur makhas te 'bruvsn yan no yaśa ṛcchāt tan naḥ sahāsad iti teṣā makhaṃ yaśa ārcchat tad ādāyāpākrāmat tad asya prāsahāditsanta taṃ paryayatanta svadhanuḥ pratiṣṭhābhyātiṣṭhat tasya dhanurārtnir ūrdhvā patitvā śiro 'cchinat sa pravargyo 'bhavad yajño vai makho yat pravargyaṃ pravṛñjanti yajñasyaiva tac chiraḥ pratidadhati
(PB 7.5.7) tad devā yaśo vyabhajanta tasyāgnī rauravaṃ prābṛhata
(PB 7.5.8) tad vai sa paśuvīryaṃ prābṛhata paśavo vai rauravam
(PB 7.5.9) paśumān bhavati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.5.10) agnir vai rūras tasyaitad rauravam
(PB 7.5.11) asurā vai devān paryayatanta tata etāv agnī rūrau viṣvañcau stobhāv apaśyat tābhyām enān pratyauṣat te pratyuṣyamāṇā aravanta yad aravanta tasmād rauravam
(PB 7.5.12) athendro yaudhājayaṃ prābṛhata tad vai sa vajraṃ prābṛhata vajro vai yaudhājayam
(PB 7.5.13) vajraṃ bhrātṛvyāya praharati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.5.14) indro vai yudhājit tasyaitad yaudhājayam
(PB 7.5.15) yudhā maryā ajaiṣmeti tasmād yaudhājayam
(PB 7.5.16) atha vāyur auśanaṃ prābṛhata
(PB 7.5.17) tad vai sa prāṇvīryaṃ prābṛhata prāṇā vā auśanam
(PB 7.5.18) sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.5.19) vāyur vā uśanaṃs tasyaitad auśanam
(PB 7.5.20) uśanā vai kāvyo 'surāṇāṃ purohita āsīt taṃ devāḥ kāmadughābhir apāmantrayanta tasmā etāny auśanāni prāyacchan kāmadughā vā auśanāni
(PB 7.5.21) kāmadughā enam upatiṣṭhante ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.5.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I become many; may I be propagated.' He stood grieving and not magnified. He perceived this <s>Āmahīyava</s> (chant of magnification). By it he created these creatures. Those, once created, were magnified. Because they were magnified (<s>amahīyanta</s>), therefore it is called <s>Āmahīyava</s>.
(PB 7.5.2) Those creatures, once created, departed from him. He seized their vital breaths with 'dwelling in heaven, he takes from the earth.' Those, with their vital breaths seized, returned to him. To them, with 'fierce shelter, great glory,' he gave back the vital breaths. But they rose up against him. From them, with 'stauṣa' (the word of praise), he released their anger. Thereupon they submitted to his supremacy.
(PB 7.5.3) His equals submit to him for supremacy — he who knows thus.
(PB 7.5.4) This <s>Āmahīyava</s> is indeed both the creation of offspring and the warding off of evil.
(PB 7.5.5) He becomes the warder of evil — he who knows thus.
(PB 7.5.6) The gods, desiring fame, sat in a <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) — <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Makha</s>. They said: 'Whatever fame comes to us, let it be shared among us.' Fame came to <s>Makha</s> among them. He took it and departed. They wished to seize it from him by force. They surrounded him. He stood firm, supported by his own bow. The tip of his bow flew up and cut off his head. That became the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ceremony). <s>Makha</s> is indeed the sacrifice. When they perform the <s>Pravargya</s>, they thereby restore the head of the sacrifice.
(PB 7.5.7) The gods divided that fame among themselves. <s>Agni</s> extracted the <s>Raurava</s> (sāman).
(PB 7.5.8) He thereby extracted the power of animals, for animals are the <s>Raurava</s>.
(PB 7.5.9) He who knows thus becomes possessed of animals.
(PB 7.5.10) <s>Agni</s> is indeed <s>Rūra</s> — this is his <s>Raurava</s>.
(PB 7.5.11) The <s>asuras</s> surrounded the gods. Then <s>Agni</s> perceived these two <s>Rūra</s> <s>stobhas</s> (exclamations), diverging in opposite directions. With them he scorched the <s>asuras</s>. Those, being scorched, cried out (<s>aravanta</s>). Because they cried out, therefore it is called <s>Raurava</s>.
(PB 7.5.12) Then <s>Indra</s> extracted the <s>Yaudhājaya</s> (sāman of victory in battle).
(PB 7.5.13) He thereby extracted the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), for the <s>vajra</s> is the <s>Yaudhājaya</s>.
(PB 7.5.14) He hurls the <s>vajra</s> against his rival — he who knows thus.
(PB 7.5.15) <s>Indra</s> is indeed <s>Yudhājit</s> (victorious in battle) — this is his <s>Yaudhājaya</s>.
(PB 7.5.16) 'By battle we heroes conquered' — therefore it is called <s>Yaudhājaya</s>.
(PB 7.5.17) Then <s>Vāyu</s> extracted the <s>Auśana</s> (sāman).
(PB 7.5.18) He thereby extracted the power of the vital breaths, for the vital breaths are the <s>Auśana</s>.
(PB 7.5.19) He lives his full lifespan — he who knows thus.
(PB 7.5.20) <s>Vāyu</s> is indeed <s>Uśanas</s> — this is his <s>Auśana</s>.
(PB 7.5.21) <s>Uśanas Kāvya</s> was the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) of the <s>asuras</s>. The gods enticed him with wish-fulfilling cows. They gave him these <s>Auśana</s> sāmans. Wish-fulfilling cows attend him — he who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 7.6.1) prajāpatir akāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti sa tūṣṇīṃ manasādhyāyat tasya yan manasy āsīt tad bṛhat samabhavat
(PB 7.6.2) sa ādadhīta garbho vai me 'yam antarhitas taṃv vācā prajanayā iti
(PB 7.6.3) sa vācaṃ vyasṛjata sā vāg rathantaram anvapadyata
(PB 7.6.4) ratham aryāḥ kṣeplātārīd iti tad rathantarasya rathantaratvam
(PB 7.6.5) tato bṛhad anu prājāyata bṛhan maryā idaṃ sa jyog antarabhūd iti tad bṛhato bṛhattvam
(PB 7.6.6) yathā vai putro jyeṣṭha evaṃ bṛhat prajāpateḥ
(PB 7.6.7) jyeṣṭhabrāhmaṇaṃ vā etat
(PB 7.6.8) pra jyaiṣṭhyam āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.6.9) yan nv ity āhur bṛhat pūrvaṃ prajāpatau samabhavat kasmād rathantaraṃ pūrvaṃ yogam ānaśa iti
(PB 7.6.10) bṛhad eva pūrvaṃ samabhavad rathantaraṃ tu pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭyāsṛjata tasmāt pūrvaṃ yogam ānaśe
(PB 7.6.11) tayoḥ samānaṃ nidhanam āsīt tasmin nātiṣṭhetāṃ ta ājim aitāṃ tayor has iti bṛhat prāṇam udajayad as iti rathantaram apānam abhisamaveṣṭata
(PB 7.6.12) prāṇāpānau vai bṛhadrathantare jyog āmayāvina ubhe kuryād apakrāntau vā etasya prāṇāpānau yasya jyog āmayati prāṇāpānāv evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 7.6.13) yan nv ity āhur ubhe bṛhadrathantare bahirṇidhane kasmād bṛhad bahirṇidhanāni bhajate 'ntarṇidhanāni rathantaram iti
(PB 7.6.14) prāṇo bṛhat tasmād bahirṇidhanāni bhajate bahir hi prāṇo 'pāno rathantaraṃ tasmād antarṇidhanāni bhajate 'ntar hy apānaḥ
(PB 7.6.15) mahāvṛkṣau vai bṛhadrathantare nidhanena samarpye
(PB 7.6.16) yad vai mahāvṛkṣau samṛcchete bahu tatra vibhagnaṃ prabhagnaṃ śete
(PB 7.6.17) airaṃ vai bṛhad aiḍaṃ rathantaraṃ mano vai bṛhad vāg rathantaraṃ sām a vai bṛhad ṛg rathantaraṃ prāṇo vai bṛhad apāno rathantaram asau vai loko bṛhad ayaṃ rathantaram etāni manasānvīkṣyodgāyet kḷptābhyām evābhyām udgāyati
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.6.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I become many, may I propagate.' He meditated silently with his mind. That which was in his mind became the <s>Bṛhat</s> (great chant).
(PB 7.6.2) He reflected: 'This embryo of mine is hidden within. Let me bring it forth with speech.'
(PB 7.6.3) He emitted speech. That speech followed after the <s>Rathantara</s> (chant).
(PB 7.6.4) 'The chariot of the noble one swiftly crossed over' — that is the nature of the <s>Rathantara</s> as '<s>Rathantara</s>.'
(PB 7.6.5) Then the <s>Bṛhat</s> was born after it: 'Great, O young men, is this — for long it was hidden within' — that is the nature of the <s>Bṛhat</s> as 'great.'
(PB 7.6.6) Just as the eldest son, so is the <s>Bṛhat</s> of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 7.6.7) This is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of primogeniture.
(PB 7.6.8) He who knows this attains primogeniture.
(PB 7.6.9) Now they ask: 'The <s>Bṛhat</s> came into being first in <s>Prajāpati</s> — why did the <s>Rathantara</s> obtain employment first?'
(PB 7.6.10) The <s>Bṛhat</s> indeed came into being first, but the <s>Rathantara</s> was emitted through creation first; therefore it obtained employment first.
(PB 7.6.11) These two had the same ending (<s>nidhana</s>). They could not stand together in it. They ran a contest. Of the two, the <s>Bṛhat</s> with 'has' won the <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath); the <s>Rathantara</s> with 'as' encompassed the <s>apāna</s> (inbreath).
(PB 7.6.12) The <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> are indeed the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>. Both should be performed for one who has been ill for a long time. The <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> have departed from one who has been ill for long. He thus places the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> back in him.
(PB 7.6.13) Now they ask: 'Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> have external endings. Why does the <s>Bṛhat</s> share in the external endings and the <s>Rathantara</s> in the internal endings?'
(PB 7.6.14) The <s>Bṛhat</s> is the <s>prāṇa</s>; therefore it shares in the external endings, for the <s>prāṇa</s> is external. The <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>apāna</s>; therefore it shares in the internal endings, for the <s>apāna</s> is internal.
(PB 7.6.15) The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are indeed two great trees brought together at the ending.
(PB 7.6.16) When two great trees come together, much lies broken and shattered there.
(PB 7.6.17) The <s>Bṛhat</s> belongs to <s>Aira</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s> belongs to <s>Aiḍa</s>. The <s>Bṛhat</s> is the mind, the <s>Rathantara</s> is speech. The <s>Bṛhat</s> is the <s>Sāman</s> (chant), the <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse). The <s>Bṛhat</s> is the <s>prāṇa</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>apāna</s>. The <s>Bṛhat</s> is that world (yonder), the <s>Rathantara</s> is this world. Having contemplated these with the mind, one should sing the <s>Udgītha</s>; he sings with these two duly arranged.

body.text:
(PB 7.7.1) paśavo vai bṛhadrathantare aṣṭākṣareṇa prathamāyā (?) ṛcaḥ prastauty aṣṭāśaphāṃs tat paśūn avarundhe
(PB 7.7.2) dvyakṣareṇottarayor ṛcoḥ prastauti dvipād yajamāno yajamānam eva yajñe paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 7.7.3) pañcākṣareṇa rathantarasya pratiharati pāṅktāṃs tat paśūn avarundhe
(PB 7.7.4) caturakṣareṇa bṛhataḥ pratiharati catuṣpadas tat paśūn avarundhe
(PB 7.7.5) na vai bṛhan na rathantaram ekaṃ chando 'yacchat tataḥ kakubhāv uttare upādadhus tasmād bṛhatī prathamā kakubhāv uttare tasmād bṛhadrathantare ekarcena kurvanti na hi te ekaṃ chando 'yacchat
(PB 7.7.6) nava bṛhato rohān rohati nava prāṇāḥ prāṇān evāvarundhe
(PB 7.7.7) trīn prathamāyāṃ rohati bhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyat tān evāvarundhe trīn madhyamāyāṃ rohaty ātmānaṃ prajāṃ paś+ūṃs tān evāvarundhe trīn uttamāyāṃ rohati traya ime lokā eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 7.7.8) sarvān kāmān avarundhe ya evaṃv vidvān bṛhato rohān rohati
(PB 7.7.9) vajreṇa vā etat prastotodgātāram abhipravartayati yad rathantaraṃ prastauti samudram antardhāyodgāyed vāg ity ādeyaṃv vāg vai samudraḥ samudram evāntardadhāty ahiṃsāyai
(PB 7.7.10) balavad geyaṃ vajram evaṃ pravṛttaṃ pratyudgṛhṇāti
(PB 7.7.11) balvalā kurvatā geyam abhilobhayateva vajram evābhilobhayati
(PB 7.7.12) kṣipraṃ geyaṃ svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 7.7.13) devaratho vai rathantaram akṣareṇākṣareṇa pratiṣṭhāpayatodgeyam areṇāreṇa hi rathaḥ pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 7.7.14) yo vai devaratham ananvālabhyātiṣṭhaty avāsmāt padyata iyaṃ vai devaratha imām ālabhyodgāyen nāsmād avapadyate
(PB 7.7.15) īśvaraṃ vai rathantaram udgātuś cakṣuḥ pramathitoḥ prastuyamāne saṃmīlet svardṛśaṃ prativīkṣeta nainaṃ cakṣur jahāti
(PB 7.7.16) prajananaṃ vai rathantaraṃ yat tasthuṣa ity āhāsthāyukodgātur vāg bhavaty api prajananaṃ hanty asthuṣa iti vaktavyaṃ susthuṣa iti vā sthāyukodgātur vāg bhavati na prajananam api hanti
(PB 7.7.17) pṛṣṭhāni vā asṛjyanta tair devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs teṣāṃ rathantaraṃ mahimnā nāśaknod utpatat
(PB 7.7.18) tasya vaśiṣṭho mahimno vinidhāya tena stutvā svargaṃl lokam ait tān saṃbhṛtyodgāyet
(PB 7.7.19) yas te goṣu mahimā yas te apsu rathe vā te stanayitnau ya u te yas te agnau mahimā tena saṃbhava rathantara draviṇavan na edhi
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.7.1) Cattle are indeed the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>. He introduces the first verse of the <s>Prastāva</s> with eight syllables — he thus secures eight-hoofed cattle.
(PB 7.7.2) He introduces the latter two verses of the <s>Prastāva</s> with two syllables — the sacrificer is two-footed. He thus establishes the sacrificer in the sacrifice among the cattle.
(PB 7.7.3) He performs the <s>Pratihāra</s> (response) of the <s>Rathantara</s> with five syllables — he thus secures cattle belonging to the group of five.
(PB 7.7.4) He performs the <s>Pratihāra</s> of the <s>Bṛhat</s> with four syllables — he thus secures four-footed cattle.
(PB 7.7.5) Neither the <s>Bṛhat</s> nor the <s>Rathantara</s> yielded a single meter. Therefore they added the <s>Kakubh</s> meters as the latter parts. Therefore <s>Bṛhatī</s> is the first and the <s>Kakubh</s> meters are the latter parts. Therefore the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are performed with single verses, for they did not yield a single meter.
(PB 7.7.6) One ascends nine steps of the <s>Bṛhat</s>. There are nine <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) — he thus secures the <s>prāṇas</s>.
(PB 7.7.7) He ascends three in the first: past, present, future — these he secures. He ascends three in the middle: self, offspring, cattle — these he secures. He ascends three in the last: there are three worlds — he becomes established in these worlds.
(PB 7.7.8) He who, knowing this, ascends the steps of the <s>Bṛhat</s> secures all desires.
(PB 7.7.9) The <s>Prastotṛ</s> (introducing chanter) sets the <s>Udgātṛ</s> in motion with a thunderbolt when he introduces the <s>Rathantara</s>. One should sing the <s>Udgītha</s> interposing the ocean: 'Speech' (<s>vāc</s>) — that is to be inserted. Speech is indeed the ocean. He thus interposes the ocean, for the sake of non-injury.
(PB 7.7.10) One should sing with force — he thus catches the thunderbolt as it is hurled.
(PB 7.7.11) If one sings weakly, he merely plays with the thunderbolt as it were — he plays with the thunderbolt.
(PB 7.7.12) One should sing swiftly, for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 7.7.13) The <s>Rathantara</s> is indeed the chariot of the gods. The <s>Udgītha</s> should be sung establishing it syllable by syllable, for a chariot is established spoke by spoke.
(PB 7.7.14) He who stands on the chariot of the gods without holding on falls from it. This world is indeed the chariot of the gods. Holding on to this world, one should sing the <s>Udgītha</s> — he does not fall from it.
(PB 7.7.15) The <s>Rathantara</s> is liable to destroy the eyesight of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>. When the <s>Prastāva</s> is being sung, he should close his eyes and then look at the sun — his eyesight does not leave him.
(PB 7.7.16) The <s>Rathantara</s> is indeed procreation. When he says 'tasthuṣa' (of one who has stood), the speech of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> becomes stationary; it even destroys procreation. One should say 'asthuṣa' or 'susthuṣa' (of one who has stood well) — the speech of the <s>Udgātṛ</s> becomes steady and does not destroy procreation.
(PB 7.7.17) The <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants were created. With them the gods went to the heavenly world. The <s>Rathantara</s>, because of its greatness, was unable to fly up.
(PB 7.7.18) <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, having set aside its greatness, praised with it and went to the heavenly world. One should sing having gathered them together.
(PB 7.7.19) 'Whatever glory of yours is in the cows, whatever is in the waters, in the chariot, or in your thunder, or whatever glory of yours is in fire — by that come together, O <s>Rathantara</s>, be rich in wealth!'

body.text:
(PB 7.8.1) apo vā ṛtvyam ārcchat tāsāṃv vāyuḥ pṛṣṭhe vyavartata tato vasu vāmaṃ samabhavat tasmin mitrāvaruṇau paryapaśyatāṃ tāv abrūtāṃv vāmaṃ maryā idaṃ deveṣv ājānīti tasmād vāmadevyam
(PB 7.8.2) tat parigṛhṇantāv abrūtām idam avidāvedaṃ nau mābhyartiḍhvam iti tat prajāpatir abravīn mad vā etad dhy ajani mama vā etad iti tad agnir abravīn māṃ (?) vā etad annam ajani mama vā etad iti tad indro 'bravīc chreṣṭhasthā vā etad ahaṃ vaḥ śreṣṭho 'smi mama vā etad iti tad viśve devā abruvann asmaddevatyaṃ vā etad yad adbhyo 'dhi samabhūd asmākaṃ vā etad iti tat prajāpatir abravīt sarveṣāṃ na idam astu sarva idam upajīvāmeti tat pṛṣṭheṣu nyadadhuḥ sarvadevatyaṃ vai vāmadevyam
(PB 7.8.3) yat kavatīṣu tena prājāpatyaṃ ko hi prajāpatir yad aniruktāsu tena prājāpatyam anirukto hi prajāpatiḥ
(PB 7.8.4) yad gāyatrīṣu tenāgneyaṃ gāyatracchandā hy agniḥ
(PB 7.8.5) yat pṛṣṭheṣu nyadadadhus tenaindraṃ sarvāṇi hi pṛṣṭhānīndrasya niṣkevalyāni
(PB 7.8.6) yan maitrāvaruṇo 'nuśaṃsati tena maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 7.8.7) yad bahudevatyam uttamaṃ padaṃ tena vaiśvadevaṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 7.8.8) prajāpatir vā etāṃ gāyatrīṃ yonim apaśyat sa ādīdhītāsmād yoneḥ pṛṣṭhāni sṛjā iti
(PB 7.8.9) sa rathantaram asṛjata tad rathasya ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
(PB 7.8.10) sa bṛhad asṛjata tat stanayitnor ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata sa vairūpam asṛjata tad vā tasya ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
(PB 7.8.11) sa vairūpam asṛjata tad agner ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
(PB 7.8.12) sa śakvarīr asṛjata tad apāṃ ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
(PB 7.8.13) sa revatīr asṛjata tad gavāṃ ghoṣo 'nvasṛjyata
(PB 7.8.14) etair vā etāni saha ghoṣair asṛjyanta
(PB 7.8.15) sarve 'smin ghoṣāḥ sarvāḥ puṇyā vāco vadanti ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.8.1) The waters reached the ritual season. <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) turned upon their back. From that the precious (<s>vāma</s>) thing came into being. <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> perceived it. They said: 'This precious thing is born among the gods, O young men.' Therefore it is called <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
(PB 7.8.2) While grasping it, they said: 'We have found this, we have found this — do not harm us!' Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said: 'This was born from me; this is mine.' Then <s>Agni</s> said: 'This food was born from me; this is mine.' Then <s>Indra</s> said: 'This came from the highest place and I am the highest among you; this is mine.' Then the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) said: 'This is of our godhead, for it arose from the waters; this is ours.' Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said: 'Let this belong to all of us; let us all live upon this.' They placed it among the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants. The <s>Vāmadevya</s> belongs to all the gods.
(PB 7.8.3) Insofar as it is in the <s>ka</s>-verses, thereby it is related to <s>Prajāpati</s>, for <s>ka</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>. Insofar as it is in the undefined verses, thereby it is related to <s>Prajāpati</s>, for <s>Prajāpati</s> is undefined.
(PB 7.8.4) Insofar as it is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, thereby it is related to <s>Agni</s>, for <s>Agni</s> has the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as his meter.
(PB 7.8.5) Insofar as it was placed among the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, thereby it is related to <s>Indra</s>, for all the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants belong exclusively to <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 7.8.6) Insofar as the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest of <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>) recites after it, thereby it is related to <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 7.8.7) Insofar as the last syllable has many deities, thereby it is related to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. He becomes established in all forms.
(PB 7.8.8) <s>Prajāpati</s> perceived this <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the womb. He reflected: 'From this womb I shall create the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants.'
(PB 7.8.9) He created the <s>Rathantara</s>. The sound of the chariot followed after it.
(PB 7.8.10) He created the <s>Bṛhat</s>. The sound of thunder followed after it. He created the <s>Vairūpa</s>. Its characteristic sound followed after it.
(PB 7.8.11) He created the <s>Vairūpa</s>. The sound of fire followed after it.
(PB 7.8.12) He created the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses. The sound of waters followed after them.
(PB 7.8.13) He created the <s>Revatī</s> verses. The sound of cows followed after them.
(PB 7.8.14) These were created together with these sounds.
(PB 7.8.15) All sounds and all auspicious words speak for him who knows this.

body.text:
(PB 7.9.1) pitā vai vāmadevyaṃ putrāḥ pṛṣṭhāni
(PB 7.9.2) etasmād vā etāni yoner asṛjyanta
(PB 7.9.3) tasmāt pṛṣṭhānāṃ stotraṃ vāmadevyenānuṣṭuvanti śāntyai
(PB 7.9.4) yad dhi putro 'śāntaṃ carati pitā tac chamayati
(PB 7.9.5) ayaṃ vai loko madhyamo vāmadevyam etasmād vā imau lokau viṣvañcāv asṛjyetāṃ bṛhac ca ratantaraṃ ca
(PB 7.9.6) yad rathantareṇa stuvanti ye rathantarāḥ paśavo 'ntarīkṣaṃ ta upaśrayanti yad bṛhatā stuvanti ye bārhatāḥ paśavo 'ntarīkṣaṃ ta upaśrayanti te vāmadevyasya stotreṇāvaruddhāḥ
(PB 7.9.7) dhruva āsīno vāmadevyenodgāyet paśūnām upavṛtyai
(PB 7.9.8) upainaṃ paśava āvartante ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.9.9) antarikṣaṃ vai vāmadevyam adhūnvatevodgeyam adhūtam ivāntarikṣaṃ paśavo vai vāmadevyam ahiṃsatevodgeyaṃ paśūnām ahiṃsāyai
(PB 7.9.10) katham iva vāmadevyaṃ geyam ity āhuḥ
(PB 7.9.11) yathāṅkulī putrān saṃdaśyāsaṃbhindantī harati yathā vāto 'psu śanair vāti
(PB 7.9.12) svadhūr vāmadevyaṃ geyam
(PB 7.9.13) yo vai svadhūr vāmadevyaṃ gāyati svadhūr bhavati
(PB 7.9.14) yāty asyānyo niyānena nānyasya niyānena yāti
(PB 7.9.15) na bṛhato na rathantarasyānurūpaṃ geyaṃ svenaivāyatanena geyam āyatanavān bhavati
(PB 7.9.16) devā vai paśūn vyabhajanta te rudram antarāyaṃs tān vāmadevyasya stotra upekṣate
(PB 7.9.17) aniruktaṃ geyam
(PB 7.9.18) yan nirāha rudrāya paśūn apidadhāti rudras tāṃ samāṃ paśūn dhātuko bhavati
(PB 7.9.19) revatīṣu vāmadevyena paśukāmaḥ stuvīta
(PB 7.9.20) āpo vai revatyaḥ paśavo vāmadevyam adbhya evāsmai paśūn prajanayati
(PB 7.9.21) anavartiḥ paśuto bhavati prajā svasya mīliteva bhavati
(PB 7.9.22) kavatībhyo hy eti prajāpateḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.9.1) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> (Sāman) is the father; the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (Sāmans) are the sons.
(PB 7.9.2) From this womb they were created.
(PB 7.9.3) Therefore they accompany the <s>stotra</s> (praise) of the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> — for pacification.
(PB 7.9.4) For when a son acts without peace, the father pacifies him.
(PB 7.9.5) This middle world is the <s>Vāmadevya</s>. From it these two worlds were created in opposite directions — the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 7.9.6) When they praise with the <s>Rathantara</s>, the cattle that belong to the <s>Rathantara</s> take refuge in the atmosphere. When they praise with the <s>Bṛhat</s>, the cattle that belong to the <s>Bṛhat</s> take refuge in the atmosphere. They are held back by the praise of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
(PB 7.9.7) Sitting firmly, one should chant the <s>Udgītha</s> with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> — for the turning of cattle toward oneself.
(PB 7.9.8) Cattle turn toward one who knows thus.
(PB 7.9.9) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is the atmosphere. It should be chanted without shaking — for the atmosphere is as if unshaken. The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is cattle. It should be chanted without harm — for non-injury to cattle.
(PB 7.9.10) 'How should the <s>Vāmadevya</s> be sung?' they ask.
(PB 7.9.11) As a mother-bird carries her young by grasping them in her beak without piercing them; as the wind blows gently on the waters.
(PB 7.9.12) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> should be sung smoothly.
(PB 7.9.13) He who sings the <s>Vāmadevya</s> smoothly becomes smooth.
(PB 7.9.14) Others travel by his path; he does not travel by the path of another.
(PB 7.9.15) It should not be sung in the manner of the <s>Bṛhat</s> nor of the <s>Rathantara</s>. It should be sung in its own seat. He becomes one who has a seat.
(PB 7.9.16) The gods divided the cattle. They left out <s>Rudra</s>. He looks upon them during the <s>stotra</s> of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
(PB 7.9.17) It should be sung without distinct utterance.
(PB 7.9.18) If one utters distinctly, one delivers the cattle to <s>Rudra</s>. <s>Rudra</s> becomes the destroyer of cattle in that year.
(PB 7.9.19) One desiring cattle should praise with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> on <s>Revatī</s> verses.
(PB 7.9.20) The waters are the <s>Revatīs</s>. The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is cattle. From the waters he generates cattle for him.
(PB 7.9.21) He does not lose his cattle. His offspring become as if flourishing.
(PB 7.9.22) For he goes forth from the <s>Kavatī</s> verses of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

body.text:
(PB 7.10.1) imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau viyantāv abrūtāṃv vivāhaṃv vivahāvahai saha nāv astv iti
(PB 7.10.2) tayor ayam amuṣmai śyaitaṃ prāyacchan naudhasam asāv asmai
(PB 7.10.3) tata enayor nidhane viparyakrāmatāṃ devavivāho vai śyaitanaudhase
(PB 7.10.4) pravasīyāṃsaṃ vivāham āpnoti ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.10.5) ito vā ime lokā ūrdhvāḥ kalpamānā yanty amuto 'rvāñcaḥ kalpamānā āyanti
(PB 7.10.6) yad rathantareṇa stuvantīmaṃl lokaṃ tena yunakty antarikṣaṃv vāmadevyena naudhasenāmuṃ yad bṛhatā stuvanty amuṃl lokaṃ tena yanakty antarikṣaṃv vāmadevyena śyaitenemam
(PB 7.10.7) kḷptān imāl lokān upāste ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.10.8) bṛhadrathantare vai śaitanaudhase yad rathantarāya naudhasaṃ prati prayuñjanti bṛhad evāsmai tat prati prayuñjanti bṛhad dhy etat paro'kṣaṃ yan naudhasaṃ yad bṛhate śyaitaṃ prati prayuñjanti rathantaram evāsmai tat prati prayuñjanti rathantaraṃ hy etat paro'kṣaṃ yac chyaitam
(PB 7.10.9) ubhabhyāṃ bṛhadrathantarābhyāṃ stute ya evaṃv veda
(PB 7.10.10) devā vai brahma vyabhajanta tāṃ nodhāḥ kākṣīvata āgacchat te 'bruvann ṛṣir na āgaṃs tasmai brahma dadāmeti tasmā etat sāma prāyacchaṃs tasmān naudhasaṃ brahma vai naudhasam
(PB 7.10.11) brahmavarcasakāma etena stuvīta brahmavarcasī bhavati
(PB 7.10.12) athaitac chyaitam
(PB 7.10.13) prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tān etena sāmnābhivyāharat te 'smā atiṣṭhanta te śetyā abhavan yac chetyā abhavaṃs tasmāc chyaitaṃ paśavo vai śyaitam
(PB 7.10.14) paśukāma etena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
(PB 7.10.15) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā aśocaṃs tāḥ śyaitena huṃmā ity abhyajighrat tato vai tāḥ samaidhanta samedhante tāṃ samāṃ prajā yatraivaṃ vidvāñ chyaitenodgāyati
(PB 7.10.16) eṣa vai yajamānasya prajāpatir yad udgātā yac chyaitena hiṅ karoti prajāpatir eva bhūtvā prajā abhijihgrati
(PB 7.10.17) vasunidhanaṃ bhavati paśavo vai vasu paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 7.10.1) These two worlds were together. As they were separating, they said: 'Let us have a wedding; let us marry; let us be together.'
(PB 7.10.2) This world gave the <s>Śyaita</s> (Sāman) to that world as a wedding gift; that world gave the <s>Naudhasa</s> to this world.
(PB 7.10.3) Then their <s>nidhanas</s> (final syllables) were exchanged. The <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Naudhasa</s> are indeed the divine wedding.
(PB 7.10.4) One who knows thus obtains an excellent wedding.
(PB 7.10.5) From here these worlds go upward as they are being arranged; from there they come hither as they are being arranged.
(PB 7.10.6) When they praise with the <s>Rathantara</s>, they yoke this world by it; the atmosphere by the <s>Vāmadevya</s>; that world by the <s>Naudhasa</s>. When they praise with the <s>Bṛhat</s>, they yoke that world by it; the atmosphere by the <s>Vāmadevya</s>; this world by the <s>Śyaita</s>.
(PB 7.10.7) One who knows thus dwells in worlds that are arranged.
(PB 7.10.8) The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are indeed the <s>Śyaita</s> and <s>Naudhasa</s>. When they employ the <s>Naudhasa</s> as the counterpart of the <s>Rathantara</s>, they employ the <s>Bṛhat</s> for him, for the <s>Naudhasa</s> is the <s>Bṛhat</s> in a hidden form. When they employ the <s>Śyaita</s> as the counterpart of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, they employ the <s>Rathantara</s> for him, for the <s>Śyaita</s> is the <s>Rathantara</s> in a hidden form.
(PB 7.10.9) One who knows thus is praised with both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 7.10.10) The gods divided the sacred knowledge. <s>Nodhas</s> the son of <s>Kakṣīvat</s> came to them. They said: 'A seer has come to us; let us give him the sacred knowledge.' They gave him this <s>Sāman</s>. Therefore it is the <s>Naudhasa</s>. The <s>Naudhasa</s> is indeed sacred knowledge.
(PB 7.10.11) One desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge should praise with this. He becomes endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge.
(PB 7.10.12) Now this is the <s>Śyaita</s>.
(PB 7.10.13) <s>Prajāpati</s> created the cattle. Having been created, they ran away from him. He addressed them with this <s>Sāman</s>. They stood still for him. They became resting. Because they became resting, it is the <s>Śyaita</s>. The <s>Śyaita</s> is indeed cattle.
(PB 7.10.14) One desiring cattle should praise with this. He becomes possessed of cattle.
(PB 7.10.15) <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. Having been created, they grieved. He sniffed them with the <s>Śyaita</s> saying 'huṃmā.' Then they thrived. Offspring thrive in that year in which one who knows thus chants with the <s>Śyaita</s>.
(PB 7.10.16) The <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest) is this <s>Prajāpati</s> of the sacrificer. When he makes the <s>hiṅkāra</s> with the <s>Śyaita</s>, becoming <s>Prajāpati</s> he sniffs the offspring.
(PB 7.10.17) It has <s>vasu</s> (wealth) as its <s>nidhana</s> (conclusion). Cattle are wealth. He becomes established among cattle.

body.text:
(PB 8.1.1) āṣkāraṇidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃv vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanam abhicaraṇīyasya brahmasāma kuryād abhinidhanaṃ mādhyandine pavamāne
(PB 8.1.2) deveṣur vā eṣā yad vaṣatkāro 'bhīti vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharad abhītyevāsmai vajraṃ prahṛtya deveṣv ā vaṣaṭkāreṇa vidhyati
(PB 8.1.3) traikakubhaṃ paśukāmāya brahmasāma kuryāt tvam aṅga praśaṃsiṣa ity etāsu
(PB 8.1.4) indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat teṣāṃ traya udaśiṣyanta rāyovājo bṛhadgiriḥ pṛthuraśmis te 'bruvan ko naḥ putrān bhariṣyantīty aham intīndro 'bravīt tāṃs trikakub adhinidhāyācarat sa etat sāmāpaśyad yat trikakub apaśyat tasmāt traikakubham
(PB 8.1.5) sa ātmānam eva punar upādhāvat tvam aṅga praśaṃsiṣo devaḥ śaviṣṭha martyaṃ na tvad anyo maghavann asti ca marḍitendra bravīmi te vaca iti sa etena ca pragāthenaitena sāmnā sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata tān ebhyaḥ prāyacchat te pratyatiṣṭhan
(PB 8.1.6) yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syād yah pratiṣṭhākāma etasmin pragātha etena sāmnā stuvīta pra sahasraṃ paśūn āpnoti pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 8.1.7) trivīryaṃ vā etat sāma trīndriyam aindrya ṛca aindraṃ sāmaindreti nidhanam indriya eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 8.1.8) traiśokaṃ jyogāmayāvine brahmasāma kuryāt
(PB 8.1.9) ime vai lokāḥ sahāsaṃs te 'śocantaṃs teṣām indra etena sāmnā śucam apāhan yat trayāṇāṃ śocatām apāhaṃs tasmāt traiśokam
(PB 8.1.10) yāsmād apāhan sā puṃścalīṃ prāviśad yām antarikṣāt sā klībaṃ yām amuṣmāt sainasvinam
(PB 8.1.11) tasmāt teṣāṃ nāśaitavyā ya eṣām āśāmeti tasmā eva śuco 'pabhajate
(PB 8.1.12) śucā vā eṣa viddho yasya jyog āmayati yat traiśokaṃ brahmasāma bhavati śucam evāsmād apahanti
(PB 8.1.13) diveti nidhanam upayanti vyuṣṭir vai divā vy evāsmai vāsayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.1.1) One should make the <s>Kāṇva</s> (Sāman) with an <s>āṣkāra</s> ending and a <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> ending as the <s>Brahmasāman</s> for one practicing sorcery, with a combined ending in the midday <s>Pavamāna</s>.
(PB 8.1.2) The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is the gods' missile. With 'attack!' <s>Indra</s> hurled the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) at <s>Vṛtra</s>. Having hurled the <s>vajra</s> at him with 'attack!', he strikes him with the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> among the gods.
(PB 8.1.3) One should make the <s>Traikakubha</s> (Sāman) the <s>Brahmasāman</s> for one desiring cattle, with the verses beginning 'You indeed, O praised one.'
(PB 8.1.4) <s>Indra</s> gave the <s>Yatis</s> (ascetics) to the wolves. Three of them survived: <s>Rāyovāja</s>, <s>Bṛhadgiri</s>, and <s>Pṛthuraśmi</s>. They said: 'Who will maintain our sons?' 'I will,' said <s>Indra</s>. He went about having placed them on the <s>Trikakubh</s>. He perceived this <s>Sāman</s>. Because he perceived the <s>Trikakubh</s>, therefore it is the <s>Traikakubha</s>.
(PB 8.1.5) He ran back to himself: 'You indeed, O praised one, O most powerful god, protect this mortal; there is none other than you, O bountiful one, who gives comfort, O <s>Indra</s> — I speak this word to you.' With this <s>pragātha</s> and this <s>Sāman</s> he created a thousand cattle and gave them to these. They became established.
(PB 8.1.6) One who desires cattle or who desires an establishment should praise on this <s>pragātha</s> with this <s>Sāman</s>. He obtains a thousand cattle and becomes established.
(PB 8.1.7) This <s>Sāman</s> has triple vigor and triple vital power — the <s>Ṛc</s> belongs to <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Sāman</s> belongs to <s>Indra</s>, the <s>nidhana</s> says 'Indra' — he becomes established in vital power and vigor.
(PB 8.1.8) One should make the <s>Traiśoka</s> (Sāman) the <s>Brahmasāman</s> for one who has been long ill.
(PB 8.1.9) These worlds were together. They grieved. <s>Indra</s> struck away their grief with this <s>Sāman</s>. Because he struck away the grief of the three who grieved, therefore it is the <s>Traiśoka</s>.
(PB 8.1.10) The grief that he struck away from this world entered a loose woman; that from the atmosphere entered a eunuch; that from yonder world entered a sinner.
(PB 8.1.11) Therefore one should not associate with these. Whoever associates with them — that grief attaches itself to him.
(PB 8.1.12) One who has been ill for a long time is indeed pierced by grief. When the <s>Traiśoka</s> becomes the <s>Brahmasāman</s>, it strikes away grief from him.
(PB 8.1.13) They approach with '<s>div</s>' (heaven) as the <s>nidhana</s>. Dawn is '<s>divā</s>' (day). It causes the dawning of light for him.

(PB 8.2.5) ātharvaṇaṃ lokakāmāya brahmasāma kuryāt
(PB 8.2.6) atharvāṇo vā etal lokākāmāḥ sāmāpaśyaṃs tenāmartyaṃl lokam apaśyan yad etat sāma bhavati svargasya lokasya prajātyai
(PB 8.2.7) abhīvartaṃ bhrātṛvyavate brahmasāma kuryāt
(PB 8.2.8) abhīvartena vai devā asurān abhyavartanta yad abhīvarto brahmasāma bhavati bhrātṛvyasyābhivṛtyai
(PB 8.2.9) śrāyantīyaṃ yajñavibhraṣṭāya brahmasāma kuryāt
(PB 8.2.10) prajāpatir uṣasam adhyait svāṃ duhitaraṃ tasya retaḥ parāpatat tad asyāṃ nyaṣicyata tad aśrīṇād idaṃ me mā duṣad iti tat sad akarot paśūn eva
(PB 8.2.11) yac chrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma bhavati śrīṇāti caivenaṃ sac ca karoti
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.2.1) For one desiring firm establishment, one should make the <s>Kāṇva</s> [chant] with the <s>āṣkāraṇi</s> ending the <s>Brahma</s> <s>sāman</s> (chant).
(PB 8.2.2) <s>Kaṇva</s> indeed perceived this <s>sāman</s> in its ending but did not attain firm establishment. He heard the sneeze of <s>Vṛṣadaṃśa</s> saying 'āṣ!' He then perceived that very ending. Thereby he attained firm establishment. This <s>sāman</s> exists for the sake of firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 8.3.1) devāś ca vā asurāś caiṣu lokeṣv aspardhanta te devāḥ prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etat sāma prāyacchad etenainān kālayiṣyaddham iti tenainān ebhyo lokebhyo 'kālayanta yad akālayanta tasmāt kāleyam
(PB 8.3.2) ebhyo vai lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ kālayate ya evaṃv veda
(PB 8.3.3) stomo vai deveṣu taro nāmāsīd yajño 'sureṣu vidadvasus te devās tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti stomena yajñam asurāṇām āvṛñjata
(PB 8.3.4) stomena yajñaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
(PB 8.3.5) sāhdyā vai nāma devā āsaṃs te 'vacchidya tṛtīyasavanaṃ mādhyandinena savanena saha svargaṃl lokam āyaṃs tad devāḥ lokeyena samatanvan yat kāleyaṃ bhavati tṛtīyasavanasya saṃtatyai
(PB 8.3.6) vidadvasu vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ yat tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti prastauti tṛtīyasavanam eva tad abhyativadati
(PB 8.3.7) sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇi kāleyaṃ yat padaprastāvaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ yad bṛhato rohān rohati tena bārhataṃ yat stobhavān pratihāras tena bārhataṃ yad dravadiḍaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.3.1) The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> competed in these worlds. The gods ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. He gave them this <s>sāman</s>: 'By this you shall drive them away.' With it they drove them from these worlds. Because they drove them away (<s>akālayanta</s>), therefore it is called <s>Kāleya</s>.
(PB 8.3.2) He who knows thus drives away the rival from these worlds.
(PB 8.3.3) The <s>stoma</s> (chant pattern) is indeed among the gods,

(PB 8.4.2) te triṣṭub jagatyai gāyatrīm abrūtām upa tvāyāveti sābravīt kiṃ me tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayasa ity abrūtāṃ sābvravīn mama sarvaṃ prātaḥsavanam aham uttare savane praṇayānīti tasmād gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ gāyatry uttare savane praṇayati

(PB 8.4.6) svādiṣṭhā vai deveṣu paśava āsan madiṣṭhā asureṣu te devāḥ svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayeti paśūn asurāṇām avṛñjata

(PB 8.4.11) sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇi saṃhitaṃ yat padaprastāvaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ yad bṛhato rohān rohati tena bārhataṃ yad padanidhanaṃ tena rāthantaraṃ sarveṣv eva rūpeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: (PB 8.4.1) There were gods called the <s>Sādhyas</s>. They went to the heavenly world together with the entire sacrifice. The gods said to the meters: 'Bring <s>Soma</s>!' They sent <s>Jagatī</s> (meter). She came back having lost three syllables, becoming a one-syllable meter. They sent <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. She came back having lost one syllable, becoming a three-syllable meter. They sent <s>Gāyatrī</s>. She has indeed four syllables.

(PB 8.5.1) uṣṇikkakubhāv ete bhavataḥ

(PB 8.5.12) athaitad āndhīgavam andhīgur vā etat paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai madhye nidhanam aiḍaṃ bhavaty etena vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ yan madhye nidhanam aiḍaṃ na syād apratiṣṭhitaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ syāt

body.translated_text:
(PB 8.5.1) These two are the <s>Uṣṇih</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> (meters).
(PB 8.5.2) With the <s>Uṣṇih</s> and <s>Kakubh</s>, <s>Indra</s> hurled the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) at <s>Vṛtra</s>. He struck with the <s>Kakubh</s> while striding forth, and struck with the <s>Uṣṇih</s>. Therefore the middle foot of the <s>Kakubh</s> has the most syllables, for that is the stride. He struck it down. Therefore the last foot of the <s>Uṣṇih</s> has the most syllables, for the thunderbolt is heavy at the front.

body.translated_text:

(PB 8.6.3) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is indeed the womb. From this womb <s>Prajāpati</s> created the sacrifice. Therefore the sacrifice
