body.translated_text:
(PB 8.7.1) From here, in the morning, the meters are yoked upward; from there they are yoked downward in the <s>stotra</s> (chant) of the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>. 'For you, O <s>Agni</s>, [we offer] sacrifices and songs of praise' — this has twelve syllables. 'We [praise] the immortal <s>Jātavedas</s>' — this has eleven syllables. 'As a dear friend, I would proclaim' — this has eight syllables.
(PB 8.7.2) One brings it to completion as the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (meter) at the end. This is indeed the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; in this

body.text:
(PB 8.8.1) devā vā agniṣṭomam abhijityokthāni nāśaknuvann abhijetuṃ te 'gnim abruvaṃs tvayā mukhenedaṃ cayāmeti so 'bravīt kiṃ me tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayasa ity abruvan so 'bravīn maddevatyāsūkthāni praṇayān iti
(PB 8.8.2) tasmād āgneyīṣūkthāni praṇayanti
(PB 8.8.3) tasmād u gāyatrīṣu gāyatracchandā hy agniḥ
(PB 8.8.4) te 'gniṃ mukhaṃ kṛtvā sākam aśvenābhyakrāman yat sākam aśvenābhyakrāmaṃs tasmāt sākamaśvam
(PB 8.8.5) tasmāt sākamaśvenokthāni praṇayanty etena hi tāny agre 'bhyajayan
(PB 8.8.6) sa indro 'bravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti varuṇas taṃv varuṇo 'nvatiṣṭhad indra āharat tasmād aindrāvaruṇam anuśasyate
(PB 8.8.7) sa evābravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti bṛhaspatis taṃ bṛhaspatir anvatiṣṭad indra āharat tasmād aindrābārhaspatyam anuśasyate sa evābravīt kaś cāhaṃ cedam anvavaiṣyāva ity ahaṃ ceti viṣṇus taṃ viṣṇur anvatiṣṭad indra āharat tasmād aindrāvaiṣṇavam anuśasyate
(PB 8.8.8) paśūn vā ebhyas tān āharat paśavo vā ukthāni paśukāma ukthena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
(PB 8.8.9) bṛhatā vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tasya tejaḥ parāpatat tat saubharam abhavat
(PB 8.8.10) jāmi vā etad yajñe kriyata ity āhur yad rathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ rathantaraṃ saṃdhir nāntarā bṛhatā stuvantīti yat saubhareṇa stuvanti bṛhataiva tad antarā stuvanti bṛhato hy etat tejo yat saubharam
(PB 8.8.11) yadi bṛhat sāmātirātraḥ syāt saubharam ukthānāṃ brahma sāma kāryaṃ bṛhad eva tat tejasā samardhayati
(PB 8.8.12) yadi rathantarasāmnā saubharaṃ kuryād ajāmitāyai
(PB 8.8.13) devānāṃ vai svargaṃl lokaṃ +yatāṃ diśo 'vlīyanta tāḥ saubhareṇo ity udastaṃbhuvaṃs tato vai tā adṛṃhanta tataḥ pratyatiṣṭhaṃs tataḥ svargaṃl lokaṃ prājānan yaḥ svargakāmaḥ syād yaḥ pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ saubhareṇa stuvīta pra svargaṃl lokaṃ jānāti pratitṣṭhati
(PB 8.8.14) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭā āśanāyaṃs tābhyaḥ saubhareṇorg ity annaṃ prāyacchat tato vai tāḥ samaidhanta
(PB 8.8.15) samedhante tāṃ samāṃ prajā yatraivaṃv vidvān saubhareṇodgāyati
(PB 8.8.16) tā abruvan subhṛtaṃ no 'bhārṣīr iti tasmāt saubharam
(PB 8.8.17) vṛṣṭiṃ vā abhyastāṃ prāyacchad annam eva
(PB 8.8.18) yo vṛṣṭikāmaḥ syād yo 'nnādyakāmo yaḥ svargakāmaḥ saubhareṇa stuvīta
(PB 8.8.19) hīṣiti vṛṣṭikāmāya nidhanaṃ kuryād ūrg ity annādyakāmāyo iti svargakāmāya
(PB 8.8.20) sarve vai kāmāḥ saubharaṃ sarveṣv eva kāmeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 8.8.21) athaitan nārmedham
(PB 8.8.22) nṛmedhasam āṅgirasaṃ sattram āsīnaṃ śvabhir abhyāhvayan so 'gnim upādhāvat pāhi no agna ekayeti taṃv vaiśvānaraḥ paryudatiṣṭhat tato vai sa pratyatiṣṭhat tato gātum avindata
(PB 8.8.23) gātuvid vā etat sāma vindate gātuṃ pratitiṣṭhaty etena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 8.8.24) naiva hy etad ahno rūpaṃ na rātrer yad ukthānām
(PB 8.8.25) kakup prathamāthoṣṇig atha purauṣṇig anuṣṭup tenānuṣṭubho nayanty acchāvākasāmnaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.8.1) The <s>devas</s> conquered the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> but were unable to conquer the <s>ukthas</s> (recitations). They said to <s>Agni</s>: 'With you as our mouth, let us conquer this.' He said: 'What would be mine from that?' 'Whatever you desire,' they said. He said: 'Let the <s>ukthas</s> be led forth in hymns addressed to me as deity.'
(PB 8.8.2) Therefore the <s>ukthas</s> are led forth in <s>Āgneya</s> (Agni-directed) verses.
(PB 8.8.3) Therefore in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for <s>Agni</s> belongs to the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter.
(PB 8.8.4) Making <s>Agni</s> their front, they advanced together with the horse. Because they advanced together with the horse, it is called <s>Sākamaśva</s> (together-with-horse).
(PB 8.8.5) Therefore the <s>ukthas</s> are led forth with the <s>Sākamaśva</s> chant, for with it they originally conquered them.
(PB 8.8.6) <s>Indra</s> said: 'Who together with me will go after this?' 'I,' said <s>Varuṇa</s>. <s>Varuṇa</s> supported him, <s>Indra</s> conquered. Therefore the <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s> recitation is recited.
(PB 8.8.7) He said again: 'Who together with me will go after this?' 'I,' said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> supported him, <s>Indra</s> conquered. Therefore the <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s> recitation is recited. He said again: 'Who together with me will go after this?' 'I,' said <s>Viṣṇu</s>. <s>Viṣṇu</s> supported him, <s>Indra</s> conquered. Therefore the <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s> recitation is recited.
(PB 8.8.8) He conquered cattle for them. Cattle are indeed the <s>ukthas</s>. He who desires cattle should praise with the <s>uktha</s>; he becomes rich in cattle.
(PB 8.8.9) With the <s>Bṛhat</s> (chant), <s>Indra</s> hurled his thunderbolt at <s>Vṛtra</s>. Its brilliance flew forth and became the <s>Saubhara</s> (chant).
(PB 8.8.10) 'A blemish of sameness (<s>jāmi</s>) is created in the sacrifice,' they say, 'when the <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) and the <s>Rathantara</s> is the junction, and one does not praise with the <s>Bṛhat</s> in between.' When they praise with the <s>Saubhara</s>, they indeed praise with the <s>Bṛhat</s> in between, for the <s>Saubhara</s> is the brilliance of the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 8.8.11) If the <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite) has the <s>Bṛhat Sāman</s>, the <s>Saubhara</s> should be made the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> of the <s>ukthas</s>; thereby one strengthens the <s>Bṛhat</s> with its own brilliance.
(PB 8.8.12) If one uses the <s>Saubhara</s> with the <s>Rathantara Sāman</s>, it is for avoiding sameness.
(PB 8.8.13) When the <s>devas</s> were going to the heavenly world, the directions collapsed. With the <s>Saubhara</s>, saying 'Rise!', they propped them up. From that they became firm, from that they stood firm, from that they knew the heavenly world. He who desires heaven, he who desires firm standing, should praise with the <s>Saubhara</s>; he knows the heavenly world and stands firm.
(PB 8.8.14) <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Once created, they hungered. With the <s>Saubhara</s>, saying 'Vigor!', he gave them food. From that they thrived.
(PB 8.8.15) The creatures thrive in that year where one who knows thus chants the <s>Saubhara</s>.
(PB 8.8.16) They said: 'You have carried well for us (<s>subhṛtam</s>).' Therefore it is called <s>Saubhara</s>.
(PB 8.8.17) He gave them rain as food.
(PB 8.8.18) He who desires rain, he who desires food, he who desires heaven should praise with the <s>Saubhara</s>.
(PB 8.8.19) The ending should be <s>hīṣ</s> for one desiring rain, <s>ūrk</s> for one desiring food, and <s>u</s> for one desiring heaven.
(PB 8.8.20) All desires are the <s>Saubhara</s>; one is established in all desires.
(PB 8.8.21) Now the <s>Nārmedha</s> (chant).
(PB 8.8.22) <s>Nṛmedhas</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, seated in a <s>sattra</s>, was challenged by dogs. He ran to <s>Agni</s>: 'Protect us, O <s>Agni</s>, with this single one.' <s>Vaiśvānara</s> stood around him. From that he stood firm, from that he found a way.
(PB 8.8.23) This <s>sāman</s> is indeed a way-finder (<s>gātuvid</s>). He who praises with it finds a way and stands firm.
(PB 8.8.24) For the <s>ukthas</s> belong neither to the form of day nor of night.
(PB 8.8.25) First <s>Kakubh</s>, then <s>Uṣṇih</s>, then <s>Purauṣṇih</s>, then <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> they lead from the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>.

body.text:
(PB 8.9.1) hārivarṇaṃ bhavati
(PB 8.9.2) asurā vā eṣu lokeṣv āsaṃs tān devā hariśriyam ity asmāl lokāt prāṇudanta virājasīty antarikṣād divo-diva ity amuṣmāt
(PB 8.9.3) tad ya evaṃ vedaibhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ praṇudyemāṃl lokān abhyārohati
(PB 8.9.4) harivarṇo vā etat paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭaiḥ
(PB 8.9.5) aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃl lokaṃ yato rakṣāṃsy anvasacanta tāny etena harivarṇo 'pāhanta yad etat sāma bhavati rakṣasām apahatyai
(PB 8.9.6) pṛṣṭhāni vā asṛjyanta teṣāṃ yat tejo raso 'tyaricyata tad devāḥ samabharaṃs tad udvaṃśīyam abhavat
(PB 8.9.7) sarveṣāṃ vā etat pṛṣṭhānāṃ tejo yad udvaṃśīyaṃ tasmād vā etat purā sajātāya nākran pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtyai
(PB 8.9.8) eṣa hy eva pṛṣṭhais tuṣṭuvāno ya udvaṃśīyena stuvate
(PB 8.9.9) sarvāṇi vai rūpāṇy udvaṃśīyam
(PB 8.9.10) gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇa eti rathantarasya rūpam eti hi rathantaram
(PB 8.9.11) ādir bṛhata ūrdhvam iva hi bṛhat
(PB 8.9.12) pariṣṭobho vairūpasya pariṣṭubhaṃ hi vairūpam
(PB 8.9.13) anutodo vairājasyānutunnaṃ hi vairājam
(PB 8.9.14) ardheḍā śakvarīṇām atisvāro revatīnām
(PB 8.9.15) ardheḍayā vai devā asurān avahatyātisvāreṇa svargaṃl lokam ārohan
(PB 8.9.16) tad ya evaṃv vedārdheḍayaiva bhrātṛvyam avahatyātisvāreṇa svargaṃl lokam ārohati
(PB 8.9.17) ardheḍayā vai pūrvaṃ yajñaṃ saṃsthāpayanty atisvāreṇottram ārabhante
(PB 8.9.18) upainam uttaro yajño namati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 8.9.19) pāṅktaṃ vā etat sāma pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavo yajña eva paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 8.9.20) āṣṭādaṃṣṭre ṛddhikāmāya kuryāt
(PB 8.9.21) aṣṭādaṃṣṭro vairūpo 'putro 'prajā ajīryat sa imāṃl lokān vicicchidvāṃ amanyata sa ete jarasi sāmanī apaśyat tayor aprayogād abibhet so 'bravīd ṛdhnavad yobhe sāmabhyāṃ stavatā iti
(PB 8.9.22) ṛṣer vā etat prāśodbhūtaṃ yad aṣṭādaṃṣṭre bhavata ṛdhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.9.1) The <s>Hārivarṇa</s> (chant) is used.
(PB 8.9.2) The <s>Asuras</s> were in these worlds. The <s>devas</s> drove them out from this world with '<s>Hariśrī</s>' (golden splendor), from the atmosphere with '<s>Virāj</s>' (sovereign meter), and from yonder world with '<s>Divo-diva</s>' (day upon day).
(PB 8.9.3) He who knows thus drives the rival from these worlds and ascends these worlds.
(PB 8.9.4) <s>Harivarṇa</s>, desiring cattle, beheld this <s>sāman</s>. With it he created a thousand cattle. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, it is for the flourishing of cattle.
(PB 8.9.5) When the <s>Āṅgirasas</s> were going to the heavenly world, demons pursued them. <s>Harivarṇa</s> drove them away with this. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, it is for driving away demons.
(PB 8.9.6) When the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants) were created, whatever brilliance and essence was surplus, the <s>devas</s> gathered together — that became the <s>Udvaṃśīya</s>.
(PB 8.9.7) The <s>Udvaṃśīya</s> is the brilliance of all the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants. Therefore formerly it was not performed for a fellow clansman, for the restraint of the worst.
(PB 8.9.8) He who praises with the <s>Udvaṃśīya</s> has indeed praised with all the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants.
(PB 8.9.9) The <s>Udvaṃśīya</s> is indeed all forms.
(PB 8.9.10) 'The <s>Gāyatrī</s> singers sing you' — this is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for the <s>Rathantara</s> goes thus.
(PB 8.9.11) The beginning is of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for the <s>Bṛhat</s> goes upward.
(PB 8.9.12) The encircling <s>stobha</s> is of the <s>Vairūpa</s>, for the <s>Vairūpa</s> has the encircling <s>stobha</s>.
(PB 8.9.13) The piercing is of the <s>Vairāja</s>, for the <s>Vairāja</s> is pierced.
(PB 8.9.14) The half-<s>iḍā</s> is of the <s>Śakvarīs</s>; the over-sounding is of the <s>Revatīs</s>.
(PB 8.9.15) With the half-<s>iḍā</s> the <s>devas</s> defeated the <s>Asuras</s>; with the over-sounding they ascended the heavenly world.
(PB 8.9.16) He who knows thus defeats the rival with the half-<s>iḍā</s> and ascends the heavenly world with the over-sounding.
(PB 8.9.17) With the half-<s>iḍā</s> they first complete the sacrifice; with the over-sounding they begin the next one.
(PB 8.9.18) The next sacrifice bows to him who knows thus.
(PB 8.9.19) This <s>sāman</s> is five-fold (<s>pāṅkta</s>). The sacrifice is five-fold. Cattle are five-fold. One is established in the sacrifice and in cattle.
(PB 8.9.20) The <s>Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra</s> should be performed for one desiring prosperity.
(PB 8.9.21) <s>Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra Vairūpa</s>, without sons and without offspring, was growing old. He thought he had destroyed these worlds. In old age he beheld these two <s>sāmans</s>. He feared their non-employment. He said: 'Let one prosper — let them praise with both <s>sāmans</s>.'
(PB 8.9.22) This <s>Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra</s> arose from the inspiration of the <s>ṛṣi</s>; it is indeed for prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 8.10.1) gāyatrīṣu brahmavarcasakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur gāyatryāṃ brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā gāyatrī saṃpadyate
(PB 8.10.2) tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
(PB 8.10.3) gāyatrīṣu paśukāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣoṣṇik saṃpadyate
(PB 8.10.4) paśavo vā uṣṇik paśūn evāvarundhe
(PB 8.10.5) gāyatrīṣu puruṣakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyuḥ kakubhi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā kakup saṃpadyate
(PB 8.10.6) puruṣo vai kakup puruṣān evāvarundhe
(PB 8.10.7) virāṭsv annādyakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣā virāṭ saṃpadyate
(PB 8.10.8) annaṃ virāḍ annādyam evāvarundhe
(PB 8.10.9) akṣarapaṅktiṣu jyaiṣṭhyakāmāyokthāni praṇayeyur uṣṇihi brahmasāmānuṣṭubhy acchāvākasāma saiṣānuṣṭup saṃpadyate
(PB 8.10.10) jyaiṣṭhyaṃ vā anuṣṭub jyaiṣṭhyam avāvarundhe
body.translated_text:
(PB 8.10.1) For one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance), the <s>ukthas</s> should be led forth in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses — with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>. This is the <s>Gāyatrī</s> completion.
(PB 8.10.2) Brilliance and <s>brahmavarcas</s> belong to the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; one obtains brilliance and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.
(PB 8.10.3) For one desiring cattle, the <s>ukthas</s> should be led forth in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses — with the <s>Uṣṇih</s>, the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>. This is the <s>Uṣṇih</s> completion.
(PB 8.10.4) Cattle belong to the <s>Uṣṇih</s>; one obtains cattle.
(PB 8.10.5) For one desiring people, the <s>ukthas</s> should be led forth in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses — with the <s>Kakubh</s>, the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>. This is the <s>Kakubh</s> completion.
(PB 8.10.6) People belong to the <s>Kakubh</s>; one obtains people.
(PB 8.10.7) For one desiring food, the <s>ukthas</s> should be led forth in <s>Virāj</s> verses — with the <s>Uṣṇih</s>, the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>. This is the <s>Virāj</s> completion.
(PB 8.10.8) Food belongs to the <s>Virāj</s>; one obtains food.
(PB 8.10.9) For one desiring preeminence, the <s>ukthas</s> should be led forth in syllable-<s>paṅkti</s> (five-fold) verses — with the <s>Uṣṇih</s>, the <s>Brahma Sāman</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>. This is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> completion.
(PB 8.10.10) Preeminence belongs to the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; one obtains preeminence.

body.text:
(PB 9.1.1) devā vā ukthāny abhijitya rātriṃ nāśaknuvann abhijetuṃ te 'surān rātriṃ tamaḥ praviṣṭāṃ nānuvyapaśyaṃs ta etam anuṣṭupśirasaṃ pragāthm apaśyan virājaṃ jyotiḥ tān virājā jyotiṣānupaśyanto 'nuṣṭubhā vajreṇa rātrer nirāghnan
(PB 9.1.2) yad eṣo 'nuṣṭupśirāḥ pragātho bhavati virāḍ eva jyotiṣānupaśyann anuṣṭubhā vajreṇa rātrer bhrātṛvyaṃ nirhanti
(PB 9.1.3) tān samantaṃ paryāyaṃ prāṇudanta yat paryāyaṃ prāṇudanta tat paryāyāṇāṃ paryāyatvam
(PB 9.1.4) prathamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanti prathamasya paryāyasya
(PB 9.1.5) prathamair hi padaiḥ punar ādāya prathamarātrāt prāṇudanta
(PB 9.1.6) pāntam ā vo andhasa iti prastauti
(PB 9.1.7) ahar vai pāntam andho rātrir ahnaiva tad rātrim ārabhante
(PB 9.1.8) tāsu vaitahavyam
(PB 9.1.9) vītahavyaḥ śrāyaso jyog niruddha etat sāmāpaśyat so 'vagacchat pratyatiṣṭhad avagacchati pratitiṣṭhaty etena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 9.1.10) tam iva vā ete praviśantiye rātrim upayanti yad eko nidhanaṃ rātrer mukhe bhavati prajñātyai
(PB 9.1.11) yadā vai puruṣaḥ svam oka āgacchati sarvaṃ tarhi prajānāti sarvam asmai divā bhavati
(PB 9.1.12) te madhyamaṃ paryāyam aśrayanta teṣām aurdhvasadmanena vācam avṛñjata
(PB 9.1.13) vācaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
(PB 9.1.14) triṇidhanaṃ bhavati
(PB 9.1.15) yathā vā ahno mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ triṇidhanāyatanam evam eṣa rātrer madhyamaḥ paryāyas triṇidhanāyatanaḥ salokatvāya
(PB 9.1.16) madhyamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanti madhyamasya paryāyasya madhyamair hi padaiḥ punar ādāyaṃ madhyamarātrāt prāṇudanta
(PB 9.1.17) ta uttamaṃ paryāyam aśrayanta teṣāṃ ghṛtaścyun nidhanena paśūn avṛñjata paśavo vai ghṛtaścyutaḥ
(PB 9.1.18) paśūn bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃv veda
(PB 9.1.19) uttamāni padāni punarādīni bhavanty uttamasya paryāyasyottamair hi padaiḥpunar ādāyam uttamarātrāt prāṇudanta
(PB 9.1.20) tān sandhinābhipalāyanta
(PB 9.1.21) tān āśvinenāsaṃhāyyam agamayan
(PB 9.1.22) asaṃhāyyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ gamayati ya evaṃv veda
(PB 9.1.23) eṣā vā agniṣṭomasya saṃmā yad rātriḥ
(PB 9.1.24) dvādaśa stotrāṇy agniṣṭomo dvādaśa strotrāṇi rātriḥ
(PB 9.1.25) eṣā vā ukthasya saṃmā yad rātriḥ
(PB 9.1.26) trīṇy ukthāni tridevatyaḥ sandhiḥ
(PB 9.1.27) yathā vā ahna ukthāny evam eṣa rātreḥ sandhir nānārūpāṇy ahna ukthāni nānārūpā ete tṛcā bhavanti
(PB 9.1.28) rathantaraṃ pratiṣṭhākāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
(PB 9.1.29) iyaṃ vai rathantaram asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 9.1.30) bṛhat svargakāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
(PB 9.1.31) svargo loko bṛhat svarga eva loke pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 9.1.32) vāravantīyaṃ vā vāmadevyaṃ vā śruddhyaṃ vai teṣām ekaṃ paśukāmāya sandhiṃ kuryāt
(PB 9.1.33) paśavo vā etāni sāmāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 9.1.34) āśvinaṃ hotānuśaṃsati
(PB 9.1.35) prajāpatir vā etat sahasram asṛjata tad devebhyaḥ prāyacchat tasmin na samarādhayaṃs te sūryaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ kṛtvājim adhāvan
(PB 9.1.36) teṣām aśvinau prathamāv adhāvatāṃ tāv anvavadan saha no 'stv iti tāv abrūtāṃ kiṃ tataḥ syād iti yat kāmayethe ity abruvaṃs tāv abrūtām asmaddevatyam idam uktham ucyātā iti tasmād āśvinam ucyate
(PB 9.1.37) sarvāḥ khalu devatāḥ śasyante
(PB 9.1.38) kṣipraṃ śasyam ājim iva hy ete dhāvanty ā sūryasyodetoḥ śaṃset sūryaṃ hi kāṣṭhām akurvata
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.1.1) The gods, having conquered the <s>uktha</s> (recitation) offerings, were unable to conquer the night. They could not perceive the <s>asuras</s> who had entered the night and darkness. They perceived this <s>Pragātha</s> (hymn pair) headed by an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — the <s>Virāj</s> as light. Perceiving them by the light of the <s>Virāj</s>, they struck them from the night with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> as thunderbolt.
(PB 9.1.2) Since this <s>Pragātha</s> is headed by an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, perceiving by the light of the <s>Virāj</s> indeed, he strikes down the rival from the night with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> as thunderbolt.
(PB 9.1.3) They drove them out through a complete cycle (<s>paryāya</s>). Because they drove them out through a cycle, that is the cyclic nature of the <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds).
(PB 9.1.4) The first words recur at the beginning of the first <s>paryāya</s>.
(PB 9.1.5) For by taking up again with the first words, they drove them from the first part of the night.
(PB 9.1.6) He introduces with '<s>pāntam ā vo andhasa</s>' ('come to the strained drink for you').
(PB 9.1.7) Day is indeed '<s>pānta</s>' (strained); '<s>andhas</s>' (Soma plant) is the night. Thereby they commence the night from the day itself.
(PB 9.1.8) In those rounds, the <s>Vaitahavya</s> (sāman is used).
(PB 9.1.9) <s>Vītahavya</s> of the <s>Śrāyasa</s> clan, long confined, perceived this <s>sāman</s>. He was released and became firmly established. He who has praised with this is released and becomes firmly established.
(PB 9.1.10) Those who approach the night enter, as it were, into it. When a single <s>nidhana</s> occurs at the mouth of the night, it is for recognition.
(PB 9.1.11) When a man comes to his own home, he then recognizes everything; everything becomes daylight for him.
(PB 9.1.12) They resorted to the middle <s>paryāya</s>. From the <s>asuras</s>, by the <s>Ūrdhvasadmana</s> (sāman), they wrested speech.
(PB 9.1.13) He wrests the speech of his rival — he who knows thus.
(PB 9.1.14) It has a triple <s>nidhana</s>.
(PB 9.1.15) Just as the midday pressing of the day has a triple-<s>nidhana</s> foundation, so this middle <s>paryāya</s> of the night has a triple-<s>nidhana</s> foundation — for sharing the same world.
(PB 9.1.16) The middle words recur at the beginning of the middle <s>paryāya</s>. For by taking up again with the middle words, they drove them from the middle of the night.
(PB 9.1.17) They resorted to the last <s>paryāya</s>. From the <s>asuras</s>, by the <s>nidhana</s> '<s>ghṛtaścyut</s>' (dripping with ghee), they wrested animals, for animals are <s>Ghṛtaścyut</s>.
(PB 9.1.18) He wrests the animals of his rival — he who knows thus.
(PB 9.1.19) The last words recur at the beginning of the last <s>paryāya</s>. For by taking up again with the last words, they drove them from the last part of the night.
(PB 9.1.20) At the juncture (<s>sandhi</s>), the <s>asuras</s> fled from them.
(PB 9.1.21) By the <s>Āśvina</s> (sāman pertaining to the <s>Aśvins</s>), they drove them to an irrecoverable defeat.
(PB 9.1.22) He sends his rival to an irrecoverable defeat — he who knows thus.
(PB 9.1.23) This night is indeed the counterpart of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
(PB 9.1.24) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has twelve <s>stotras</s> (chants); the night has twelve <s>stotras</s>.
(PB 9.1.25) This night is indeed the counterpart of the <s>Uktha</s> ceremony.
(PB 9.1.26) There are three <s>ukthas</s>; the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture chant) has three deities.
(PB 9.1.27) Just as the <s>ukthas</s> of the day are, so is this <s>sandhi</s> of the night. The <s>ukthas</s> of the day are of various forms — these <s>tṛcas</s> (hymn-triplets) too are of various forms.
(PB 9.1.28) One should make the <s>sandhi</s> with the <s>Rathantara</s> for one desiring firm establishment.
(PB 9.1.29) This world is the <s>Rathantara</s> — he becomes firmly established in this very world.
(PB 9.1.30) One should make the <s>sandhi</s> with the <s>Bṛhat</s> for one desiring heaven.
(PB 9.1.31) The heavenly world is the <s>Bṛhat</s> — he becomes firmly established in the heavenly world.
(PB 9.1.32) One should make the <s>sandhi</s> with the <s>Vāravantīya</s>, or the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, or one of the <s>Śruddhya</s> (sāmans), for one desiring animals.
(PB 9.1.33) These <s>sāmans</s> are indeed animals — he becomes firmly established in animals.
(PB 9.1.34) The <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the <s>Āśvina</s> litany.
(PB 9.1.35) <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed created this thousand and gave it to the gods. They could not manage it. They made the sun the goal and ran a race.
(PB 9.1.36) Of them, the <s>Aśvins</s> ran first. The others called after them: 'Let us share together!' They said: 'What would come of that?' The others said: 'Whatever you desire.' The <s>Aśvins</s> said: 'Let this <s>uktha</s> be recited with us as its deities.' Therefore the <s>Āśvina</s> (litany) is recited.
(PB 9.1.37) All deities indeed are praised in it.
(PB 9.1.38) The recitation should be rapid, for they run as in a race. He should recite until sunrise, for they made the sun the goal.

body.text:
(PB 9.2.1) pāntam ā vo andhasa iti vaitahavyam anyakṣetraṃvā ete prayanti ye rātrim upayanti yad okonidhanaṃ rātrer mukhe bhavaty okaso 'pracyāvāya
(PB 9.2.2) pra va indrāya mādanam iti gaurīvitam
(PB 9.2.3) brahma yad devā vyakurvata tato yad atyaricyata tad gaurīvitam abhavat
(PB 9.2.4) atiriktaṃ gaurīvitam atiriktam etat stotraṃ yad rātrir atirikta evātiriktaṃ dadhāti
(PB 9.2.5) vayam u tvā tad id arthā iti kāṇvam
(PB 9.2.6) etena vai kaṇva indrasya sāṃvidyam agacchad indrasyaivaitena sāṃvidyaṃ gacchati
(PB 9.2.7) indrāya madvane sutam iti śrautakakṣaṃ kṣatrasāma pra kṣatram evaitena bhavati
(PB 9.2.8) ayaṃ ta indra soma iti daivodāsam
(PB 9.2.9) agniṣṭomena vai devā imaṃl lokam abhyajayann antarikṣam ukthenātirātreṇāmuṃ. ta imaṃl lokaṃ punar abhyakāmayanta ta ihety asmiṃl loke pratyatiṣṭhan yad etat sāma bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 9.2.10) ūrdhvasadmanam api śarvarīṣu prohanti
(PB 9.2.11) asurā vā eṣu lokeṣv āsaṃs tān devā ūrdhvasadmanenaibhyo lokebhyaḥ prāṇudanta
(PB 9.2.12) tad ya evaṃv vedaibhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ praṇudya sva āyatane sattram āste
(PB 9.2.13) ā tū na indra kṣumantam ity ākūpāram
(PB 9.2.14) akūpārāṅgirasasyāsīt tasyā yathā godhāyās tvag eva tvag āsīt tām etena triḥsāmnendraḥ pūtvā sūryatvacasam akarot tad vāva sā tarhy akāmayata yatkāmā etena sāmnā stuvate sa ebhyaḥ kāmaḥ samṛdhyate
(PB 9.2.15) abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sutaṃ ity ārṣabhaṃ kṣatrasāma kṣatram evaitena bhavati
(PB 9.2.16) idaṃv vaso sutam andha iti gāram etena vai gara indram aprīṇāt prīta evāsyaitenendro bhavati
(PB 9.2.17) idaṃ hy anv ojaseti mādhucchandasaṃ prajāpater vā eṣā tanūr ayātayāmnī prayujyate
(PB 9.2.18) ā tv etā niṣīdateti daivātitham
(PB 9.2.19) devātithiḥ saputro 'śanāyaṃś carann araṇya urvārūṇy avindat tāny etena sāmnopāsīdat tā asmai gāvaḥ pṛśnayo bhūtvodatiṣṭhan yad etat sām a bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
(PB 9.2.20) yoge-yoge tavastaram iti saumedhaṃ rātriṣāma rātrer eva samṛdhyai
(PB 9.2.21) indra suteṣu someṣv iti kautsam
(PB 9.2.22) kutsaś ca luśaś cendraṃ vyahvayetāṃ sa indraḥ kutsam upāvartata taṃ śatena vārdhrībhir āṇḍayor abadhnāt taṃ luśo 'bhyavadat pramucyasva pari kutsād ihāgahi kim u tvāvān āṇḍayor baddha āsātā iti tās saṃcchidya prādravat sa etat kutsaḥ sāmāpaśyat tenainam anvavadat sa upāvartata
(PB 9.2.23) yad etat sāma bhavati sendratvāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.2.1) '<s>Pāntam ā vo andhasa</s>' — with the <s>Vaitahavya</s> (sāman). Those who approach the night go indeed to a foreign land. Since the <s>nidhana</s> 'home' (<s>oka</s>) occurs at the mouth of the night, it is to prevent displacement from one's dwelling.
(PB 9.2.2) '<s>Pra va Indrāya mādanam</s>' — with the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 9.2.3) When the gods fashioned the sacred formulation (<s>brahman</s>), what was left over became the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 9.2.4) The <s>Gaurīvita</s> is the surplus. This <s>stotra</s> is the surplus — the night is the surplus. He places the surplus upon the surplus.
(PB 9.2.5) '<s>Vayam u tvā tad id arthā</s>' — with the <s>Kāṇva</s>.
(PB 9.2.6) By this <s>Kaṇva</s> attained the intimate friendship of <s>Indra</s>. By this he attains the intimate friendship of <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 9.2.7) '<s>Indrāya madvane sutam</s>' — with the <s>Śrautakakṣa</s>, a <s>kṣatra</s>-sāman (sāman of rulership). By this he attains <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power) indeed.
(PB 9.2.8) '<s>Ayaṃ ta Indra soma</s>' — with the <s>Daivodāsa</s>.
(PB 9.2.9) By the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> the gods conquered this world, by the <s>Uktha</s> the atmosphere, by the <s>Atirātra</s> the yonder world. They desired this world again. By 'here' (<s>iha</s>) they became firmly established in this world. Since this <s>sāman</s> occurs, it is for firm establishment.
(PB 9.2.10) The <s>Ūrdhvasadmana</s> (sāman) is also employed during the night watches.
(PB 9.2.11) The <s>asuras</s> dwelt in these worlds. The gods, by the <s>Ūrdhvasadmana</s>, drove them from these worlds.
(PB 9.2.12) He who knows thus, having driven his rival from these worlds, sits in his own seat in the sacrificial session.
(PB 9.2.13) '<s>Ā tū na Indra kṣumantam</s>' — with the <s>Ākūpāra</s>.
(PB 9.2.14) <s>Akūpāra</s> belonged to the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> clan. Her skin was like the skin of a monitor lizard. <s>Indra</s>, having purified her with this triple <s>sāman</s>, made her sun-complexioned. Whatever desire one has when praising with this <s>sāman</s>, that desire is fulfilled for him.
(PB 9.2.15) '<s>Abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sutam</s>' — with the <s>Ārṣabha</s>, a <s>kṣatra</s>-sāman. By this he attains <s>kṣatra</s> indeed.
(PB 9.2.16) '<s>Idaṃ vaso sutam andha</s>' — with the <s>Gāra</s>. By this <s>Gara</s> pleased <s>Indra</s>. <s>Indra</s> becomes pleased with him by this.
(PB 9.2.17) '<s>Idaṃ hy anv ojasā</s>' — with the <s>Mādhucchandasa</s>. This body of <s>Prajāpati</s>, which has not been previously employed, is put to use.
(PB 9.2.18) '<s>Ā tv etā niṣīdata</s>' — with the <s>Daivātitha</s>.
(PB 9.2.19) <s>Devātithi</s>, together with his son, wandering hungry in the wilderness, found gourds. By this <s>sāman</s> he worshipped them. They arose for him as dappled cows. Since this <s>sāman</s> occurs, it is for the nourishment of animals.
(PB 9.2.20) '<s>Yoge-yoge tavastaram</s>' — with the <s>Saumedha</s>, the night-sāman. It is for the fulfillment of the night itself.
(PB 9.2.21) '<s>Indra suteṣu someṣu</s>' — with the <s>Kautsa</s>.
(PB 9.2.22) <s>Kutsa</s> and <s>Luśa</s> both called upon <s>Indra</s>. <s>Indra</s> turned toward <s>Kutsa</s>. <s>Luśa</s> bound him by the testicles with a hundred straps. <s>Luśa</s> taunted him: 'Free yourself from <s>Kutsa</s> and come here! How could a great one like you sit bound by the testicles?' <s>Indra</s>, breaking those straps, ran away. Then <s>Kutsa</s> perceived this <s>sāman</s> and called after him with it. <s>Indra</s> turned back.
(PB 9.2.23) Since this <s>sāman</s> occurs, it is for the companionship of <s>Indra</s>.

body.text:
(PB 9.3.1) yadi sattrāya dīkṣerann atha sāmy uttiṣṭhet somam apabhajya viśvajitātirātreṇa yajeta sarvavedasena sarvasmā eva dīkṣate sarvam āpnoti
(PB 9.3.2) yā id dakṣiṇā dadāti tābhir iti prayuṅkte
(PB 9.3.3) yadi paryāyair astutam abhivyucchet pancadaśabhir hotre stuyuḥ pañcabhiḥ-pañcabhir itarebhyaḥ
(PB 9.3.4) agne vivasvad uṣasa iti sandhinā stuyuḥ prāṇā vai trivṛt stomānāṃ pratiṣṭhā rathantaraṃ sāmnāṃ prāṇāṃs caivopayanti pratiṣṭhāṃ ca
(PB 9.3.5) ṣaṣṭiṃ ca trīṇi ca śatāni hotā śaṃsati
(PB 9.3.6) tāvatyaḥ saṃvatsarasya rātrayaḥ saṃvatsarasaṃmitābhir eva tad ṛgbhir āśīvinam āpnoti
(PB 9.3.7) yad arvāk stuvanti tad astutaṃ yat samprati stuvanti tat stutaṃ yad atiṣṭuvanti tat suṣṭutam
(PB 9.3.8) yady arvāk stuyur yāvatībhir na stuyus tāvatībhir vātiṣṭuyur bhūyo 'kṣarābhir vā
(PB 9.3.9) yady atiṣṭuyur yāvatībhir atiṣṭuyus tāvatībhir vā na stuyuḥ kanīyo 'kṣarābhir vā
(PB 9.3.10) yady arvāk stuyus trīḍam agniṣṭomasāma kāryaṃ nidhanam ekeḍayā ye dve tābhyām eva tat samaṃ kriyate
(PB 9.3.11) yady atiṣṭuyuḥ svāram agniṣṭomasāma kāryam ūnam iva vā etat sāmno yat svaras tenaiva tat samaṃ kriyate
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.3.1) If they should consecrate themselves for a <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) and then a dispute over precedence should arise, having distributed the <s>Soma</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s> (all-conquering overnight sacrifice), giving all one's wealth. He thus consecrates himself for everything and obtains everything.
(PB 9.3.2) Whatever gifts he gives, with those he proceeds.
(PB 9.3.3) If the unpraised portion should be left over from the <s>paryāya</s> (turn-cycle), they should praise for the <s>Hotṛ</s> with fifteen, and with five each for the others.
(PB 9.3.4) They should praise with the <s>sandhi</s> (junction) verse 'O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vivasvat</s>, O dawns.' The vital breaths are the <s>trivṛt</s> (threefold <s>stoma</s>), the foundation of the <s>stomas</s>. The <s>Rathantara</s> is the foundation of the <s>Sāmans</s>. They thereby attain both the vital breaths and a foundation.
(PB 9.3.5) The <s>Hotṛ</s> recites three hundred and sixty.
(PB 9.3.6) That many are the nights of a year. With <s>Ṛc</s> verses equal in measure to the year, he obtains the full blessing.
(PB 9.3.7) When they praise less than required, that is 'unpraised.' When they praise the exact amount, that is 'praised.' When they praise more than required, that is 'well-praised.'
(PB 9.3.8) If they praise less than required, they should over-praise with as many as they fell short, or with more syllables.
(PB 9.3.9) If they over-praise, they should under-praise with as many as they over-praised, or with fewer syllables.
(PB 9.3.10) If they praise less than required, the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Sāman</s> should be made with the <s>trīḍa</s> ending. Where there are two <s>eḍas</s>, by those two it is made equal.
(PB 9.3.11) If they over-praise, the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Sāman</s> should be made with the <s>svāra</s> accent. The <s>svāra</s> is, as it were, less than the <s>Sāman</s>. By that it is made equal.

body.text:
(PB 9.4.1) yadi somau saṃsutau syātāṃ mahati rātreḥ prātaranuvākam upākuryāt
(PB 9.4.2) pūrvo vācaṃ pūrvaś chandāṃsi pūrvo devatā vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.3) vṛṣaṇvatīṃ pratipadaṃ kuryād indro vai vṛṣā prātaḥsavanād evaiṣām indraṃv vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.4) atho khalv āhuḥ savanamukhe-savanamukhe kāryā savanamukhāt-savanamukhād evaiṣām indraṃv vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.5) susamiddhe hotavyam agnir vai sarvā devatāḥ sarvā eva devatāḥ paśyañ juhoti
(PB 9.4.6) saṃveśāyopaveśāya gāyatryai cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāhā saṃveśāyopaveśāya triṣṭubhe cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāhā saṃveśāyopaveśāya jagatyai cchandase 'bhibhūtaye svāheti juhoti
(PB 9.4.7) cchandāṃsi vā abhibhūtayas tair evainān abhibhavaty ubhe bṛhadrathantare kārye
(PB 9.4.8) yatra vā indrasya harī tad indraḥ. indrasya vai harī bṛhadrathantare yad ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavataḥ pūrva evendrasya harī ārabhante
(PB 9.4.9) tair aśravase kārye
(PB 9.4.10) turaśravasaś ca vai pārāvatānāṃ ca somau saṃsutāv āstāṃ tata ete turaśravāḥ sāmanī apaśyat tābhyām asmā indraḥ śalmalināṃ yamunāyā havyaṃ nirāvahat yat tair aśravase bhavato havyam evaiṣāṃv vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.11) pūrve 'bhiṣuṇuyuḥ
(PB 9.4.12) yā vai pūrvāḥ prasnānti tāḥ pūrvās tīrthaṃ jayanti pūrva evendram ārabhante
(PB 9.4.13) vihavyaṃ śasyam
(PB 9.4.14) jamadagneś ca vā ṛṣīṇāṃ ca somau saṃsutāv āstāṃ tata etaj gamadagnir vihavyam apaśyat tam indra upāvartata yad vihavyaṃ hotā śaṃsatīndram evaiṣāṃv vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.15) yadītaro 'gniṣṭomaḥ syād ukthaḥ kāryo yady uktho 'tirātro yo vai bhūyān yajñakratuḥ sa indrasya priyo bhūyasaivaiṣāṃ yajnakratunendraṃv vṛṅkte
(PB 9.4.16) atho khalv āhur duṣprāpa iva vai paraḥ panthā yam evāgre yajñakratum ārabheta tasmān neyād iti
(PB 9.4.17) sajanīyaṃ śasyam agastyasya kayāśubhīyaṃ śasyam
(PB 9.4.18) asyā amuṣyā adyaśvān mithunād ahorātrābhyām evainān nirbhajati
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.4.1) If two <s>Soma</s> sacrifices should coincide on the same day, one should begin the morning <s>Anuvāka</s> (recitation) during the great part of the night.
(PB 9.4.2) He who acts first wins speech, meters, and deities first.
(PB 9.4.3) One should make the opening verse one that contains the word '<s>vṛṣan</s>' (bull, virile). <s>Indra</s> is the bull. From the very morning pressing one wins <s>Indra</s> from them.
(PB 9.4.4) But they also say: 'It should be done at the beginning of each pressing. From each pressing-beginning one wins <s>Indra</s> from them.'
(PB 9.4.5) The offering should be made in a well-kindled fire. <s>Agni</s> is all the gods. Seeing all the gods, he makes the offering.
(PB 9.4.6) He offers: 'For resting, for dwelling, for the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, for overcoming — <s>svāhā</s>! For resting, for dwelling, for the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, for overcoming — <s>svāhā</s>! For resting, for dwelling, for the <s>Jagatī</s> meter, for overcoming — <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 9.4.7) The meters are the overcomers. With them he overcomes the others. Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> should be employed.
(PB 9.4.8) Where <s>Indra</s>'s two steeds are, there is <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are indeed <s>Indra</s>'s two steeds. When both are present, one first takes hold of <s>Indra</s>'s two steeds.
(PB 9.4.9) The <s>Turaśravas</s> Sāmans should be employed.
(PB 9.4.10) The <s>Soma</s> sacrifices of <s>Turaśravas</s> and the <s>Pārāvatas</s> coincided. Then <s>Turaśravas</s> perceived these <s>Sāmans</s>. With them, <s>Indra</s> carried away the offering of the <s>Śalmalins</s> from the <s>Yamunā</s> for him. Since the <s>Turaśravas</s> Sāmans are employed, one wins the offering from them.
(PB 9.4.11) They should press first.
(PB 9.4.12) Those who press first win the crossing-place first. They first take hold of <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 9.4.13) The <s>Vihavya</s> recitation should be recited.
(PB 9.4.14) The <s>Soma</s> sacrifices of <s>Jamadagni</s> and the other <s>Ṛṣis</s> coincided. Then <s>Jamadagni</s> perceived this <s>Vihavya</s>. <s>Indra</s> turned to him. When the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the <s>Vihavya</s>, he wins <s>Indra</s> from them.
(PB 9.4.15) If the other sacrifice is an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, one should make it an <s>Uktha</s>. If it is an <s>Uktha</s>, one should make it an <s>Atirātra</s>. Whichever sacrificial rite is greater, that is dear to <s>Indra</s>. By the greater sacrificial rite one wins <s>Indra</s> from them.
(PB 9.4.16) But they say: 'The remote path is hard to attain. One should not deviate from whichever sacrificial rite one undertook first.'
(PB 9.4.17) The <s>Sajanīya</s> recitation and the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> of <s>Agastya</s> should be recited.
(PB 9.4.18) By 'this one' and 'that one,' by 'today' and 'tomorrow,' he distributes them between the pair of day and night.

body.text:
(PB 9.5.1) yadi somam akrītam apahareyur anyaḥ kretavyaḥ
(PB 9.5.2) yadi krītaṃ yo 'nyo 'bhyāśaṃ syāt sa āhṛtyaḥ somavikrayaṇe tu kiṃ cid dadyāt
(PB 9.5.3) yadi somaṃ na vindeyuḥ pūtīkān abhiṣuṇuyur yadi na pūtīkān arjjunāni
(PB 9.5.4) gāyatrī somam āharat tasyā anu visṛjya somarakṣiḥ parṇam acchinat tasya yo 'ṃśuḥ parāpatat sa pūtīko 'bhavat tasmin devā ūtim avindann ūtīko vā eṣa yat pūtīkān abhiṣuṇvanty ūtim evāsmai vindanti
(PB 9.5.5) pratidhuk ca prātaḥ pūtīkāś ca śṛtaṃ ca madhyandine pūtīkāś ca dadhi cāparāhṇe pūtīkāś ca
(PB 9.5.6) somapītho vā etasmād apakrāmatīty āhur yasya somam apaharantīti sa oṣadhīś ca paśūṃś ca praviśati tam oṣadhibhyaś ca paśubhyaś cāvarundhe
(PB 9.5.7) indro vṛtram ahaṃs tasya yo nastaḥ somaḥ samadhāvat tāni babhrutūlāny arjunāni yo vapāyā utkhinnāyās tāni lohitatūlāni yāni babhrutūlāny arjunāni tāny abhiṣuṇuyād etad vai brahmaṇo rūpaṃ sākṣād eva somam abhiṣuṇoti
(PB 9.5.8) śrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma kāryaṃ sad evainaṃ karoti
(PB 9.5.9) yajñāyajñīyam anuṣṭubhi prohed vācaivainaṃ samardhayati vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryam indriyasya vīryasya parigṛhītyai
(PB 9.5.10) pañca dakṣiṇā deyāḥ
(PB 9.5.11) pāṅkto yajño yāvān yajñas tam evārabhate
(PB 9.5.12) avabhṛthād udetya punar dīkṣeta
(PB 9.5.13) tatra tad dadyād yad dāsyaṃ syāt
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.5.1) If they should carry away the <s>Soma</s> that has not been purchased, another should be purchased.
(PB 9.5.2) If the purchased <s>Soma</s> is taken, whatever other is nearby should be brought. But something should be given at the <s>Soma</s>-selling place.
(PB 9.5.3) If they should not find <s>Soma</s>, they should press <s>Pūtīka</s> plants (substitutes). If not <s>Pūtīka</s>, then <s>Arjuna</s> plants.
(PB 9.5.4) <s>Gāyatrī</s> brought the <s>Soma</s>. As she released it, the <s>Soma</s>-guardian cut off a leaf. The shoot that fell away became the <s>Pūtīka</s> plant. In it the gods found aid. This <s>Pūtīka</s> is indeed an 'aid-giver.' When they press <s>Pūtīka</s> plants, they find aid for him.
(PB 9.5.5) The <s>pratidhuk</s> (additional milking) and <s>Pūtīkas</s> for the morning; cooked grain and <s>Pūtīkas</s> for midday; curd and <s>Pūtīkas</s> for the afternoon.
(PB 9.5.6) 'The <s>Soma</s>-drinking departs from him whose <s>Soma</s> is carried away,' they say. It enters into the herbs and cattle. He recovers it from the herbs and cattle.
(PB 9.5.7) <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. The <s>Soma</s> that had been hidden within him flowed out. Those were the brown-wooled <s>Arjuna</s> plants. The red-wooled ones are from the cut-away <s>vapā</s> (omentum). Those that are brown-wooled <s>Arjuna</s> plants should be pressed. This is the form of <s>Brahman</s>. One presses the <s>Soma</s> directly.
(PB 9.5.8) The <s>Śrāyantīya</s> should be made the <s>Brahmasāman</s>. It makes him what he truly is.
(PB 9.5.9) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> should be chanted in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. By speech he brings him to fullness. The <s>Vāravantīya</s> should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Sāman</s> — for grasping vital power and vigor.
(PB 9.5.10) Five gifts should be given.
(PB 9.5.11) The sacrifice is fivefold. Whatever the sacrifice amounts to, that is what one takes hold of.
(PB 9.5.12) Having emerged from the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), one should consecrate oneself again.
(PB 9.5.13) There one should give what is to be given.

body.text:
(PB 9.6.1) yadi kalaśo dīryeta vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanaṃ brahmasāma kuryāt
(PB 9.6.2) avaṣaṭkṛto vā etasya somaḥ parāsicyate yasya kalaśo dīryate yad vaṣaṭkāraṇīdhanaṃ brahmasāma bhavati vaṣaṭkṛta evāsya somo bhavati
(PB 9.6.3) vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ samane bahūnām ity etāsu kāryam
(PB 9.6.4) eṣa hi bahūnāṃ samane dīryate yat kalaśaḥ
(PB 9.6.5) tad āhur na vā ārtyārtir anūdyārtyā vā eṣa ārtim anuvadati yaḥ kalaśo dīrṇe dadrāṇavatīṣu karotīti
(PB 9.6.6) śrāyantīyam eva kāryam
(PB 9.6.7) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa dugdho riricāno 'manyata sa etac chrāyantīyam apaśyat tenātmānaṃ samaśrīṇāt prajayā paśubhir indriyeṇa
(PB 9.6.8) dugdha iva eṣa riricāno yasya kalaśo dīryate yac chrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma bhavati punar evātmānaṃ saṃśrīṇāti prajayā paśubhir indriyeṇa
(PB 9.6.9) yadi śrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma syād vaiṣṇavīṣv anuṣṭupsu vaṣaṭkāraṇidhanaṃ kuryāt
(PB 9.6.10) yad vai yajñasya sravati vācaṃ pratisravati vāg anuṣṭup yajño viṣṇur vācaiva yajñasya cchidram apidadhāti
(PB 9.6.11) yad vai yajñasya sravaty antataḥ sravati vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kāryaṃ yajñasyaiva cchidraṃ vārayate
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.6.1) If the <s>kalaśa</s> (Soma vessel) should break, one should make the <s>Brahmasāman</s> with the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> ending.
(PB 9.6.2) The <s>Soma</s> of one whose vessel breaks is spilled without the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> consecration. When the <s>Brahmasāman</s> has the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> ending, his <s>Soma</s> becomes consecrated with the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.
(PB 9.6.3) It should be done with the verses 'The shining one running in the assembly of many.'
(PB 9.6.4) For it is the vessel that breaks in the assembly of many.
(PB 9.6.5) They say: 'One should not speak of distress upon distress. He who uses verses with <s>dadrāṇa</s> (running, leaking) when the vessel has broken is speaking of distress upon distress.'
(PB 9.6.6) The <s>Śrāyantīya</s> should be employed.
(PB 9.6.7) <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. He felt milked dry and depleted. He perceived this <s>Śrāyantīya</s>. With it he restored himself with offspring, cattle, and vital power.
(PB 9.6.8) He whose vessel breaks is as if milked dry and depleted. When the <s>Śrāyantīya</s> becomes the <s>Brahmasāman</s>, he restores himself with offspring, cattle, and vital power.
(PB 9.6.9) If the <s>Śrāyantīya</s> is already the <s>Brahmasāman</s>, one should make it with the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> ending on <s>Vaiṣṇavī Anuṣṭubh</s> verses.
(PB 9.6.10) What flows out of the sacrifice flows away as speech. Speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; the sacrifice is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. By speech he covers the gap in the sacrifice.
(PB 9.6.11) What flows out of the sacrifice flows from within. The <s>Vāravantīya</s> should be made the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Sāman</s>. He thereby blocks the gap of the sacrifice.

body.text:
(PB 9.7.1) yadi prātassavanāt somo 'tiricyeta asti somo ayaṃ suta iti marutvatīṣu gāyatreṣu stuyuḥ
(PB 9.7.2) mādhyandinaṃ vā eṣa savanaṃ nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yaḥ prātassavanād atiricyate tasmān marutvatīṣu stuvanti marutvad dhi mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ tasmād u gāyatrīṣu gāyatraṃ hi prātassavanam
(PB 9.7.3) yasmāt stomād atiricyate sa eva stomaḥ kāryaḥ salomatvāya
(PB 9.7.4) aindrāvaiṣṇavaṃ hotānuśaṃsati
(PB 9.7.5) vīryaṃ vā indro yajño viṣṇur vīrya eva yajñe pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 9.7.6) yadi mādhyandināt savanād atiricyeta baṇ mahāṃ asi sūryety ādityavatīṣu gaurīvitena stuyuḥ
(PB 9.7.7) tṛtīyasavanaṃ vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo mādhyandināt savanād atiricyate tasmād ādityavatīṣu stuvanty ādityaṃ hi tṛtīyasavanaṃ tasmād u bṛhatīṣu bārhataṃ hi mādhyandinaṃ savanam
(PB 9.7.8) yasmāt stomād atiricyeta sa eva stomaḥ kāryaḥ salomatvāyaindrāvaiṣṇavaṃ hotānuśaṃsati vīryaṃ vā indro yajño viṣṇur vīrya eva yajñe pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 9.7.9) yadi tṛtīyasavanād atiricyeta viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭavatīṣu gaurīvitena stuyuḥ
(PB 9.7.10) yajño vai viṣṇuś śipiviṣṭo yajña eva viṣṇau pratitiṣṭhaty atiriktaṃ gaurīvitam atirikta evātiriktaṃ dadhāti
(PB 9.7.11) etad anyat kuryur ukthāni praṇayeyur ukthāni vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo 'gniṣṭomād atiricyate yady ukthyebhyo 'tiricyetātirātraḥ kāryo rātriṃ vā eṣa nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate ya ukthyebhyo 'tiricyate yadi rātrer atiricyeta viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭavatīṣu bṛhatā stuyur eṣu tu vā atiricyata ity āhur yo rātrer atiricyata iti
(PB 9.7.12) amuṃ vā eṣa lokaṃ nikāmayamāno 'bhyatiricyate yo rātrer atiricyate bṛhatā stuvanti bṛhad amuṃ lokam āptum arhati tam evāpnoti
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.7.1) If <s>Soma</s> is left over from the morning pressing, they should praise with the verse 'There is this <s>Soma</s>, pressed' in the <s>Marutvatī</s> (verses addressed to the <s>Maruts</s>) set to <s>Gāyatrī</s> meters.
(PB 9.7.2) The one that is left over from the morning pressing overflows desiring the midday pressing. Therefore they praise with the <s>Marutvatī</s> verses, for the midday pressing belongs to the <s>Maruts</s>. And therefore in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meters, for the morning pressing belongs to the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
(PB 9.7.3) Whatever <s>stoma</s> (hymn-form) it overflows from, that same <s>stoma</s> should be employed, for the sake of consistency.
(PB 9.7.4) The <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) recites the <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s> (hymn to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>).
(PB 9.7.5) <s>Indra</s> is indeed vigor, the sacrifice is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — he thus becomes established in vigor in the sacrifice.
(PB 9.7.6) If it is left over from the midday pressing, they should praise with 'Indeed, you are great, O <s>Sūrya</s>' in the <s>Ādityavatī</s> (verses addressed to <s>Āditya</s>) with the <s>Gaurīvita</s> (chant).
(PB 9.7.7) The one that is left over from the midday pressing overflows desiring the third pressing. Therefore they praise with the <s>Ādityavatī</s> verses, for the third pressing belongs to <s>Āditya</s>. And therefore in <s>Bṛhatī</s> meters, for the midday pressing belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 9.7.8) Whatever <s>stoma</s> it overflows from, that same <s>stoma</s> should be employed, for the sake of consistency. The <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s>. <s>Indra</s> is indeed vigor, the sacrifice is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — he thus becomes established in vigor in the sacrifice.
(PB 9.7.9) If it is left over from the third pressing, they should praise with the verses containing '<s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>' using the <s>Gaurīvita</s> chant.
(PB 9.7.10) The sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s> (the radiant one) — he thus becomes established in <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the sacrifice. The <s>Gaurīvita</s> is the surplus; he thus places the surplus upon the surplus.
(PB 9.7.11) Otherwise they should do this: they should extend the <s>Uktha</s> recitations. The one that overflows from the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> overflows desiring the <s>Uktha</s> rites. If it overflows from the <s>Uktha</s> rites, an <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite) should be performed. The one that overflows from the <s>Uktha</s> rites overflows desiring the night rite. If it overflows from the night rite, they should praise with the verses containing '<s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>' using the <s>Bṛhat</s>. But some say: 'He does overflow among these — he who overflows from the night rite.'
(PB 9.7.12) The one who overflows from the night rite overflows desiring that world (yonder). They praise with the <s>Bṛhat</s> — the <s>Bṛhat</s> is worthy of reaching that world; he indeed reaches it.

body.text:
(PB 9.8.1) yadi dīkṣitānāṃ pramīyate dagdhvāsthīny upanahya yo nediṣṭhī syāt taṃ dīkṣayitvā saha yajeran
(PB 9.8.2) etad anyat kuryur abhiṣutyānyat somam agṛhītvā grahān yāsau dakṣiṇā sraktis tad vā stuyur mārjālīye vā
(PB 9.8.3) api vā etasya yajñe yo dīkṣitaḥ pramīyate tam etena niravadayante
(PB 9.8.4) yāmena stuvanti yamalokam evainaṃ gamayanti
(PB 9.8.5) tisṛbhiḥ stuvanti tṛtīye hi loke pitaraḥ
(PB 9.8.6) parācībhiḥ stuvanti parāṅ hīto 'sau lokaḥ
(PB 9.8.7) sarparājñyā ṛgbhiḥ stuvanti
(PB 9.8.8) arbudaḥ sarpa etābhir mṛtāṃ tvacam apāhata mṛtām evaitābhis tvacam apaghnate
(PB 9.8.9) tā ṛco 'nubruvantas trir mārjālīyaṃ pariyanti savyān ūrūn āghnānāḥ
(PB 9.8.10) stutam anuśaṃsaty amuṣminn evainaṃ loke nidhnuvanti
(PB 9.8.11) yanti vā ete patha ity āhur ye mṛtāya kurvantīty aindravāyavāgrān grahān gṛhṇate punaḥ panthānam apiyanti
(PB 9.8.12) agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti pratipatkāryā ya eva jīvanti teṣv āyur dadhāti
(PB 9.8.13) saṃvatsare 'sthīni yājayeyuḥ saṃvvatsaro vai sarvasya śāntir yat purā saṃvvatsarād yājayeyur vācam aruṣkṛtāṃ krūrām ṛccheyuḥ
(PB 9.8.14) vṛtaḥ pavamānāḥ syuḥ saptadaśam itarat sarvam
(PB 9.8.15) yat trivṛtaḥ pavamānā bhavanti prāṇā vai trivṛt prāṇān evopayanti yat saptadaśam itarat sarvaṃ prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajatim evopayanti
(PB 9.8.16) prāṇāpānair vā ete vyṛdhyanta ity āhur ye mṛtāya kurvantīti maitrāvaruṇāgrān grahān gṛhṇate prāṇāpānau mitrāvaruṇau prāṇāpānair eva samṛdhyante
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.8.1) If one of the consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>) dies, having cremated him and tied up the bones, they should consecrate the nearest kinsman and sacrifice together.
(PB 9.8.2) Otherwise they should do this: having pressed <s>Soma</s> again, without having taken the cups (<s>graha</s>), they should praise at the southern edge or with the <s>Mārjālīya</s> (purificatory chant).
(PB 9.8.3) Or indeed, in the sacrifice of him who, being consecrated, dies — they dismiss him with this.
(PB 9.8.4) They praise with the <s>Yāma</s> (chant related to <s>Yama</s>) — they thus send him to the world of <s>Yama</s>.
(PB 9.8.5) They praise with three verses, for the ancestors are in the third world.
(PB 9.8.6) They praise with inverted verses, for that world is turned away.
(PB 9.8.7) They praise with the verses of the <s>Sarparājñī</s> (Snake Queen).
(PB 9.8.8) <s>Arbuda</s>, the serpent — with these he struck off the dead skin. With these they strike off the dead skin.
(PB 9.8.9) Reciting those verses, they go around the <s>Mārjālīya</s> three times, striking their left thighs.
(PB 9.8.10) He recites after the praise — they thus deposit him in that world.
(PB 9.8.11) 'Those who perform for the dead go along a dangerous path,' they say. They take the <s>Aindrāvāyava</s> (cups of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>) first — they return to the path.
(PB 9.8.12) 'O <s>Agni</s>, purify the life-spans' — this should be used as the opening verse. He places life in those who are living.
(PB 9.8.13) After a year they should have the bones sacrificed upon. The year is indeed the pacification of everything. If they were to sacrifice before a year, they would encounter harsh, cruel speech.
(PB 9.8.14) The <s>Pavamāna</s> (purificatory chants) should be threefold; all the rest should be seventeenfold.
(PB 9.8.15) When the <s>Pavamāna</s> chants are threefold — the <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) are indeed threefold — they thus approach the <s>prāṇas</s>. When all the rest is seventeenfold — <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed seventeenfold — they thus approach procreation.
(PB 9.8.16) 'Those who perform for the dead become weakened in <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,' they say. They take the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> cups first — <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> are <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>. They thus prosper through <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.

(PB 9.9.2) tad āhuḥ payo 'vanayed iti
(PB 9.9.3) atho khalv āhur antarhitam iva vā etad yat payo hiraṇyam evāpo'bhyavanayed dhiraṇyam abhyunnayed iti
(PB 9.9.4) prāṇā vā āpo 'mṛtaṃ hiraṇyam amṛta evāsya prāṇān dadhāti sa sarvam āyur eti
(PB 9.9.5) yasya nārāśaṃsa upavāyati nārāśaṃsam evāsyopa+vāyantaṃ prāṇo 'nūpadasyati prāṇo hi somaḥ
(PB 9.9.6) yam adhvaryur antato grahaṃ gṛhṇīyāt tasyāptum avanayet
(PB 9.9.7) prāyaścityai vai graho gṛhyate prāyaścityevāsmai prāyaścittiṃ karoti
(PB 9.9.8) yadi pītāpītau somau saṃgaccheyātām antaḥ paridhyaṅgārān nirvartya juhuyāt hutasya cāhutasya cāhutasya hutasya ca / pītāpītasya somasyendrāgnī pibataṃ sutaṃ svāheti saiva tasya prāyaścittiḥ
(PB 9.9.9) prajāpataye svāhety abhakṣaṇīyasya juhuyād uttarārdhyapūrvārdhya uparavaḥ
(PB 9.9.10) indur indum avāgād ity avavṛṣṭasya bhakṣayet
(PB 9.9.11) tasya ta indrav indrapītasyendriyāvatas sarvagaṇasya sarvagaṇa upahūta upahūtasya bhakṣayāmi
(PB 9.9.12) hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra ity ājyenābhyupākṛtasya juhuyād agnīdhraṃ paretya bhūtānāṃ jātaḥ patir eka āsīt sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyām utemāṃ tasmai ta indo haviṣā vidhema svāheti saiva tasya prāyaścittiḥ
(PB 9.9.13) yadi grāvāpi śīryate paśubhir yajamāno vyṛdhyate paśavo vai grāvāṇo dyutānasya mārutasya sāmnā stuyuḥ
(PB 9.9.14) mārutā vai grāvāṇaḥ svenaivaināṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 9.9.15) yadi somam abhidahed grahān adhvaryuḥ spāśayeta stotrāṇy udgātā śastrāṇi hotātha yathāpūrvaṃ yajñena careyuḥ pañca dakṣiṇā deyāḥ pāṅkto yajño yāvān yajñas tam ārabhate 'vabhṛthād udetya punar dīkṣate tatra tad dadyād yad dāsyaṃ syāt purā dvādaśyā dīkṣeta yad dvādaśīm atinayed antardhīyeta
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.9.1) When someone's vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>) leaks, as his vessel leaks, his <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) leaks along with it, for <s>Soma</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>.
(PB 9.9.2) On this they say: 'He should lower milk into it.'
(PB 9.9.3) Now others say: 'Milk is something concealed, as it were. He should lower gold into the water and raise the gold up.'
(PB 9.9.4) The waters are indeed the <s>prāṇas</s>; gold is the immortal. He thus places the immortal in his <s>prāṇas</s>. He lives his full lifespan.
(PB 9.9.5) When someone's <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (cup) blows over, as his <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> blows over, his <s>prāṇa</s> leaks along with it, for <s>Soma</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>.
(PB 9.9.6) The <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) should lower into it the cup he would take last.
(PB 9.9.7) A cup is taken for expiation — he thus makes an expiation for the expiation.
(PB 9.9.8) If drunk and undrunk <s>Soma</s> juices come together, he should remove the coals from within the enclosure and make an offering: 'Of the offered and the unoffered, of the unoffered and the offered, of the drunk and undrunk <s>Soma</s>, may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> drink the pressed juice, <s>svāhā</s>!' That is indeed the expiation for this.
(PB 9.9.9) 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — he should offer for what should not be partaken of, at the <s>uparava</s> (place of rest) on the upper and lower halves.
(PB 9.9.10) 'The drop went to the drop' — he should partake of what has overflowed.
(PB 9.9.11) 'Of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, possessing <s>Indra</s>'s power, of all the hosts, invoked among all hosts — I partake of you, the invoked one.'
(PB 9.9.12) 'The golden embryo arose in the beginning' — he should offer with ghee for what has been brought near. Going to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's shed): 'He was born the sole lord of beings. He upheld this earth and heaven. To you, O <s>Soma</s> drop, we offer with oblation, <s>svāhā</s>!' That is indeed the expiation for this.
(PB 9.9.13) If the pressing stone (<s>grāvan</s>) breaks, the sacrificer becomes weakened in cattle, for cattle are the pressing stones. They should praise with the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) of the shining <s>Māruta</s>.
(PB 9.9.14) The pressing stones belong to the <s>Maruts</s>. He thus restores them with their own form.
(PB 9.9.15) If the <s>Soma</s> is burned, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should touch the cups, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> the <s>stotras</s> (praise chants), the <s>Hotṛ</s> the <s>śastras</s> (recitations), and then they should proceed with the sacrifice as before. Five gifts should be given — the sacrifice is fivefold. He takes hold of the full sacrifice. Rising from the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), he undergoes consecration again. There he should give whatever is to be given. He should be consecrated before the twelfth day. If he exceeds the twelfth day, he perishes.

body.text:
(PB 9.10.1) yadi mahāvīro bhidyeta taṃ bhinnam abhimṛśed ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ purā jatrubhya ātṛdaḥ / saṃdhātā saṃdhiṃ maghavā purūvasur niṣkartā vihrutaṃ punaḥ mā bhema niṣṭyā ivendra tvad araṇā iva / vanāni na prajahitāny adrivo duroṣāso amanmahi / amanmahīd anāśavo 'nugrābhaś ca vṛtrahan / sakṛt sute mahatā śūra rādhasānu stomaṃ mademahīti mahāvīraṃ bhinnam abhimṛśet saiva tasya prāyaścittiḥ
(PB 9.10.2) asuryaṃ vā etasmād varṇaṃ kṛtvā teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ prajāḥ paśavo 'pakrāmanti yasya yūpo virohati sa īśvaraḥ pāpīyān bhavitoḥ
(PB 9.10.3) tvāṣṭraṃ paśuṃ bahurūpam ālabheta tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ rūpāṇāṃ vikartā tam eva tad upadhāvati sa enaṃ tejaseindriyeṇa vīryeṇānnādyena prajayā paśubhiḥ punas samardhayati saiva tasya prāyaścittiḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 9.10.1) If the <s>mahāvīra</s> (great hero vessel) breaks, he should touch the broken one with this verse: 'You who even without binding, before the collar-bones, pierced through — <s>Maghavan</s> (the bountiful one), the joiner of joints, the mender of what is torn, of many dwellings, restores what is broken. Let us not fear, O <s>Indra</s>, like outsiders, like those far from you. Not abandoned like forests, O wielder of the stone — we have found difficult shelter. We have found refuge, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, we who were without refuge, without support. At a single pressing, O hero, with great bounty, let us rejoice in the <s>stoma</s> (hymn)!' — he should touch the broken <s>mahāvīra</s>. That is indeed the expiation for this.
(PB 9.10.2) Demonic nature, radiance, power, vigor, the eating of food, offspring, and cattle depart from him whose sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) sprouts. He is liable to become worse off.
(PB 9.10.3) He should offer a multi-formed animal to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> (the divine craftsman). <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is indeed the fashioner of the forms of cattle. He thus resorts to him. He restores him with radiance, power, vigor, the eating of food, offspring, and cattle. That is indeed the expiation for this.

body.translated_text:
(PB 10.1.1) Through <s>Agni</s>, the earth, and the plants — by this, this world is three-fold. Through <s>Vāyu</s>, the atmosphere, and the birds — by this, that world is three-fold. Through <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), the sky, and the stars, who is the one within — by this, yonder world is three-fold. This is the abode of the <s>Trivṛt</s> (three-fold); this is its connection.
(PB 10.1.2) He who knows thus becomes one who has an abode and a connection.
(PB 10.1.3) And they say regarding its firm establishment: the three-fold

Because he created them from the priestly principle (<s>ṛtvya</s>), that is the origin of the priests' (<s>ṛtvij</s>) nature. With them he performed this twelve-day rite. He succeeded.

body.translated_text:
(PB 10.4.1) The past is the first <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite); the future is the last. The earth is the first <s>Atirātra</s>; heaven is the last. <s>Agni</s> is the first <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the last. The in-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is the first <s>Atirātra</s>; the out-breath (<s>udāna</s>) is the last.
(PB 10.4.2) The two eyes are the two <s>Atirātras</s>; the two pupils are the two <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>. Because between the two <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> the two <s>Atirātras</s> [are placed], therefore the two pupils, being between [the eyes], enjoy.

(PB 10.5.11) chandāṃsy evāsyās tṛtīyaṃ trirātraṃ vahanti
(PB 10.5.12) tāṃ vā etāṃ pratīcīṃ tiraścīṃ parācīm āsate 'nnādyāya tasmāt pratyañcaṃ tiryañcaṃ parāñcaṃ prajāḥ paśum upajīvanti
(PB 10.5.13) chandāṃsi vā anyo'nyasya lokam abhadhyāyan gāyatrī triṣṭubhas triṣṭub jagatyā jagatī gāyatryās tāni vyauhan yathālokaṃ tato vai tāni yaṃ-yaṃ kāmam akāmayanta tam asanvan
(PB 10.5.14) yatkāmo vyūḍhacchandasā dvadaśāhena yajate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate
(PB 10.5.15) oko vai devānāṃ dvādaśāho yatho vai manuṣyā imaṃ lokam āviṣṭā evaṃ devatā dvādaśāham āviṣṭā devatā ha vā etena yajate ya evaṃv vidvān dvādaśāhena yajate
(PB 10.5.16) gṛhā vai devānāṃ dvādaśāho nāgṛhatāyā bhayyam
(PB 10.5.17) yo vai dvādaśāham agniṣṭomena kalpamānaṃ veda kalpate 'smai prātaḥsavanenaiva prathamas trirātraḥ kalpate mādhyandinena dvitīyas tṛtīyasavanena tṛtīyo 'gniṣṭomasāmnaiva daśamam ahaḥ kalpate
(PB 10.5.18) kalpate 'smai ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 10.5.1) These three three-night periods constitute this twelve-day rite: the first has the <s>Gāyatra</s> at the beginning, the second has the <s>Gāyatra</s> in the middle, the third has the <s>Gāyatra</s> at the end.
(PB 10.5.2) Because the first has the <s>Gāyatra</s> at the beginning, therefore <s>Agni</s> blazes upward. Because the second has the <s>Gāyatra</s> in the middle, therefore <s>Vāyu</s> blows sideways.
(PB 10.5.3) [text missing]
(PB 10.5.4) [text missing]
(PB 10.5.5) With brilliance they set forth, brilliance they place in the middle, with brilliance they rise up. With light they set forth, light they place in the middle, with light they rise up. With sight they set forth, sight they place in the middle, with sight they rise up. With breath they set forth, breath they place in the middle, with breath they rise up. Those who set forth with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, place the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in the middle, and rise up with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
(PB 10.5.6) This twelve-day rite is a warp that is stretched out; its pegs are the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — for the sake of non-disintegration.
(PB 10.5.7) <s>Girikṣit Auccāmanyava</s> — thus spoke <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣasenī</s>: 'How is the twelve-day rite constituted?' 'Just as the rim encircles the spokes, so the <s>Gāyatrī</s> encircles it — for the sake of non-collapse. Just as the spokes are held in the nave, so the twelve-day rite is held in it.'
(PB 10.5.8) They sit, having transformed the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> for the sake of obtaining food, when they perform this twelve-day rite.
(PB 10.5.9) The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> with eight syllables extends through the first day of the twelve-day rite, with eleven through the second, with twelve through the third.
(PB 10.5.10) One syllable and three syllables remain; those are distributed over the latter three-night period.
(PB 10.5.11) The meters themselves carry its third three-night period.
(PB 10.5.12) They sit with this turned backward, sideways, and away — for the sake of obtaining food. Therefore creatures live upon cattle that goes backward, sideways, and away.
(PB 10.5.13) The meters coveted each other's world — the <s>Gāyatrī</s> that of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> that of the <s>Jagatī</s>, the <s>Jagatī</s> that of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. They rearranged them according to their worlds. From that, whatever desire they desired, they attained it.
(PB 10.5.14) Whatever desire one has who sacrifices with a twelve-day rite of rearranged meters — that desire is fulfilled for him.
(PB 10.5.15) The twelve-day rite is the abode of the <s>devas</s>. Just as humans have entered this world, so the deities have entered the twelve-day rite. He sacrifices with the deities who, knowing thus, sacrifices with the twelve-day rite.
(PB 10.5.16) The twelve-day rite is the house of the <s>devas</s>. There is no fear for one who has a house.
(PB 10.5.17) He who knows the twelve-day rite as conforming to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> — it conforms for him: the first three-night period conforms through the morning pressing, the second through the midday pressing, the third through the third pressing; the tenth day conforms through the <s>Agniṣṭoma Sāman</s> itself.
(PB 10.5.18) It conforms for him who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 10.6.1) eti prety āśumad vītimad rukmat tejasvad yuñjānaṃ prathamasyāhno rūpaṃ trivṛtaḥ stomasya gāyatrasya chandaso rathantarasya sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.2) vṛṣavad vṛtravad rayimad viśvavad upasthitaṃ dvitīyasyāhno rūpaṃ pañcadaśasya stomasya traiṣṭubhasya chandaso bṛhataḥ sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.3) udvat trivad digvat gomaṭ ṭaṣabhavat tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ saptadaśasya stomasya jāgatasya chandaso vairūpasya sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.4) rājanvaj janavadvat sūryavad virāḍanutodavac caturthasyāhno rūpam ekaviṃśasya stomasyānuṣṭubhasya chandaso (?) rājasya vai sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.5) citravac chiśumat paṅktiḥ śakvarī dyūnākṣarā gomad ṛṣabhavad vajryabhimat pañcamasyāhno rūpaṃ triṇavasya stomasya pāṅktena chandaso śakvarīṇāṃ sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.6) parivat prativat saptapadā dvipadā vinārāśaṃsā gomad ṛṣabhavat ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ trayastriṃśasya stomasya sarveṣāṃ chandasāṃ rūpaṃ (?) revatīnāṃ sāmnaḥ
(PB 10.6.7) yasmād eṣā samānā satī ṣaḍahavibhaktir nānārūpā tasmād virūpaḥ saṃvvatsaraḥ
(PB 10.6.8) virūpam enam anuprajāyate ya evaṃv veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 10.6.1) The form of the first day has the character of going, coming, swiftness, movement, brightness, and brilliance — it is yoked. It has the nine-fold (<s>trivṛt</s>) <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Gāyatra</s> meter, and the <s>Rathantara Sāman</s>.
(PB 10.6.2) The form of the second day has the character of bullishness, <s>Vṛtra</s>-slaying, wealth, and universality — it is established. It has the fifteen-fold <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> meter, and the <s>Bṛhat Sāman</s>.
(PB 10.6.3) The form of the third day has the character of rising, threefoldness, directionality, cattle, and bull-like nature. It has the seventeen-fold <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Jāgata</s> meter, and the <s>Vairūpa Sāman</s>.
(PB 10.6.4) The form of the fourth day has the character of royalty, populousness, sun-like quality, and sovereign-like piercing. It has the twenty-one-fold <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Anuṣṭubha</s> meter, and the <s>Vairāja Sāman</s>.
(PB 10.6.5) The form of the fifth day has the character of variety, youthfulness, five-foldness, the <s>Śakvarī</s>, heavenly syllables, cattle, bull-like nature, and thunderbolt-likeness. It has the twenty-seven-fold (<s>triṇava</s>) <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Pāṅkta</s> meter, and the <s>Śakvarī Sāmans</s>.
(PB 10.6.6) The form of the sixth day has the character of encompassing, countering, seven-footedness, two-footedness, absence of praise-recitations, cattle, and bull-like nature. It has the thirty-three-fold <s>stoma</s>, the form of all meters, and the <s>Revatī Sāmans</s>.
(PB 10.6.7) Because this, though being the same six-day division, has various forms, therefore the year is of various forms.
(PB 10.6.8) Various forms are born to him who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 10.7.1) agna iti prathamasyāhno rūpam agnivibhakter agnim iti dvitīyasyāgnineti tṛtīyasyāgnir iti caturthasya
(PB 10.7.2) devā vai śriyam aicchaṃs tān na prathame 'hany avindan na dvitīye na tṛtīye tāñ caturthe 'hany avindan vindate śriyaṃ ya evaṃ vedāgner iti pañcamasya teno śrīḥ pratyupoditety āhuḥ
(PB 10.7.3) aprativādy enaṃ bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 10.7.4) agna iti ṣaṣṭhasya yenaiva rūpeṇa prayanti tad abhyudyanti
(PB 10.7.5) yasmād eṣā samānā saty agnivbhaktir nānārūpā tasmād yathartv ādityas tapati
body.translated_text:
(PB 10.7.1) '<s>Agna</s>' (O Agni, vocative) is the form of the first day — of the <s>Agni</s>-declension. '<s>Agnim</s>' (accusative) of the second; '<s>Agninā</s>' (instrumental) of the third; '<s>Agniḥ</s>' (nominative) of the fourth.
(PB 10.7.2) The <s>devas</s> desired glory. They did not find it on the first day, nor on the second, nor on the third. They found it on the fourth day. He who knows thus finds glory. '<s>Agneḥ</s>' (genitive/ablative) of the fifth — therefore they say that glory has shone forth.
(PB 10.7.3) The rival becomes unable to speak against him who knows thus.
(PB 10.7.4) '<s>Agna</s>' (vocative) of the sixth — they rise up with the same form with which they set forth.
(PB 10.7.5) Because this, though being the same <s>Agni</s>-declension, has various forms, therefore the sun heats according to the seasons.

body.text: (PB 10.8.1) indreti prathamasyāhno rūpam indravibhakter indram iti dvitīyasyendreṇeti tṛtīyasyendra iti caturthasyendrād iti pañcamasyendreti ṣaṣṭhasya yenaiva rūpeṇa prayanti tad abhyudyanti yasmād eṣā samānā satīndravibhaktir nānārūpā tasmād yathartv oṣadhayaḥ pacyante
body.translated_text: (PB 10.8.1) '<s>Indra</s>' (vocative) is the form of the first day — of the <s>Indra</s>-declension. '<s>Indram</s>' (accusative) of the second; '<s>Indreṇa</s>' (instrumental) of the third; '<s>Indra</s>' (vocative) of the fourth; '<s>Indrāt</s>' (ablative) of the fifth; '<s>Indra</s>' (vocative) of the sixth — they rise up with the same form with which they set forth. Because this, though being the same <s>Indra</s>-declension, has various forms, therefore herbs ripen according to the seasons.

body.text:
(PB 10.9.1) yad ṛcā prastauti tat prathamasyāhno rūpam svaravibhakter yat purastāt stobhaṃ tad dvitīyasya yad ubhayataḥ stobhaṃ tat tṛtīyasya yad anutunnaṃ tac caturthasya yad abhyārabdhaṃ tat pañcamasya yad ihakāreṇābhyastaṃ tat ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam
(PB 10.9.2) svarāṇāṃ yasmād eṣā samānā satī svaravibhaktir nnānārūpā tasmād yathartu vāyuḥ pavate
body.translated_text:
(PB 10.9.1) When one starts the chant with an <s>ṛc</s> verse, that is the form of the first day — of the melody-variation (<s>svara</s>-declension). When the <s>stobha</s> (exclamatory syllable) comes before, that is the second. When the <s>stobha</s> is on both sides, that is the third. When it is pierced through, that is the fourth. When it is taken hold of, that is the fifth. When it is intensified with the syllable <s>iha</s>, that is the form of the sixth day.
(PB 10.9.2) Among the melodies — because this, though being the same melody-variation, has various forms, therefore <s>Vāyu</s> blows according to the seasons.

body.text: (PB 10.10.1) padanidhanaṃ prathamasyāhno rūpam nidhanavibhakter bahirṇidhanaṃ dvitīyasya niṃnidhanaṃ tṛtīyasyenidhanañ caturthasyāthakāraṇidhanaṃ pañcamasya yad ihākāreṇābhyastaṃ tat ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ nidhanānāṃ yasmād eṣā samānā satī nidhanavibhaktir nnānārūpā tasmād ime lokāḥ saha santo nānaiva
body.translated_text: (PB 10.10.1) The foot-ending (<s>padanidhana</s>) is the form of the first day — of the ending-variation. The external ending (<s>bahirṇidhana</s>) of the second. The descending ending (<s>niṃnidhana</s>) of the third. The <s>ī</s>-ending of the fourth. The <s>atha</s>-syllable ending of the fifth. What is intensified with the syllable <s>iha</s> is the form of the sixth day — of the endings. Because this, though being the same ending-variation, has various forms, therefore these worlds, though existing together, are yet distinct.

body.text: (PB 10.11.1) dravadiḍaṃ prathamasyāhno rūpam iḍāvibhakter ūrdhveḍaṃ dvitīyasya pariṣṭubdheḍaṃ tṛtīyasyeḍābhir aiḍaṃ caturthasyādhyardheḍaṃ pañcamasya yad ihākāreṇābhyastaṃ tat ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam iḍānāṃ yasmād eṣā samānā satīḍāvibhaktir nnānārūpā tasmāt samānāḥ santaḥ paśavo nānārūpāḥ
body.translated_text: (PB 10.11.1) The flowing <s>iḍā</s> (<s>dravadiḍā</s>) is the form of the first day — of the <s>iḍā</s>-variation. The ascending <s>iḍā</s> (<s>ūrdhveḍā</s>) of the second. The encircling <s>iḍā</s> (<s>pariṣṭubdheḍā</s>) of the third. The <s>iḍā</s> with <s>iḍā</s>s (<s>iḍābhir aiḍā</s>) of the fourth. The half-and-more <s>iḍā</s> (<s>adhyardheḍā</s>) of the fifth. What is intensified with the syllable <s>iha</s> is the form of the sixth day — of the <s>iḍā</s>s. Because this, though being the same <s>iḍā</s>-variation, has various forms, therefore cattle, though being the same, are of various forms.

body.text:
(PB 10.12.1) bharadvājāyanā vai sattram āsata tān apṛcchan kiṃ prathamenāhnā kuruteti praivaimeti kiṃ dvitīyenety avasam evākurmahīti kiṃ tṛtīyeneti pary evāplavāmahīti kiṃ caturtheneti sataiva sad apyadadhmeti kiṃ pañcameneti prāṇān eva vicchindanta aimeti kiṃ ṣaṣṭhenetīdam evāgacchāmeti iti
(PB 10.12.2) yasya padena prastauty atha svāram abhi vāva tena devāḥ paśūn apaśyan yat purastāt stobhaṃ atha svāram ud eva tenāsṛjanata yad ubhayataḥ stobham atha svāram ebhya eva tena lokebhyo devāḥ paśubhyo 'nnādyaṃ prāyacchan yad anutunnam atha svāram upaiva tenāśikṣan yasya madhye nidhanam atha svāraṃ garbhāṃs tenādadhata tāni havatāsvāreṇa prājanayan
(PB 10.12.3) imaṃ vāva devā lokaṃ padanidhanenābhy ajayann amuṃ bahirṇidhanenāntarikṣaṃ diṅnidhanenāmṛtatvam īnidhanenāgacchan brahmavarcasam athanidhanenāvārundhatāsminn eva loka ihanidhanena pratyatiṣṭhan
(PB 10.12.4) imaṃ vāva devā lokaṃ dravadiḍenābhy ajayann amum ūrdhveḍenāntarikṣaṃ pariṣṭubdheḍena pratiṣṭhām iḍābhir aiḍenāvārundhata pratiṣṭhāyādhyardheḍena vyajayantāsminn eva loka iheḍena pratyatiṣṭhan
(PB 10.12.5) na vāk saṃvatsaram ativadatīḍaiva saṃvatsaram ativadati garbheṇa saṃvatsare paryāvṛtya prajāyete tenātivadati
(PB 10.12.6) tā vā etāś catasraḥ ṣaḍahaṃ parācya iḍā atiyanty eṣā nūtaiṣā viṣūcy eṣā pratīcy etad vīḍam
(PB 10.12.7) saṃvatsaro 'gnir vāk samvatsaro yad agnir vibhajyate vācam eva tad vibhajanti
(PB 10.12.8) dve dve akṣare vibhajanti dvau dvau hi māsāv ṛturatho māsānām eva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 10.12.9) ṣaḍ ahāni vibhajanti ṣaḍ ṛtava ṛtūnāṃ dhṛtyā ṛtūnāṃ pratiṣṭhityā atho ṛtūnām eva tad rūpaṃ kriyate ṣaḍ u puruṣā yān agnir anuvihriyate
(PB 10.12.10) yad idaṃ bahudhāgnir vihriyate tad asāv ādityaḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ pratyaṅ tasmād ete devate vibhaktim ānaśāte nāto 'nyā kā cana
(PB 11.1.1) stomo yujyate sattriyebhyo ' harbhyaḥ pratnavatībhiś copavatībhiś ca
(PB 11.1.2) yat pratnavatyo upavatībhyaḥ pūrvā yujyante brahma tat pūrvaṃ kṣatrād yujyate brahma hi pūrvaṃ kṣatram
(PB 11.1.3) manas tat pūrvaṃ vāco yujyate mano hi yad dhi manasābhigacchati tad vācā vadati
(PB 11.1.4) bṛhat tat pūrvaṃ rathantarād yujyate bṛhad dhi pūrvaṃ rathantarād vijityā tu vai rathantaraṃ pūrvaṃ yogam ānaśe
(PB 11.1.5) sambhāryās tṛcā bhavanti yathāśiṣṭhān vahiṣṭhān sambhared evam evaitān sambharanti gatyai
(PB 11.1.6) nava bhavanti navāhasya yuktyā ṛcarcaivāhar yunakti yathāprārthasya śamyā avadadhyād evam evaitan navāhasya śamyā avadadhāti gatyai
(PB 11.1.7) trivṛd eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya
body.translated_text: (PB 10.12.1) The <s>Bharadvājāyanas</s> indeed sat in a sacrificial session (<s>sattra</s>). They were asked: 'What did you accomplish on the first day?' 'We went forth.' 'On the second?' 'We merely made an abode.' 'On the third?' 'We bathed all around.' 'On the fourth?' 'We placed that which is upon that which is.' 'On the fifth?' 'We severed the vital breaths.' 'On the sixth?' 'We arrived at this very [place].'

body.text:
(PB 11.2.1) ubhābhyāṃ vai rūpābhyāṃ bahiṣpavamānyo yujyante yatsāmā stomo bhavati tad ājyeṣu
(PB 11.2.2) nirāhāvanty ājyāni bhavanti yuktam eva tair āhvayati
(PB 11.2.3) agna āyāhi vītaya ā no mitrāvaruṇāyāhi suṣamā hi ta indrāgnī āgataṃ sutam iti rāthantaram eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati stomaḥ iti
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.2.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamānīya</s> chants are yoked with both forms: whatever <s>sāman</s> (chant melody) the <s>stoma</s> (chant pattern) takes, that is used in the <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblation) chants.
(PB 11.2.2) The <s>ājya</s> chants are without the <s>āhāva</s> (call). He summons the one that has been yoked by them.
(PB 11.2.3) 'O <s>Agni</s>, come to the feast!' 'Come, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>!' 'For your pressing is good!' '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>]!' — thereby one manifests the very form of the <s>Rathantara</s> [chant]. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.3.1) pra somāso vipaścita iti gāyatrī bhavati pretyā abhidroṇāni babhrava ity abhikrāntyai stutā indrāya vāyava iti saṃskṛtyai pra soma deva vītaya iti pretyai pra tu draveti pretyai pra vā etenāhnā yanti
(PB 11.3.2) gāyatraṃ bhavati
(PB 11.3.3) yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.3.4) āśvaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.3.5) aśvo vai bhūtvā prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa prājāyata bahur abhavat prajāyate bahur bhavaty āśvena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.3.6) ekākṣaraṃ nidhanam upayanti rathantarasyānativādāya
(PB 11.3.7) anativādy enaṃ bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 11.3.8) somasāma bhavati
(PB 11.3.9) yathā vā imā anyā oṣadhayaḥ evaṃ soma āsīt sa tapo 'tapyata sa etat somasāmāpaśyat tena rājyamādhipatyam agacchad yaśo 'bhavad rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati yaśo bhavati somasāmnā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.3.10) yaudhājayaṃ bhavati yad eva yaudhājayasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.3.11) auśanaṃ yad auśanasya stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.3.1) 'The <s>Soma</s> juices, full of wisdom' — this is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> (meter), for the purpose of going forth. 'O <s>Soma</s> drops, tawny ones, to the vessels' — for the purpose of advance. 'For <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, praised' — for the purpose of consecration. 'O divine <s>Soma</s>, go forth to the feast' — for going forth. 'Go forth indeed' — for going forth. By this day they indeed go forth.
(PB 11.3.2) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> [pattern].
(PB 11.3.3) Whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (ritual explanation) of the <s>Gāyatra</s> [applies here].
(PB 11.3.4) The horse-related

body.text:
(PB 11.4.1) abhi tvā śūra no nu ma ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rathantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.4.2) kayā naś citra ābhuvad iti kavatyas tena prājāpatyāḥ ko hi prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai
(PB 11.4.3) taṃ vo dasmam ṛtīṣahaṃ vasor mandānam andhaso 'bhivatsaṃ na svasareṣu dhenava ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rathantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.4.4) indraṃ gīrbhir havāmaha iti havanta evainam
(PB 11.4.5) tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti stomo vai taro yajño vidadvasuḥ stomena vai yajño yujyate yat tarobhir vo vidadvasum ity āha yajñam eva tad yunakti
(PB 11.4.6) rathantaraṃ bhavati brahma vai rathantaraṃ brahma prāyaṇīyam ahar brahmaṇa eva tad brahmākramya prayanti
(PB 11.4.7) iyaṃ vai rathantaram asyām eva pratiṣṭhāya sattram āsate
(PB 11.4.8) vāmadevyaṃ bhavati paśavo vai vāmadevyaṃ paśūnām avaruddhyai prājāpatyaṃ vai vāmadevyaṃ prajāpatāv eva pratiṣṭhāya sattram āsate
(PB 11.4.9) naudhasaṃ bhavati brahma vai naudhasaṃ brahma prāyaṇīyam ahar brahmaṇa eva tad rahmākramante
(PB 11.4.10) kāleyaṃ bhavati samānaloke vai kāleyañ ca rathantarañ ceyaṃ vai rathantaraṃ paśavaḥ kāleyam asyāñ caiva paśuṣu ca pratiṣṭhāya sattram āsate
(PB 11.4.11) dravadiḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpaṃ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.4.1) 'We indeed [praise] you, O hero, not now' — this is an <s>abhi</s> (approach) hymn. This is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 11.4.2) 'With what, O wondrous one, have you come to us?' — these are the <s>kavatī</s> (interrogative) verses, thereby they belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>. For who is <s>Prajāpati</s>? — for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 11.4.3) 'Him, the wondrous one, conquering in truth, rejoicing in the good [<s>Soma</s>] of the vessel, like cows in their stalls toward a calf' — this is an <s>abhi</s> hymn of the <s>Rathantara</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.5.1) pra somāso madacyuta iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavṛt tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāty ayā pasvasva devayur ity eti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ pavate 'har yato harir iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bṛhad eva tad etasminn ahani yunakti tad yuktaṃ śva ārabhante pra sunvānāyāndhasa iti pravatyo bhavanti praṇinīṇyam iva hy etad ahar abhi priyāṇi pavate ca nohita ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.5.2) yajñā yajñā vo agnaya ity agner vai yajño yajña eva tad yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 11.5.3) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.5.4) saṃhitaṃ bhavati vyakṣaraṇidhanaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai pratiṣṭhāyaiva sattram āsate
(PB 11.5.5) saphaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.6) saphena vai devā imān lokān samāpnuvvan yat samāpnuvaṃs tat saphasya saphatvam imān evaitena lokān samāpya sattram āsate
(PB 11.5.7) ākṣāraṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.8) aṣṭau vā etāḥ kādughā āsaṃs tāsām (?) ekā samaśīryata sā kṛṣir abhavad ṛdhyate 'smai kṛṣau ya evaṃ veda
(PB 11.5.9) tāsu devāsurā aspardhanta te devā asurān kāmadughābhya ākṣāreṇānudanta nudate bhrātṛvyaṃ kāmadughābhya ākṣāreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.5.10) ebhyo vai lokebhyo raso 'pākrāmat taṃ prajāpatir ākṣāreṇākṣārayad yad ākṣārayat tad ākṣārasyākṣāratvam
(PB 11.5.11) tasmād yaḥ purā puṇyo bhūtvā paścāt pāpīyān syād ākṣāraṃ brahma sāma kurvītātmany eved indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam ākṣārayati
