(PB 11.5.12) januṣaikarco bhavato 'hno dhṛtyai yad vā etasyāhno 'dhṛtaṃ tad etābhyāṃ dādhāra
(PB 11.5.13) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.14) gaurīvitir vā etac chāktyo brāhmaṇo 'tiriktam apaśyat tad gaurīvitam abhavat
(PB 11.5.15) atiriktaṃ vā etad atiriktena stuvanti yad gaurīvitenāhīnāñ chavastanavad bhavaty api prajāyā upakḷptam
(PB 11.5.16) vṛṣā vā etad vājisāma vṛṣabho retodhā adya stuvanti śvaḥ prajāyate
(PB 11.5.17) anuṣṭubhi chandasāṃ kriyate 'nuṣṭub bhi chandasāṃ yoniḥ svāyām eva tad yonau reto dhatte prajātyai
(PB 11.5.18) prajāyate bahur bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 11.5.19) dvyudāsaṃ bhavaty etau vā udāsau svargasya lokasyāvasānadarśau pūrveṇa pūrvam ahaḥ saṃsthāpayanty uttareṇottaram ahar abhyativadanti
(PB 11.5.20) tad yathādaḥ pūrvedyuḥ spaṣṭaṃ tṛṇodakam anvavasyanto yanty evam eva tābhyāṃ svargaṃ lokam anvavasyanto yanti
(PB 11.5.21) gautamaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.22) sāmārṣeyavat svargāya yujyate svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.5.23) yad u caivānuṣtṭubhasya madhye nidhanasya brāhmaṇaṃ tad du caitasya
(PB 11.5.24) kāvaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.25) lokabinduḥ sāma vindate lokaṃ kāvena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.5.26) svārasu svareṇa svareṇa hi devebhyo 'ntato 'nnādyaṃ pradīyate svareṇaiva tad devebhyo 'ntato 'nnādyaṃ pra yacchati
(PB 11.5.27) yajñāyajñīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.5.28) vāg yajñāyajñīyaṃ vāci yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhito vācy eva tad yajñam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti taṃ vāco 'dhi śva ārabhante
(PB 11.5.29) trivṛd eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.5.1) '<s>Pra somāso madacyutaḥ</s>' — it is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The third pressing is indeed full of intoxication and juice — thereby he places intoxication and juice. '<s>Ayā pasvasva devayuḥ</s>' — this goes to the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this is a <s>Rāthantara</s> day. '<s>Pavate 'har yato hariḥ</s>' — this is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; he yokes the <s>Bṛhat</s> itself on this day; what is yoked, they take up the next day. '<s>Pra sunvānāyāndhasa</s>' — these are progressive, for this day is like one to be led forward. '<s>Abhi priyāṇi pavate ca nohitaḥ</s>' — the word '<s>abhi</s>' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this is a <s>Rāthantara</s> day.
(PB 11.5.2) '<s>Yajñā yajñā vo agnaye</s>' — sacrifice is indeed of <s>Agni</s>; thereby he establishes the sacrifice upon the sacrifice.
(PB 11.5.3) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> — for whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (explanatory portion) of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 11.5.4) It is in connected form, with a syllable-<s>nidhana</s> — for firm establishment. They sit in the <s>sattra</s> for firm establishment itself.
(PB 11.5.5) It has the <s>Sapha</s> (hoof-form).
(PB 11.5.6) By the <s>Sapha</s> the gods encompassed these worlds. Because they encompassed them, that is the <s>sapha</s>-nature of the <s>Sapha</s>. Having encompassed these worlds with this, they sit in the <s>sattra</s>.
(PB 11.5.7) It has the <s>Ākṣāra</s> (dripping-form).
(PB 11.5.8) There were eight wish-fulfilling cows. One of them crumbled away and became agriculture. Agriculture prospers for him — he who knows thus.
(PB 11.5.9) The gods and <s>asuras</s> contended over these. The gods drove the <s>asuras</s> from the wish-fulfilling cows with the <s>Ākṣāra</s>. He drives his rival from the wish-fulfilling cows — he who has praised with the <s>Ākṣāra</s>.
(PB 11.5.10) The essence departed from these worlds. <s>Prajāpati</s> caused it to flow back (<s>ākṣārayat</s>) by the <s>Ākṣāra</s>. Because he caused it to flow, that is the <s>ākṣāra</s>-nature of the <s>Ākṣāra</s>.
(PB 11.5.11) Therefore, one who was formerly meritorious but has subsequently become sinful should perform the <s>Ākṣāra</s> as the <s>Brahma-sāman</s> — he thereby causes vital power, vigor, and essence to flow into his own self.
(PB 11.5.12) The single-verse hymns at birth serve for upholding the day. Whatever of this day was not upheld, that is upheld by these two.
(PB 11.5.13) It has the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 11.5.14) <s>Gaurīviti</s> the <s>Śāktya</s> <s>brāhmaṇa</s> perceived the surplus — that became the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 11.5.15) This is the surplus; they praise with the surplus, namely with the <s>Gaurīvita</s>. In the <s>Ahīna</s> ceremonies, it comes to be like a breast, suited for offspring.
(PB 11.5.16) This is indeed a bull among <s>Vāji-sāmans</s> — a bull, a seed-placer. Today they praise; tomorrow offspring is born.
(PB 11.5.17) It is rendered in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is indeed the womb of the meters. Thereby he places seed in its own womb — for procreation.
(PB 11.5.18) He is procreated and becomes abundant — he who knows thus.
(PB 11.5.19) It has the two <s>Udāsa</s> portions. These two <s>Udāsas</s> are indeed the boundary-markers of the heavenly world. By the former they conclude the former day; by the latter they surpass the latter day.
(PB 11.5.20) Just as those going after cattle and water seen on the previous day follow along, even so by these two they follow along to the heavenly world.
(PB 11.5.21) It has the <s>Gautama</s>.
(PB 11.5.22) With a <s>sāman</s> connected to a <s>ṛṣi</s> lineage, one is yoked to heaven. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 11.5.23) Whatever is the explanatory portion of the <s>nidhana</s> of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> in the middle, that is also the explanation of this.
(PB 11.5.24) It has the <s>Kāva</s>.
(PB 11.5.25) The <s>Lokabindu</s> <s>sāman</s> finds a world — he who has praised with the <s>Kāva</s> obtains a world.
(PB 11.5.26) In the <s>Svāra</s> portions, by the <s>svara</s> (tonal accent) — for by the <s>svara</s> food-eating is given to the gods at the very end. Thereby he gives food-eating to the gods at the end by the <s>svara</s>.
(PB 11.5.27) It has the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>.
(PB 11.5.28) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is speech. The sacrifice is established in speech. Thereby they establish the sacrifice in speech at the very end. From that speech they take up the next day.
(PB 11.5.29) The <s>stoma</s> is <s>trivṛt</s> (nine-fold) only — for brilliance and brahmanical splendor.

body.text:
(PB 11.6.1) pratipad bhavati
(PB 11.6.2) samārabhate dvirātrasyāvrisraṃsāya
(PB 11.6.3) pavasvendo vṛṣāsuta ity anurūpyo bhavati vṛṣāvad vā eta aindraṃ traiṣṭubham ahar yat dvitīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 11.6.4) pūrvam u tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam
(PB 11.6.5) anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 11.6.6) stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 11.6.7) vṛṣaṇvantas tṛcā bhavatīndriyasya vīryasyāvarudhyai
(PB 11.6.8) tṛca uttamo bhavati
(PB 11.6.9) yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 11.6.10) pañdadaśa eva stomo bhavati
(PB 11.6.11) ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhati ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.6.1) There is an introductory verse (<s>pratipad</s>).
(PB 11.6.2) He commences — so that the two-day rite does not fall apart.
(PB 11.6.3) '<s>Pavasva indo vṛṣā sutaḥ</s>' — it corresponds in form. This second day is indeed a bull-like <s>Aindra</s> (pertaining to <s>Indra</s>) <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> (in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>) day — that is what it addresses.
(PB 11.6.4) It echoes the previous form with the subsequent form. Because it echoes the previous form with the subsequent form, that is the corresponding nature (<s>anurūpatva</s>) of the <s>Anurūpa</s> (echo-verse).
(PB 11.6.5) A son corresponding to him is born — he who knows thus.
(PB 11.6.6) The <s>stotrīya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> are two <s>tṛcas</s> (verse-triplets) — for the obtainment of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(PB 11.6.7) The <s>tṛcas</s> contain the word '<s>vṛṣan</s>' (bull) — for the obtainment of vital power and vigor.
(PB 11.6.8) The last one is a <s>tṛca</s>.
(PB 11.6.9) By whatever breath they proceed, by that they rise up.
(PB 11.6.10) The <s>stoma</s> is <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold) only.
(PB 11.6.11) Thereby he becomes firmly established in power and vigor. Power and vigor are the <s>pañcadaśa</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.7.1) ubhābhyāṃ vai rūpābhyāṃ bahiṣpavamānyo yujyante yatsāmā stomo bhavati tad ājyeṣu
(PB 11.7.2) nirāhopasthitāny ājyāni bhavanti
(PB 11.7.3) agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha indram id gāthino bṛhad indro agnā namo bṛhad iti bārhatam eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.7.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (outer purification chants) are yoked with both forms. Whatever <s>sāman</s> becomes the <s>stoma</s>, that applies in the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-offering chants).
(PB 11.7.2) The <s>ājya</s> chants are without the <s>nirāha</s> and <s>upasthita</s> (ritual approaches).
(PB 11.7.3) '<s>Agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe</s>,' '<s>Mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe</s>,' '<s>Indram id gāthino bṛhat</s>,' '<s>Indro agnā namo bṛhat</s>' — thereby the <s>Bārhata</s> (pertaining to <s>Bṛhat</s>) form is made to shine forth. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.8.1) vṛṣā pavasva dhārayeti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
(PB 11.8.2) vṛṣaṇvatyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.8.3) punānas soma dhārayeti dhṛtyai
(PB 11.8.4) vṛṣā śoṇo abhikanikradad gā iti
(PB 11.8.5) vṛṣaṇvatyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa samṛddhā vṛṣaṇvad vā etad aindraṃ traiṣṭubham ahar yat dvitīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 11.8.6) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.8.7) yauktāśvaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.8.8) yuktāśvo va āṅgirasaḥ śiśū jātau viparyaharat tasmān mantro 'pākrāmat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad yauktāśvam apaśyat taṃ mantra upāvartata tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sama yauktāśvaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 11.8.9) āyāsye bhavataḥ
(PB 11.8.10) ayāsyo vā āṅgirasa ādityānāṃ dīkṣitānām annādyam āśnāt taṃ śug ārcchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa ete āyāsye apaśyat tābhyāṃ śucam apāhatāpa śucaṃ hata āyāsyābhyāṃ tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.8.11) ebhyo vai lokebhyo vṛṣṭir apākrāmat tām ayāsya āyāsyābhyām acyāvayat cyāvayati vṛṣṭim āyāsyābhyāṃ tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.8.12) annādyaṃ vāva tad ebhyo lokebhyo 'pākrāmat tad ayāsya āyāsyābhyām acyāvayat cyāvayaty annādyam āyāsyābhyāṃ tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.8.13) vāsiṣṭhaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.8.14) vasiṣṭho vā etena vaiḍavaḥ stutvāñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.8.1) '<s>Vṛṣā pavasva dhāraya</s>' — it is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, for upholding the day.
(PB 11.8.2) The verses contain '<s>vṛṣan</s>' (bull), in the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for this is a <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> day.
(PB 11.8.3) '<s>Punānas soma dhāraya</s>' — for upholding.
(PB 11.8.4) '<s>Vṛṣā śoṇo abhikanikradad gāḥ</s>' —
(PB 11.8.5) The verses contain '<s>vṛṣan</s>', in the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, complete and bull-like. This second day is indeed a bull-like <s>Aindra Traiṣṭubha</s> day — that is what it addresses.
(PB 11.8.6) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> — for whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 11.8.7) It has the <s>Yauktāśva</s>.
(PB 11.8.8) <s>Yuktāśva</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> switched around his two newly-born children. The sacred formula departed from him. He performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity). He perceived this <s>Yauktāśva</s> (sāman). The formula returned to him. Whatever desire one had at that time — the <s>Yauktāśva</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 11.8.9) It has the two <s>Āyāsya</s> (sāmans).
(PB 11.8.10) <s>Ayāsya</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> ate the food-offering of the <s>Ādityas</s> when they were consecrated. Grief came upon him. He performed <s>tapas</s>. He perceived these two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans. By them he struck away grief. He strikes away grief — he who has praised with the two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans.
(PB 11.8.11) Rain departed from these worlds. <s>Ayāsya</s> caused it to flow by the two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans. He causes rain to flow — he who has praised with the two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans.
(PB 11.8.12) Food-eating indeed departed from these worlds. <s>Ayāsya</s> caused it to flow by the two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans. He causes food-eating to flow — he who has praised with the two <s>Āyāsya</s> sāmans.
(PB 11.8.13) It has the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>.
(PB 11.8.14) <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> the <s>Vaiḍava</s>, having praised with this, directly perceived the heavenly world — for a vision of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.9.1) tvām id dhi havāmaha iti tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.9.2) abhipravaḥ surādhasam iti yuñjate vai pūrveṇāhnā hy etena prayanti
(PB 11.9.3) tvām idā hyo nara ity adya caiva hyaś ca samārabhate dvirātrasyāvisraṃsāya
(PB 11.9.4) bṛhad bhavati varṣma vai bṛhad varṣma dvitīyam ahar varṣmaṇa eva tad varṣmākramante
(PB 11.9.5) śyetaṃ bhavati sāmnorvāho yajñasya santatyai
(PB 11.9.6) mādhucchandasaṃ bhavati sāmārṣeyavat svargāya yujyate svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.9.7) ūrdhveḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpaṃ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.9.1) '<s>Tvām id dhi havāmahe</s>' — the word '<s>tvam</s>' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this is a <s>Bārhata</s> day.
(PB 11.9.2) '<s>Abhipravaḥ surādhasam</s>' — they yoke with the former day, for by this they proceed.
(PB 11.9.3) '<s>Tvām idā hyo nara</s>' — 'today' and 'yesterday' — he commences, so that the two-day rite does not fall apart.
(PB 11.9.4) It has the <s>Bṛhat</s>. The <s>Bṛhat</s> is indeed height; the second day is height. By height itself they advance upon height.
(PB 11.9.5) It has the <s>Śyeta</s> — for the yoke-animal of the <s>sāman</s>, for the continuation of the sacrifice.
(PB 11.9.6) It has the <s>Mādhucchandasa</s>. With a <s>sāman</s> connected to a <s>ṛṣi</s> lineage, one is yoked to heaven. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 11.9.7) The <s>Iḍā</s> portion is upward — for such is indeed the form of this day. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.10.1) yas te mado vareṇya iti gāyatrī bhavati
(PB 11.10.2) madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 11.10.3) pavasva madhumattama iti pavanta iva hy etenāhnā madhumattama ity annaṃ vai madhv annādyam eva tad yajamāne dadhāti
(PB 11.10.4) indram accha sutā ima itīndriyasya vīryasyāvarudhyai
(PB 11.10.5) ayaṃ pūṣā rayir bhaga iti
(PB 11.10.6) anuṣṭubhaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.10.7) vṛṣāmatīnāṃ pavate vicakṣaṇa iti jagatyaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 11.10.8) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.10.9) hāviṣmataṃ bhavati
(PB 11.10.10) haviṣmāṃś ca vai haviṣkṛc cāṅgirasāv āstāṃ dvitīye 'hani haviṣmān arādhnon navame 'hani haviṣkṛt
(PB 11.10.11) ayaṃ haviṣmān ity eva jātam ahar jātaṃ somaṃ prāha devebhyaḥ sāmnaivāsmā āśiṣam āśāste sāma hi saty āśīḥ
(PB 11.10.12) śaṅku bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai yad vā adhṛtaṃ śaṅkunā tad dādhāra
(PB 11.10.13) tad u sīdantīyam iy āhur etena vai prajāpatir ūrdhva imān lokān asīdad yad asīdat tat sīdantīyasya sīdantīyatvam ūrdhva imān lokān sīdati sīdantīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.10.14) sujñānaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.10.15) svarvad vai rāthantaraṃ rūpaṃ svarṇadhanaṃ bārhatam
(PB 11.10.16) svarṇadhanaṃ bhavati tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 11.10.17) pluvau vā etāv upohante svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 11.10.18) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 11.10.19) krauñcaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.10.20) vāg vai krauñcaṃ vāg dvādaśāho vācy eva tad vācā stuvate yajñasya prabhūtyai
(PB 11.10.21) yāmaṃ bhavati
(PB 11.10.22) etena vai yamo 'napajayyam amuṣya lokasyādhipatyam āśnutānapajayyam amuṣya lokasyādhipatyam aśnute yāmena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 11.10.23) etena vai yamī yamaṃ svargaṃ lokam agamayat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.10.1) 'Your intoxication, O choiceworthy one' — this is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter.
(PB 11.10.2) The third pressing is intoxicating and juicy. It places intoxication and juice.
(PB 11.10.3) 'Purify yourself, O most honied one' — for they purify as it were by this day. 'Most honied' — honey is food. He places food-eating in the sacrificer.
(PB 11.10.4) 'These pressed juices go toward <s>Indra</s>' — for the attainment of vital power and vigor.
(PB 11.10.5) 'This <s>Pūṣan</s> is wealth, <s>Bhaga</s>'
(PB 11.10.6) These are truly <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses in the form of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for this day is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> form.
(PB 11.10.7) 'The discerning one purifies among the bull-mothers' — these are truly <s>Jagatī</s> verses in the form of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for this day is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> form.
(PB 11.10.8) The <s>Gāyatra</s> (Sāman) is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.
(PB 11.10.9) The <s>Hāviṣmata</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 11.10.10) <s>Haviṣmat</s> and <s>Haviṣkṛt</s> were two <s>Aṅgirasas</s>. On the second day <s>Haviṣmat</s> succeeded; on the ninth day <s>Haviṣkṛt</s>.
(PB 11.10.11) 'This <s>Haviṣmat</s>' — he announces to the gods the day that has been born and the <s>Soma</s> that has been born. By the <s>Sāman</s> he wishes him a blessing, for the <s>Sāman</s> is indeed a blessing.
(PB 11.10.12) The <s>Śaṅku</s> (Sāman) is used — for the support of the day. Whatever was unsupported, the <s>Śaṅku</s> supported.
(PB 11.10.13) They call it the <s>Sīdantīya</s>. By this, <s>Prajāpati</s> sat upon these worlds from above. Because he sat, that is the <s>Sīdantīya</s>-nature of the <s>Sīdantīya</s>. He who has praised with the <s>Sīdantīya</s> sits upon these worlds from above.
(PB 11.10.14) The <s>Sujñāna</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 11.10.15) The <s>Rāthantara</s> form is heavenly (<s>svarvat</s>); the <s>Bārhata</s> has <s>svar</s> (heaven) as its ending.
(PB 11.10.16) It has <s>svar</s> as its ending, for such is the form of this day.
(PB 11.10.17) These two float upward together — for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 11.10.18) The <s>Gaurīvita</s> (Sāman) is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Gaurīvita</s> applies here.
(PB 11.10.19) The <s>Krauñca</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 11.10.20) Speech is the <s>Krauñca</s>. Speech is the twelve-day rite. By speech they praise with speech — for the abundance of the sacrifice.
(PB 11.10.21) The <s>Yāma</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 11.10.22) By this, <s>Yama</s> attained unconquerable sovereignty over that world. He who has praised with the <s>Yāma</s> attains unconquerable sovereignty over that world.
(PB 11.10.23) By this, <s>Yamī</s> led <s>Yama</s> to the heavenly world — for the recognition of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 11.11.1) ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi ta ity ehivatyai bhavanti tṛtīyasyāhna upahavāya santatyai
(PB 11.11.2) apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāya
(PB 11.11.3) evāhy asi vīrayur iti samānaṃ vadantīdam ittham asad iti
(PB 11.11.4) indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann ity avardhanta hy etarhi yajamānam evaitayā vardhanti
(PB 11.11.5) sākam aśvaṃ bhavaty ukthānām abhijityā abhikrāntyai
(PB 11.11.6) etena hy agra ukthāny adhyajayann etenābhyakrāman
(PB 11.11.7) āmahīyavaṃ bhavati kḷptiś cānnādyañ ca samānaṃ vadantīṣu kriyata idam ittham asad iti
(PB 11.11.8) kṣatraṃ vā etad ahar abhinirvadati yat pañcadaśaṃ yad gāyatrīṣu brahmasāma bhavati brahma caiva tat kṣatrañ ca sayujī karoti brahmaiva kṣatrasya purastān nidadhati brahmaṇe kṣatrañ ca viśañ cānuge karoti
(PB 11.11.9) brahma vai pūrvam ahaḥ kṣatraṃ dvitīyaṃ yad gāyatrīṣu brahma sāma bhavati brahma tad yaśasārdhayati brahma hi gāyatrī
(PB 11.11.10) tad u samānaṃ vadantīṣu kriyate samṛddhyai
(PB 11.11.11) āṣṭādaṃṣṭre bhavataḥ
(PB 11.11.12) aiyāhā iti vā indro vṛtram ahann aiyādohoveti nyagṛhṇād vārtraghne sāmanī vīryavatī
(PB 11.11.13) ojo evaitābhyāṃ vīryam avarundhe
(PB 11.11.14) pañcadaśa eva stomo bhavaty ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhaty ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 11.11.1) 'Come, let me tell you' — these become the <s>Ehivatī</s> verses, for the invitation and continuity of the third day.
(PB 11.11.2) The <s>Uktha</s> chants are as if a severed branch of the sacrifice. Since he goes — for smoothness.
(PB 11.11.3) 'Thus indeed you are, O heroic one' — they speak the same; 'This is thus' they say.
(PB 11.11.4) 'All have strengthened <s>Indra</s>' — for they increased at that time. They strengthen the sacrificer with this.
(PB 11.11.5) The <s>Sākam-aśva</s> (Sāman) is used — for the conquering and overcoming of the <s>Uktha</s> chants.
(PB 11.11.6) For by this they first conquered the <s>Uktha</s> chants, by this they overcame.
(PB 11.11.7) The <s>Āmahīyava</s> (Sāman) is used — arrangement and food-eating are made when they speak the same: 'This is thus.'
(PB 11.11.8) This <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold) day produces <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power). When the <s>Brahmasāman</s> is on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, it makes <s>Brahman</s> (sacred power) and <s>Kṣatra</s> united. It places <s>Brahman</s> before <s>Kṣatra</s>. It makes <s>Kṣatra</s> and <s>Viś</s> (people) follow <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 11.11.9) The first day is <s>Brahman</s>; the second is <s>Kṣatra</s>. When the <s>Brahmasāman</s> is on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, it strengthens <s>Brahman</s> with glory, for the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 11.11.10) It is performed when they speak the same — for prosperity.
(PB 11.11.11) The <s>Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra</s> Sāmans are used.
(PB 11.11.12) With 'aiyāhā' <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>; with 'aiyādohovā' he pressed him down. These two <s>Vṛtra</s>-slaying <s>Sāmans</s> are powerful.
(PB 11.11.13) With these two he attains might and vigor.
(PB 11.11.14) The <s>stoma</s> is the <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold). It thereby becomes established in might and vigor, for might and vigor are the <s>pañcadaśa</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.1.1) davidyutaty āruceti tṛtīyasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
(PB 12.1.2) davidyutatī vai gāyatrī pariṣṭobhantī triṣṭub gavāśīr jagatī trīṇi rūpāṇi samārabhate trirātrasyāvisraṃsāya
(PB 12.1.3) ete asṛgram indava ity anurūpo bhavati
(PB 12.1.4) eta iti vai prajāpatir devān asṛjatāsṛgram iti manuṣyān indava iti pit.ṛṃs tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.1.5) pūrvam u caiva tad repam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpam apareṇa rūpaṇo 'nuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.1.6) stotrīyānurūpau tṛco bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 12.1.7) rājā medhābhir īyate pavamāno manāv adhy antarikṣeṇa yātava iti
(PB 12.1.8) antarikṣadevatyas tṛco bhavaty antarikṣadevatyam etad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.1.9) pañcarcau bhavati pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅktam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.1.10) tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhy upayānti
(PB 12.1.11) saptadaśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.1.1) 'Flashing forth with brightness' becomes the opening verse of the third day.
(PB 12.1.2) 'Flashing' is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the embellishment is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; 'milk of cows' is the <s>Jagatī</s>. It takes hold of three forms — for the non-dissolution of the three-night rite.
(PB 12.1.3) 'These drops have flowed forth' becomes the <s>Anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse).
(PB 12.1.4) By 'these' <s>Prajāpati</s> created the gods; by 'they flowed forth' the humans; by 'drops' the ancestors. He addresses that very thing.
(PB 12.1.5) The earlier form is addressed by the later form. Since the earlier form is addressed by the later form, that is the <s>Anurūpa</s>-nature of the <s>Anurūpa</s>. A son conforming to him is born to one who knows thus.
(PB 12.1.6) The <s>Stotrīya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> are in groups of three — for the attainment of <s>prāṇa</s> (inhalation) and <s>apāna</s> (exhalation).
(PB 12.1.7) 'The king moves with wisdom, the purifying one above the mind; going through the atmosphere.'
(PB 12.1.8) The <s>tṛca</s> (group of three) has the atmosphere as its deity. This third day has the atmosphere as its deity. He addresses that very thing.
(PB 12.1.9) It is in a group of five. The <s>Paṅkti</s> meter has five feet. Food is of the <s>Paṅkti</s>. For the attainment of food-eating.
(PB 12.1.10) The last is a group of three. They approach that very breath by which they go forth.
(PB 12.1.11) The <s>stoma</s> is the <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold) — for establishment and procreation.

body.text:
(PB 12.2.1) agnināgniḥ samidhyata ity āgreyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.2.2) pūrve eva tad ahanī samiddhe tṛtīyam ahar abhisamindhe
(PB 12.2.3) mitraṃ huve pūtadakṣam iti rāthantaram maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 12.2.4) huva iti vai rāthantaraṃ rūpam
(PB 12.2.5) rathantaram etat parokṣaṃ yad vairūpaṃ rāthantaram eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati
(PB 12.2.6) indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣusa ity aindram
(PB 12.2.7) sam iva vā ime lokā dadṛśire 'ntarikṣadevatyam etad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.2.8) tā huve yayor idam iti rāthantaram aindrāgnam
(PB 12.2.9) huva iti vai rāthantaraṃ rūpaṃ rathantaram etat parokṣaṃ yad vairūpaṃ rāthantaram eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.2.1) '<s>Agni</s> is kindled by <s>Agni</s>' — the <s>Ājya</s> (chant) is of <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 12.2.2) The first two days having been kindled, it kindles the third day further.
(PB 12.2.3) 'I call <s>Mitra</s> of pure skill' — this is the <s>Rāthantara</s>, belonging to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 12.2.4) 'I call' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 12.2.5) The <s>Vairūpa</s> is the <s>Rathantara</s> in hidden form. It reveals the <s>Rāthantara</s> form.
(PB 12.2.6) 'With <s>Indra</s> let us look together' — this belongs to <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 12.2.7) These worlds have as it were looked together. This third day has the atmosphere as its deity. He addresses that very thing.
(PB 12.2.8) 'I call those two under whose rule is this' — this is the <s>Rāthantara</s>, belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 12.2.9) 'I call' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>. The <s>Vairūpa</s> is the <s>Rathantara</s> in hidden form. It reveals the <s>Rāthantara</s> form. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.3.1) uccā te jātam andhasa iti gāyatrī bhavati
(PB 12.3.2) udvad vā etad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.3.3) andhasvatī bhavaty ahar vā andho 'hna ārambhaḥ
(PB 12.3.4) abhi somāsa āyava iti
(PB 12.3.5) abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayoḥ saha rūpam upaity ubhau hi varṇāv etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.3.6) tisro vāca īrayati pravahnir iti tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ tena tṛtīyam ahar ārabhante
(PB 12.3.7) triṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa jāgataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.3.8) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.3.9) vaiṣṭambhaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.3.10) ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā vaiṣṭambhair vyaṣṭabhnuvaṃs tad vaiṣṭambhasya vaiṣṭambhatvam
(PB 12.3.11) diśa iti nidhanam upayanti diśāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 12.3.12) paurūmadgaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.3.13) ahar vā etad avlīyamānaṃ tad rakṣāṃsy anvasacanta tasmād devāḥ paurūmadgena rakṣāṃsy apāghnann apa pāpmānaṃ hate paurūmadgena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.3.14) devāś ca vāsurāś cāspardhanta te devā asurāṇāṃ paurūmadgena puro 'majjayan yat puro 'majjayaṃs tasmāt paurūmadgaṃ pāpmānam evaitena bhrātṛvyaṃ majjayati
(PB 12.3.15) gautamaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.3.16) yad eva gautamasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.3.17) ubhayataḥ stotraṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 12.3.18) antarikṣaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.3.19) antarikṣadevatyam etad ahar yat tṛtīyam antarikṣa eva tad antarikṣeṇa stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 12.3.20) āṣkāraṇidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.3.21) as iti vai rāthantaraṃ rūpaṃ has iti bārhataṃ tṛtīyam eva tad rūpam upayanti samṛdhyai
(PB 12.3.22) aṅgirasāṃ saṃkrośo bhavati
(PB 12.3.23) etena vā aṅgirasaḥ saṃkrośamānāḥ svargaṃ lokam āpan svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.3.1) 'High-born from the <s>Soma</s> plant is yours' — it is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter.
(PB 12.3.2) The third day is indeed elevated. He addresses that very quality.
(PB 12.3.3) It contains the word 'plant' (<s>andhas</s>). The day is indeed the <s>andhas</s> (Soma plant); the day is the starting point.
(PB 12.3.4) 'The <s>Soma</s> juices, O descendants of <s>Āyu</s>.'
(PB 12.3.5) '<s>Abhi</s>' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>; '<s>bṛhat</s>' is of the <s>Bṛhat</s>. He approaches the form of both together, for both forms belong to this day.
(PB 12.3.6) 'He sends forth three utterances, the conveyor' — this is the form of the third day. With this they take hold of the third day.
(PB 12.3.7) The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses are true, being of the <s>Jagatī</s> form, for this day belongs to the <s>Jagatī</s>.
(PB 12.3.8) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> form — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.
(PB 12.3.9) It is the <s>Vaiṣṭambha</s> (propping chant).
(PB 12.3.10) This day was slipping away. The gods propped it up with the <s>Vaiṣṭambha</s> chants. That is the nature of the <s>Vaiṣṭambha</s> as 'propping.'
(PB 12.3.11) They approach the ending with 'the directions' — for the support of the directions.
(PB 12.3.12) It is the <s>Paurūmadga</s> (chant).
(PB 12.3.13) This day was slipping away, and the <s>rakṣas</s> (demons) followed after it. Therefore the gods struck away the <s>rakṣas</s> with the <s>Paurūmadga</s>. He who praises with the <s>Paurūmadga</s> strikes away evil.
(PB 12.3.14) The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were in competition. The gods submerged the cities of the <s>Asuras</s> with the <s>Paurūmadga</s>. Because they submerged the cities, therefore the <s>Paurūmadga</s> — with it he submerges the evil rival.
(PB 12.3.15) It is the <s>Gautama</s> (chant).
(PB 12.3.16) Whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gautama</s> applies here.
(PB 12.3.17) There is praise on both sides — for such is the form of this day.
(PB 12.3.18) It belongs to the atmosphere.
(PB 12.3.19) This third day has the atmosphere as its deity. They praise with the atmosphere for the sake of firm establishment.
(PB 12.3.20) It is the <s>Kāṇva</s> (chant) with the <s>āṣkāra</s> ending.
(PB 12.3.21) 'As' is the <s>Rathantara</s> form; 'has' is the <s>Bṛhat</s> form. They thus approach the form of the third day, for prosperity.
(PB 12.3.22) It is the clamor of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.
(PB 12.3.23) With this, the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, clamoring, reached the heavenly world — for the proclamation of the heavenly world. He who has praised with this <s>stoma</s> does not fall from the heavenly world.

body.text:
(PB 12.4.1) yady āva indra te śatam iti śatavatyo bhavanti
(PB 12.4.2) śatavad vai paśūnāṃ rūpaṃ sahasravat paśūnām evaitābhī rūpam avarūndhe
(PB 12.4.3) vayaṅ ghatvā sutāvanta iti satobṛhatyo varṣīyaś chanda ākramate 'napabhraṃśāya
(PB 12.4.4) taraṇir it siṣāsati vājaṃ purandhyā yujā/ āva indraṃ puruhūtaṃ na me girety āvad akṣaram uddhatam iva vai tṛtīyam ahar yad eva tāvad akṣaraṃ bhavaty ahar evaitena pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 12.4.5) pañcanidhanaṃ vairūpaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati diśāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 12.4.6) pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅktam annam annāghasyāvarūdhyai
(PB 12.4.7) diśāṃ vā etat sāma yad vairūpaṃ diśo hy evaitenābhivadati
(PB 12.4.8) atha yat pañcanidhanaṃ tenartūnāṃ pañca hy ṛtavaḥ
(PB 12.4.9) ṛtubhiś ca vā ime lokā digbhiś cāvṛtās teṣv evobhayeṣu yajamānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati yajamānaṃ vā anupratitiṣṭhantam udgātā pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ vidvān vairūpeṇodgāyati
(PB 12.4.10) digvad bhavati bhrātṛvyasyāpanutyai
(PB 12.4.11) diśaṃ viśam iti nidhanam upayanti diśāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 12.4.12) has ity upariṣṭād diśāṃ nidhanam upayanti tena bārhatam
(PB 12.4.13) rāthantaro vā ayaṃ loko bārhato 'sāv ubhe eva tad bṛhadrathantarayo rūpeṇāparādhnoti
(PB 12.4.14) anaḍvāhau vā etau devayānau yajamānasya yad bṛhadrathantare tāv eva tad yunakti svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 12.4.15) aśvavad bhavati prajātyai
(PB 12.4.16) yathā maṇḍūka āṭ karoty evaṃ nidhanam upayanty ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 12.4.17) dvādaśa vairūpāṇi bhavanti dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 12.4.18) virūpaḥ saṃvatsaro virūpam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.4.19) mahāvaiṣṭambhaṃ brahmasāma bhavaty annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.4.20) yadā vai puruṣo 'nnam atty athāntarato viṣṭabdhaḥ
(PB 12.4.21) diśa iti nidhanam upayanti diśāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 12.4.22) sato bṛhatīṣu stuvanti pūrvayor ahnoḥ pratyudyamāya
(PB 12.4.23) rauravam acchāvākasāma bhavati
(PB 12.4.24) agnir vai rūro rūdro 'gniḥ
(PB 12.4.25) agnir vā etasya paśūn apakramayati yasya paśavo 'pakrāmanty agnir eva tasya paśūn abhikramayati yasya paśavo 'bhikrāmanti
(PB 12.4.26) abhy abhy evāsya paśavaḥ krāmanti ya evaṃ vidvān rauraveṇa stuvate
(PB 12.4.27) pariṣṭubdheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpaṃ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.4.1) 'If, O <s>Indra</s>, a hundred were yours' — they contain the word 'hundred.'
(PB 12.4.2) 'Hundred' is indeed the form of cattle, 'thousand' is of cattle. With these he secures the form of cattle.
(PB 12.4.3) 'We who have pressed <s>Soma</s> for you' — they are <s>Satobṛhatī</s> verses. He steps into a greater meter, to avoid falling away.
(PB 12.4.4) 'The swift one seeks to win the prize, with wisdom as his companion. <s>Indra</s> of many invocations — not through my songs does he' — the syllable '<s>āva</s>' is raised up, as it were. The third day is raised up. When there is such a syllable, he establishes the day with it.
(PB 12.4.5) The <s>Vairūpa</s> (chant) with five endings is the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) — for the support of the directions.
(PB 12.4.6) Five-footed is the <s>Paṅkti</s> (fivefold meter). Food belongs to the <s>Paṅkti</s> — for the securing of food.
(PB 12.4.7) The <s>Vairūpa</s> is indeed the <s>Sāman</s> of the directions, for with it he addresses the directions.
(PB 12.4.8) And because it has five endings, thereby it relates to the seasons, for the seasons are five.
(PB 12.4.9) These worlds are enclosed by both seasons and directions. He establishes the sacrificer in both of these. The <s>Udgātṛ</s> is established following the sacrificer who is being established — he who, knowing this, sings the <s>Udgītha</s> with the <s>Vairūpa</s>.
(PB 12.4.10) It contains a directional element — for the repelling of the rival.
(PB 12.4.11) 'The direction, the people' — they approach the ending — for the support of the directions.
(PB 12.4.12) With 'has' they approach the ending above the directions — thereby it is related to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 12.4.13) This world belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>, that world to the <s>Bṛhat</s>. He thus does not fail with respect to the form of both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 12.4.14) The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are indeed the two divine oxen of the sacrificer. He thus yokes them for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 12.4.15) It contains a horse element — for procreation.
(PB 12.4.16) Just as a frog croaks '<s>āṭ</s>,' so they approach the ending — for the non-staleness of the rite.
(PB 12.4.17) There are twelve <s>Vairūpa</s> chants. Twelve are the months of the year. He becomes established in the year.
(PB 12.4.18) The year is manifold (<s>virūpa</s>). The manifold is for the securing of the eating of food.
(PB 12.4.19) The <s>Mahāvaiṣṭambha</s> (great propping chant) is the <s>Brahma-Sāman</s> — for the securing of the eating of food.
(PB 12.4.20) When a person eats food, he is then propped up from within.
(PB 12.4.21) They approach the ending with 'the directions' — for the support of the directions.
(PB 12.4.22) They praise with <s>Satobṛhatī</s> verses — for the counterbalancing of the two previous days.
(PB 12.4.23) The <s>Raurava</s> (chant) is the <s>Acchāvāka</s> (calling priest's) <s>Sāman</s>.
(PB 12.4.24) <s>Agni</s> is indeed <s>Ruru</s>; <s>Rudra</s> is <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 12.4.25) <s>Agni</s> causes the cattle to depart from him whose cattle depart. <s>Agni</s> causes the cattle to approach him whose cattle approach.
(PB 12.4.26) Cattle indeed approach him who, knowing this, praises with the <s>Raurava</s>.
(PB 12.4.27) Surrounded by <s>Triṣṭubh</s> — for such is the form of this day's <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.5.1) ''tisro vāca udīrata'' iti tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ tena tṛtīyam ahar ārabhante
(PB 12.5.2) udvad vā etat trivad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.5.3) ''ā sotā pariṣiñcata'' iti parivatyo bhavanti
(PB 12.5.4) anto vai tṛtīyam ahas tasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
(PB 12.5.5) ''sakhāya āniṣīdata'' ity uddhattam iva vai tṛtīyam ahar yad āha niṣīdatety ahar evaitena pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 12.5.6) ''sutāso madhumattamā'' ity anuṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa jāgataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.5.7) ''pavitraṃ te vitataṃ brahmaṇaspata'' iti
(PB 12.5.8) vitatam iva vā idam antarikṣam antareme antarikṣadevatyam etad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 12.5.9) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.5.10) pāṣṭhauhaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.5.11) paṣṭhavāḍ vā etenāṅgirasaś caturthasyāhno vācaṃ vadantīm upāśṛṇot sa ho vāg iti nidhanam upait tad asyābhyuditaṃ tad ahar avasat
(PB 12.5.12) vācaḥ sāma bhavati
(PB 12.5.13) vāg vai dvādaśāho vācy eva tad vācā stuvate yajñasya prabhūtyai
(PB 12.5.14) niṣkirīyāḥ sattram āsata te tṛtīyam ahar na prājānaṃs tān etat sāma gāyamānān vāg upāplavat tena tṛtīyam ahaḥ prājānaṃs te 'bruvann iyaṃ vāva nas tṛtīyam ahar adīdṛśad iti tṛtīyasyaivaiṣāhno dṛṣṭiḥ
(PB 12.5.15) śauktaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.5.16) śuktir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.5.17) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.5.18) tvāṣṭrīsāma bhavati
(PB 12.5.19) indraṃ vā akṣyāmayiṇaṃ bhūtāni nāsvāpayaṃs tam etena tvāṣṭrayo 'svāpayaṃs tad vāva tās tarhy akāmayanta
(PB 12.5.20) kāmasani sāma tvāṣṭrīsāma kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 12.5.21) indro vṛtrād vibhyad gāṃ prāviśat taṃ tvāṣṭrayo 'bruvaṃ janayāmeti tam etaiḥ sāmabhir ajanayaṃ jāyāmahā iti vai sattram āsate jāyanta eva
(PB 12.5.22) ariṣṭaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.5.23) devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta yaṃ devānām aghnan na sa samabhavad yam asurāṇāṃ saṃ so 'bhavat te devās tapo 'tapyanta ta etad ariṣṭam apaśyaṃs tato 'yaṃ devānām aghnat saṃ so 'bhavad yam asurāṇāṃ na sa samabhavad anenāriṣāmeti tad ariṣṭasyāriṣṭatvam ariṣṭayā evāriṣṭam antataḥ kriyate
(PB 12.5.24) trīḍaṃ bhavati trirātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 12.5.25) dravantīm iḍām uttamām upayanti caturthasyāhnaḥ santatyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.5.1) 'Three speeches arise' — this is the form of the third day. By it they commence the third day.
(PB 12.5.2) This third day is indeed ascending, three-fold. Thereby one declares it.
(PB 12.5.3) 'O pressers, pour around' — these are the encircling (<s>parivatī</s>) verses.
(PB 12.5.4) The third day is indeed the end. These serve for its completion.
(PB 12.5.5) 'Friends, sit down'

body.text:
(PB 12.6.1) pramaṃhiṣṭhāya gāyateti
(PB 12.6.2) yad gāyateti mahasa eva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 12.6.3) ''taṃ te mad aṅgaṇīm asīti madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 12.6.4) ''śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyā'' iti śrutyā eva
(PB 12.6.5) pramaṃhiṣṭhīya bhavati
(PB 12.6.6) pramaṃhiṣṭhīyena vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāvartayat tam astṛṇuta bhrātṛvyavān pramaṃhiṣṭhīyenokthāni praṇayeta stṛṇute bhrātṛvyaṃ vasīyāṃ ātmanā bhavati
(PB 12.6.7) hārivarṇaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.6.8) indraś ca vai namuciś cāsuraḥ samadadhātāṃ na no naktan na divāhanan nārdreṇa na śuṣkeṇeti tasya vyuṣṭāyām anudita āditye 'pāṃ phenena śiro 'chinad etad vai na naktaṃ na divā yat vyuṣṭāyām anudita āditya etan nārdran na śuṣkaṃ yad apāṃ phenas tad enaṃ pāpīyāṃ vācaṃ vadad anvavartata vīrahan na druho druha iti tan narcā na sāmnāpahantum aśaknot
(PB 12.6.9) hārivarṇasyaiva nidhanenāpāhata
(PB 12.6.10) apaśucaṃhate hārivarṇasya nidhanena śriyaṃ ca haraś copaiti tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.6.11) tairaścayaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.6.12) aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yanto rakṣāṃsy anvasacanta tāny etena tiraścāṅgirasas tiryaṅ paryavaid yat tiryaṅ aparyavait tasmāt tairaścyaṃ pāpmā vāva sa tān asacata taṃ tairaścyenāpāghnatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate tairaścyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.6.13) saptadaśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.6.1) 'Sing to the most bountiful one!'
(PB 12.6.2) When he says 'sing,' thereby the form of greatness is produced.
(PB 12.6.3) 'This of yours, the intoxicating drink' — the third pressing is indeed intoxicating and full of essence. Thereby one places intoxication and essence.
(PB 12.6.4) 'Hear the call from across' — through hearing indeed.
(PB 12.6.5) It is the <s>Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya</s> [chant].
(PB 12.6.6) The <s>Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya</s>

body.text:
(PB 12.7.1) ''pra ta āśvinīḥ pavamānadhenava'' iti caturthasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
(PB 12.7.2) āpte trirātre rūpeṇa gāyatryo dvitīyaṃ prayanti prati vai gāyatryā rūpam
(PB 12.7.3) jagatī pratipad bhavati jāgatam etad ahar yat tṛtīyaṃ jagatyā eva taj jagatīm abhisaṃkrāmanti
(PB 12.7.4) yad ato 'nyā pratipatsyāt pratikūlaṃ vānukūlaṃ vā syāt
(PB 12.7.5) pavamāno ajījanad ity anurūpo bhavati
(PB 12.7.6) janadvad vā etad ahar yac caturtham annādyaṃ janayati virājaṃ janayaty ekaviṃśaṃ stomaṃ janayati
(PB 12.7.7) pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam
(PB 12.7.8) anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.7.9) stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 12.7.10) ṣaḍṛcau bhavata ṛtūnāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 12.7.11) tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 12.7.12) ekaviṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.7.1) 'Your <s>Aśvin</s>-related cows, O <s>Pavamāna</s>' — this is the opening verse of the fourth day.
(PB 12.7.2) When the three-day group is completed, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses go forth a second time as their form. The form is indeed that of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
(PB 12.7.3) The opening is in <s>Jagatī</s> (meter). This day belongs to the <s>Jagatī</s>, which is the third. By the <s>Jagatī</s> they cross over to the <s>Jagatī</s>.
(PB 12.7.4) Whatever other

body.text:
(PB 12.8.1) ''janasya gopā ajaniṣṭa jāgṛviḥ'' ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.8.2) janadvad vā etad ahar yac caturtham annādyaṃ janayati virājaṃ janayaty ekaviṃśaṃ stomaṃ janayati
(PB 12.8.3) ''ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvarūṇā-'' iti bārhataṃ maitrāvarūṇam
(PB 12.8.4) bṛhad etat parokṣaṃ yad vairājaṃ bārhatam eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati
(PB 12.8.5) ''indro dadhīco asthabhir'' iti dādhīcas tṛco bhavati
(PB 12.8.6) dadhyaṅ vā āṅgiraso devānāṃ purodhānīya āsīd annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhā annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.8.7) ''iyaṃ vāmasya manmana'' ity aindrāgnam
(PB 12.8.8) ''indrāgnī pūrvyastutir abhrād vṛṣṭir ivājani-'' ity ānuṣṭubhī vai vṛṣṭir ānuṣṭubham etad ahar yac caturthaṃ samīcyau virājau dadhāty annādyāya stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.8.1) 'The guardian of people is born, the wakeful one' — this <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblation chant) belongs to <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 12.8.2) This fourth day is indeed one that generates. It generates food. It generates the <s>Virāj</s> [meter]. It generates the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) <s>stoma</s>.
(PB 12.8.3) 'This for you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — this is the <s>Bārhat</s> (Bṛhat-related) <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [chant].
(PB 12.8.4) The <s>Bṛhat</s> is this in a hidden form — that which is <s>Vairāja</s> (belonging to Virāj) is <s>Bārhat</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.9.1) ''payasva dakṣasādhana'' iti gāyatrī bhavati sidhyai
(PB 12.9.2) yat pavasveti tad bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.9.3) ''tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa sakhya indo dive dive/ purūṇi babhro nicaranti mām ava paridhīṃr atitāṃ ihi-'' iti
(PB 12.9.4) ati hy āyañ chakunā iva paptim ety ati hy apatat
(PB 12.9.5) punāno akramīd abhīti
(PB 12.9.6) gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 12.9.7) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.9.8) caturṇidhanam ātharvaṇaṃ bhavati catūrātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 12.9.9) catuṣpadānuṣṭubhānuṣṭubham etad ahar yac caturtham
(PB 12.9.10) bheṣajaṃ vātharvaṇāni bheṣajam eva tat karoti
(PB 12.9.11) nidhanakāmaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.9.12) ekaṃ vā anyena niruktena nidhanena kāmaṃ sanoty athaitan nidhanakāmaṃ sarveṣāṃ kāmānām avarudhyai
(PB 12.9.13) āṣṭādaṃṣṭraṃ bhavati
(PB 12.9.14) yad evāṣṭādaṃṣṭrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.9.15) ābhīśavaṃ bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
(PB 12.9.16) yad vā adhṛtam abhīśunā tad dādhāra
(PB 12.9.17) anutunnaṃ gāyati tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 12.9.18) caturṇidhanam āṅgirasaṃ bhavati catūrātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 12.9.19) svaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 12.9.20) sattrāsāhīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.9.21) yad vā asurāṇām asoḍham āsīt tad devāḥ sattrāsāhīyenāsahanta sattrainān asakṣmahīti tat sattrāsāhīyasya sattrāsāhīyatvam
(PB 12.9.22) sattrā bhrātṛvyaṃ sahate sattrāsāhīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.9.23) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 12.9.24) vṛṣaṇvatyo gāyatrayo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān nayanti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.9.1) 'Be full of milk, O accomplisher of skill' — this is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, for the sake of success.
(PB 12.9.2) That it says 'purify yourself' — that is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 12.9.3) 'O <s>Soma</s>, I delight in your friendship, O <s>Indu</s>, day after day. Many things, O tawny one, flow toward me — pass beyond the enclosures.'
(PB 12.9.4) For this one flies beyond like a bird in flight — for it has flown beyond.
(PB 12.9.5) 'Purifying himself, he strode forth.'
(PB 12.9.6) The <s>Gāyatrīs</s> are true but have the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; therefore they are performed in the realm of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 12.9.7) It is of the <s>Gāyatra</s> type — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 12.9.8) The <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> chant with four-fold ending is used, for sustaining the four-night period.
(PB 12.9.9) The fourth day has four-footed <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> — this day is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 12.9.10) The <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> chants are indeed medicine; thereby one makes medicine.
(PB 12.9.11) It has the ending of desire (<s>nidhanakāma</s>).
(PB 12.9.12) With one specific ending one obtains one desire; but this ending-of-desire is for obtaining all desires.
(PB 12.9.13) The <s>Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra</s> chant is used.
(PB 12.9.14) Whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Āṣṭādaṃṣṭra</s>.
(PB 12.9.15) The <s>Ābhīśava</s> chant is used, for sustaining the day.
(PB 12.9.16) What was not held firm, the rein held firm.
(PB 12.9.17) He sings in the piercing style (<s>anutunna</s>), for such is the form of this day.
(PB 12.9.18) The <s>Āṅgirasa</s> chant with four-fold ending is used, for sustaining the four-night period.
(PB 12.9.19) The <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) belongs to heaven (<s>svar</s>), for such is the form of this day.
(PB 12.9.20) The <s>Sattrāsāhīya</s> chant is used.
(PB 12.9.21) What was unconquered among the <s>Asuras</s>, the <s>devas</s> conquered with the <s>Sattrāsāhīya</s>, saying 'We have conquered them in the <s>sattra</s>!' That is the <s>Sattrāsāhīya</s>-ness of the <s>Sattrāsāhīya</s>.
(PB 12.9.22) He who praises with the <s>Sattrāsāhīya</s> completely conquers the rival.
(PB 12.9.23) They praise in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses for the sake of firm establishment and <s>brahmavarcas</s>. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.
(PB 12.9.24) The <s>Gāyatrīs</s> contain the word <s>vṛṣan</s> (bull); thereby they lead from the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> form. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.10.1) ''pibā somam indra mandatu tvā yante suṣāva haryaśvādriḥ/ sotur bāhubhyāṃ suyato nārvā-'' ity ayatam iva vai caturtham ahas tasyaiva yatyai
(PB 12.10.2) viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhṛtarannara ity atijagatī varṣīyayaś chanda ākramate 'napabhraṃśāya
(PB 12.10.3) apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yaj jayāyasaś chandasaḥ kanīyaś chanda upaiti yad eṣā caturthe 'hany atijagatī kriyate 'napabhraṃśāya
(PB 12.10.4) yo rājā carṣaṇīnām iti
(PB 12.10.5) rājye hy etarhi vāco 'gacchan rājyam evaitayā yajamānaṃ gamayanti
(PB 12.10.6) chandobhir vai devā ādityaṃ svargaṃ lokam aharan sa nādhriyata taṃ vairājasya nidhanenādṛṃhaṃs tasmāt parāṅ cārvāṅ cādityas tapati parāṅ cārvāṅ cekāraḥ
(PB 12.10.7) prastāvaṃ prastutya viṣṭambhān viṣṭabhnoti mukhata eva tad annādyaṃ dhatte mukhaṃ hi sāmnaḥ prastāvaḥ
(PB 12.10.8) daśakṛtvo viṣṭabhnoti daśākṣarā virāṅ vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.10.9) triṃśatkṛtvo viṣṭabhnoti bhūyaso 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.10.10) vairājaṃ sāma bhavati virāṭsu stuvanti vairājā viṣṭambhāḥ samīcīr virājo dadhāty annādyāya
(PB 12.10.11) anutunnaṃ gāyati retodheyāyānutunnād dhi reto dhīyate
(PB 12.10.12) dakṣiṇa ūrāv udgatur agniṃ manthanti dakṣiṇato hi retaḥ sicyate
(PB 12.10.13) upākṛte 'hiṅkṛte manthanti jātam abhihiṅkaroti
(PB 12.10.14) tasmāj jātaṃ putraṃ paśavo 'bhihiṅkurvanti
(PB 12.10.15) tasmai jātāyāmīmāṃsanta gārhapatye praharāmā3 āgnīdhrā3 āhavanīyā3 iti
(PB 12.10.16) āhavanīye praharanty etad āyatano vai yajamāno yadā havanīye svam eva tad āyatanaṃ jyotiṣmat karoti
(PB 12.10.17) jyotiṣmān brahmavarcasī bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.10.18) abhijuhoti śāntyai
(PB 12.10.19) ājyenābhijuhoti tejo vā ājyaṃ teja eva tad ātman dhatte
(PB 12.10.20) ''preddho agne dīdihi puro na'' iti virājābhijuhoty annaṃ virāḍ annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.10.21) traiśokaṃ brahmasāma bhavati
(PB 12.10.22) atijagatīṣu stuvanty ahna utkrāntyā ud vā etenāhnā krāmanti
(PB 12.10.23) diveti nidhanam upayanti pāpmano 'pahatyā apapāpmānaṃ hate traiśokena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.10.24) bhāradvājasya pṛśny achāvākasāma bhavati
(PB 12.10.25) annaṃ vai devāḥ pṛśnīti vadanty annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 12.10.26) iḍābhir aiḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpaṃ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.10.1) 'Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, may it delight you; the pressing stone with bay horses has pressed well for you; well-fashioned from the presser's arms, like a swift one' — the fourth day is as if unregulated; this verse is for its regulation.
(PB 12.10.2) 'He who has conquered all hosts, O warrior' — this is in <s>Atijagatī</s> (extended <s>Jagatī</s>), a greater meter; one attains it to prevent falling away.
(PB 12.10.3) It is as though a fall occurs when one goes from a greater meter to a lesser one. When this <s>Atijagatī</s> is used on the fourth day, it is to prevent falling away.
(PB 12.10.4) 'He who is the king of peoples.'
(PB 12.10.5) For at that point they attained the kingship of speech. With this verse they cause the sacrificer to attain kingship.
(PB 12.10.6) The <s>devas</s> carried the sun to the heavenly world with meters, but he was not firm. They made him firm with the ending of the <s>Vairāja</s>. Therefore the sun heats both away and toward; the <s>eka</s> syllable also goes both away and toward.
(PB 12.10.7) Having chanted the <s>prastāva</s> (introduction), he props up with <s>viṣṭambhas</s> (supports). Thereby he places food from the very mouth, for the <s>prastāva</s> is the mouth of the <s>sāman</s>.
(PB 12.10.8) He props up ten times. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; the <s>Vairāja</s> chant corresponds to the <s>Virāj</s>. It is for obtaining food.
(PB 12.10.9) He props up thirty times — for obtaining greater food.
(PB 12.10.10) The <s>Vairāja Sāman</s> is used. They praise in <s>Virāj</s> verses. The <s>Vairāja</s> supports are used. He places the <s>Virāj</s> verses in alignment — for obtaining food.
(PB 12.10.11) He sings in the piercing style (<s>anutunna</s>) — for the placing of seed, for seed is placed through piercing.
(PB 12.10.12) They churn fire on the right thigh of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, for seed is shed from the right side.
(PB 12.10.13) They churn when the <s>upākṛta</s> call has been made but before the <s>hiṅkāra</s>. When born, one sounds the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over it.
(PB 12.10.14) Therefore cattle sound the <s>hiṅkāra</s> over a newborn calf.
(PB 12.10.15) For that newborn one they deliberated: 'Shall we place it in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire? In the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>? In the <s>Āhavanīya</s>?'
(PB 12.10.16) They place it in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, for the sacrificer's abode is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. When placed in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he makes his own abode luminous.
(PB 12.10.17) He becomes luminous and possessed of <s>brahmavarcas</s> who knows thus.
(PB 12.10.18) He makes an additional offering for appeasement.
(PB 12.10.19) He makes the additional offering with ghee (<s>ājya</s>), for ghee is brilliance. Thereby he places brilliance in himself.
(PB 12.10.20) 'Kindled, O <s>Agni</s>, shine before us' — he makes the additional offering with a <s>Virāj</s> verse. Food is the <s>Virāj</s>; it is for obtaining food.
(PB 12.10.21) The <s>Traiśoka</s> becomes the <s>Brahma Sāman</s>.
(PB 12.10.22) They praise in <s>Atijagatī</s> verses — for the transcendence of the day. With this day one indeed transcends.
(PB 12.10.23) They reach the ending 'Heaven' (<s>div</s>) — for driving away sin. He who praises with the <s>Traiśoka</s> drives away sin.
(PB 12.10.24) The <s>Bhāradvāja Pṛśni</s> becomes the <s>Acchāvāka Sāman</s>.
(PB 12.10.25) The <s>devas</s> say that <s>Pṛśni</s> is food; it is for obtaining food.
(PB 12.10.26) The <s>iḍā</s> with <s>iḍā</s>s — for such is the form of this day. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 12.11.1) ''paripriyā divaḥ kavir'' iti parivatyo bhavanty anto vai caturtham ahas tasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
(PB 12.11.2) tvaṃ hy aṅga daivyeti tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.11.3) somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇā vyaṃvāraṃ vidhāvati/ agre vācaḥ pavamānaḥ kanikradad iti
(PB 12.11.4) agraṃ hy etarhi vāco 'gacchann agram evaitayā yajamānaṃ gamayanti
(PB 12.11.5) ''puro jitīvo andhasā-'' iti virājau vairājaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 12.11.6) ''somaḥ pavate janitā matīnām'' iti prātassavane ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhītaṃ taṃ tṛtīyasavane prajanayanti
(PB 12.11.7) triṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 12.11.8) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 12.11.9) aurṇāyavaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.10) aṅgiraso vai sattram āsata teṣām āptaḥ spṛtaḥ svargo loka āsīt panthānaṃ tu devayānaṃ na prājānaṃs teṣāṃ kalyāṇa āṅgiraso dhyāyam udavrajat sa ūrṇāyuṃ gandharvam apsarasāṃ madhye preṅkhayamāṇam upait sa iyām iti yāṃ yām abhyadiśat sainam akāmayata tam abhyavadat kālyāṇā3 ity āso vai vaḥ spṛtaḥ svargo lokaḥ panthānaṃ tu devayānaṃ na prajānīthedaṃ sāma svargyaṃ lokam eṣy atha mā tu vocoham adarśam iti
(PB 12.11.11) sa ait kalyāṇaḥ so 'bravīd āpto vai naḥ spṛtaḥ svargo lokaḥ panthānaṃ tu devayānaṃ prajānīma idaṃ sāma svargyaṃ tena stutvā svargaṃ lokam eṣyāma iti kas te 'vocad ity aham evādarśam iti tena stutvā svargaṃ lokam āyann ahīyata kalyāṇo 'nṛtaṃ hi so 'vadat sa eṣaḥ śvitraḥ
(PB 12.11.12) svargyaṃ vā etat sāma svargalokaḥ puṇyaloko bhavaty aurṇāyavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.11.13) bṛhatkaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.14) sāmārṣeyeṇa praśastaṃ tvaṃ hīty annādyasyāvarudhyai hīti vā annaṃ pradīyate ṣoḍaśinam u caivaitenodyacchati
(PB 12.11.15) ātīṣādīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.16) āyur vā ātīṣādīyam āyuṣo 'ṣarudhyai
(PB 12.11.17) ātamitor nidhanam upayanty āyur eva sarvam āpnuvanti
(PB 12.11.18) nānadaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.19) jyāyo 'bhyārambham atihāya pañcam ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhna ārambhas tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
(PB 12.11.20) ṣoḍaśākṣareṇa prastauti ṣoḍaśinam u caivaitenodyacchati
(PB 12.11.21) āndhīgavaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.22) kayor annādyam avarūndha āndhīgavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.11.23) vātsapraṃ bhavati
(PB 12.11.24) etasmin vai vairājaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ pratitiṣṭhati vātsapreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.11.25) vatsaprīr bhālandanaḥ śraddhāṃ nāvindata sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad vātsapram apaśyat sa śraddhām avindata śraddhā vindāmahā iti vai sattram āsate vindate śraddhām
(PB 12.11.26) īnidhanaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpaṃ nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.11.1) 'The dear poet circles around from heaven' — these are the encircling (<s>parivatī</s>) verses. The fourth day is indeed the end. These serve for its completion.
(PB 12.11.2) 'For you indeed, O divine one' — 'you' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s> [chant], for this day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 12.11.3) '<s>Soma</s>, being purified, runs with a wave through the filter, <s>Pavamāna</s> roaring at the forefront of speech.'
(PB 12.11.4) For this is indeed the forefront.

body.text:
(PB 12.12.1) ''agniṃ vo vṛdhantam'' iti
(PB 12.12.2) avardhanta hy etarhi yajamānam eva tathā vardhayanti
(PB 12.12.3) ''vayam u tvām apūrvya-'' ity apūrvāṃ hy etarhi prajāpates tanūm agacchann apūrvam evaitayā yajamānaṃ gamayanti
(PB 12.12.4) ''imam indra sutaṃ piba jyeṣṭham amartyaṃ madam'' iti jyaiṣṭhaṃ hy etarhi vāco 'gacchan jyaiṣṭhyam evaitayā yajamānaṃ gamayanti
(PB 12.12.5) saindhukṣitaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.12.6) sindhukṣid vai rājanyarṣir jyog aparuddhaś caran sa etat saindhukṣitam apaśyat so 'vāgacchat pratyatiṣṭhad avagacchati pratitiṣṭhati saindhukṣitena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 12.12.7) saubharaṃ bhavati bṛhatas tejaḥ
(PB 12.12.8) pannam iva vai caturtham ahas tad etena bṛhatas tejasottabhnoti saubhareṇa
(PB 12.12.9) vasiṣṭhasya priyaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.12.10) etena vai vasiṣṭha indrasya premāṇam agacchat premāṇaṃ devatānāṃ gacchati vāsiṣṭhena tuṣṭuvānaḥ stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.12.1) 'Let your <s>Agni</s> be increased.'
(PB 12.12.2) For at that time they increased. Thereby they increase the sacrificer in the same way.
(PB 12.12.3) 'We to you, O unprecedented one' — for at that time they reached the unprecedented body of <s>Prajāpati</s>. By this verse they lead the sacrificer to what is unprecedented.
(PB 12.12.4) 'Drink, O <s>Indra</s>, this pressed [<s>Soma</s>], the foremost, the immortal intoxication' — the foremost

body.text:
(PB 12.13.1) indraś ca bṛhac ca samabhavatāṃ tam indraṃ bṛhad ekayā tanvāty aricyata tasyā abibhedanayā mābhibhaviṣyatīti so 'bravīt ṣoḍaśī te 'yaṃ yajñakratur astv iti sa ṣoḍaśy abhavat tad asya janma
(PB 12.13.2) atiśriyā bhrātṛvyaṃ ricyate yo gāyatrīṣu dvipadāsu bṛhatā ṣoḍaśinā stute
(PB 12.13.3) ''upa no haribhiḥ stutam'' ity etā vai gāyatryo dvipadā etāsu stotavyam
(PB 12.13.4) indraḥ prajāpatim upādhāvad vṛtraṃ hanānīti tasmā etām anuṣṭubham apaharasaṃ prāyacchat tayā nāstṛṇuta yad astṛtā vyanadat tan nānadasya nānadatvam
(PB 12.13.5) taṃ punar upādhāvat tasmai saptānāṃ hotrāṇāṃ haro nirmāya prāyacchat tam astṛṇuta
(PB 12.13.6) stṛṇute taṃ yaṃ tustūrṣate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.7) tasmād dharivatīṣu stuvanti harivatīḥ śaṃsanti harivatīṣu graho gṛhyate haro hy asmai nirmāya prāyacchat
(PB 12.13.8) ekaviṃśāyatano vā eṣa yat ṣoḍaśī sapta hi prātassavane hotrā vaṣaṭkurvanti sapta mādhyandine savane sapta tṛtīyasavane
(PB 12.13.9) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati
(PB 12.13.10) gaurīvitir vā etac chāktyo brahmaṇo 'tiriktam apaśyat tad gaurīvitam abhavad atiriktaṃ etad atiriktena stuvanti yad gaurīvitena ṣoḍaśinaṃ śvastanavān bhavaty api prajāyā upakḷptaḥ
(PB 12.13.11) viśālaṃ libjayā śrūtyābhyadhād iti hovācopoditir gopāleyo 'nuṣṭubhi nānadam akar gaurīvitena ṣoḍaśinam astoṣṭāñjasā śriyam upāgān na śriyā avapadyata iti
(PB 12.13.12) eṣa vai viśālaṃ libjayā bhūtyābhidadhāti yo 'nuṣṭubhi nānadaṃ kṛtvā gaurīvitena ṣoḍaśinā stute 'ñjasā śriyam upaiti na śriyā avapadyate
(PB 12.13.13) śakvarīṣu ṣoḍaśinā stuvīta yaḥ kāmayeta vajrī syām iti
(PB 12.13.14) vajro vai ṣoḍaśī vajraḥ śakvaryo vajreṇaivāsmai vajraṃ spṛṇoti vajrī bhavati
(PB 12.13.15) anuṣṭupsu ṣoḍaśinā stuvīta yaḥ kāmayeta na mā vāg ativadet
(PB 12.13.16) vajro vai ṣoḍaśī vāg anuṣṭub vajreṇaivāsmai vācaṃ spṛṇoti nainaṃ vāg ativadati
(PB 12.13.17) ''asāvi soma indra ta'' ity etāsu stotavyam
(PB 12.13.18) virāṭsv annādyakāmaḥ ṣoḍaśinā stuvīta vajro vai ṣoḍaśī vairājam annaṃ vajreṇaivāsmā annaṃ spṛṇoty annādo bhavati
(PB 12.13.19) ''pra vo mahe vṛdhe bharadhvam'' ity etāsu stotavyam
(PB 12.13.20) trayastriṃśadakṣarā vā etā virājo yad ekaviṃśatiḥ pratiṣṭhā sā yad dvādaśa prajātiḥ sā
(PB 12.13.21) pratiṣṭhāya prajāyate no cāntasthāyāṃ jīryate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.22) atha vā etā ekapadās tryakṣarā viṣṇoś chando bhurijaḥ śakvaryaḥ
(PB 12.13.23) etābhir vā indro vṛtram ahan kṣipraṃ vā etābhiḥ pāpmānaṃ hanti kṣipraṃ vasīyān bhavati
(PB 12.13.24) catustriṃśadakṣarāḥ saṃstuto bhavati trayastriṃśaddevattāḥ prajāpatiś catustriṃśo devatānāṃ prajāpatim evopayanty ariṣṭyai
(PB 12.13.25) hiraṇyaṃ sampradāyaṃ ṣoḍaśinā stuvate jyotiṣmān asya ṣoḍaśī bhavati
(PB 12.13.26) aśvaḥ kṛṣṇa upatiṣṭhati sāmyekṣayāya bhrātṛvyalokam eva sa vidhamaṃs tiṣṭhati
(PB 12.13.27) ekākṣaraṃ vai devānām avamaṃ chanda āsīt saptākṣaraṃ paramaṃ navākṣaram asurāṇām avamaṃ chanda āsīt pañcadaśākṣaraṃ paramaṃ devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta tān prajāpatir ānuṣṭubho bhūtvāntarātiṣṭhat taṃ devāsurā vyahvayanta sa devān upāvartata tato devā abhavan parāsurāḥ
(PB 12.13.28) bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.29) te devā asurāṇām ekākṣareṇaiva pañcadaśākṣaram avṛñjata dvyakṣareṇa caturdaśākṣaraṃ tryakṣareṇa trayodaśākṣaraṃ caturakṣareṇa dvādaśākṣaraṃ pañcākṣareṇaikādaśākṣaraṃ ṣaḍakṣareṇa daśākṣaraṃ saptākṣareṇa navākṣaram aṣṭābhir evāṣṭāv avṛñjata
(PB 12.13.30) evam eva bhrātṛvyād bhūtiṃ vṛṅkte ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.31) aparuddhayajña iva vā eṣa yat ṣoḍaśī kanīyasvina iva vai tarhi devā āsan bhūyasvino 'surāḥ kanīyasvina bhūyasvinaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ vṛṅkte ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.32) ''yasmād anyo na paro 'sti jāto ya ābabhūva bhuvanāni viśvā/ prajāpatiḥ prajayā samvidānas trīṇi jyotīṃ ṣi sacate sa ṣoḍaśī-'' ity udgātā graham avekṣate
(PB 12.13.33) jyotiṣmān asya ṣoḍaśī bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 12.13.34) ekaviṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 12.13.1) <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Bṛhat</s> came into being together. The <s>Bṛhat</s> surpassed <s>Indra</s> with one body. He was afraid of it, thinking 'It will overpower me.' He said: 'Let this sixteenth (<s>ṣoḍaśī</s>) sacrificial rite be yours.' Thus he became the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>. That is its birth.
(PB 12.13.2) He surpasses the rival with excess glory who praises with the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> in two-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.
(PB 12.13.3) 'Come to us, praised with the bay horses' — these are indeed the two-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses. One should praise with these.
(PB 12.13.4) <s>Indra</s> ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'Let me slay <s>Vṛtra</s>!' He gave him this <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (verse), of irresistible force. With it he could not overpower him. Because he was not overpowered, he roared — that is the nature of the <s>Nānada</s> (roar) as 'roaring.'
(PB 12.13.5) He ran to him again. He fashioned for him the force of seven oblations and gave it to him. With that he overpowered him.
(PB 12.13.6) He who knows this overpowers him whom he wishes to overpower.
(PB 12.13.7) Therefore they praise with verses containing 'bay horse' (<s>hari</s>), they recite verses containing 'bay horse,' the cup is taken with verses containing 'bay horse' — for he fashioned the force and gave it to him.
(PB 12.13.8) The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> has a twenty-one-fold basis, for seven oblation priests utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call at the morning pressing, seven at the midday pressing, and seven at the third pressing.
(PB 12.13.9) It is the <s>Gaurīvita</s> (chant).
(PB 12.13.10) <s>Gaurīviti</s>, the descendant of <s>Śakti</s>, perceived the surplus of <s>Brahman</s>. That became the <s>Gaurīvita</s>. This is a surplus — they praise with the surplus using the <s>Gaurīvita</s> for the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>. He who has breasts (i.e., cows to milk) tomorrow is well-prepared even for offspring.
(PB 12.13.11) <s>Upoditi Gopāleya</s> said: 'He covered <s>Viśāla</s> with the hearing of <s>Libjā</s>. He made the <s>Nānada</s> roar in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, praised with the <s>Gaurīvita</s> for the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, and directly attained glory — he did not fall from glory.'
(PB 12.13.12) He indeed covers <s>Viśāla</s> with the prosperity of <s>Libjā</s> who, having made the <s>Nānada</s> roar in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, praises with the <s>Gaurīvita</s> for the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>. He directly attains glory and does not fall from glory.
(PB 12.13.13) One who desires 'May I wield the thunderbolt' should praise with the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> in the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses.
(PB 12.13.14) The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is indeed the thunderbolt. The <s>Śakvarī</s> verses are the thunderbolt. He wins the thunderbolt for him with the thunderbolt. He becomes a wielder of the thunderbolt.
(PB 12.13.15) One who desires 'May speech not surpass me' should praise with the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses.
(PB 12.13.16) The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is the thunderbolt. Speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. He wins speech for him with the thunderbolt. Speech does not surpass him.
(PB 12.13.17) 'This <s>Soma</s> has been pressed for you, O <s>Indra</s>' — one should praise with these verses.
(PB 12.13.18) One desiring the eating of food should praise with the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> in <s>Virāj</s> verses. The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is the thunderbolt. Food belongs to the <s>Virāj</s>. He wins food for him with the thunderbolt. He becomes an eater of food.
(PB 12.13.19) 'Offer for the great increase' — one should praise with these verses.
(PB 12.13.20) These <s>Virāj</s> verses have thirty-three syllables: twenty-one is the firm foundation, and twelve is procreation.
(PB 12.13.21) He who knows this is firmly established and procreates, and does not grow old while standing within.
(PB 12.13.22) Now, these are one-footed, three-syllabled, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s meter — the <s>bhurij Śakvarī</s> verses.
(PB 12.13.23) With these <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. Swiftly with these he slays evil. He swiftly becomes more prosperous.
(PB 12.13.24) The concluded praise has thirty-four syllables. There are thirty-three deities. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the thirty-fourth. He approaches <s>Prajāpati</s> among the deities, for freedom from harm.
(PB 12.13.25) He who praises with the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> while giving gold as a gift — his <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> becomes luminous.
(PB 12.13.26) A black horse stands in attendance, for the surveying of the <s>Sāman</s>. He stands destroying the world of the rival.
(PB 12.13.27) The smallest meter of the gods was one-syllabled; the greatest was seven-syllabled. The smallest meter of the <s>Asuras</s> was nine-syllabled; the greatest was fifteen-syllabled. The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were in competition. <s>Prajāpati</s>, having become the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, stood between them. The gods and <s>Asuras</s> called to him. He turned toward the gods. Therefore the gods prevailed; the <s>Asuras</s> were vanquished.
(PB 12.13.28) He prevails by himself; his rival is vanquished — he who knows this.
(PB 12.13.29) The gods wrested from the <s>Asuras</s> the fifteen-syllabled with the one-syllabled, the fourteen-syllabled with the two-syllabled, the thirteen-syllabled with the three-syllabled, the twelve-syllabled with the four-syllabled, the eleven-syllabled with the five-syllabled, the ten-syllabled with the six-syllabled, the nine-syllabled with the seven-syllabled. With eight they wrested eight.
(PB 12.13.30) He who knows this likewise wrests prosperity from his rival.
(PB 12.13.31) The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is like a sacrifice that has been blocked. At that time the gods were few and the <s>Asuras</s> were many. He who knows this, being few, wrests from the more numerous rival.
(PB 12.13.32) 'Than whom no other higher has been born, who became all worlds — <s>Prajāpati</s>, united with offspring, he joins the three lights — that is the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>' — thus the <s>Udgātṛ</s> gazes at the cup.
(PB 12.13.33) His <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> becomes luminous — he who knows this.
(PB 12.13.34) The <s>stoma</s> is indeed twenty-one-fold, for firm establishment. He becomes firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 13.1.1) ''govit pavasva vasuvid dhiraṇyavid'' iti pañcamasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
(PB 13.1.2) govid vā etad vasuvid dhiraṇyavidyac chakvaryaḥ
(PB 13.1.3) paśavaś śakvaryaḥ sarvaṃ paśubhir vindate
(PB 13.1.4) ''tvaṃ suvīro asi somaviśvavid'' ity eṣa yāva suvīro yasya paśavas tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 13.1.5) tās te kṣarantu madhumad ghṛtaṃ paya'' iti madhumad vai ghṛtaṃ payaḥ paśavaḥ kṣaranti tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 13.1.6) ''pavamānasya viśvavid'' ity anurūpo bhavati
(PB 13.1.7) viśvam eva tadvit tam abhivadati viśvaṃ hi paśubhir vindate
(PB 13.1.8) ''pra te sargā asṛkṣata-'' iti sṛṣṭānīva hy etarhy ahāni
(PB 13.1.9) pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam, anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda stotrīyānurupau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 13.1.10) saptarcau bhavataḥ chandasāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 13.1.11) caturṛco bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.1.12) tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhy udyanti
(PB 13.1.13) triṇava eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai puṣṭyai trivṛd vā eṣa puṣṭaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.1.1) 'Purify yourself, finder of cows, finder of wealth, finder of gold' — this is the opening verse of the fifth day.
(PB 13.1.2) This is a finder of cows, a finder of wealth, a finder of gold — for such are the <s>Śakvarī</s> (verses).
(PB 13.1.3) Cattle are the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses. He finds everything through cattle.
(PB 13.1.4) 'You are rich in heroes, O <s>Soma</s>, finder of all' — he who has cattle is indeed rich in heroes. He addresses that very quality.
(PB 13.1.5) 'Let these flow with honey, ghee, and milk' — honey, ghee, and milk are indeed cattle that flow. He addresses that very quality.
(PB 13.1.6) 'Of the purifying <s>Pavamāna</s>, finder of all' — this is the corresponding verse.
(PB 13.1.7) He addresses the one who finds everything. For he finds everything through cattle.
(PB 13.1.8) 'Your streams have been released' — for the days are as if released at this point.
(PB 13.1.9) He echoes the earlier form with a later form. That he echoes with the earlier form — that is the nature of the corresponding verse as 'corresponding.' A son resembling him is born to him who knows this. The <s>stotrīya</s> and the corresponding verse are triplets of three, for the securing of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(PB 13.1.10) They are sets of seven — for the support of the meters.
(PB 13.1.11) It has four verses — for firm establishment.
(PB 13.1.12) The last is a triplet — with the very <s>prāṇa</s> with which they go forth, they rise up.
(PB 13.1.13) The <s>stoma</s> is indeed <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold), for firm establishment and nourishment. The threefold is indeed this nourished one.

body.text:
(PB 13.2.1) ''tava śriyo varṣasy eva vidyuta'' ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.2.2) śrīr vai paśavaḥ śrīḥ śakvaryaḥ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 13.2.3) ''agneś cikitra uṣasām ivetaya'' itītānīva hy etarhy ahānīti
(PB 13.2.4) ''ā te yatente rathyo yathā pṛthag'' ity eva hy etarhy ahāni yatante
(PB 13.2.5) ''purūruṇā cid dhy asty avo nūnaṃ vāṃ varuṇa-'' iti maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 13.2.6) yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇāti tad eva tad avayajati
(PB 13.2.7) ''uttiṣṭhann ojasā saha-'' ity aindram
(PB 13.2.8) pañca vā ṛtava utthānasya rūpam ojasā sahety ojasaiva vīryeṇa sahottiṣṭhanti
(PB 13.2.9) ''indrāgnī yuvām ima'' iti rāthantaram aindrāgnam
(PB 13.2.10) rathantaram etat parokṣaṃ yac chakvaryo rāthantaram eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.2.1) 'Your glories are like the lightnings of the rain-cloud' — the <s>Ājya</s> (ghee libation) belongs to <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 13.2.2) Glory is indeed cattle. Glory is the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses. He addresses that very quality.
(PB 13.2.3) 'O <s>Agni</s>, distinguished like the dawns' — for the days are as if distinguished at this point.
(PB 13.2.4) 'Your chariot-parts stretch out separately' — for the days stretch out at this point.
(PB 13.2.5) 'O widely expansive one, O <s>Varuṇa</s>' — this belongs to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 13.2.6) Whatever of the sacrifice is ill-performed, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes. He thus expiates that.
(PB 13.2.7) 'Rising up with vigor' — this belongs to <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 13.2.8) Five are the seasons. Rising is the form. 'With vigor' — they rise up with vigor and power.
(PB 13.2.9) 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, you two' — this is the <s>Rathantara</s> belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 13.2.10) The <s>Rathantara</s> is present in a hidden form as the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses. He reveals that very <s>Rathantara</s> form. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 13.3.1) ''arṣā soma dyumattama'' iti viṣṇumatyo gāyatryo bhavanti
(PB 13.3.2) brahma vai gāyatrī yajño viṣṇur brahmaṇy eva tad yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 13.3.3) ''soma uṣvāṇas sotṛbhir'' iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivaitās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 13.3.4) ''yat soma citram ukthyam'' iti gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 13.3.5) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 13.3.6) yaṇvaṃ bhavati paśavo vai yaṇvaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 13.3.7) santataṃ gāyati yajñasya santatye
(PB 13.3.8) adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 13.3.9) śākalaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.10) etena vai śakalaḥ pañcame 'hani pratyatiṣṭhat pratitiṣṭhati śākalena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.3.11) vārśaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.12) vṛśo vaijānas tryaruṇasya traidhātavasyaikṣvākasya purohita āsīt sa aikṣvāko 'dhāvayat brāhmaṇakumāraṃ rathena vyacchinat sa purohitam abravīt tava mā purodhāyām idam īdṛg upāgād iti tam etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vārśaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 13.3.13) adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 13.3.14) mānavaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.15) etena vai manuḥ prajāpatiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati mānavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.3.16) ānūpaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.17) etena vai vadhryaśva ānūpaḥ paśūnāṃ bhūmānam āśnuta paśūnāṃ bhūmānam aśnuta ānūpena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.3.18) vāmraṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.19) māmārṣeyeṇa praśastaṃ yaṃ vai gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ praśaṃsanti vāma iti taṃ praśaṃsanty ahar evaitena praśaṃsanti
(PB 13.3.20) adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
(PB 13.3.21) triṇidhanam āgneyaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.3.22) agriḥ sṛṣṭo nodadīpyata taṃ prajāpatir etena sāmnopādhamat sa udadīpyata dīptiś ca vā etat sāma brahmavarcasaṃ ca dīptiś caivaitena brahmavarcasaṃ cāvarundhe
(PB 13.3.23) śaiśavaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.3.24) śiśur vā āṅgiraso mantrakṛtāṃ mantrakṛd āsīt sa pit.ṛn putrakā ity āmantrayata, taṃ pitaro 'bruvan na dharmaṃ karoṣi yo naḥ pit.ṛn sataḥ putrakā ity āmantrayama iti, so 'bravīd ahaṃ vāva vaḥ pitāsmi yo mantrakṛd asmīti, taṃ deveṣv apṛcchanta te devā abuvann eṣa vāva pitā yo mantrakṛd iti tad vai sa udajayad ujjayati śaiśavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.3.25) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 13.3.26) viṣṇumatyo gāyatryo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān na yanti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.3.1) 'Flow, O <s>Soma</s>, most brilliant' — these are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses containing the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(PB 13.3.2) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>Brahman</s> (sacred power); the sacrifice is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. He thereby establishes the sacrifice in <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 13.3.3) '<s>Soma</s>, eager with the pressers' — this is the form of the <s>Simā</s> verses. He brings them to fullness by their own form.
(PB 13.3.4) 'What is wondrous and praiseworthy, O <s>Soma</s>' — these are truly <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses in the form of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Therefore they are performed in the world of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 13.3.5) The <s>Gāyatra</s> (Sāman) is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.
(PB 13.3.6) The <s>Yaṇva</s> (Sāman) is used. Cattle are the <s>Yaṇva</s> — for the attainment of cattle.
(PB 13.3.7) He sings continuously — for the continuity of the sacrifice.
(PB 13.3.8) It has one and a half <s>Iḍā</s> portions — for such is the form of this day.
(PB 13.3.9) The <s>Śākala</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.10) By this, <s>Śakala</s> became established on the fifth day. He who has praised with the <s>Śākala</s> becomes established.
(PB 13.3.11) The <s>Vārśa</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.12) <s>Vṛśa Vaijāna</s> was the <s>Purohita</s> (chief priest) of <s>Tryaruṇa Traidhātava</s>, the <s>Aikṣvāka</s> king. That <s>Aikṣvāka</s> king ran over a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy and cut him in two with his chariot. He said to his <s>Purohita</s>: 'Under your priestly office, this calamity has befallen me.' He raised him up with this <s>Sāman</s>. What he desired at that time he obtained. The <s>Vārśa</s> <s>Sāman</s> fulfills desires — one attains one's desire through it.
(PB 13.3.13) It has one and a half <s>Iḍā</s> portions — for such is the form of this day.
(PB 13.3.14) The <s>Mānava</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.15) By this, <s>Manu</s> attained the fullness of <s>Prajāpati</s>. He who has praised with the <s>Mānava</s> prospers and becomes great.
(PB 13.3.16) The <s>Ānūpa</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.17) By this, <s>Vadhryaśva Ānūpa</s> attained the fullness of cattle. He who has praised with the <s>Ānūpa</s> attains the fullness of cattle.
(PB 13.3.18) The <s>Vāmra</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.19) It was praised by the son of <s>Māmā Ṛṣi</s>. A cow, a horse, a man whom they praise — they praise him as 'dear' (<s>vāma</s>). With this they praise the day itself.
(PB 13.3.20) It has one and a half <s>Iḍā</s> portions — for such is the form of this day.
(PB 13.3.21) The triple-ending belonging to <s>Agni</s> is used — for establishment.
(PB 13.3.22) <s>Agni</s>, when created, did not blaze up. <s>Prajāpati</s> blew upon him with this <s>Sāman</s>. He blazed up. This <s>Sāman</s> is radiance and the splendor of sacred knowledge. By it one attains both radiance and the splendor of sacred knowledge.
(PB 13.3.23) The <s>Śaiśava</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 13.3.24) <s>Śiśu Āṅgirasa</s> was a mantra-maker among mantra-makers. He addressed his fathers as 'little sons.' The fathers said to him: 'You are not acting properly, you who address us, your fathers, as "little sons."' He said: 'I am indeed your father, I who am the mantra-maker.' They asked the gods about him. The gods said: 'He is indeed the father who is the mantra-maker.' He won that dispute. He who has praised with the <s>Śaiśava</s> wins.
(PB 13.3.25) They praise on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses — for establishment and for the splendor of sacred knowledge. They approach that very breath by which they go forth.
(PB 13.3.26) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses contain the name of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. But they do not depart from the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> form. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 13.4.1) indraḥ prajāpatim upādhāvad vṛtraṃ hanānīti tasmā etac chandobhya indriyaṃ vīryaṃ nirmāya prāyacchad etena śaknuhīti tac chakvarīṇāṃ śakvarītvaṃ sīmānam abhinat tat simā mahnyam akarot tan mahnyā mahān ghoṣa āsīt tan mahānāmnyaḥ
(PB 13.4.2) diśaḥ pañcapadā dādhārartūn ṣaṭpadā chandāṃsi saptapadā puruṣaṃ dvipadā
(PB 13.4.3) dvyopaśāḥ saṃstutā bhavanti tasmād dvyopaśāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 13.4.4) iḍe abhito 'thakāraṃ tasmāc chṛṅge tīkṣṇīyasī stūpāt
(PB 13.4.5) upakṣudrā gāyati tasmād upakṣudrāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 13.4.6) aṃsaśliṣṭā gāyati tasmād asaṃśliṣṭāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 13.4.7) nānārūpā gāyati tasmān nānārūpāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 13.4.8) āpo vai kṣīrarasā āsaṃste devāḥ pāpavasīyasād abibhayur yad apa upanidhāya stuvate pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtyai
(PB 13.4.9) vidhṛtiḥ pāpavasīyaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 13.4.10) gāyatram ayanaṃ bhavati brahmavarcasakāmasya svarṇidhanaṃ madhunāmuṣmiṃl loka upatiṣṭhate, traiṣṭubham ayanaṃ bhavaty ojaskāmasyāthakāraṇidhana mājyenāmuṣmiṃl loka upatiṣṭhate, jāgatam ayanaṃ bhavati paśukāmasyeḍānidhanaṃ payasāmuṣmiṃl loka upatiṣṭhate
(PB 13.4.11) añjasāryo mālyaḥ śakvarīḥ prārautsīd iti hovācālammaṃ pārijānataṃ rajanaḥ kauṇayo yady enāḥ pratiṣṭhāpaṃ śakṣyatīty etad vā etāsām añjayati pratiṣṭhitā ya ābhiḥ kṣipraṃ prastutya kṣipram udgāyati
(PB 13.4.12) śakvarībhiḥ stutvā purīṣeṇa stuvate
(PB 13.4.13) paśavo vai śakvaryo gauṣṭhaḥ purīṣaṃ goṣṭham eva tat paśubhyaḥ paryasyanti tam evainān pravartyanty avisraṃsāya
(PB 13.4.14) ''indro madāya vāvṛdha'' ity avardhanta hy etarhi
(PB 13.4.15) tāsu bārhadgiram
(PB 13.4.16) ''svādor itthā viṣuvata'' iti viṣuvān vai pañcamam ahas tāsu rāyovājīyam
