(PB 13.4.7) indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat teṣāṃ traya udaśiṣyanta pṛthuraśmir bṛhadgirī rāyovājas te 'bruvan ko na imān putrān bhariṣyatīty aham itīndro 'bravīt tān ādhinidhāya paricāryaṃ carad (?) vardhayaṃs tān vardhayitvābravīt kumārakā varān vṛṇīdhvam iti, kṣatraṃ mahyam ity abravīt pṛthuraśmis tasmā etena pārthuraśmena kṣatraṃ prāyacchat kṣatrakāma etena stuvīta kṣatrasyaivāsya prakāśo bhavati, brahmavarcasaṃ mahyam ity abravīt bṛhādgiris tasmā etena bārhadgireṇa prāyacchat brahmavarcasakāma etena stuvīta brahmavarcasī bhavati, paśūn mahyam ity abravīd rāyovājas tasmā etena rāyovājīyena paśūn prāyacchat paśukāma etena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
(PB 13.4.18) pārthuraśmaṃ rājanyāya brahmasāma kuryāt bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇāya rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyāya svenaivenāṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.4.1) <s>Indra</s> ran to <s>Prajāpati</s> saying: 'I want to slay <s>Vṛtra</s>.' <s>Prajāpati</s> fashioned vital power and vigor for him from the meters and gave it to him saying: 'Succeed with this!' That is the <s>Śakvarī</s>-nature of the <s>Śakvarīs</s>. He cut through the boundary. He made the boundary great. In the greatness there was a great sound. Those are the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (Great Names).
(PB 13.4.2) The five-footed (meter) supports the directions; the six-footed, the seasons; the seven-footed, the meters; the two-footed, man.
(PB 13.4.3) The chanted praises have pairs of supporting feet. Therefore cattle have pairs of supporting feet.
(PB 13.4.4) On both sides of the <s>Iḍā</s> is the syllable 'atha.' Therefore the horns are sharper than the hump.
(PB 13.4.5) He sings with small sounds. Therefore cattle are small.
(PB 13.4.6) He sings with shoulder-joined sounds. Therefore cattle are joint-connected.
(PB 13.4.7) He sings with various forms. Therefore cattle are of various forms.
(PB 13.4.8) The waters had the flavor of milk. The gods feared worse garments. When they praise placing the waters nearby, it is for the separation of worse garments.
(PB 13.4.9) He who knows thus has a separation from worse garments.
(PB 13.4.10) The <s>Gāyatra</s> rite is for one desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge — having <s>svar</s> (heaven) as its ending, one stands in that world with honey. The <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> rite is for one desiring might — having the syllable 'atha' as its ending, one stands in that world with ghee. The <s>Jāgata</s> rite is for one desiring cattle — having <s>Iḍā</s> as its ending, one stands in that world with milk.
(PB 13.4.11) '<s>Añjasa</s> the <s>Mālya</s> has set the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses in motion,' said <s>Ālamma Pārijānata</s>, <s>Rajana Kauṇāya</s>: 'if he will be able to establish them.' This is the straightening of these: they are established when one quickly begins the chant and quickly sings the <s>Udgītha</s>.
(PB 13.4.12) Having praised with the <s>Śakvarīs</s>, they praise with <s>Purīṣa</s> (earth) verses.
(PB 13.4.13) The <s>Śakvarīs</s> are cattle; <s>Purīṣa</s> is the cattle-pen. They surround the cattle-pen for the cattle. They drive them in — for non-dissolution.
(PB 13.4.14) '<s>Indra</s> has grown for intoxication' — for they increased at that time.
(PB 13.4.15) On those verses, the <s>Bārhadgira</s> (Sāman).
(PB 13.4.16) 'Of the sweet one, thus at the equinox' — for the fifth day is the equinox. On those verses, the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> (Sāman).
(PB 13.4.17) <s>Indra</s> gave the <s>Yatis</s> (ascetics) to the wolves. Three of them survived: <s>Pṛthuraśmi</s>, <s>Bṛhadgiri</s>, and <s>Rāyovāja</s>. They said: 'Who will maintain these our sons?' 'I will,' said <s>Indra</s>. He placed them in his care and went about attending them, nourishing them. Having nourished them he said: 'Young ones, choose boons.' <s>Pṛthuraśmi</s> said: 'Ruling power for me.' He gave him ruling power with this <s>Pārthuraśma</s> Sāman. One desiring ruling power should praise with this — the manifestation of ruling power becomes his. <s>Bṛhadgiri</s> said: 'The splendor of sacred knowledge for me.' He gave him that with this <s>Bārhadgira</s> Sāman. One desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge should praise with this — he becomes endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge. <s>Rāyovāja</s> said: 'Cattle for me.' He gave him cattle with this <s>Rāyovājīya</s> Sāman. One desiring cattle should praise with this — he becomes possessed of cattle.
(PB 13.4.18) The <s>Pārthuraśma</s> should be made the <s>Brahmasāman</s> for a <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior); the <s>Bārhadgira</s> for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> for a <s>Vaiśya</s>. He thereby brings them to fullness by their own form. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 13.5.1) ''asāvy aṃśur madāya-'' iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 13.5.2) ''abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśa'' ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayos saha rūpam upaity ubhau hi varṇāv etad ahaḥ
(PB 13.5.3) ''prāṇā śiśur mahīnām'' iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ mahyo hi simāḥ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 13.5.4) ''pavasva vājasātaya'' iti vaiṣṇavyo 'nuṣṭubho bhavanti
(PB 13.5.5) yajño vai viṣṇur yad atra nāpi kriyate tad viṣṇunā yajñenāpi karoti
(PB 13.5.6) ''indur vājī pavate gonyoghā'' iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 13.5.7) triṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 13.5.7) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 13.5.9) santani bhavati pañcamasyāhnas santatyai
(PB 13.5.90) vāg vā eṣā pratatā yad dvādaśāhas tasyā eṣa viṣuvān yat pañcamam ahas tām evaitena santanoti
(PB 13.5.11) cyāvanaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.5.12) prajātir vai cyāvanaṃ prajāyate bahur bhavati cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.5.13) ebhyo vai lokebhyo vṛṣṭir apākrāmat tāṃ prajāpatiś cyāvanenācyāvayad yad acyāvayat tac cyāvanasya cyāvanatvaṃ cyāvayati vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.5.14) kroṣa bhavati
(PB 13.5.15) etena vā indra indrakrośe viśvāmitrajamadagnī imā gāva ity ākrośat paśunām avarudhyai krośaṃ kriyate
(PB 13.5.16) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 13.5.17) ṛṣabhaḥ śākvaro bhavati
(PB 13.5.18) paśavo vai śakvaryaḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apy arjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
(PB 13.5.19) pārthaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.5.20) etena vai pṛthur vainya ubhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam āśnutobhayeṣāṃ paśunām ādhipatyam aśnute pārthena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.5.21) aṣṭeḍaḥ padastobho bhavati
(PB 13.5.22) indro vṛtrāya vajram udayacchat taṃ ṣoḍaśabhir bhogaiḥ paryabhujat sa etaṃ padastobham apaśyat tenāpāveṣṭayad apāveṣṭayann iva gāyet pāpmano 'pahatyai
(PB 13.5.23) pāpmā vāva sa tam agṛhṇāt taṃ padastobhenāpāhatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate padastobhena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.5.24) pador uttamam apaśyat tat padastobhasya padastobhatvam
(PB 13.5.25) dvādaśanidhano bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.5.26) dāśaspatyaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.5.27) yāṃ vai gāṃ praśaṃsanti dāśaspatyeti tāṃ praśaṃsanty ahar evaitena praśaṃsanti
(PB 13.5.28) nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.5.1) '<s>Asāv aṃśur madāya</s>' — it is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The third pressing is indeed full of intoxication and juice — thereby he places intoxication and juice.
(PB 13.5.2) '<s>Abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśaḥ</s>' — the word '<s>abhi</s>' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>; the word '<s>bṛhat</s>' — it takes up the form of both together, of both the <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this day has both characters.
(PB 13.5.3) '<s>Prāṇā śiśur mahīnām</s>' — this is the form of the <s>Simā</s> cows, for the great ones are <s>Simā</s> cows. Thereby he enriches them with their own proper form.
(PB 13.5.4) '<s>Pavasva vājasātaye</s>' — these are <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s>) <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses.
(PB 13.5.5) <s>Viṣṇu</s> is indeed the sacrifice. Whatever is not performed here, that he performs by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the sacrifice.
(PB 13.5.6) '<s>Indur vājī pavate gonyoghāḥ</s>' — this is the form of the <s>Simā</s> cows. Thereby he enriches them with their own proper form.
(PB 13.5.7) The <s>Triṣṭubhs</s> are true, in the form of <s>Jagatī</s>. Therefore they are rendered in the world of the <s>Jagatīs</s>.
(PB 13.5.8) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> — for whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 13.5.9) It has the <s>Santani</s> — for the continuation of the fifth day.
(PB 13.5.10) Speech is indeed what is stretched out, namely the twelve-day rite. The fifth day is the <s>Viṣuvān</s> (solstice day) of it. By this he weaves it together.
(PB 13.5.11) It has the <s>Cyāvana</s>.
(PB 13.5.12) Procreation is indeed the <s>Cyāvana</s>. He is procreated and becomes abundant — he who has praised with the <s>Cyāvana</s>.
(PB 13.5.13) Rain departed from these worlds. <s>Prajāpati</s> caused it to flow (<s>acyāvayat</s>) by the <s>Cyāvana</s>. Because he caused it to flow, that is the <s>cyāvana</s>-nature of the <s>Cyāvana</s>. He causes rain to flow — he who has praised with the <s>Cyāvana</s>.
(PB 13.5.14) It has the <s>Kroṣa</s> (calling-chant).
(PB 13.5.15) By this <s>Indra</s>, at the <s>Indrakroṣa</s>, called out to <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>: 'These are my cows!' The <s>Kroṣa</s> is performed for the obtainment of animals.
(PB 13.5.16) It has the <s>Gaurīvita</s> — for whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 13.5.17) It has the <s>Ṛṣabha</s> (bull-chant) in <s>Śakvara</s> verses.
(PB 13.5.18) <s>Śakvara</s> verses are indeed animals. Thereby he procures a mating pair among animals — for procreation. For animals are not born without a bull.
(PB 13.5.19) It has the <s>Pārtha</s>.
(PB 13.5.20) By this <s>Pṛthu Vainya</s> attained sovereignty over both kinds of animals. He attains sovereignty over both kinds of animals — he who has praised with the <s>Pārtha</s>.
(PB 13.5.21) It has the <s>Padastobha</s> with eight <s>Iḍā</s> portions.
(PB 13.5.22) <s>Indra</s> raised his <s>vajra</s> against <s>Vṛtra</s>. <s>Vṛtra</s> encoiled it with sixteen coils. <s>Indra</s> perceived this <s>Padastobha</s>. By it he unwound it. One should sing as if unwinding — for the removal of evil.
(PB 13.5.23) Evil indeed seized him. By the <s>Padastobha</s> he struck it away. He strikes away evil — he who has praised with the <s>Padastobha</s>.
(PB 13.5.24) He perceived the highest in the foot-exclamation — that is the <s>padastobha</s>-nature of the <s>Padastobha</s>.
(PB 13.5.25) It has twelve <s>nidhanas</s> — for firm establishment.
(PB 13.5.26) It has the <s>Dāśaspatya</s>.
(PB 13.5.27) The cow that they praise is praised as '<s>dāśaspatya</s>' — they praise the day itself with this.
(PB 13.5.28) The <s>Pavamānas</s> end with <s>nidhanas</s> — for upholding the day. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 13.6.1) ''āte agna idhīmahi-'' iti
(PB 13.6.2) apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
(PB 13.6.3) ''indrāya sāma gāyata-'' iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhas tenānaśanāyuko bhavati
(PB 13.6.4) puruṣo vai kakup puruṣam eva tan madhyataḥ prīṇāti
(PB 13.6.5) ''asāvi soma indra ta'' iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivaināṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
(PB 13.6.6) sañjayaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.6.7) devāś ca vā asurāś ca samadadhata yatare naḥ sañjayāṃs teṣāṃ naḥ paśavo 'sān iti te devā asurān sañjayena samajayan yat samajayaṃs tasmāt sañjayaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai sañjayaṃ kriyate
(PB 13.6.8) saumitraṃ bhavati
(PB 13.6.9) dīrghajihvī vā idaṃ rakṣo yajñahā yajñiyān avalihaty acarat tām indraḥ kayācana māyayā hantuṃ nāśaṃsatātha ha sumitraḥ kutsaḥ kalyāṇa āsa tam abravīd imām acchā brūṣveti tām acchā brūta sainam abravīn nāhaitan na śuśruva priyam iva tu me hṛdayasyeti tām ajñapayat tāṃ saṃskṛte 'hatāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma saumitraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 13.6.10) sumitraḥ san krūram akar ity enaṃ vāg abhyavadat taṃ śug ārcchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etat saumitram apaśyat tena śucam apāhatāpaśucaṃ hate saumitreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.6.11) mahāvaiśvāmitraṃ bhavati
(PB 13.6.12) pāpmānaṃ hatvā yad amahīyanta tan mahāvaiśvāmitrasya mahāvaiśvāmitratvam
(PB 13.6.13) hāyā ihayā ohā oheti paśūn evaitena nyauhanta
(PB 13.6.14) trīḍaṃ bhavati trirātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 13.6.15) dravantīm iḍām uttamām upayanti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ santatyai
(PB 13.6.16) triṇava eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai puṣṭyai trivṛd vā eṣa puṣṭhaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.6.1) '<s>Ā te agna idhīmahi</s>' —
(PB 13.6.2) The <s>uktha</s> portions are, as it were, a severed limb of the sacrificial body. When it goes, it is for wholeness.
(PB 13.6.3) '<s>Indrāya sāma gāyata</s>' — the <s>Kakubh</s> (peak-meter) verses are complete. Thereby one becomes free from hunger.
(PB 13.6.4) The person is indeed the <s>Kakubh</s> — thereby he pleases the person from the middle.
(PB 13.6.5) '<s>Asāvi soma Indra te</s>' — this is the form of the <s>Simā</s> cows. Thereby he enriches them with their own proper form.
(PB 13.6.6) It has the <s>Sañjaya</s> (conquering-chant).
(PB 13.6.7) The gods and <s>asuras</s> made a compact: 'Whichever of us conquers, theirs shall be the animals.' The gods conquered the <s>asuras</s> with the <s>Sañjaya</s>. Because they conquered (<s>samajayan</s>), therefore it is the <s>Sañjaya</s>. For the obtainment of animals, the <s>Sañjaya</s> is performed.
(PB 13.6.8) It has the <s>Saumitra</s>.
(PB 13.6.9) A long-tongued <s>rakṣas</s> (demon), a sacrifice-destroyer, roamed about licking the sacrificers. <s>Indra</s> was unable to kill it by any means. Now <s>Sumitra</s> <s>Kutsa</s> was a beautiful man. <s>Indra</s> said to him: 'Speak to her.' He spoke to her, and she said: 'I have not heard this, but it is dear to my heart.' He made her known to <s>Indra</s>. When she was caught, she was slain. Whatever desire they had at that time — the <s>Saumitra</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 13.6.10) 'Though being a friend (<s>sumitra</s>), he did a cruel deed' — thus speech reproached him. Grief came upon him. He performed <s>tapas</s>. He perceived this <s>Saumitra</s>. By it he struck away grief. He strikes away grief — he who has praised with the <s>Saumitra</s>.
(PB 13.6.11) It has the <s>Mahāvaiśvāmitra</s>.
(PB 13.6.12) Having slain evil, they were magnified — that is the <s>mahāvaiśvāmitra</s>-nature of the <s>Mahāvaiśvāmitra</s>.
(PB 13.6.13) '<s>Hāyā ihayā ohā oha</s>' — by this they drove down animals.
(PB 13.6.14) It has a threefold <s>Iḍā</s> — for the upholding of the three-night rite.
(PB 13.6.15) They approach the flowing <s>Iḍā</s> as the last — for the continuation into the sixth day.
(PB 13.6.16) The <s>stoma</s> is <s>triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold) only — for firm establishment and nourishment, for the <s>trivṛt</s> is the nourished form of this.

body.text:
(PB 13.7.1) ''jyotir yajñasya pavate madhupriyam'' iti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
(PB 13.7.2) jyotir vai gāyatrī chandamāṃ jyotiḥ revatī sāmnāṃ jyotis trayastriṃśaḥ stomānāṃ jyotir eva tat samyak saṃdadhāsy api ha putrasya putro jyotiṣmān bhavati
(PB 13.7.3) ''madhu priyam'' iti paśavo vai revatyo madhupriyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 13.7.4) ''madintamo matsara indriyo rasa'' itīndriyaṃ vai vīryaṃ rasaḥ paśavas tad eva tad abhivadati
(PB 13.7.5) ''amṛkṣata pravājina'' ity anurūpo bhavati
(PB 13.7.6) sṛṣṭānīva hy etarhy ahāni
(PB 13.7.7) pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 13.7.8) daśarcau bhavato daśākṣarā virāṭ vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 13.7.9) uttaro daśarco bhavati sodarka indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya
(PB 13.7.10) yatra ve devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
(PB 13.7.11) caturṛco bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.7.12) dhvasre vai puruṣantī tarantapurumīḍhābhyāṃ vaitadaśvibhyāṃ sahasrāṇy aditsatāṃ tāv aikṣetāṃ kathaṃ nāv idam āttam apratigṛhītaṃ syād iti tau praty etāṃ dhvasrayoḥ puruṣantyor ā sahasrāṇi dadmahe (daprahe) tarat sa mandī dhāvatīti tato vai tat tayor āttam apratigṛhītam abhavat
(PB 13.7.13) āttam asyāpratigṛhītaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 13.7.14) vinārāśaṃso bhavaty ubhayasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai mānuṣasya ca daivasya ca
(PB 13.7.15) tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 13.7.16) trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
(PB 13.8.1) ''imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa'' ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
(PB 13.8.2) ''prativāṃ sūra udita'' iti sūravan maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 13.8.3) anto vai sūro 'nta etat ṣaṣṭham ahar ahnām anta eva tad ante stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.8.4) ''bhindhi viśvā apadviṣa'' ity aindraṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
(PB 13.8.5) ''yajñasya hi stha ṛtvija'' ity aindrāgnaṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.7.1) 'The light of the sacrifice purifies, honey-sweet' — this is the opening verse of the sixth day.
(PB 13.7.2) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the light of the meters, the <s>Revatī</s> is the light of the <s>sāmans</s>, the thirty-three-fold is the light of the <s>stomas</s>. Thereby one rightly joins light to light. Even the son of his son becomes luminous.
(PB 13.7.3) 'Honey-sweet' — cattle are indeed the <s>Revatīs</s>, honey-sweet; that is what it refers to.
(PB 13.7.4) 'The most intoxicating, exhilarating, endowed with <s>Indra</s>'s power, rich in essence' — <s>Indra</s>'s power is vigor; essence is cattle; that is what it refers to.
(PB 13.7.5) 'He did not crush, O prize-winner' — this is the response-verse (<s>anurūpa</s>).
(PB 13.7.6) For at this point the days are as if released.
(PB 13.7.7) One echoes the first form with the later form. That the first form is echoed by the later form — that is the <s>anurūpa</s>-nature of the <s>anurūpa</s>. A son resembling him is born to one who knows thus. The <s>stotrīya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> are each three-verse groups (<s>tṛca</s>), for obtaining both inbreath and outbreath.
(PB 13.7.8) They are ten-verse groups (<s>daśarca</s>). The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables. The <s>Vairāja</s> is food; it is for obtaining food.
(PB 13.7.9) The latter is a ten-verse group with a concluding verse (<s>sodarka</s>), for not squandering <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence.
(PB 13.7.10) Wherever the <s>devas</s> saw <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence slipping away, they pierced through after it.
(PB 13.7.11) It has a four-verse group, for firm establishment.
(PB 13.7.12) The two <s>Dhvasras</s> and <s>Puruṣantīs</s> wished to give thousands to <s>Tarantapurumīḍha</s> and <s>Vaitadaśvin</s>. The two thought: 'How can what we give not be received by them?' They gave back, saying: 'We give thousands to the two <s>Dhvasras</s> and <s>Puruṣantīs</s> — let the delightful one run across.' Thereby what they gave became unreceived.
(PB 13.7.13) What he gives becomes unreceived by him who knows thus.
(PB 13.7.14) It is without the <s>Ārāśaṃsa</s> recitation, for obtaining food of both kinds — human and divine.
(PB 13.7.15) The final verse-group is a three-verse group (<s>tṛca</s>). With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.
(PB 13.7.16) The <s>stoma</s> is the thirty-three-fold, for firm establishment. It is established among the deities.
(PB 13.8.1) 'This hymn for <s>Jātavedas</s> who deserves it' — the <s>Āgneya</s> (Agni-directed) <s>ājya</s> (ghee-hymn) has a concluding verse, for not squandering <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence. Wherever the <s>devas</s> saw power, vigor, and essence slipping away, they pierced through after it.
(PB 13.8.2) 'Facing you, O <s>Sūrya</s>, as you rise' — the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> verse contains the word sun.
(PB 13.8.3) The sun is the end; this sixth day is the end of the days. They praise at the end for firm establishment.
(PB 13.8.4) 'Split all hostile forces' — this is the <s>Aindra</s> (Indra-directed) verse with a concluding verse, for not squandering <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence. Wherever the <s>devas</s> saw power, vigor, and essence slipping away, they pierced through after it.
(PB 13.8.5) 'For you are the priests of the sacrifice' — this is the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (Indra-and-Agni-directed) verse with a concluding verse, for not squandering <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence. Wherever the <s>devas</s> saw power, vigor, and essence slipping away, they pierced through after it. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 13.9.1) ''indrāyendo marutvata'' iti marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti
(PB 13.9.2) marutvad dhi mādhyandinaṃ savanam
(PB 13.9.3) ''mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya-'' iti simānāṃ rūpam
(PB 13.9.4) samānaṃ vai simānāṃ rūpaṃ revatīnāṃ ca simābhyo hy adhirevatyaḥ prajāyante
(PB 13.9.5) ''etam u tyaṃ daśa kṣipa'' ity ādityā ādityā vā imāḥ prajās tāsām eva madhyataḥ pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 13.9.6) gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 13.9.7) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 13.9.8) iṣovṛdhīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.9.9) paśavo vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ paśūnām avarudhyā iṣe vai pañcamam ahar vṛdhe ṣaṣṭham avardhanta hy etarhi yajamānam evaitena vardhayanti
(PB 13.9.10) krauñcaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.9.11) kruṅṅ eṣyam ahar avindad eṣyam iva vai ṣaṣṭham ahar evaitena vindanti
(PB 13.9.12) vājadāvaryo bhavanti
(PB 13.9.13) annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai yadā hi vā annam atha gaur athāśvo 'tha puruṣo vājī
(PB 13.9.14) revatyo bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.9.15) ṣaṇṇidhanī ṣaḍrātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 13.9.16) āpo vai revatyas tā yat pṛṣṭhaṃ kuryur apaśur yajamānaḥ syāt paśūn asya nirdaheyur yatra vā āpo vivartante tad oṣadhayo jāyante 'tha yatrāvatiṣṭhante nirmṛtukās tatra bhavanti tasmāt pavamāne kurvanti parācā hi pavamānena stuvate
(PB 13.9.17) methī vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ rajjuḥ krauñcaṃ vatso vājadāvaryo revatyo mātaro yad etāny evaṃ sāmāni kriyanta evam eva prattāṃ dugdhe
(PB 13.9.18) aukṣṇorandhre bhavataḥ
(PB 13.9.19) ukṣṇorandhro vā etābhyāṃ kāvyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.9.20) vājajid bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvaṃ vā ete vājaṃ jayanti ye ṣaṣṭham ahar āgacchanti
(PB 13.9.21) annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 13.9.22) varuṇasāma bhavati
(PB 13.9.23) etena vai varuṇo rājyam ādhipatyam agacchad yaśo 'bhavad rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati yaśo bhavati varuṇasāmnā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.9.24) aṅgirasāṃ goṣṭho bhavati
(PB 13.9.25) paśavo vai revatyo gauṣṭham eva tat paśubhyaḥ paryasyanti tam evainān pravartayanty avisraṃsāya
(PB 13.9.26) ihavad vāmadevyaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.9.27) etena vai vāmadevo 'nnasya purodhām agacchad annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhā annasyāvarudhyai
(PB 13.9.28) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarñcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 13.9.29) marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān na yanti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.9.1) 'For <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Indu</s>, accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>' — the <s>Gāyatrīs</s> contain reference to the <s>Maruts</s>.
(PB 13.9.2) For the midday pressing belongs to the <s>Maruts</s>.
(PB 13.9.3) 'Being purified, O skilled one' — this is the form of the <s>simās</s> (boundaries).
(PB 13.9.4) The form of the <s>simās</s> and the <s>Revatīs</s> is the same, for the <s>Revatīs</s> are born from the <s>simās</s>.
(PB 13.9.5) 'Cast this ten-fold one' — these are the <s>Ādityas</s>. The <s>Ādityas</s> are indeed these creatures; one establishes oneself in their midst.
(PB 13.9.6) The <s>Gāyatrīs</s> are true but have the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; therefore they are performed in the realm of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 13.9.7) It is of the <s>Gāyatra</s> type — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 13.9.8) The <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s> chant is used.
(PB 13.9.9) Cattle are indeed the <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s> — for obtaining cattle. The fifth day is for nourishment (<s>iṣe</s>), the sixth for growth (<s>vṛdhe</s>). They indeed grew then; thereby they make the sacrificer grow.
(PB 13.9.10) The <s>Krauñca</s> chant is used.
(PB 13.9.11) The <s>Kruṅ</s> bird found the approaching day. The sixth day is as if approaching; with this they find it.
(PB 13.9.12) The <s>Vājadāvaryās</s> (prize-giving) are used.
(PB 13.9.13) Food is indeed the prize (<s>vāja</s>) — for obtaining food. For when there is food, then there is a cow, then a horse, then a person is a prize-winner.
(PB 13.9.14) The <s>Revatīs</s> are used, for firm establishment.
(PB 13.9.15) It has six endings, for sustaining the six-night period.
(PB 13.9.16) The <s>Revatīs</s> are waters. If they were made a <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), the sacrificer would be without cattle — they would burn away his cattle. Where waters turn, there herbs grow; but where they stand still, there becomes season-less. Therefore they use them in the <s>Pavamāna</s> (purification chant), for one praises with the <s>Pavamāna</s> facing away.
(PB 13.9.17) The <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s> is the stake, the <s>Krauñca</s> is the rope, the calf is the <s>Vājadāvaryā</s>, the <s>Revatīs</s> are the mothers. When these <s>sāmans</s> are performed thus, one milks from what is tied thus.
(PB 13.9.18) The <s>Aukṣṇorandhra</s> chants are used.
(PB 13.9.19) With these two <s>Aukṣṇorandhra</s> chants, <s>Kāvya</s> directly saw the heavenly world — for the recognition of the heavenly world. He who praises thus does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 13.9.20) The <s>Vājajit</s> (prize-winning) chant is used, for obtaining all and conquering all. Those who reach the sixth day indeed win the entire prize.
(PB 13.9.21) Food is indeed the prize — for obtaining food.
(PB 13.9.22) The <s>Varuṇa Sāman</s> is used.
(PB 13.9.23) With this, <s>Varuṇa</s> attained kingship, sovereignty, and fame. He who praises with the <s>Varuṇa Sāman</s> attains kingship, sovereignty, and fame.
(PB 13.9.24) It becomes the cowpen of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>.
(PB 13.9.25) Cattle are indeed the <s>Revatīs</s>. They encircle the cowpen for the cattle. They set them in motion for the sake of non-collapse.
(PB 13.9.26) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> chant containing <s>iha</s> (here) is used.
(PB 13.9.27) With this, <s>Vāmadeva</s> attained the pre-eminence of food. Food is the pre-eminence of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; it is for obtaining food.
(PB 13.9.28) They praise in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for firm establishment and <s>brahmavarcas</s>. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.
(PB 13.9.29) The <s>Gāyatrīs</s> contain reference to the <s>Maruts</s>; thereby they do not depart from the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> form. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

(PB 13.10.1) yātayāmāny anyāni chandāṃsy ayātayāmā gāyatrī tasmād gāyatrīṣu stuvanti
(PB 13.10.2) ''surūpa kṛtnum ūtaya'' ity abhyārambheṇa ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
(PB 13.10.3) ''ubhe yad indra rodasī'' iti ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
(PB 13.10.4) revatīṣu vāravantīyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.10.5) apāṃ vā eṣa raso yad revatyo revatīnāṃ raso yad vāravantīyaṃ sarasā eva tad revatīḥ prayuṅkte yad vāravantīyena pṛṣṭhena stuvate
(PB 13.10.6) revad vā etad raivatyaṃ yad vāravantīyam asya revān revātyā jāyate
(PB 13.10.7) revān bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 13.10.8) keśine vā etad dālbhyāya sāmāvir abhavat tad enam abravīd agātāro mā gāyanti mā mayodgāsiṣur iti kathaṃ ta āgā bhagava ity abravīd āgeyam evāsmy āgāyann iva gāyet pratiṣṭhāyai tad alammaṃ pārijānataṃ paścādakṣaṃ śayānam etām āgāṃ gāyantam ajānāt tam abravīt puras tvā dadhā iti tam abruvan ko nv ayaṃ kasmā alam ity alaṃ nu vai mahyam iti tad alammasyālammatvam
(PB 13.10.9) iheheti gāyet pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 13.10.11) ṛṣabho raivato bhavati
(PB 13.10.11) paśavo vai raivatyaḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apyarjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
(PB 13.10.12) śyeno bhavati
(PB 13.10.13) śyeno ha vai pūrvapretāni vayāṃsy āpnoti pūrvapretānīva vai pūrvāṇy ahāni teṣām āptyai śyenaḥ kriyate
(PB 13.10.14) śyeno vā etad ahaḥ sampārayitum arhati sa hi vayasām āśiṣṭhas tasyānapahananāya sampāraṇāyaitat kriyate 'nto hi ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca
(PB 13.10.15) brahmavādino vadanti yad bṛhad āyatanāni pṛṣṭhāny athaite dve gāyatryau dve jagatyau kva tarhi bṛhatyo bhavantīti
(PB 13.10.16) ye dve jagatyoḥ pade te gāyatryā upasampadyete tat sarvā bṛhatyo bhavanty āyatane pṛṣṭhāni yātayatyāyatanavān bhavati
(PB 13.10.17) ṣaṭpadāsu stuvanti ṣaḍrātrasya dhṛtyai
(PB 13.10.18) saptapadayā yajati saptamasyāhnaḥ santatyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.10.1) The other meters are exhausted, but the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is not exhausted. Therefore they chant in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.
(PB 13.10.2) 'Of beautiful form, the maker, for protection' — these are six-footed verses, having the nature of the sixth day, by which they commence the sixth day, for the sake of continuity.
(PB 13.10.3) 'When, O <s>Indra</s>, both the worlds' — these are six-footed verses, having the nature of the sixth day, by which they commence the sixth day.

body.text:
(PB 13.11.1) ''parisvāno giriṣṭhā'' iti parivatyo gāyatryo bhavanti sarvasya paryāptyai

(PB 13.11.4) vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca
(PB 13.11.5) yad etau vālakhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgayāvyatisraṃsāya santatyai

(PB 13.11.11) bharadvājasya lomata bhavati
(PB 13.11.12) paśavo vai loma paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 13.11.13) tad u dīrgham ity āhur āyur vai dīrgham āyuṣo 'varudhyai
(PB 13.11.14) kārṇaśravasaṃ bhavati śṛṇvanti tuṣṭuvānam

(PB 13.11.16) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati gaur:ivitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 13.11.17) madhuścyunnidhanaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.11.18) paramasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai paramaṃ vā etad annādya yan madhu
(PB 13.11.19) prajāpater vā etau stanau yad ghṛtaścyunnidhanaṃ ca madhuścyunnidhanaṃ ca yajño vai prajāpatis tam etābhyāṃ dugdhe yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate taṃ dugdhe
(PB 13.11.20) krauñce bhavataḥ
(PB 13.11.22) śnauṣṭhaṃ bhavati
(PB 13.11.23) śnuṣṭir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāt lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 13.11.24) agner vā etad vaiśvānaraṃ sāma dīdihīti nidhanam upayanti dīdā eva hy agnir vaiśvānaraḥ
(PB 13.11.25) nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.11.1) 'The one dwelling on the mountain, sounding around' — these are encircling (<s>parivatī</s>) <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for the completion of everything.
(PB 13.11.2) 'The one to be pressed with good pressings, of riches' — cattle are indeed wealth. For the securing of cattle.
(PB 13.11.3) 'Him, for your intoxication, O companions' — these are the <s>Vālakhilya</s> [hymns].
(PB 13.11.4) These two <s>tṛcas</s> (groups of three verses) are the <s>Vālakhilyas</s> on the sixth and seventh days.
(PB 13.11.5) When these

(PB 13.12.6) gotamasya bhandra bhavati
(PB 13.12.7) āśiṣam evāsmā etenāśāste sāma hi satyāśīḥ
(PB 13.12.8) etena vai gotamo jemānaṃ mahimānam agacchat tasmād ye ca parāñco gotamād ye cārvāñcas ta ubhaye gotamā ṛṣayo bruvate
(PB 13.12.9) udvaṃśaputrā bhavati
(PB 13.12.10) yad vā udvaṃśīyaṃ tad udvaṃśaputraḥ
(PB 13.12.11) ardheḍām atisvarati
(PB 13.12.12) tasmād ūdhardhārā ati carantīḍāyām antataḥ paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 13.12.13) kḷpta upariṣṭād ṛk sāma ca vimucyete abhy u svareṇa saptamam ahaḥ svarati santatyai

(PB 13.12.16) trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 13.12.1) The <s>brahmavādins</s> (theological disputants) say: 'From the introductory rite, two-footed [verses] should be made; from the concluding rite, likewise.'
(PB 13.12.2) They should be made from the concluding rite. The person is two-footed — for firm establishment.
(PB 13.12.3) By speech indeed they stretch out the entire sacrifice. Therefore a person speaks all speech, for all [speech] that has been chanted in him becomes established.
(PB 13.12.4) He becomes a mute.
