body.text:
(PB 14.1.1) āpyante vā etat stomāś chandāṃsi yat ṣaḍaha āpyate
(PB 14.1.2) āpte ṣaḍahe chandāṃsi stomān kṛtvā prayanti
(PB 14.1.3) ''pra kāvyam uśanevara bruvāṇa'' iti gāyatryā rūpeṇa prayanti
(PB 14.1.4) iyaṃ vai gāyatry asyām eva pratiṣṭhāya prayanti
(PB 14.1.5) triṣṭup pratipad bhavati
(PB 14.1.6) ojo vīryaṃ triṣṭubojasyeva vīrye parākramya prayanti
(PB 14.1.7) stotrīyas tṛco bhavati prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 14.1.8) harivatyo bhavanti chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 14.1.9) dvādaśarcau bhavataḥ
(PB 14.1.10) dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
(PB 14.1.11) caturviṃśatir bhavanti caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
(PB 14.1.12) dṛta aindrota iti hovācābhipratārī kākṣasenir ye mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ gacchanti ka te tato bhavanti prarājan pakṣiṇaḥ patanty avāpakṣāḥ padyante
(PB 14.1.13) ye vai vidvāṃsas te pakṣiṇo ye 'vidvāṃsas te 'pakṣās trivṛt pañcadaśāv eva stomau pakṣau kṛtvā svarga lokaṃ prayanti
(PB 14.1.14) caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati teja se brahmavarcasāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.1.1) When the six-day period is completed, the <s>stomas</s> (chant patterns) and meters are indeed fulfilled.
(PB 14.1.2) When the six-day period is completed, the meters, having been made into <s>stomas</s>, go forth.
(PB 14.1.3) 'The poetic work of <s>Uśanas</s>, proclaiming' — they go forth in the form of <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
(PB 14.1.4) This is indeed the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Having established themselves in this, they go forth.
(PB 14.1.5) The opening verse is in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 14.1.6)

body.text:
(PB 14.2.1) ''mūrdhānaṃ divo aratim pṛthivyā'' ity āgreyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.2.2) mūrdhā vā eṣa divo yas tṛtīyas trirātraḥ
(PB 14.2.3) ''vaiśvānaram ṛta ājātam agnim'' iti vaiśvānara iti vā agneḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
(PB 14.2.4) ''pra vo mitrāya gāyata-'' iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī vai mitrāvaruṇayoḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainau tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
(PB 14.2.5) ''indrāyāhi citrabhānav'' ity ārbhavam aindram ṛbhavo vā indrasya priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
(PB 14.2.6) ''tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā-'' ity aniruktam aindrāgnaṃ devatānām anabhidharṣāyottamārdhe 'nirāha devatānām apraṇāśāya stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.2.1) 'The crown of heaven, the hub of the earth' — this <s>ājya</s> (chant) belongs to <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 14.2.2) The crown of heaven is indeed this third three-night period.
(PB 14.2.3) '<s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, born in the cosmic order' — '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' is indeed the beloved abode of <s>Agni</s>. With this beloved abode one approaches him in a hidden manner.
(PB 14.2.4) 'Sing forth to <s>Mitra</s> for you'

body.text:
(PB 14.3.1) ''vṛṣā pavasva dhāraya-'' iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
(PB 14.3.2) vṛṣaṇvatyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.3.3) ''punānaḥ soma dhāraya-'' iti dhṛtyai
(PB 14.3.4) ''pro ayāsīd indur indrasya niṣkṛtam'' iti pravatyo bhavanti praṇinīṣeṇyam iva hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.3.5) jagatyaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 14.3.7) santani bhavati saptamasyāhnaḥ santatyai
(PB 14.3.8) yathā vai vyokasau vipradravata evam ete ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca vipradravatas tau yathā samānīya saṃyujyād evam evaite etena sāmnā saṃyunakti
(PB 14.3.10) yajño vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat sa suparṇarūpaṃ kṛtvācarat taṃ devā etaiḥ sāmabhirārabhanta yajña iva vā eṣa yac chandomā yajñasyaivaiṣa ārambhaḥ
(PB 14.3.11) rohitakūlīyaṃ bhavaty ājijityāyai
(PB 14.3.12) etena vai viśvāmitro rohitābhyāṃ rohitakūla ājim ajayat
(PB 14.3.13) viśvāmitro bharatānāṃ manassatyāyāt so 'dantibhir nāma janatayāṃśaṃ prāsyate māṃ māṃ yūyaṃ astikāṃ jayāthemāni mahyaṃ yūyaṃ pūrayātha yadīmāv idaṃ rohitāv aśmācitaṃ kūlam udvahāta iti sa ete sāmanī apaśyat tābhyāṃ yuktvā prāsedhat sa udjayat
(PB 14.3.14) ājir vā eṣa pratato yad dvādaśāhas tasyaite ujjityai
(PB 14.3.15) kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tejo vā etad rathantarasya yat kaṇvarathantaram
(PB 14.3.16) sarasam eva tad rathantaraṃ prayuṅkte yat kaṇvarathantareṇa saptame 'hani stuvate
(PB 14.3.17) jāmi dvādaśāhasyāstīti ha smāhogradevo rājanir bārhataṃ ṣaṣṭham ahar bārhataṃ saptamaṃ yat kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tenājāmi
(PB 14.3.18) gauṅgavaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.3.19) agnir akāmayatānnādaḥ syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad gauṅgavam apaśyat tenānnādo 'bhavad yad annaṃ vitvā gardadyad agaṅgūyat tad gauṅgavasya gauṅgavatvam annādyasyāvarudhyai gauṅgavaṃ kiyate
(PB 14.3.20) yat sāma devatā praśaṃyati tena yajamānāḥ satyāśiṣaḥ satyāśiṣo 'sāmeti vai sattram āsate satyāśiṣa eva bhavanti
(PB 14.3.21) āyāsyaṃ bhavati tiraścīnanidhanaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 14.3.22) ayāsyo vā āṅgirasa ādityānāṃ dīkṣitānām annam āśnāt sa vyabhraṃśata sa etāny āyāsyāny apaśyat tair ātmānaṃ samaśrīṇād vibhraṣṭam iva vai saptamam ahar yad etat sāma bhavaty ahar eva tena saṃśrīṇāti
(PB 14.3.23) pravadbhargavaṃ bhavati
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.3.1) 'O bull, purify yourself, sustain' — this is in <s>Gāyatrī</s>, for sustaining the day.
(PB 14.3.2) The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses have the bull-like form, for this day belongs to the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 14.3.3) 'Being purified, O <s>Soma</s>, sustain' — for sustaining.
(PB 14.3.4) 'The <s>Soma</s> drop has gone forth to <s>Indra's</s> purification' — these are the outgoing (<s>pravatī</s>) verses, for this day is one that needs to be led forth.
(PB 14.3.)

body.text:
(PB 14.4.1) ''vayaṃ ghatvā sutāvanta'' iti bṛhatyo varṣīyaśchanda ākramate 'napabhraṃśāya
(PB 14.4.2) ''nakiṣ ṭaṃ karmaṇā naśad'' iti bṛhatyaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa jagatyaḥ
(PB 14.4.3) apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yaj jyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa jagatyo bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
(PB 14.4.4) abhinidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃ bhavita
(PB 14.4.5) abhinidhanena vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tam astṛṇuta stṛṇute bhrātṛvyam abhinidhanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.4.7) vaikhānasā vā ṛṣaya indrasya priyā āsaṃs tān rahasyur devamalimluḍ munimaraṇe 'mārayat taṃ devā abruvan kva tarṣayo (?) 'bhūvānn iti tān praiṣam aicchat tān nāvindat sa imān lokān ekadhāreṇāpunāt tān munimaraṇe 'vindat tān etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vaikhānasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.4.1) 'We, possessing pressed [<s>Soma</s>], indeed to you' — these are in <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter]. One advances to a larger meter, to prevent falling away.
(PB 14.4.2) 'No one shall destroy him by any action' — these are <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses; truly with the approach they become <s>Jagatī</s> verses.
(PB 14.4.3) There is, as it were, a falling away when one descends from a greater <s>stoma</s> to a lesser <s>stoma</s>. Because these become <s>Jagatī</s> verses through the approach, of the day indeed

body.text:
(PB 14.5.1) ''yas te mado vareṇya'' iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 14.5.2) ''eṣasya dhārayā suta'' iti kakubhaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa triṣṭubhaḥ
(PB 14.5.3) apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yat jyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa triṣṭubho bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
(PB 14.5.4) ''sakhāya āniṣīdata-'' iti vālakhilyā vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca yad etau vākhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgāyāvyavasraṃsāya santatyai
(PB 14.5.5) ''purojitī vo andhasa'' iti virāḍ annaṃ virāḍ annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.5.6) ''pra vājy akṣār'' ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtiḥ
(PB 14.5.7) atho etad (?) dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante
(PB 14.5.8) brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
(PB 14.5.9) ''ye somāsaḥ parāvati-'' iti parāvatam iva vā etarhi yajño gatas tam evaitenānvicchanti
(PB 14.5.12) dakṣaṇidhanaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.5.13) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā asmāt sṛṣṭā abalā ivācchadayaṃs tāsv etena sāmnā dakṣāyety ojo vīryam adadhād yad etat sāma bhavaty oja eva vīryam ātman dhatte
(PB 14.5.14) śārkaraṃ bhavati
(PB 14.5.15) indraṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny astuvan sa śarkaraṃ śiśumārarṣim upetyābravīt stuhi meti so 'paḥ praskandann abravīd etāvato 'haṃ tvāṃ stuyām iti tasmād apāṃ vegam avejayat sa hīna ivāmanyata sa etat sāmāpaśyat tenāpo 'nusamāśnuta tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma śārkaraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 14.5.13) plavo bhavati
(PB 14.5.17) samudraṃ vā ete prasnāntīty āhur ye dvādaśāham upayantīti yo vā aplavaḥ samudraṃ prarunāti na sa tata udeti yata plavo bhavati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
(PB 14.5.18) ativiśvāni duritā taremeti yad evaiṣāṃ duṣṭutaṃ duśśastaṃ tad etena taranti
(PB 14.5.19) ekādaśākṣaraṇidhano bhavaty ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub ojīvīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasy eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 14.5.20) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brahmaṇam
(PB 14.5.21) kārtayaśaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.5.22) hīti nidhanam upayanti pāpmano 'pahatyai
(PB 14.5.23) apa pāpmānaṃ hate kārtayaśena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.5.24) sāhaiviṣaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.5.25) suhavir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.5.26) brahmāvādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣaś chandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadā chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 14.5.27) jarābodhīyaṃ bhavaty annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.5.28) annaṃ vai jarābodhīyaṃ mukhaṃ gāyatrī mukha eva tad annaṃ dhatte 'nnam atti
(PB 14.5.29) annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 14.5.30) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 14.5.31) iḍāntāḥ pāvamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍāḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.5.1) '<s>Yas te mado vareṇya</s>' — it is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The third pressing is indeed full of intoxication and juice — thereby he places intoxication and juice.
(PB 14.5.2) '<s>Eṣasya dhārayā sutaḥ</s>' — the <s>Kakubh</s> verses are true, with supporting <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses.
(PB 14.5.3) It is, as it were, a falling off when they go from a greater <s>stoma</s> to a lesser <s>stoma</s>. Since these become <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses with support, it is for propping up the day itself.
(PB 14.5.4) '<s>Sakhāya āniṣīdata</s>' — these are <s>Vālakhilya</s> (supplementary hymns). These two <s>Vālakhilya</s> <s>tṛcas</s> are for the sixth and seventh days. Since these two <s>Vālakhilya</s> <s>tṛcas</s> occur, they serve to interlink the days, to prevent falling apart, and for continuation.
(PB 14.5.5) '<s>Purojitī vo andhasa</s>' — this is in <s>Virāj</s>. Food is <s>Virāj</s> — for the obtainment of food-eating.
(PB 14.5.6) '<s>Pra vājy akṣāḥ</s>' — this is the <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s> (syllable-<s>Paṅkti</s>), the origin of <s>stomas</s>.
(PB 14.5.7) Moreover, this is indeed the meter that is unfatigued at this point, namely the <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s>. By it the <s>chandomās</s> (meter-measures) are rendered unfatigued.
(PB 14.5.8) The speakers of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'When in the six-day rite the <s>stomas</s> and meters are exhausted, what remains as meter-measure of the meters?' One should answer: 'These <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s> verses are the remainder of the meter.'
(PB 14.5.9) '<s>Ye somāsaḥ parāvati</s>' — the sacrifice has, as it were, gone far away at this point. By this they seek it out again.
(PB 14.5.12) It has the <s>Dakṣa</s>-<s>nidhana</s>.
(PB 14.5.13) <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Those, once created, covered him as if powerless. By this <s>sāman</s>, saying '<s>dakṣāya</s>' (for vigor), he placed power and vigor in them. Since this <s>sāman</s> occurs, he places power and vigor in his own self.
(PB 14.5.14) It has the <s>Śārkara</s>.
(PB 14.5.15) All beings praised <s>Indra</s>. He approached <s>Śarkara</s>, the <s>Śiśumāra</s> (crocodile) <s>ṛṣi</s>, and said: 'Praise me!' He, leaping over the waters, said: 'I would praise you this much.' Therefore <s>Indra</s> caused the force of the waters to rush. <s>Śarkara</s> felt as if abandoned. He perceived this <s>sāman</s>. By it he caught up with the waters. Whatever desire he had at that time — the <s>Śārkara</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 14.5.16) It has the <s>Plava</s> (raft-chant).
(PB 14.5.17) They say: 'Those who undertake the twelve-day rite swim across the ocean, as it were.' He who attempts to cross the ocean without a raft does not emerge from it. Therefore there is the <s>Plava</s> — for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 14.5.18) 'May we cross over all difficulties' — whatever was badly praised or badly recited by them, by this they cross over that.
(PB 14.5.19) It has an eleven-syllable <s>nidhana</s>. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> has eleven syllables; power and vigor are the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Thereby he becomes firmly established in power and vigor.
(PB 14.5.20) It has the <s>Gaurīvita</s> — for whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 14.5.21) It has the <s>Kārtayaśa</s>.
(PB 14.5.22) They approach the <s>nidhana</s> '<s>hī</s>' — for the removal of evil.
(PB 14.5.23) He strikes away evil — he who has praised with the <s>Kārtayaśa</s>.
(PB 14.5.24) It has the <s>Sāhaiviṣa</s>.
(PB 14.5.25) <s>Suhavi</s> the <s>Sauśravasa</s> of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> clan directly perceived the heavenly world by this — for a vision of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 14.5.26) The speakers of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'When in the six-day rite the <s>stomas</s> and meters are exhausted, what remains as meter-measure of the meters?' One should answer: 'The person is the meter.' For the person is five-fold; the person is the two-footed meter-measure — for the unfatiguedness of the meter-measures.
(PB 14.5.27) It has the <s>Jarābodhīya</s> — for the obtainment of food-eating.
(PB 14.5.28) Food is the <s>Jarābodhīya</s>; the mouth is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Thereby he places food at the mouth. He eats food.
(PB 14.5.29) He becomes a food-eater — he who knows thus.
(PB 14.5.30) They praise with <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses — for firm establishment and brahmanical splendor. By whatever vital breath they proceed, by that they rise up.
(PB 14.5.31) The <s>Pavamānas</s> end with <s>Iḍā</s> portions. Animals are <s>Iḍā</s>; animals are the meter-measures. Thereby he places animals among animals. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.6.1) ''ā te vatso mano yamad'' ity apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
(PB 14.6.2) ''tvaṃ na indrābhara-'' iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhaḥ
(PB 14.6.3) apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yaj jayāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etāḥ pūrṇāḥ kakubho bhavanty anapabhraṃśāya
(PB 14.6.6) vatsaś ca vai medhātithiś ca kāṇvāv āstāṃ taṃ vatsaṃ medhātithir ākrośad abrāhmaṇo 'si śūdrāputra iti so 'bravīd ṛtenāgniṃ vyayāva yataro nau brahmīyān iti vātsena vatso vyain maidhātithena medhātithis tasya na loma ca nauṣat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vātsaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 14.6.7) sauśravasaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.6.8) upagur vai sauśravasaḥ kutsasyauravasya purohita āsīt sa kutsaḥ paryaśapad ya indraṃ yajātā iti sa indraḥ suśravasam upetyābravīd yajasva māśanāyāmivā iti tam ayajata sa indraḥ puroḍāśas taḥ kutsam upetyābravīd ayakṣata mā kva te pariśaptam abhūd iti kas tvā yaṣṭeti suśravā iti sa kutsa aurava upāgāḥ sauśravasasyodgāyata audumbaryā śiro 'cchinat sa śuśravā indram abravīt tvattanād vai medam īdṛg upāgād iti tam etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma sauśravasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 14.6.9) vīṅkaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.6.10) cyavano vai dādhīco 'śvinoḥ priya āsīt so 'jīryat tam etena sāmnāpsu vyaiṅkayatāṃ taṃ punaryuvānam akurutāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma vīṅkaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 14.6.11) caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.6.1) '<s>Ā te vatso mano yamat</s>' — the <s>uktha</s> portions are, as it were, a severed limb of the sacrificial body. When it goes, it is for wholeness.
(PB 14.6.2) '<s>Tvaṃ na Indrābhara</s>' — the <s>Kakubh</s> verses are complete.
(PB 14.6.3) It is, as it were, a falling off when they go from a greater <s>stoma</s> to a lesser <s>stoma</s>. Since these become complete <s>Kakubh</s> verses, it is to prevent falling off.
(PB 14.6.6) <s>Vatsa</s> and <s>Medhātithi</s>, both of the <s>Kāṇva</s> clan, were there. <s>Medhātithi</s> reviled <s>Vatsa</s>: 'You are not a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>! You are the son of a <s>Śūdra</s>!' He said: 'Let us separate the fire by truth — whichever of us is more priestly.' <s>Vatsa</s> separated it with the <s>Vātsa</s> sāman, <s>Medhātithi</s> with the <s>Maidhātitha</s>. Not a hair of <s>Vatsa</s>'s was singed. Whatever desire he had at that time — the <s>Vātsa</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 14.6.7) It has the <s>Sauśravasa</s>.
(PB 14.6.8) <s>Upagur Sauśravasa</s> was the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) of <s>Kutsa Aurava</s>. <s>Kutsa</s> cursed: 'Whoever sacrifices for <s>Indra</s>!' <s>Indra</s> approached <s>Suśravas</s> and said: 'Sacrifice for me — I am like one starving!' He sacrificed for <s>Indra</s>. <s>Indra</s>, from the offering cakes, approached <s>Kutsa</s> and said: 'He has sacrificed for me. Where is your curse now?' 'Who sacrificed for you?' '<s>Suśravas</s>.' <s>Kutsa Aurava</s> went to the singing of the <s>Sauśravasa</s> and cut off <s>Suśravas</s>'s head with the <s>Audumbarī</s> (fig-wood implement). <s>Suśravas</s> said to <s>Indra</s>: 'Because of my connection to you, this has come upon me.' <s>Indra</s> revived him with this <s>sāman</s>. Whatever desire he had at that time — the <s>Sauśravasa</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 14.6.9) It has the <s>Vīṅka</s>.
(PB 14.6.10) <s>Cyavana Dādhīca</s> was dear to the <s>Aśvins</s>. He grew old. They immersed him in the waters with this <s>sāman</s> and made him young again. Whatever desire they had at that time — the <s>Vīṅka</s> fulfills desires; by this he obtains the desire.
(PB 14.6.11) The <s>stoma</s> is <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-fold) only — for brilliance and brahmanical splendor.

body.text:
(PB 14.7.1) ''śiśuṃ jajñānaṃ haryataṃ mṛjanti'' ity aṣṭam asy āhnaḥ pratid bhavati
(PB 14.7.2) śiśur iva vā eṣa saptamenāhnā jāyate tam aṣṭamenāhnā mṛjanti
(PB 14.7.3) stotrīyas tṛco bhavati prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 14.7.4) harivatyo bhavanti chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 14.7.5) navarcā bhavanti
(PB 14.7.7) pañcarco bhavati pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅktam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.7.8) bāṇavān bhavaty anto vai bāṇo 'nta etad aṣṭamam ahnām anta eva tad antena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 14.7.9) trayas tṛcā bhavanti prāṇāpānānāṃ santatyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.7.1) '<s>Śiśuṃ jajñānaṃ haryataṃ mṛjanti</s>' — this becomes the introductory verse (<s>pratipad</s>) of the eighth day.
(PB 14.7.2) It is as if a child is born on the seventh day — on the eighth day they cleanse it.
(PB 14.7.3) The <s>stotrīya</s> is a <s>tṛca</s> (verse-triplet) — for the obtainment of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(PB 14.7.4) The verses contain '<s>hari</s>' (tawny, pertaining to horses) — for the unfatiguedness of the meter-measures.
(PB 14.7.5) They consist of nine verses.
(PB 14.7.7) It has five verses. The <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; food belongs to the group of five — for the obtainment of food-eating.
(PB 14.7.8) It has the <s>Bāṇa</s> (arrow-chant). The <s>Bāṇa</s> is the end; the eighth is the end of the days. Thereby he praises with the end at the end — for firm establishment.
(PB 14.7.9) There are three <s>tṛcas</s> — for the continuation of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.8.1) ''agniṃ vo devam agnibhiḥ sajoṣā'' ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.8.2) agnibhir ity eva pūrvāṇy ahāni abhi samiddhāny aṣṭamam ahar abhisamindhe
(PB 14.8.3) ''mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha'' iti bārhataṃ maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 14.8.4) ugragādham iva vā etac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyātiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya
(PB 14.8.5) ''tam indraṃ vājayāmasi-'' ity aindram
(PB 14.8.6) aṣṭamena vai devā ahnendram avājayan navamena pāpmānam aghnann ahar evaitena vājayanti
(PB 14.8.7) ''indre agnā namo bṛhad'' iti bārhatam aindrāgnam
(PB 14.8.8) ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rape vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.8.1) '<s>Agniṃ vo devam agnibhiḥ sajoṣāḥ</s>' — the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-offering chant) pertains to <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 14.8.2) '<s>Agnibhiḥ</s>' (by the fires) — thus the previous days were fully kindled; the eighth day is fully kindled.
(PB 14.8.3) '<s>Mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe</s>' — a <s>Bārhata</s> (pertaining to <s>Bṛhat</s>) <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> chant.
(PB 14.8.4) The meter-measures are, as it were, at a deep ford. Just as at a deep ford one interlocks and wades, even so he interlocks the forms — so that the meter-measures are not scattered.
(PB 14.8.5) '<s>Tam Indraṃ vājayāmasi</s>' — pertaining to <s>Indra</s>.
(PB 14.8.6) On the eighth day the gods strengthened <s>Indra</s>; on the ninth they slew evil. They thereby strengthen the day itself.
(PB 14.8.7) '<s>Indre agnā namo bṛhat</s>' — a <s>Bārhata</s> chant pertaining to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 14.8.8) The meter-measures are, as it were, at a deep ford. Just as at a deep ford one interlocks and wades, even so he interlocks the forms — so that the meter-measures are not scattered. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.9.1) ''adhvaryo adribhiḥ sutam'' iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
(PB 14.9.2) gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubhorūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.9.3) ''abhi somāsa āyava'' ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayoḥ saha rūpam upaity ubhau hi varṇāv etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.9.4) ''dhartā divaḥ pavate kṛtvyo rasa'' ity adhṛta iva vā eṣas tryaho yad dharteti dhṛtyā eva
(PB 14.9.5) jagatyas satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubho loke kriyante
(PB 14.9.6) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 14.9.7) vairūpaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.8) paśavo vai vairūpaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai virūpaḥ saṃvatsaro virūpam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.9.9) āśu bhārgavaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.10) ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā āśunābhyadhinvaṃs tad āśor āśutvam
(PB 14.9.11) mārgīyavaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.12) devaṃ vā etaṃ mṛgayur iti vadanty etena vai sa ubhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam āśnutobhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam aśnute mārgīyaveṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.9.13) saumitraṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.14) yad eva saumitrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 14.9.15) aiṭataṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.16) iṭan vā etena kāvyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.9.17) sākamaśvaṃ bhavati yad eva sākamaśvasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 14.9.18) tad u dhurāṃ sāmety āhuḥ prāṇā vai dhuraḥ prāṇānām avarudhyai
(PB 14.9.19) vilambasauparṇaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.20) ātmā vā eṣa sauparṇānāṃ yad aṣṭame 'hani pakṣāv etāv abhito bhavato ye saptamanavamayor vīva vā antarātmā pakṣau lambate yadantarātmā pakṣau vilambate tasmād vilambasauparṇam
(PB 14.9.22) svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai sauparṇaṃ kriyate
(PB 14.9.23) dvitīyaṃ hy etad rūpaṃ yac chandomāḥ
(PB 14.9.24) paśavo vai vāmadevyaṃ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn saṃdadhāti
(PB 14.9.25) gāyatrapārśvaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.26) ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā gāyatrapārśvena samatanvaṃs tasmād gāyatrapārśvam
(PB 14.9.27) trirātro yad vyaśīryata tam etaiḥ sāmabhir abhiṣajyan gāyatrapārśvenopāyacchan santaninā samatanvan saṃkṛtinā samaskurvan pratiṣṭhitau pūrvau trirātrāv apratiṣṭhita eṣa yad etāny eva sāmāni kriyanta etasyaiva pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 14.9.28) pauruhanmanaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.29) puruhanmā vā etena vaikhānaso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.9.30) abhyāghātyaṃ bhavaty abhyāghātyasāmāno hi chandomāḥ
(PB 14.9.31) dvaigataṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.32) dvigad vā etena bhārgavo dviḥ svargaṃ lokam agacchad āgatya punar agacchat dvayoḥ kāmayor avarudhyai dvaigataṃ kriyate
(PB 14.9.33) hārāyaṇaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.34) indras tejaskāmo haraskāmas tapo 'tapyata, sa etad dhārāyaṇam apaśyat tena tejo haro 'vārundha tejasvī harasvī bhavati hārāyaṇena tuṣtuvānaḥ
(PB 14.9.35) achidraṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.66) yad vā etasyāhnaś chidram āsīt tad devā acchidreṇāpy auhaṃs tad acchidrasyācchidratvam
(PB 14.9.37) bārhadukthaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.38) bṛhaduktho vā etena vāmneyo 'nnasya purodhām agacchad annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhām annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.9.39) udvad bhārgavaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.9.40) pravatā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāyann udvatodāyan
(PB 14.9.41) nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.9.1) 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, what has been pressed with the stones' — this is a <s>Gāyatrī</s>, for the support of the day.
(PB 14.9.2) These are truly <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses in the form of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for this day is of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> form.
(PB 14.9.3) 'The <s>Soma</s> juices of the <s>Āyu</s> people' — '<s>abhi</s>' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>; '<s>bṛhat</s>' is the <s>Bṛhat</s>. One approaches the form of both together, for both tones belong to this day.
(PB 14.9.4) 'The supporter of heaven purifies, the skillful juice' — this three-day period is as if unsupported. Since it says 'supporter,' it provides support.
(PB 14.9.5) These are truly <s>Jagatī</s> verses in the form of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Therefore they are performed in the world of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 14.9.6) The <s>Gāyatra</s> (Sāman) is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.
(PB 14.9.7) The <s>Vairūpa</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.8) Cattle are the <s>Vairūpa</s> — for the attainment of cattle. The year is of varied form; food is of varied form — for the attainment of food-eating.
(PB 14.9.9) The <s>Āśu Bhārgava</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.10) This day became hidden. The gods urged it forward with the <s>Āśu</s> (swift one). That is the swiftness of the <s>Āśu</s>.
(PB 14.9.11) The <s>Mārgīyava</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.12) They call him the divine <s>Mṛgayu</s> (hunter). By this he attains sovereignty over both kinds of cattle. He who has praised with the <s>Mārgīyava</s> attains sovereignty over both kinds of cattle.
(PB 14.9.13) The <s>Saumitra</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.14) Whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Saumitra</s> applies here.
(PB 14.9.15) The <s>Aiṭata</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.16) By this, <s>Iṭan Kāvya</s> directly perceived the heavenly world — for the recognition of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 14.9.17) The <s>Sākamaśva</s> (Sāman) is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching on the <s>Sākamaśva</s> applies here.
(PB 14.9.18) They call it the yoke-<s>Sāman</s>. The vital breaths are the yokes — for the attainment of the vital breaths.
(PB 14.9.19) The <s>Vilamba-Sauparṇa</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.20) The self of the <s>Sauparṇa</s> Sāmans is on the eighth day; the wings are on either side, on the seventh and ninth days. As the inner self hangs between the wings — because the inner self hangs down between the wings, therefore it is the <s>Vilamba-Sauparṇa</s> (hanging <s>Sauparṇa</s>).
(PB 14.9.22) The <s>Sauparṇa</s> is performed for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(PB 14.9.23) The <s>Chandomā</s> days are the second form.
(PB 14.9.24) Cattle are the <s>Vāmadevya</s>; cattle are the <s>Chandomā</s> days. He thereby joins cattle to cattle.
(PB 14.9.25) The <s>Gāyatrapārśva</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.26) This day became hidden. The gods spread it out with the <s>Gāyatrapārśva</s>. Therefore the <s>Gāyatrapārśva</s>.
(PB 14.9.27) The three-night period fell apart. They healed it with these <s>Sāmans</s>: they held it together with the <s>Gāyatrapārśva</s>, they stretched it out with the <s>Santanin</s>, they made it whole with the <s>Saṃkṛtin</s>. The first two three-night periods are established; this one is unestablished. Since these very <s>Sāmans</s> are performed, it is for the establishment of this one.
(PB 14.9.28) The <s>Pauruhanmana</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.29) By this, <s>Puruhanman Vaikhānasa</s> directly perceived the heavenly world — for the recognition of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 14.9.30) The <s>Abhyāghātya</s> (Sāman) is used — for the <s>Chandomā</s> days have <s>Abhyāghātya</s> Sāmans.
(PB 14.9.31) The <s>Dvaigata</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.32) By this, <s>Dvigat Bhārgava</s> went twice to the heavenly world — having gone, he went again. For the attainment of two desires the <s>Dvaigata</s> is performed.
(PB 14.9.33) The <s>Hārāyaṇa</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.34) <s>Indra</s>, desiring radiance and vigor, performed austerity. He perceived this <s>Hārāyaṇa</s>. By it he attained radiance and vigor. He who has praised with the <s>Hārāyaṇa</s> becomes radiant and vigorous.
(PB 14.9.35) The <s>Acchidra</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.36) Whatever gap there was in this day, the gods filled it with the <s>Acchidra</s>. That is the gapless nature of the <s>Acchidra</s>.
(PB 14.9.37) The <s>Bārhaduktha</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.38) By this, <s>Bṛhaduktha Vāmneya</s> attained the priestly office of food. Food is the priestly office of <s>Brahman</s> — for the attainment of food-eating.
(PB 14.9.39) The <s>Udvad Bhārgava</s> (Sāman) is used.
(PB 14.9.40) The gods went to the heavenly world by the downward slope and rose up by the upward slope.
(PB 14.9.41) The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants end with <s>nidhanas</s> (conclusions) — for the support of the day. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.10.1) ''ka īṃ veda sute sacā-'' iti satobṛhatyaḥ
(PB 14.10.2) apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yas saptame 'hani satobṛhatyo bhavanti nāṣṭame tasmād aṣṭame kāryā anapabhraṃśāya
(PB 14.10.3) tadāhuḥ śithilam iva vā etac chando yat satobṛhātīty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā bṛhatī yā punaḥpadā yad indra prāg apāg udag iti diśāṃ vimarśaḥ pratiṣṭityai
(PB 14.10.4) tāsu naipātithaṃ brahmasāma
(PB 14.10.5) sāmārṣeyavat svargāya yujyate svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.10.6) ''ubhayaṃ śṛṇavac ca na'' iti
(PB 14.10.7) yac ca pṛṣṭhāni yāni caitāny ahāni teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ santatyai
(PB 14.10.8) tāsu vaiyaśvam
(PB 14.10.9) vyaśvo vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyā etat pṛṣṭhānām antataḥ kriyate stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.10.1) 'Who knows him at the pressing?' — these are <s>Satobṛhatī</s> verses.
(PB 14.10.2) It is as if a fall that <s>Satobṛhatī</s> verses occur on the seventh day but not on the eighth. Therefore they should be used on the eighth day — to prevent a fall.
(PB 14.10.3) They say: 'The <s>Satobṛhatī</s> meter is as if loose.' But this <s>Bṛhatī</s> with a repeated foot is the established one. 'O <s>Indra</s>, east, west, north' — this is a touching of the directions, for establishment.
(PB 14.10.4) On those verses, the <s>Naipātitha</s> <s>Brahmasāman</s>.
(PB 14.10.5) It is yoked like a <s>Sāman</s> of the seers' lineage, for heaven. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.
(PB 14.10.6) 'May he hear both for us.'
(PB 14.10.7) These are the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> days and these other days — for the continuity of both.
(PB 14.10.8) On those verses, the <s>Vaiyaśva</s> (Sāman).
(PB 14.10.9) By this, <s>Vyaśva Āṅgirasa</s> directly perceived the heavenly world — for the recognition of the heavenly world. This is performed at the end of the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> days. The <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.11.1) ''pavasva deva āyuṣag indraṃ gacchatu te mada'' iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 14.11.3) ''prāṇā śiśur mahīnām'' iti prāṇavatyo bhavanti prāṇān eva tad yajamāne dadhāti
(PB 14.11.4) ''abhī no vājasātamam'' ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.11.5) ''pavasva soma mahān samudra'' ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtir atho etad dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
(PB 14.11.6) ''hinvanti sūram usraya'' iti gāyatryaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 14.11.7) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 14.11.8) svāśirām arko bhavati
(PB 14.11.9) annaṃ vā arko 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai prāṇā vai svāśiraḥ prāṇānām arudhyai
(PB 14.11.90) surūpaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.12) paśavo vai surūpaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 14.11.12) bhāsaṃ bhavati bhāti tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.11.13) padanidhanaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.11.14) svarbhānur vā āsura ādityaṃ tamasāvidhyat sa na vyarocata tasyātrir bhāsena tamo 'pāhan sa vyarocata yad vai tad bhā abhavat tad bhāsasya bhāsatvam
(PB 14.11.15) tama iva vā etāny ahāni yac chandomās tebhya etena sāmnā vivāsayati
(PB 14.11.16) kākṣīvataṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.17) kākṣīvān vā etenauśijaḥ prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati kākṣīvatena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.11.18) āsitaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.19) asito vā etena daivalas trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ dṛṣṭim apaśyat trayāṇāṃ kāmānām avarudhyā āsitaṃ kriyate
(PB 14.11.20) aiṣiraṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.22) traitaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 14.11.23) padanidhanaṃ rāthantaraṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 14.11.24) nāthavindu sāma vindate nāthaṃ nāthavindūny etāny ahāni yat chandomā nātham evaitair vindate
(PB 14.11.25) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 14.11.26) kautsaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.27) etena vai kutso 'ndhaso vipānam apaśyat sa ha sma vai surādṛtinopavasathaṃ dhārayaty ubhayasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai kautsaṃ kriyate
(PB 14.11.28) śuddhāśuddhīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.29) indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat tam aślīlā vāg abhyavadat so 'śuddho 'manyata sa etac chuddhāśuddhīyam apaśyat tenāśudhyac chudhyati śuddhāśuddhīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.11.30) krauñcaṃ bhavati yad eva krauñcasya brāhmaṇaṃ yat dvitīye 'hani
(PB 14.11.31) rayiṣṭhaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.32) paśavo vai rayiṣṭhaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 14.11.33) audalaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.34) udalo vā etena vaiśvāmitraḥ prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavaty audalena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.11.36) brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣachandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadāś chandomānām ayātayāmatayau
(PB 14.11.37) viśoviśīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.11.38) agnir akāmayata viśo viśo 'tithis syāṃ viśo viśa ātithyam aśnuvīyeti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad viśoviśīyam apaśyat tena viśo viśo 'tithir abhavat viśo viśa ātithyam aśnuta viśo viśo 'tithir bhavati viśo viśa ātithyam aśnute viśoviśīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.11.39) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 14.11.40) iḍāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.11.1) 'Purify yourself, O divine one, for long life; let your intoxication go to <s>Indra</s>' — this is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. The third pressing is intoxicating and full of essence; thereby one places intoxication and essence.
(PB 14.11.3) 'The breath of the great ones, the child' — they contain breath; thereby one places breath in the sacrificer.
(PB 14.11.4) 'Come to our greatest prize' — the word <s>abhi</s> is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 14.11.5) 'Purify yourself, O <s>Soma</s>, the great ocean' — this is in syllable-<s>paṅkti</s> (five-fold), the abundance of the <s>stomas</s>. This is the unworn meter at this point — the syllable-<s>paṅkti</s>. Thereby the <s>chandomā</s> days are made unworn. The theologians ask: 'When in the six-day rite the <s>stomas</s> and meters are obtained, what meters are for the <s>chandomā</s> days?' One should reply: 'These syllable-<s>paṅktis</s> are the meters.'
(PB 14.11.6) 'The rays impel the sun' — these are <s>Gāyatrīs</s> true but in the form of <s>Jagatī</s>; therefore they are performed in the realm of the <s>Jagatī</s>.
(PB 14.11.7) It is of the <s>Gāyatra</s> type — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Gāyatra</s>.
(PB 14.11.8) The <s>Svāśirā Arka</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.9) The <s>Arka</s> is food — for obtaining food. The <s>Svāśiras</s> are breaths — for obtaining breaths.
(PB 14.11.10) The <s>Surūpa</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.12) Cattle are indeed the <s>Surūpa</s> — for obtaining cattle.
(PB 14.11.12) The <s>Bhāsa</s> chant is used. He who praises with it shines.
(PB 14.11.13) The ending is the foot-ending (<s>padanidhana</s>), for this day belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 14.11.14) <s>Svarbhānu</s> the <s>Asura</s> struck the sun with darkness; the sun did not shine. <s>Atri</s> drove away its darkness with the <s>Bhāsa</s> chant; then it shone. That radiance (<s>bhā</s>) that appeared — that is the <s>Bhāsa</s>-ness of the <s>Bhāsa</s>.
(PB 14.11.15) The <s>chandomā</s> days are like darkness; with this <s>sāman</s> one illuminates them.
(PB 14.11.16) The <s>Kākṣīvata</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.17) <s>Kākṣīvān Auśija</s> with this attained abundant progeny. He who praises with the <s>Kākṣīvata</s> procreates and becomes many.
(PB 14.11.18) The <s>Āsita</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.19) <s>Asita Daivaḷa</s> with this beheld the vision of the three worlds — for obtaining the three desires, the <s>Āsita</s> is employed.
(PB 14.11.20) The <s>Aiṣira</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.22) The <s>Traita</s> chant is used, for firm establishment.
(PB 14.11.23) The ending is the foot-ending, for this day belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(PB 14.11.24) The <s>Nāthavind</s> chant finds a protector (<s>nātha</s>). These <s>chandomā</s> days are without a protector; with these one finds a protector.
(PB 14.11.25) The <s>Gaurīvita</s> chant is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Gaurīvita</s>.
(PB 14.11.26) The <s>Kautsa</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.27) With this, <s>Kutsa</s> beheld the drinking of the <s>Soma</s> juice. He would keep a skin of <s>surā</s> (liquor) at the <s>upavasatha</s> (fasting day) — for obtaining food of both kinds, the <s>Kautsa</s> is employed.
(PB 14.11.28) The <s>Śuddhāśuddhīya</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.29) <s>Indra</s> gave the <s>Yatis</s> to the wolves. An unseemly speech accused him; he considered himself impure. He beheld this <s>Śuddhāśuddhīya</s>. With it he became pure. He who praises with the <s>Śuddhāśuddhīya</s> becomes pure.
(PB 14.11.30) The <s>Krauñca</s> is used — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching of the <s>Krauñca</s> on the second day.
(PB 14.11.31) The <s>Rayiṣṭha</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.32) Cattle are indeed the <s>Rayiṣṭha</s> — for obtaining cattle.
(PB 14.11.33) The <s>Audala</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.34) <s>Udala Vaiśvāmitra</s> with this attained abundant progeny. He who praises with the <s>Audala</s> procreates and becomes many.
(PB 14.11.36) The theologians ask: 'When in the six-day rite the <s>stomas</s> and meters are obtained, what meters are for the <s>chandomā</s> days?' One should reply: 'The meters of <s>puruṣa</s> (the human).' For the human is five-fold, and the human is two-footed — these are the unworn meters of the <s>chandomā</s> days.
(PB 14.11.37) The <s>Viśoviśīya</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.11.38) <s>Agni</s> desired: 'May I be the guest of every clan, may I enjoy the hospitality of every clan.' He performed austerity. He beheld this <s>Viśoviśīya</s>. With it he became the guest of every clan and enjoyed the hospitality of every clan. He who praises with the <s>Viśoviśīya</s> becomes the guest of every clan and enjoys the hospitality of every clan.
(PB 14.11.39) They praise in <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for firm establishment and <s>brahmavarcas</s>. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.
(PB 14.11.40) The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants end with <s>iḍā</s>. Cattle are <s>iḍā</s>, cattle are the <s>chandomā</s> days. Thereby one places cattle among cattle. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 14.12.1) ''preṣṭhaṃ vo atithim'' ity ātithyasyaiva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
(PB 14.12.2) ''aindra no gadhi priya-'' itīndriyasya vīryasyāvarudhyai
(PB 14.12.3) ''purāṃ bhindur yuvā kavir amitaujā ajāyata/ indro viśvasya karmaṇo dhartā vajrī puruṣṭuta'' iti dhṛtyā eva
(PB 14.12.4) auśanaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.12.5) uśanā vai kāvyo 'kāmayata yāvān itareṣāṃ kāvyānāṃ lokas tāvantaṃ spṛṇuyām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad auśanam apaśyat tena tāvantaṃ lokam aspṛṇod yāvān itareṣāṃ kāvyānām āsīt tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāmauśanaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
(PB 14.12.6) sāṃvartaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.12.7) devānāṃ vai yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsy ajighāṃsaṃs tāny etena indraḥ saṃvartam apāvapad yat saṃvartam apāvapat tasmāt sāṃvartaṃ pāpmā vāva sa tān asacata taṃ sāṃvartenāpāghnatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate sāṃvartena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 14.12.8) mārutaṃ bhavati
(PB 14.12.9) māsā vai raśmayo maruto raśmayo maruto vai devānāṃ bhūyiṣṭhā bhūyiṣṭhā asāmeti vai sattram āsate bhūyiṣṭhā eva bhavanty ṛtumanti pūrvāṇy ahāny anṛtavaḥ chandomā yad etat sāma bhavati tenaitāny ahāny ahāny ṛtumanti bhavanti
(PB 14.12.10) catuścatvāriṃśa eva stomo bhavaty ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhaty ojo vīrye triṣṭup
(PB 15.1.1) ''akrān samudraḥ parame vidharmann'' iti navamasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
(PB 15.1.2) paramaṃ vā etad ahar vidharma vidharma vā etad anyair aharbhir ahar yan navamaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ hi variṣṭham
(PB 15.1.3) ''matsi vāyum iṣṭaye rādhase na'' iti vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇati tad eva tad avayajati
(PB 15.1.4) stotrīyas tṛco bhavati prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
(PB 15.1.5) daśarco bhavati daśākṣarā virāṭa vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 15.1.6) saprabhṛtayo bhavāntīndriyasya vīryasya rasasyānaticārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
(PB 15.1.7) aṣṭarco bhavati
(PB 15.1.8) (aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśas tat paśūn āpnoti) aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
(PB 15.1.9) ṣaḍṛcā bhavanty ṛtūnāṃ dhṛtyai
(PB 15.1.10) catvāraḥ ṣaḍṛcā bhavanti caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 15.1.11) savān uttamaḥ ṣaḍṛco bhavaty ubhayasya parokṣapratyakṣasyāvarudhyai
(PB 15.1.12) tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
(PB 15.1.13) aṣṭācatvāriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 14.12.1) 'Your most beloved guest' — thereby the form of hospitality (<s>ātithya</s>) is created.
(PB 14.12.2) 'O <s>Indra</s>, come to us, dear one' — for obtaining <s>Indra</s>'s power and vigor.
(PB 14.12.3) 'The youthful poet, destroyer of cities, of immeasurable strength was born — <s>Indra</s>, upholder of all deeds, thunderbolt-wielder, much-praised' — this is for sustenance.
(PB 14.12.4) The <s>Auśana</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.12.5) <s>Uśanas Kāvya</s> desired: 'May I reach as great a world as that of the other <s>Kāvyas</s>.' He performed austerity. He beheld this <s>Auśana</s>. With it he reached a world as great as that of the other <s>Kāvyas</s>. He desired that at that time — the <s>Auśana</s> is a desire-fulfilling <s>sāman</s>; with it one indeed obtains one's desire.
(PB 14.12.6) The <s>Sāṃvarta</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.12.7) Demons sought to destroy the sacrifice of the <s>devas</s>. <s>Indra</s> drove them away with this <s>Saṃvarta</s>. Because he drove away the <s>Saṃvarta</s>, therefore it is called <s>Sāṃvarta</s>. Sin indeed beset them; with the <s>Sāṃvarta</s> they drove it away. He who praises with the <s>Sāṃvarta</s> drives away sin.
(PB 14.12.8) The <s>Māruta</s> chant is used.
(PB 14.12.9) The months are rays; the <s>Maruts</s> are rays. The <s>Maruts</s> are the most numerous of the <s>devas</s>. Those who sit in a <s>sattra</s> saying 'May we be more numerous' indeed become more numerous. The earlier days have seasons; the <s>chandomā</s> days are seasonless. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, these days become endowed with seasons.
(PB 14.12.10) The <s>stoma</s> is the forty-four-fold, for establishment in strength and vigor. Strength and vigor belong to the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 15.1.1) 'The ocean sounded in the highest sphere' — this is the opening verse of the ninth day.
(PB 15.1.2) This day is the highest sphere (<s>parama vidharman</s>). This day is distinct from the other days — the ninth, being the greatest and the most excellent.
(PB 15.1.3) 'Rejoice <s>Vāyu</s> for the offering, for our bounty' — this belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>. Whatever in the sacrifice is ill-performed, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes. Thereby one expiates it.
(PB 15.1.4) The <s>stotrīya</s> (praise-verse) is a three-verse group (<s>tṛca</s>), for obtaining both inbreath and outbreath.
(PB 15.1.5) It is a ten-verse group. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables. The <s>Vairāja</s> is food — for obtaining food.
(PB 15.1.6) They have introductions (<s>saprabhṛti</s>), for not letting <s>Indra</s>'s power, vigor, and essence slip away. Wherever the <s>devas</s> saw power, vigor, and essence slipping away, they pierced through after it.
(PB 15.1.7) It is an eight-verse group.
(PB 15.1.8) (Animals have eight hooves; by hooves one obtains cattle.) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has eight syllables. Brilliance and <s>brahmavarcas</s> belong to the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; one obtains brilliance and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.
(PB 15.1.9) There are six-verse groups, for sustaining the seasons.
(PB 15.1.10) There are four six-verse groups — twenty-four; the half-months of the year are twenty-four. Thus one is established in the year.
(PB 15.1.11) The last is a six-verse group, for obtaining what is both hidden and manifest.
(PB 15.1.12) The final is a three-verse group. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.
(PB 15.1.13) The <s>stoma</s> is the forty-eight-fold, for firm establishment and procreation.

body.text:
(PB 15.2.1) ''aganma mahā namasā yaviṣṭham'' ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.2.2) gacchantīva vā ete ye navamam ahar gacchanti
(PB 15.2.3) ''yo dīdāya samiddhasve duroṇa'' iti dīdāyeva hy eṣa yo navabhir aharbhis tuṣṭuvānaḥ ''svāhutam'' iti svāhuto hy eṣa yo navabhir aharbhir āhuto ''viśvataḥ pratyañcam'' iti viśvato hy eṣa pratyaṅ
(PB 15.2.4) ''tvaṃ varuṇa uta mitro agna'' iti vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇati tad eva tad avayajati
(PB 15.2.5) ''mitraṃ huve pūtadakṣam'' iti rāthantaraṃ maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 15.2.6) ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya
(PB 15.2.7) ''mahāṃ indro ya ojasā-'' ity aindram aṣṭamena vai devā ahnendram avājayann avamena pāpmānam aghnann ahar evaitena mahayanti
(PB 15.2.8) ''tā huve yayor idam'' iti rāthantaram aindrāgnam
(PB 15.2.9) ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.2.1) 'We have come with great homage to the youngest' — the <s>Ājya</s> (ghee libation) belongs to <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 15.2.2) Those who reach the ninth day are as if going forth.
(PB 15.2.3) 'He who shone brightly, kindled in the house' — he indeed shines who has praised for nine days. 'Well-offered' — he is indeed well-offered who has been offered upon for nine days. 'Turned toward from all directions' — for he is indeed turned toward from all directions.
(PB 15.2.4) 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are <s>Varuṇa</s> and also <s>Mitra</s>' — this is addressed to <s>Varuṇa</s>. Whatever of the sacrifice is ill-performed, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes. He thus expiates that.
(PB 15.2.5) 'I invoke <s>Mitra</s> of purified skill' — this is the <s>Rathantara</s> belonging to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 15.2.6) The <s>chandomas</s> (metrical days) are like a deep fording place. Just as one crosses a deep ford by interweaving, so here he interweaves the forms — for the non-confusion of the <s>chandomas</s>.
(PB 15.2.7) 'Great is <s>Indra</s> who with might' — this belongs to <s>Indra</s>. With the eighth day the gods won <s>Indra</s>; with the lowest they struck evil. They magnify the day with this.
(PB 15.2.8) 'I invoke those two, to whom this belongs' — this is the <s>Rathantara</s> belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
(PB 15.2.9) The <s>chandomas</s> are like a deep fording place. Just as one crosses a deep ford by interweaving, so here he interweaves the forms — for the non-confusion of the <s>chandomas</s>. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 15.3.1) ''pavamānasya jighnato hareś candrā asṛkṣata'' iti harivatyo gāyatryo bhavanti chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 15.3.2) ''pavamānasya jighnata'' iti vai bṛhato rūpaṃ ''hareś candrā asṛkṣata-'' iti jagatyā ubhayoḥ saharūpam upaiti sāmnaś ca chandasaś ca
(PB 15.3.3) ''parīto ṣiñcatā sutam'' iti parivatyo bhavanty anto vai navamam ahas tasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
(PB 15.3.4) ''asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā harir'' iti jagatyas satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 15.3.5) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.3.6) bharadvājasyādārasṛd bhavati
(PB 15.3.7) divodāsaṃ vai bharadvājapurohitaṃ nanājanāḥ paryayanta sa upāsīdad ṛṣe gātuṃ me vindeti tasmā etena sāmnā gātum avindad gātuvid vā etatsāmānena dāre nāsṛnmeti tad adārasṛto 'dārasṛttvaṃ vindate gātuṃ na dāre dhāvaty adārasṛtā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.8) surūpaṃ bhavati yad eva surūpasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.3.9) hariśrīnidhanaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.3.10) paśavo vai hariśriyaḥ paśūnām avarudhyai śriyaṃ ca haraś copaiti tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.11) saindhukṣitaṃ bhavati yad eva saindhukṣitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.3.12) gatanidhanaṃ vābhravaṃ bhavati gatyai
(PB 15.3.13) vabhrur vā etena kaumbhyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.14) iḍānāṃ saṃkṣāro bhavati
(PB 15.3.15) paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti
(PB 15.3.16) ṛṣabhaḥ pāvamāno bhavati
(PB 15.3.17) paśavo vai chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apyarjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
(PB 15.3.18) pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.3.19) pṛṣṭhaṃ vā etad ahnāṃ yan navamaṃ pṛṣṭha eva tat pṛṣṭhena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 15.3.20) kaulmalabarhiṣaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.3.21) kulmalabarhir vā etena svargaṃ lokam apaśyat prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati kaulmalabarhiṣeṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.22) arkapuṣpaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.3.23) annaṃ vai devā arka iti vadanti rasam asya puṣpām iti sarasam evānnādyam avarundhe 'rkapuṣpeṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.24) dairghyaśravasaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.3.25) dīrghaśravā vai rājanya ṛṣir jyog aparuddho 'śanāyaṃś caran sa etad dairghaśravasam apaśyat tena sarvābhyo digbhyo 'nnādyam avārundha sarvābhyo adigbhyo 'nnādyam avārundhe dairghaśravasena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.26) vaiyaśvaṃ bhavati yad eva vaiyaśvasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.3.27) abhīśavaṃ yad ābhīśavasya
(PB 15.3.28) devasthānaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai saṃskṛti bhavati saṃṃskṛtyai
(PB 15.3.29) ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā devasthāne tiṣṭhantaḥ saṃkṛtinā samaskurvaṃs tat saṃkṛteḥ saṃkṛtitvaṃ devasthānena vai devāḥ svarge loke pratyatiṣṭhan svarge loke pratitiṣṭām ety etat
(PB 15.3.30) varuṇāya devatā rājyāya nātiṣṭhanta sa etad devasthānam apaśyat tato vai tās tasmai rājyāyātiṣṭhanta tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śreṣṭhyāya
(PB 15.3.31) kṣatrasyevāsya prakāśo bhavati pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 15.3.32) bhargo bhargeṇa tuṣṭuvāno bhavati yaśo yaśasā
(PB 15.3.33) vāsiṣṭhaṃ bhavati yad eva vāsiṣṭhasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.3.34) dīrghatamaso 'rko bhavaty annaṃ vā arko 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 15.3.35) sāmarājaṃ bhavati sāmrājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati sāmarājñā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.3.36) tad u saṃvad ity āhuḥ saṃvatā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāyann udvatodāyan
(PB 15.3.37) nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.3.1) 'Of the striking <s>Pavamāna</s>, the radiant drops of the bay horse have flowed forth' — they are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses containing 'bay horse' (<s>hari</s>), for the non-staleness of the <s>chandomas</s>.
(PB 15.3.2) 'Of the striking <s>Pavamāna</s>' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; 'the radiant drops of the bay horse have flowed' is of the <s>Jagatī</s>. He approaches the combined form of both — of the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) and the <s>chandas</s> (meter).
(PB 15.3.3) 'Pour the pressed juice around' — they are encircling verses. The ninth day is indeed the end. These are for its completion.
(PB 15.3.4) 'This <s>Soma</s>, tawny, the bull, the bay one, has been pressed' — they are <s>Jagatī</s> verses that are true, in the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Therefore they are performed in the realm of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 15.3.5) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> form — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.
(PB 15.3.6) It is the <s>Adārasṛt</s> of <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
(PB 15.3.7) <s>Divodāsa</s>, whose <s>purohita</s> (priest) was <s>Bharadvāja</s>, was besieged by enemies. He approached him: 'O sage, find a way for me.' With this <s>Sāman</s> he found a way for him. This <s>Sāman</s> is indeed a finder of ways. 'With this he did not stray to his wife' — that is the nature of the <s>Adārasṛt</s> as 'not running to wife.' He finds a way and does not run to his wife, he who praises with the <s>Adārasṛt</s>.
(PB 15.3.8) It is the <s>Surūpa</s> (beautiful-form chant) — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Surūpa</s> applies here.
(PB 15.3.9) It has the <s>Hariśrī</s> ending.
(PB 15.3.10) Cattle are indeed the <s>hariśrīs</s> (golden glories) — for the securing of cattle. He attains both glory and force, he who praises.
(PB 15.3.11) It is the <s>Saindhukṣita</s> — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Saindhukṣita</s> applies here.
(PB 15.3.12) It is the <s>Vābhrava</s> (chant) with the 'going' ending — for movement.
(PB 15.3.13) <s>Vabhru Kaumbhya</s> directly perceived the heavenly world with this. For the proclamation of the heavenly world — he does not fall from the heavenly world, he who praises.
(PB 15.3.14) It is the mixing of the <s>Iḍā</s> portions.
(PB 15.3.15) Cattle are the <s>Iḍā</s>; cattle are the <s>chandomas</s>. He places cattle among the cattle.
(PB 15.3.16) It is the bull among the <s>Pāvamāna</s> (purificatory chants).
(PB 15.3.17) Cattle are the <s>chandomas</s>. He thus brings a pair among the cattle for procreation. For without a bull, cattle do not procreate.
(PB 15.3.18) It is a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
(PB 15.3.19) The ninth day is indeed the back (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>) of the days. He praises with the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> at the back, for firm establishment.
(PB 15.3.20) It is the <s>Kaulmalabarhiṣa</s> (chant).
(PB 15.3.21) <s>Kulmalabarhis</s> perceived the heavenly world with this. He attained procreation and abundance. He procreates and becomes many, he who praises with the <s>Kaulmalabarhiṣa</s>.
(PB 15.3.22) It is the <s>Arkapuṣpa</s> (sun-flower chant).
(PB 15.3.23) The gods call food '<s>arka</s>'; 'flower' is its essence. He secures food with its essence, he who praises with the <s>Arkapuṣpa</s>.
(PB 15.3.24) It is the <s>Dairghyaśravasa</s> (chant).
(PB 15.3.25) <s>Dīrghaśravas</s>, a <s>rājanya</s> (royal) sage, long excluded and wandering hungry, perceived this <s>Dairghyaśravasa</s>. With it he secured food from all directions. He secures food from all directions, he who praises with the <s>Dairghyaśravasa</s>.
(PB 15.3.26) It is the <s>Vaiyaśva</s> (chant) — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Vaiyaśva</s> applies here.
(PB 15.3.27) The <s>Abhīśava</s> — whatever is its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> applies.
(PB 15.3.28) It is the <s>Devasthāna</s> (abode of the gods), for firm establishment. It is the <s>Saṃskṛti</s> (refinement), for refinement.
(PB 15.3.29) This day was slipping away. The gods, standing in the <s>Devasthāna</s>, refined it with the <s>Saṃkṛti</s>. That is the nature of the <s>Saṃkṛti</s> as 'refinement.' With the <s>Devasthāna</s> the gods became firmly established in the heavenly world. He becomes established in the heavenly world — this is the meaning.
(PB 15.3.30) The deities did not stand for <s>Varuṇa</s>'s sovereignty. He perceived this <s>Devasthāna</s>. Then they stood for his sovereignty. His equals stand for his pre-eminence.
(PB 15.3.31) The brightness of his <s>kṣatra</s> (sovereign power) becomes manifest. He becomes firmly established, who knows this.
(PB 15.3.32) He becomes glory with glory when praising. He becomes fame with fame.
(PB 15.3.33) It is the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> (chant) — whatever is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> applies here.
(PB 15.3.34) It is the <s>Arka</s> of <s>Dīrghatamas</s>. Food is the <s>arka</s> — for the securing of food.
(PB 15.3.35) It is the <s>Sāmarāja</s> (sovereign-rule chant). He attains supreme sovereignty and overlordship, he who praises with the <s>Sāmarāja</s>.
(PB 15.3.36) They call that the '<s>Saṃvat</s>' (year). With the <s>Saṃvat</s> the gods went upward to the heavenly world.
(PB 15.3.37) The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants end with the ending (<s>nidhana</s>) — for the support of the day. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 15.4.1) ''śrāyanta iva sūryam'' iti sūryavatyo bhavanti
(PB 15.4.2) ādityadevatyaṃ hy etad ahar anto vai sūro 'nta etan navamam ahnām anta eva tad antena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 15.4.3) ''yata indra bhayāvahe tato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi/ maghavañ chagdhi tava tan na ūtaye vidviṣo vimṛdho jahi-'' iti dviṣaś caiva mṛdhaś ca navamenāhnā vihatya daśamenāhnottiṣṭhanti
(PB 15.4.5) śrīr vai śrāyantīyaṃ śrīr navamam ahaḥ śriyam eva tac chriyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 15.4.6) samantaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.4.7) samantena paśukāmaḥ stuvīta purodhākāmaḥ samantena stuvīta
(PB 15.4.8) āgneyī pṛthivy āgneyo brāhmaṇa aindrī dyaur aindro rājanyo 'ntarikṣeṇa dyāvāpṛthivī samante antarikṣeṇaivainaṃ samantaṃ karoti vindate paśūn pra purodhām āpnoti ya evaṃ vidvān samantena stuvate stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.4.1) 'Hastening as toward the sun' — they contain the sun.
(PB 15.4.2) This day has <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) as its deity. The sun is the end; this ninth is the end of the days. He praises at the end with the end, for firm establishment.
(PB 15.4.3) 'From that which you fear, O <s>Indra</s>, make us free from fear. O <s>Maghavan</s>, grant us that for our aid. Strike down the enemies and the hostile ones' — having struck down both enemies and hostilities with the ninth day, they rise up on the tenth day.
(PB 15.4.5) Glory is the <s>Śrāyantīya</s>. Glory is the ninth day. He establishes glory in glory.
(PB 15.4.6) It is the <s>Samanta</s> (encompassing chant).
(PB 15.4.7) One desiring cattle should praise with the <s>Samanta</s>. One desiring the office of <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) should praise with the <s>Samanta</s>.
(PB 15.4.8) The earth belongs to <s>Agni</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> belongs to <s>Agni</s>. Heaven belongs to <s>Indra</s>, the <s>rājanya</s> (warrior) belongs to <s>Indra</s>. With the atmosphere he makes heaven and earth complete in the <s>Samanta</s> — with the atmosphere he makes it encompassing. He finds cattle and attains the office of <s>purohita</s>, he who, knowing this, praises with the <s>Samanta</s>. This is the <s>stoma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 15.5.1) ''tvaṃ somāsi dhārayur'' iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 15.5.2) ''tvaṃ hy aṅga daivyā'' iti tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 15.5.3) ''pavasva deva vītaya'' iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
(PB 15.5.4) ''parityaṃ haryataṃ harim'' iti parivatyo bhavanty anto vai navamam ahasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
(PB 15.5.5) ''pavasva soma mahe dakṣāya-'' ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtir atho etad dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
(PB 15.5.6) ''upoṣu jātam apturam'' iti gāyatryas satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāt jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
(PB 15.5.7) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brahmaṇam
(PB 15.5.8) āśvasūktaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.9) agniṃ vai pūrvair aharbhir ājuhoty athaitad ādityadaivatyam ahaḥ śukra āhuta ity asau vā ādityaḥ śukras tam evaitenājuhoti
(PB 15.5.10) śāmmadaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.11) śammad vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.5.13) āśiṣam evāsmā etenāśāste sāma hi satyāśīḥ
(PB 15.5.14) dāvasur vā etad āṅgirasaḥ paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjat yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
(PB 15.5.15) pratīcīneḍaṃ kāśītaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.16) parācībhir vā anyābhir iḍābhī reto dadhad athaitat pratīcīneḍaṃ kāśītaṃ prajātyai tasmāt parāñco garbhāḥ sambhavanti pratyañcaḥ prajāyante tasmād ute 'vācīnabilebhyo nāvapadyanta etena hy eva te dhṛtāḥ
(PB 15.5.17) hāviṣkṛtaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai kṛtānuvāda eva saḥ
(PB 15.5.18) sauparṇaṃ bhavati yad eva sauparṇasya brahmaṇam
(PB 15.5.19) vaiśvamanasaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.20) viśvamanasaṃ vā ṛṣim adhyāyam udvrajitaṃ rakṣo 'gṛhṇāt tam indro 'cāyad ṛṣiṃ vai rakṣo 'grahīd iti tam abhyavadad ṛṣe kas tvaiṣa iti, sthāṇur iti brūhīti rakṣo 'bravīt, sa sthāṇur ity abravīt tasmai vā etena praharety asmā iṣīkāṃ vajraṃ prayacchann abravīt tenāsya sīmānam abhinat saiṣendreṇateṣīkā pāpmā vāva sa tam agṛhṇāt taṃ vaiśvamanasenāpāhatāpapāpmānaṃ hate vaiśvamanasena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.5.21) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.5.22) nihavo bhavaty annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 15.5.23) hīti vā annaṃ pradīyata īty āgrir annam atti
(PB 15.5.24) ṛṣayo vā indraṃ pratyakṣa nāpaśyan sa vasiṣṭho 'kāmayata katham indraṃ pratyakṣaṃ paśyeyam iti sa etan nihavam apaśyat tato vai sa indraṃ pratyakṣam apaśyat, sa enam abravīd brāhmaṇaṃ te vakṣyāmi yathā tvatpurohitā bharatāḥ prajaniṣyante 'tha mānyebhya ṛṣibhyo mā pravoca iti tasmā etān stomabhāgān abravīt tato vai vasiṣṭhapurohitā bharatāḥ prājāyanta sendraṃ vā etat sāma yad etat sāma bhavati sendratvāya
(PB 15.5.25) yad vāhiṣṭhīyaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.26) brahmayaśasaṃ vā etāni sāmāny ṛcā śrotrīyāṇi brahmāyaśasī bhavati yad vāhiṣṭhīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.5.27) āsitaṃ bhavati yad evāsitasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.5.28) sādhraṃ bhavati siddhyai
(PB 15.5.29) ākūpāraṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.30) akūpāro vā etena kaśyapo jemānaṃ mahimānam agacchaj jemānaṃ mahimānaṃ gacchaty ākūpāreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
(PB 15.5.31) vidharma bhavati dharmasya vidhṛtyai
(PB 15.5.32) brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣacchandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadā chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
(PB 15.5.33) śrudhyaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.5.34) paśavo vai śrudhyaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 15.5.35) prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tān etena sāmnā śrūdhiyā ehiyety anvahvayat ta enam upāvartanta yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnām upāvṛtyai
(PB 15.5.36) upainaṃ paśava āvartante ya evaṃ veda
(PB 15.5.37) gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyantīḍāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.5.1) 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, are the sustainer' — this is in <s>Gāyatrī</s>, for sustaining the day. 'You' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s> [chant], for this day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 15.5.2) 'You indeed, O divine one' — 'you' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 15.5.3) 'Purify yourself, O god, for the feast' — this is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
(PB 15.5.4) 'Going around, O bay one'

body.text:
(PB 15.6.1) āgreyīṣu pūrveṣām ahnām ukthāni praṇayanty athaitasyāhna āgneyy aindrayāṃ praṇayanty ubhayor eva rūpayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 15.6.2) aidhmavāhaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.6.3) āgneyy aindrīṣu stuvanti brahma caiva tat kṣatraṃ ca sayujīkaroti brahmaiva kṣatrasya purastān nidadhāti brāhmaṇe kṣatraṃ ca viśaṃ cānuge karoti
(PB 15.6.4) traikakubhaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.6.5) ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhaty ojo vīryaṃ traikakubham
(PB 15.6.6) udvaṃśīyaṃ bhavati yad evodvaṃśīyasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.6.7) aṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
(PB 15.7.1) gāyatraṃ vai saptamam ahas traiṣṭubham aṣṭamaṃ jāgataṃ navamam athaitad ānuṣṭubham ahar yad daśamam
(PB 15.7.2) tad āhur yad ānuṣṭubhaṃ stomyāṃ pratyakṣam upeyuḥ parāṃ parāvataṃ yajamāno gacchen na pratitiṣṭhed iti yā vai caturviṃśatir gāyatryas tā aṣṭādaśānuṣṭubho 'nuṣṭubham eva tat stomyāṃ parokṣam upayanti pratiṣṭhāyai pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 15.7.3) prajāpatiṃ vā etenāhnā pariveviṣati tatra vyavavadyaṃ yad vai śreṣṭhe pariviṣyamāṇo vadaty annādyasya so 'vagrahas tasmān na vyavavadyam annādyasyānavagrāhāya
(PB 15.7.4) tad u vyavavadyaṃ yathā śreṣṭhāya baliṃ hriyamāṇaṃ panthānaṃ paryanuvedayati gatyai tathā tat
(PB 15.7.5) yāvaty anuṣṭup tāvatīṃ vācaṃ sampādya vibrūyus tad v anatiriktaṃ svasyo caiva yajñasyāriṣṭyai
(PB 15.7.6) abhi vā ete devān ārohantīty āhur ye daśabhir aharbhiḥ stuvata iti pañcānām ahnām anurūpaiḥ pratyavayanti yathābhyāruhya pratyavarohet tathā tan navarco bhavati yā evāmūḥ prayacchan yā avadadhāti tā etā udasyati
(PB 15.7.7) vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇāti tad eva tad avayajaty ādityaiṣā bhavatīyaṃ vā aditir asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 15.7.8) caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmarcasāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.6.1) On previous days they lead forth the <s>ukthas</s> (recitation portions) in the <s>Āgneya</s> (Agni-related) [verses], but on this day they lead them forth in the <s>Āgneya-Aindra</s> (Agni-and-Indra-related) [verses]. Thereby one becomes established in both forms.
(PB 15.6.2) It has the <s>Aidhmavāha</s> (fuel-carrying) [chant].
(PB 15.6.3) They chant in <s>Āgneya</s> verses that are <s>Aindrī</s> (Indra-related). Thereby one unites both <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly power) and <s>Kṣatra</s> (the warrior power). One places <s>Brahman</s> before <s>Kṣatra</s>. The <s>Kṣatra</s> in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and

body.text:
(PB 15.8.1) ''suṣamiddho na āvaha-'' ity āpriya ājyāni bhavanti
(PB 15.8.2) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa dugdho riricānāmanyata sa etāny āpriya ājyāny apaśyat tair ātmānam āprīṇāt dugdha iva vā eṣa riricāno yo daśabhir aharbhis tuṣṭuvāno yad etāny āpriya ājyāni bhavanty ātmānam evaitair āprīṇāti
(PB 15.8.3) ''yad adya sūra udita'' iti sūravan maitrāvaruṇam
(PB 15.8.4) anto vai sūro 'nta etad daśamam ahnām anta eva tadantena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
(PB 15.8.5) ''ut tvā madantu somā'' ity udvad aindram utthānasya rūpam
(PB 15.8.6) ''indrāgnī āgataṃ sutam'' iti yenaiva rūpeṇa prayanti tad abhyudyanti stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.8.1) 'Well-kindled, bring [the gods] to us' — these are the <s>Āprī</s> (propitiatory) <s>ājya</s> chants.
(PB 15.8.2) <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. Having been milked dry, he considered himself diminished. He perceived these <s>Āprī ājya</s> chants. With them he gratified himself. He who, having chanted for ten days, is as if milked dry and diminished — when these <s>Āprī ājya</s> chants are employed, he gratifies himself with them.

body.text:
(PB 15.9.1) ''uccā te jātam andhasa'' ity udvatyo gāyatryo bhavanty utthānasya rūpam
(PB 15.9.2) ''punānas soma dhāraya-'' iti panthānam eva tat paryavayanti
(PB 15.9.3) ''ā jāgṛvir vipra ṛtaṃ matīnām'' iti yad āpte pravatīḥ kuryur atipadyer anyad āvatyo bhavanty anatipādāya
(PB 15.9.4) gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
(PB 15.9.5) āmahīyavaṃ bhavati kḷptiś cānnādyaṃ ca kḷptiṃ caivaitenānnādyaṃ cābhyuttiṣṭhanti
(PB 15.9.6) ājigaṃ bhavaty ājijityāyai
(PB 15.9.7) ājir vā eṣa pratato yat dvādaśāhas tasyaitad ujjityai
(PB 15.9.8) ābhīkaṃ bhavaty abhikrāntyai
(PB 15.9.9) āṅgirasas tapas tepānāḥ śucam aśocaṃs ta etat sāmāpaśyaṃs tān abhīke 'bhyavarṣat tena śucam aśamayanta yad abhīke 'bhyavarṣat tasmād ābhīkaṃ yām eva pūrvair aharbhiḥ śucaṃ śocanti tām etenānna śamayitvottiṣṭhanti
(PB 15.9.10) utsedho bhavati
(PB 15.9.11) utsedhena vai devāḥ paśūn udasedhan niṣedhena paryagṛhṇan
(PB 15.9.12) antarotsedhaniṣedhau yajñāyajñīyam
(PB 15.9.13) paśavo 'nnādyaṃ yajñāyajñīyaṃ paśūn eva tad annādyam utsedhaniṣedhābhyāṃ parigṛhṇāti
(PB 15.9.14) mādhyandine vai pavamāne devā yajñāyajñīyena yajñaṃ saṃsthāpya svargaṃ lokam ārohaṃs tad ya evaṃ veda mādhyandina evaitat pavamāne yajñāyajñīyena yajñaṃ saṃsthāpya svargaṃ lokam ārohati
(PB 15.9.15) atho parokṣam anuṣṭubhaṃ sampadyate 'har eṣā vai pratyakṣam anuṣṭup yad yajñāyajñīyaṃ tad yat tṛtīyasavane kuryuḥ pratyakṣam anuṣṭubham ṛccheyus tasmān mādhyandine kurvanti tena parokṣam anuṣṭubham upayanti
(PB 15.9.16) gaurīvitaṃ bhavati
(PB 15.9.17) etad vai yajñasya śvastanaṃ yad gaurīvitam etad āyatano yajamāno yan madhyandino yad gaurīvitaṃ madhyandine bhavati śvastanam eva tad yajamāna ātman dhatte stomaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 15.9.1) 'Your high-born [<s>Soma</s>] from the plant' — these are ascending (<s>udvatī</s>) <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, having the form of arising.
(PB 15.9.2) 'Being purified, O <s>Soma</s>, sustain' — thereby they circumambulate the path.
(PB 15.9.3) 'The wakeful, the wise one, the truth of hymns' — if upon completion one were to make outgoing (<s>pravatī</s>) verses, one would pass beyond. Therefore there are <s>āvatī</s> (approaching) verses, to prevent passing beyond.
(PB 15.9.4) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> [pattern].

(PB 15.11.2) It is in the <s>Gāyatra</s> [pattern]. Whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (ritual explanation) of the <s>Gāyatra</s> [applies here].

(PB 15.12.1) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> in <s>Virāj</s> verses becomes the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>-<s>Sāman</s> — for pacification and arrangement.
(PB 15.12.2) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is the essence of <s>Sāmans</s>; the <s>Virāj</s> is the essence of meters; the thirty-three is the essence of <s>stomas</s>. Joining the ends of these essences, they rise. One obtains even the existence of a son.
(PB 15.12.3) The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'From which <s>sattra</s> did you arise? From the standing one?' If they should say 'from which,' one should tell them: 'You will be without foundation, without offspring.' If they say 'from the standing one,' one should tell them: 'Your prosperity will be lasting; you will not become wealthier.' They should say: 'From the full we have risen to the full.'
(PB 15.12.4) Those who rise having praised with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> — they rise from fullness to fullness.
(PB 15.12.5) The <s>Vāmadevya</s> is the atmosphere. By the atmosphere all this is full.
(PB 15.12.6) This thirty-three is the prosperous <s>stoma</s>. In the thirty-three-syllable verses they become established in prosperity.
(PB 15.12.7) These are the form of all meters: since they have three feet, they are <s>Gāyatrīs</s>; since the feet have eleven syllables, they are <s>Triṣṭubhs</s>; since one foot has twelve syllables, they are <s>Jagatīs</s>; since they have thirty-three syllables, they are <s>Virājs</s>; and thereby <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s> too — for they do not deviate by even a single syllable.
(PB 15.12.8) The <s>stoma</s> is the thirty-three — for establishment. It is established among the gods.
(PB 16.1.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> alone was this universe. There was no day, there was no night. He crept about in this blind darkness. He desired. He discovered this. Then light dawned for him. This dawning is brought to him. That which became light — that is the light-nature of light.
(PB 16.1.2) This is the first of all sacrifices. He who, not having sacrificed with this, then sacrifices with another, falls into the pit or dies.
(PB 16.1.3) Just as from the fire once born, other fires are taken, so from this sacrifice other sacrifices are taken.
(PB 16.1.4) The threefold one kindles any other sacrificial rite that one attains. The fifteenfold kindles it; the seventeenfold kindles it; the twenty-onefold kindles it.
(PB 16.1.5) This is what they say: 'The sacrifice is one.' For all become <s>Jyotiṣṭomas</s> (light-praisings).
(PB 16.1.6) This is an uninterrupted continuous sacrifice, for two <s>stomas</s> carry each pressing: the threefold and fifteenfold for the morning pressing, the fifteenfold and seventeenfold for the midday pressing, the seventeenfold and twenty-onefold for the third pressing.
(PB 16.1.7) Even if the gifts are limited, this one should be performed. This world is light; this is the controller of the unlimited. This one is able to control it.
(PB 16.1.8) It has one hundred and ninety <s>Stotrīya</s> verses. Of those, one hundred and eighty are <s>Virāj</s> verses of thirty-six syllables each. There are six seasons — he becomes established in the seasons through the <s>Virāj</s>.
(PB 16.1.9) The remaining ten constitute the personal <s>Virāj</s>. In this <s>Virāj</s> man is established.
(PB 16.1.10) A cow, a horse, a mule, a donkey, goats, sheep, rice, barley, sesame, and beans — he becomes established in this very <s>Virāj</s>.
(PB 16.1.11) Its gifts are one hundred and twelve.
(PB 16.1.12) He who presses <s>Soma</s> is the slayer of heroes among the gods. The hundred compensate the enmity with the gods. The ten — there are ten vital breaths — with these he nourishes the vital breaths. The eleventh is for the self. The twelfth is the gift itself.
(PB 16.1.13) The gifts are the grease of the sacrifice. A chariot without grease does not carry, but with a greased one, whatever desire one desires, one attains it. So with this gift-endowed sacrifice, whatever desire one desires, one attains it.
(PB 16.1.14) The gifts are the adornments of the sacrifice. When one sacrifices with gifts, one places beauty in the sacrifice.
(PB 16.2.1) Now this is the <s>Gau</s> (cow-sacrifice).
(PB 16.2.2) With the cow the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> from these worlds. He who knows thus drives his hostile rival from these worlds.
(PB 16.2.3) Because the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> from these worlds with the cow — that is the cow-nature of the cow.
(PB 16.2.4) He who knows thus drives away evil and the hostile rival.
(PB 16.2.5) Its <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is fifteenfold. The fifteen is the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt). He places the <s>vajra</s> in front. By it he conquers.
(PB 16.2.6) This is the animal-<s>stoma</s>. An animal is shaped thus: the head is thicker, the neck is thinner, the sides are broader, the thighs are broadest.
(PB 16.2.7) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is fifteenfold; the <s>Ājya</s> chants are threefold; the midday pressing is seventeenfold; the third pressing is twenty-onefold. He brings it to fullness by its own form.
(PB 16.2.8) One of the chanted praises exceeds the <s>Virāj</s>. Therefore there is an excess at the rear of the animal.

(PB 16.3.2) āyuṣā vai devā asurān āyuvatāyute bhrātṛvyaṃ ya evaṃ veda
(PB 16.3.3) svargakāmo yajeta
(PB 16.3.4) ūrdhvāḥ stomā yanty anapabhraṃśāya

(PB 16.3.7) svargyā vā ete stomā yat jyotir bhavati jyotir evāsmai sa purastād dharaty athaiṣa gaur ekayā virājam atirikta ārambhaṇam eva tad athaiṣa āyur ekasyā virāja ūna āsāda eva so 'tho ūnātiriktau stomau mithunau prajātyai

body.translated_text:
(PB 16.3.1) Now this is the <s>Āyus</s> (life-span sacrifice).
(PB 16.3.2) With life-span the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s>. He who knows thus drives his hostile rival with life-span.
(PB 16.3.3) One desiring heaven should sacrifice with this.
(PB 16.3.4) The <s>stomas</s> go upward — to prevent a fall.
(PB 16.3.5) One should make a sick person sacrifice with this. An <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice) should be performed.
(PB 16.3.6) It attains the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>prāṇa</s> (breath); this one is life-span. He places both life-span and breath together in him.
(PB 16.3.7) These <s>stomas</s> lead to heaven. Since there is <s>Jyotis</s> (light), it holds the light before him. Now this cow-sacrifice exceeds by one <s>Virāj</s> — that is a handle. And this life-span sacrifice falls short of one <s>Virāj</s> — that is a seat. The two <s>stomas</s>, the exceeding and the deficient, are a pair — for procreation.
(PB 16.3.8) These are the <s>Trikadruka</s> <s>stomas</s>. With these <s>Indra</s> satisfied all satisfaction.
(PB 16.3.9) He who knows thus is satisfied with offspring and cattle.

(PB 16.4.2) tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śraiṣṭhyāya ya evaṃ veda
(PB 16.4.3) so 'kāmayatendro me prajāyāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ syād iti tām asmai srajaṃ pratyamuñcat tato vā indrāya prajāḥ śraiṣṭhyāyātiṣṭhanta tac chilpaṃ paśyantyo yat pitary apaśyan
(PB 16.4.4) tasmād yaḥ putrāṇāṃ dāyaṃ dhanatamam ivopaiti taṃ manyante 'yam evedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti
(PB 16.4.5) tato vā idam indro viśvam ajayad yad viśvam ajayat tasmād viśvajit
(PB 16.4.6) so 'kāmayata yan me 'nabhijitaṃ tad abhijayeyam iti sa etam abhijitam apaśyat tenānabhijitam abhyajayat
(PB 16.4.7) yad abhijid bhavaty anābhijitasyābhijityai
(PB 16.4.8) tau vā etāv indrastomau vīryavantau śilpaṃ vā etau nāma stomāv āstām
(PB 16.4.9) paśyate gṛhe śilpaṃ ya evaṃ veda
(PB 16.4.10) na vai yamau nāma stomau sto yo yamābhyāṃ yajetaitābhyāṃ yajeta samṛdhyai
(PB 16.4.11) punarabhyāvartaṃ stomā bhavanti punarabhyāvartaṃ hy etābhyām indro 'jitam ajayat
(PB 16.4.12) trīṃs trivṛdabhijitaḥ praṇayati trīn pañcadaśaḥ trīn saptadaśaḥ trīn ekaviṃśas te dvādaśa saṃpadyante dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatim evāpnoti
(PB 16.4.13) caturas trivṛdviśvajitaḥ praṇayati caturaḥ pañcadaśaś caturaḥ saptadaśas te dvādaśa saṃpadyante dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatim evāpnoti
body.translated_text:
(PB 16.4.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> created beings. They would not stand for his supremacy. He extracted the essence of those directions and beings, made a garland, and put it on. Then the beings stood for his supremacy.
(PB 16.4.2) His equals stand for his supremacy, he who knows this.
(PB 16.4.3) He desired: 'Let <s>Indra</s> be the foremost among my offspring.' He put that garland on him. Then the beings stood for <s>Indra</s>'s supremacy, seeing in him the skill that they had seen in the father.
(PB 16.4.4) Therefore, whichever of the sons approaches the inheritance as if the wealthiest, they think: 'He will be the one.'
(PB 16.4.5) Then <s>Indra</s> conquered all this. Because he conquered all, therefore it is the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering rite).
(PB 16.4.6) He desired: 'What remains unconquered by me, let me conquer that.' He perceived this <s>Abhijit</s> (conquering rite). With it he conquered what was unconquered.
(PB 16.4.7) When the <s>Abhijit</s> takes place, it is for the conquering of the unconquered.
(PB 16.4.8) These two are indeed <s>stomas</s> of <s>Indra</s>, full of vigor. They were called 'skill' (<s>śilpa</s>).
(PB 16.4.9) He who knows this perceives skill in his household.
(PB 16.4.10) They are not called 'twins' (<s>yama</s>). He who would sacrifice with the twin rites should sacrifice with these — for prosperity.
(PB 16.4.11) The <s>stomas</s> involve turning back. For with these <s>Indra</s> turned back and conquered what was unconquered.
(PB 16.4.12) He extends three threefold for the <s>Abhijit</s>, three fifteenfold, three seventeenfold, three twenty-one-fold — these amount to twelve. Twelve are the months of the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. He thus reaches <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 16.4.13) He extends four threefold for the <s>Viśvajit</s>, four fifteenfold, four seventeenfold — these amount to twelve. Twelve are the months of the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. He thus reaches <s>Prajāpati</s>.

body.text:
(PB 16.5.1) ''upa tvā jāmayo gira'' ity upavatī pratipad bhavati stomasya rūpam
(PB 16.5.2) prāṇair vā eṣa vyṛdhyata ity āhur yaḥ sarvaṃ dadāti sarvān stomān sarvāṇi pṛṣṭhāny upaitīti yad vāyavyā bhavati prāṇānāṃ samṛdhyai
(PB 16.5.3) sarasvataś ca sarasvatyāś cottare bhavataḥ
(PB 16.5.4) mithunaṃ vā etad yat sarasvāṃś ca sarasvatī ca mithunam evāsya yajñamukhe dadhāti prajananāya
(PB 16.5.5) sāvitrī caturthī bhavati
(PB 16.5.6) duṣkaraṃ vā eṣa karoti yaḥ sarvaṃ dadāti yat sāvitrī bhavati savitṛprasṛtaṃ me karmāsad iti savitṛprasūtam evāsya karma bhavati
(PB 16.5.7) brāhmaṇaspatyā pañcamī bhavati
(PB 16.5.8) brahma vai brahmaṇaspatir brahmaivāsya yajñamukhe dadhāti
(PB 16.5.9) āgnipāvamānī ṣaṣṭhī bhavati
(PB 16.5.10) agnir evainaṃ niṣṭapati pavamānaḥ punāti pūtam evainaṃ yajñiyaṃ pṛṣṭhāny upanayati
(PB 16.5.11) yanti vā ete patha ity āhur ye saṃbhāryāḥ kurvate
