(PB 18.10.1) yo vai savād eti nainaṃ sava upanamaty atha yaḥ sāmabhya eti pāpīyān suṣuvāṇo bhavati
(PB 18.10.2) saṃbhāryā bhavanti pṛṣṭhāny eva tābhir yunakti
(PB 18.10.3) etāni vāva sāmāni yat pṛṣṭhāni
(PB 18.10.4) yat saṃbhāryā bhavanti tad eva sāmabhyo naiti
(PB 18.10.5) yāni devarājñāṃ sāmāni tair amuṣmin loka ṛdhnoti yāni manuṣyarājñāṃ tair asminn ubhayor anayor lokayor ṛdhnoti devaloke ca manuṣyaloke ca
(PB 18.10.6) sāmatriṣṭubhy adhy abhiṣicyate vīryaṃ vai sāma triṣṭup vīrya evādhy abhiṣicyate
(PB 18.10.7) ekādaśa rājasāmāni bhavanty ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub ojo vīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasy eva vīrye 'dhy abhiṣicyate
(PB 18.10.8) yat trivṛtam abhiṣecanīye kuryur brahma kṣatrāyāpidadhyur yat trivṛtam uddharanti brahma tat kṣatrād uddharanti tasmād bharatāṃ pratidaṇḍā brahmaṇā na hi te trivṛtam abhiṣecanīye kurvanti
(PB 18.10.9) ekaviṃśo 'bhiṣecanīyasyottamaḥ saptadaśo daśapeya ekaviṃśaḥ keśavapanīyasya prathamaḥ kṣatraṃ vā ekaviṃśo viṭ saptadaśaḥ kṣatreṇaivāsmai viśam ubhayataḥ parigṛhṇāty anapakrāmukāsmād viṭ bhavati
(PB 18.10.10) yad vai rājasūyenābhiṣicyate tat svargaṃ lokam ārohati sa yad imaṃ lokaṃ nopāvarohed ati janaṃ vā gacched ud vā mādyed yad eṣo 'rvācīnastomaḥ keśavapanīyo bhavaty asya lokasyānuddhānāya yathā śākhāyāḥ śākhām ālambham upāvarohed evam etenemaṃ lokam upāvarohati pratiṣṭhāyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 18.10.1) He who departs from the pressing — the pressing does not bend toward him. And he who departs from the <s>sāmans</s> (chants) — the one who has performed the pressing becomes worse.
(PB 18.10.2) They become to be collected. One yokes the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) [<s>sāmans</s>] with them.
(PB 18.10.3) The <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> are indeed the [true] <s>sāmans</s>.
(PB 18.10.4) Because they become to be collected, thereby one does not depart from the <s>sāmans</s>.
(PB 18.10.5) The <s>sāmans</s> that belong to the kings of the gods —

body.text:
(PB 18.11.1) indro vṛtram ahan sa viṣyaṅvīryeṇa vyabhraṃśata sa etac chrāyantīyam apaśyat tenātmānaṃ samaśrīṇād indriyeṇa vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yo rājasūyenābhiṣicyate vṛtraṃ hi hanti yac chrāyantīyaṃ brahmasāma bhavati punar evātmānaṃ saṃśrīṇāti
(PB 18.11.2) yajñāyajñīyam anuṣṭubhi bhavati vācā vā eṣa vyṛdhyate yo rājasūyenābhiṣicyate vṛtraṃ hi hanti vāg anuṣṭub vāco raso yajñāyajñīyaṃ vācy evāsya rasaṃ dadhāti
(PB 18.11.3) vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma bhavatīndriyeṇa vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yo rājasūyenābhiṣicyate vṛtraṃ hi hanti yad vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma bhavatīndriyasya vīryasya parigṛhītyai
(PB 18.11.4) aśrayan vāva śrāyantīyenāvārayanta vāravantīyenendriyasya vā eṣā vīryasya parigṛhītiḥ
(PB 18.11.5) apratiṣṭhito vā eṣa yo rājasūyenābhiṣicyate yadā vā etena dvirātreṇa yajate 'thaiva pratiṣṭhā
(PB 18.11.6) yāvanti saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇi tāvatya etāḥ stotrīyāḥ saṃvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 18.11.7) agniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar atirātra uttaraṃ nānaivāhorātrayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 18.11.8) amāvāsyāyāṃ pūrvam ahar udriṣṭa [em. Caland: uddṛṣṭa] uttaraṃ nānaivārdhamāsayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati paurṇamāsyāṃ pūrvam ahar vyaṣṭakāyām uttaraṃ nānaiva māsoḥ pratitiṣṭhati tad āhur ya eva samānapakṣe puṇyāhanī syātāṃ tayor eva kāryaṃ samṛdhyai
(PB 18.11.9) apaśavyo dvirātra ity āhur dve hy ete chandasī gāyatraṃ ca traiṣṭubhaṃ ca jagatīm antaryantīti na tena jagatī kṛtā yat tṛtīyasavane kriyate
(PB 18.11.10) yadā vā eṣāhīnasyāhar bhajate sāhvasya vā savanam athaiva jagatī kṛtā traiśokam uttarasyāhno brahmasāma bhavati vaikhānasam acchāvākasāma yac chukriye savane kriyete tenaiva jagatī kṛtā tena paśavyaḥ
(PB 18.11.11) vyuṣṭir vā eṣa dvirātro vy evāsmai vāsayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 18.11.1) <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. He became shattered, his vigor scattered. He perceived this <s>Śrāyantīya</s> (chant). With it he restored himself. He who is consecrated with the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration) becomes weakened in power and vigor, for he slays <s>Vṛtra</s>. When the <s>Śrāyantīya</s> is the <s>Brahma-Sāman</s>, he restores himself again.
(PB 18.11.2) The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> (chant) is in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. He who is consecrated with the <s>Rājasūya</s> becomes weakened in speech, for he slays <s>Vṛtra</s>. Speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. The <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is the essence of speech. He places the essence in his speech.
(PB 18.11.3) The <s>Vāravantīya</s> is the <s>Agniṣṭoma-Sāman</s>. He who is consecrated with the <s>Rājasūya</s> becomes weakened in power and vigor, for he slays <s>Vṛtra</s>. When the <s>Vāravantīya</s> is the <s>Agniṣṭoma-Sāman</s>, it is for the encompassing of power and vigor.
(PB 18.11.4) They took shelter with the <s>Śrāyantīya</s> and were warded with the <s>Vāravantīya</s>. This is the encompassing of power and vigor.
(PB 18.11.5) He who is consecrated with the <s>Rājasūya</s> is without firm foundation. When he sacrifices with this two-night rite, then he has firm foundation.
(PB 18.11.6) As many as are the day-and-nights of the year, so many are these <s>stotrīya</s> (praise verses). He becomes established in the year.
(PB 18.11.7) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day, the <s>Atirātra</s> the second. He becomes established differently in each of the day-and-night.
(PB 18.11.8) The first day at the new moon, the second at the intended day — he becomes established differently in the two half-months. The first day at the full moon, the second at the eighth day — he becomes established differently in the two months. On this they say: whichever two auspicious days fall in the same fortnight, on those it should be performed, for prosperity.
(PB 18.11.9) 'The two-night rite is without cattle,' they say, 'for these two meters, the <s>Gāyatra</s> and the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s>, exclude the <s>Jagatī</s>.' But the <s>Jagatī</s> is not thereby eliminated, since it is performed at the third pressing.
(PB 18.11.10) When this obtains a day of a multi-day rite or a pressing of a single-day rite, then the <s>Jagatī</s> is established. The <s>Traiśoka</s> is the <s>Brahma-Sāman</s> of the second day. The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is the <s>Acchāvāka-Sāman</s>. Since it is performed at the auspicious pressing, by that the <s>Jagatī</s> is established. Therefore it contains cattle.
(PB 18.11.11) This two-night rite is indeed a dawning. He causes it to dawn for him.

body.text:
(PB 19.1.1) athaiṣa rāṭ
(PB 19.1.2) yo rājya āśaṃsamāno rājyaṃ na prāpnuyāt sa etena yajeta rājaivainaṃ rājānaṃ karoti taṃ tu vairājeti vadeyur yaṃ rājā rājānaṃ kuryād rājaivainaṃ rājānaṃ karoti
(PB 19.1.3) chando 'nye yajñāḥ saṃpadyante stomam eṣa vīryaṃ vai stomo vīrya evādhy abhiṣicyate
(PB 19.1.4) aṣṭāv ekaviṃśāḥ saṃstuto bhavaty aṣṭau vai vīrā rāṣṭraṃ samudyacchanti rājabhrātā ca rājaputraś ca purohitaś ca mahiṣī ca sūtaś ca grāmaṇī ca kṣattā ca saṃgrahītā caite vai vīrā rāṣṭraṃ samudyacchanty eteṣv evādhy abhiṣicyate
(PB 19.1.5) kṣatraṃ vā ekaviṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhā kṣatrasyevāsya prakāśo bhavati pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.1.1) Now this is the <s>Rāṭ</s> (sovereign).
(PB 19.1.2) He who aspires to kingship but does not attain it should sacrifice with this. It makes him a king among kings. But they would call him <s>Vairāja</s> (endowed with sovereignty) — he whom a king makes a king. The king himself makes him a king.
(PB 19.1.3) Other sacrifices are measured by meter; this one by <s>stoma</s> (hymn-form). The <s>stoma</s> is vigor. He is consecrated upon vigor itself.
(PB 19.1.4) The concluded praise has eight twenty-one-fold parts. Eight heroes uphold the kingdom: the king's brother, the king's son, the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest), the chief queen, the charioteer, the village headman, the chamberlain, and the chariot-driver. These heroes uphold the kingdom. He is consecrated upon these.
(PB 19.1.5) The twenty-one-fold is <s>kṣatra</s> (sovereign power), it is firm foundation. The brightness of his <s>kṣatra</s> becomes manifest. He becomes firmly established, who knows this.

body.text:
(PB 19.2.1) athaiṣa virāḍ annādyakāmo yajeta
(PB 19.2.2) parokṣam anye yajñā virājaṃ saṃpadyante pratyakṣam eṣa virājaṃ saṃpannaḥ
(PB 19.2.3) pratyakṣam etenānnādyam avarundhe 'nnādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.2.4) sarvo daśadaśī bhavati daśākṣarā virāḍ vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
(PB 19.2.5) tā u pañca pañca bhavanti pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktā paśavo yajña eva paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 19.2.6) etenaiva pratiṣṭhākāmo yajeta daśabhir vā idaṃ puruṣaḥ pratiṣṭhito 'syām eva pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.2.1) Now this is the <s>Virāj</s>. One desiring food should sacrifice with it.
(PB 19.2.2) Other sacrifices achieve the <s>Virāj</s> indirectly. This one achieves the <s>Virāj</s> directly.
(PB 19.2.3) He directly secures food with this. He becomes an eater of food who knows this.
(PB 19.2.4) It is entirely ten-by-ten. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables. Food belongs to the <s>Virāj</s> — for the securing of food.
(PB 19.2.5) They are also five-by-five. The sacrifice is fivefold. Cattle are fivefold. He becomes established in the sacrifice and in cattle.
(PB 19.2.6) One desiring firm establishment should sacrifice with this. A person is established by ten. He becomes established in this world.

body.text:
(PB 19.3.1) athaiṣa aupaśadaḥ
(PB 19.3.2) gandharvāpsarasāṃ stomaḥ prajākāmo yajeta gandharvāpsaraso vai manuṣyasya prajāyā vāprajastāyā veśate teṣām atra somapīthas tān svena bhāgadheyena prīṇāti te 'smai tṛptāḥ prītāḥ prajāṃ prayacchanti
(PB 19.3.3) ekaikā stotrīyopajāyate prajām evāsmā upajanayati
(PB 19.3.4) kakubhaṃ prācīm udūhati puruṣo vai kakub garbha eva sa madhyato dhīyate
(PB 19.3.5) atha yad eṣā dvipadā kakubho loke kriyate garbha eva tad dhi taṃ prajanayati
(PB 19.3.6) cyāvanaṃ bhavati prajātir vai cyāvanam
(PB 19.3.7) prajāyate bahur bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.3.8) vasiṣṭhasya janitre bhavato vasiṣṭho vā ete putrahataḥ sāmanī apaśyat sa prajayā paśubhiḥ prājāyata yad ete sāmanī bhavataḥ prajātyai
(PB 19.3.9) dve saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyete dve striyā ūne prajananāya prajananam eva tat kriyate prajātyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.3.1) Now this is the <s>Aupaśada</s> (approach-offering).
(PB 19.3.2) It is the <s>stoma</s> of the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>. One desiring offspring should sacrifice with it. The <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> enter into a person's fertility or infertility. Here is their <s>Soma</s>-drinking. He gratifies them with their own share. Gratified and pleased, they grant him offspring.
(PB 19.3.3) One <s>stotrīya</s> (praise verse) is added for each. He generates offspring for him.
(PB 19.3.4) He draws forth the <s>Kakubh</s> (meter) eastward. The person is the <s>Kakubh</s>. The embryo is placed in the middle.
(PB 19.3.5) And when this two-footed one is performed in the realm of the <s>Kakubh</s>, it generates the embryo.
(PB 19.3.6) It is the <s>Cyāvana</s> (stirring chant). Procreation is the <s>Cyāvana</s>.
(PB 19.3.7) He procreates and becomes many, who knows this.
(PB 19.3.8) It is of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s birth-chants. <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, whose sons had been slain, perceived these two <s>Sāmans</s>. He procreated with offspring and cattle. When these two <s>Sāmans</s> are performed, it is for procreation.
(PB 19.3.9) Two of the concluded praise exceed the <s>Virāj</s>. Two are the female deficiency — for procreation. Procreation is thus effected, for begetting.

body.text:
(PB 19.4.1) athaiṣa punaḥstomaḥ
(PB 19.4.2) yo bahu pratigṛhya garagīr iva manyeta sa etena yajeta
(PB 19.4.3) yaikādaśī yad eva pūrvavayase bahu pratigṛhṇāti yad garaṃ girati yad anannam atti prātaḥsavanāya tan niharati
(PB 19.4.4) atha yā dvādaśī yad evottaravayase bahu pratigṛhṇati yad garaṃ girati yad anannam atti tṛtīyasavanāya tan niharati
(PB 19.4.5) vairājo vai puruṣaḥ sa madhyato 'śuddho madhyata evainaṃ pāpmano muñcati
(PB 19.4.6) śuddhāśuddhīye bhavataḥ
(PB 19.4.7) indro yatīn sālāvṛkeyebhyaḥ prāyacchat tam aślīlā vāg abhyavadat so 'śuddho 'manyata sa ete śuddhāśuddhīye apaśyat tābhyām aśudhyat
(PB 19.4.8) yad eva bahu pratigṛhṇāti yad garaṃ girati yad anannam atti yad aśuddho manyate tad etābhyāṃ śudhyati
(PB 19.4.9) gauṣūktaṃ cāśvasūktaṃ ca bhavataḥ
(PB 19.4.10) gauṣūktiś cāśvasūktiś ca bahu pratigṛhya garagirāv amanyetāṃ tāv ete sāmanī apaśyatāṃ tābhyāṃ garaṃ niraghnātām
(PB 19.4.11) yad eva bahu pratigṛhṇāti yad garaṃ girati yad anannam atti tad etābhyāṃ nirhate
(PB 19.4.12) pañcadaśa stotrāṇi bhavanty ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśaḥ pāpmana evainaṃ muktvaujasā vīryeṇa samardhayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.4.1) Now this is the <s>Punaḥstoma</s> (re-praise).
(PB 19.4.2) He who, having received much, considers himself a swallower of poison should sacrifice with this.
(PB 19.4.3) The elevenfold — whatever he receives much in his earlier life, whatever poison he swallows, whatever non-food he eats — he casts that off at the morning pressing.
(PB 19.4.4) The twelfth — whatever he receives much in his later life, whatever poison he swallows, whatever non-food he eats — he casts that off at the third pressing.
(PB 19.4.5) A person is of the <s>Virāj</s> nature. He is impure in the middle. He frees him from evil in the middle.
(PB 19.4.6) It has the two <s>Śuddhāśuddhīya</s> (pure-impure chants).
(PB 19.4.7) <s>Indra</s> gave the <s>Yatis</s> (ascetics) to the <s>Sālāvṛkas</s> (wolves). Ugly speech assailed him. He considered himself impure. He perceived these two <s>Śuddhāśuddhīya</s> chants. With them he was purified.
(PB 19.4.8) Whatever he receives much, whatever poison he swallows, whatever non-food he eats, whatever impurity he considers — from that he is purified with these two.
(PB 19.4.9) It has the <s>Gauṣūkta</s> (cow-hymn) and the <s>Aśvasūkta</s> (horse-hymn).
(PB 19.4.10) <s>Gauṣūkti</s> and <s>Aśvasūkti</s>, having received much, considered themselves swallowers of poison. They perceived these two <s>Sāmans</s>. With them they expelled the poison.
(PB 19.4.11) Whatever he receives much, whatever poison he swallows, whatever non-food he eats — that is expelled with these two.
(PB 19.4.12) There are fifteen <s>stotras</s> (praise chants). Vigor and power are the fifteenfold. Having freed him from evil, he restores him with vigor and power.

body.text:
(PB 19.5.1) athaiṣa catuṣṭomaḥ
(PB 19.5.2) paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 19.5.3) yac catasṛbhir bahiṣpavamānaṃ bhavati catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśūn evāvarundhe
(PB 19.5.4) yad aṣṭābhir ājyāny aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśas tat paśūn āpnoti
(PB 19.5.5) yat dvādaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāno dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraṃ paśavo 'nu prajāyante tān evāvarundhe
(PB 19.5.6) yat ṣoḍaśāni pṛṣṭhāni ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ paśavaḥ kalāśas tat paśūn āpnoti
(PB 19.5.7) yad viṃśa ārbhavaḥ pāṅktatvam eṣāṃ tad āpnoti
(PB 19.5.8) yac caturviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaś caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
(PB 19.5.9) prāṇo gāyatrī prajananaṃ prāṇād eva gāyatryāḥ prajāyate
(PB 19.5.10) ekaṃ sāma bahūni chandāṃsi tasmād eko bahūn poṣān puṣyati
(PB 19.5.11) ātmā vā agniṣṭomaḥ paśavaś chandāṃsy ātmany eva tat paśūn pratiṣṭhāpayati noktho nāgniṣṭomo na hi grāmyāḥ paśavo nāraṇyāḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.5.1) Now this is the <s>Catuṣṭoma</s> (four-fold praise).
(PB 19.5.2) One desiring cattle should sacrifice with it.
(PB 19.5.3) When the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (external purification chant) is in groups of four — cattle are four-footed — he secures cattle.
(PB 19.5.4) When the <s>Ājya</s> (ghee libation) chants are in groups of eight — cattle have eight hooves — he obtains cattle hoof by hoof.
(PB 19.5.5) When the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is twelvefold — twelve are the months of the year; cattle reproduce throughout the year — he secures them.
(PB 19.5.6) When the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants are sixteenfold — cattle have sixteen parts — he obtains cattle part by part.
(PB 19.5.7) When the <s>Ārbhava</s> is twentyfold — its fivefold nature he obtains.
(PB 19.5.8) When the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is twenty-four-fold — the <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables; the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is radiance and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s> — he secures radiance and the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
(PB 19.5.9) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), it is procreation. From <s>prāṇa</s> and the <s>Gāyatrī</s> he procreates.
(PB 19.5.10) One <s>Sāman</s> and many meters — therefore one person nourishes many nourishments.
(PB 19.5.11) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the self; cattle are the meters. He establishes cattle in the self. Neither the <s>Uktha</s> nor the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> — for neither domestic cattle nor wild ones.

body.text:
(PB 19.6.1) atha yasya catvāri stotrāṇi catasṛbhiś catvāry aṣṭābhiś catvāri dvādaśabhiś catvāri ṣoḍaśabhiḥ sa gāṃ nātivadati
(PB 19.6.2) ṣoḍaśakalāḥ paśavaḥ kalāśas tat paśūn [KSS & BI: praśūn] āpnoti
(PB 19.6.3) ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśimān bhavati paśavo vā ukthāni vajraḥ ṣoḍaśī vajreṇaivāsmai paśūn parigṛhṇāty anapakrāmukā asmāt paśavo bhavanti noktho nātirātro na hi grāmyāḥ paśavo nāraṇyāḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.6.1) Now, he whose four <s>stotras</s> (praise chants) are in groups of four, four in groups of eight, four in groups of twelve, four in groups of sixteen — he does not surpass the cow.
(PB 19.6.2) Cattle have sixteen parts. He obtains cattle part by part.
(PB 19.6.3) It is an <s>Uktha</s> rite with the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>. Cattle are the <s>Uktha</s> recitations. The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is the thunderbolt. With the thunderbolt he holds cattle fast for him. Cattle do not depart from him. Neither the <s>Uktha</s> nor the <s>Atirātra</s> — for neither domestic cattle nor wild ones.

body.text:
(PB 19.7.1) asurāṇāṃ vai balas tamasā prāvṛto 'śmāpidhānaś cāsīt tasmin gavyaṃ vasv antar āsīt taṃ devā nāśaknuvan bhettuṃ te bṛhaspatim abruvann imān na utsṛjeti sa udbhidaiva balaṃ vyacyāvayad balabhidābhinat tān utsedhenaivodasṛjan niṣedhena paryagṛhṇāt
(PB 19.7.2) paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 19.7.3) yad udbhidā yajeta balam evasmai vicyāvayati yad balabhidā balam evāsmai bhinatti
(PB 19.7.4) utsedhaniṣedhau brahmasāmanī bhavata utsedhenaivāsmai paśūn utsidhya niṣedhena parigṛhṇāti
(PB 19.7.5) ''yajña indram avardhayad'' iti brahmaṇa ājyaṃ rūpeṇa samṛddham
(PB 19.7.6) saptisaptadaśau bhavato yat saptabhiḥ stuvanti sapta grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ paśūn evāvarūndhe saptapadā śakvarī paśavaḥ śakvarī paśūn evāvarūndhe 'tha yat saptadaśabhiḥ prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajāpatim evāpnoti
(PB 19.7.7) gāyatrīṃ saṃpadyate tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe prāṇo gāyatrī prajananaṃ prāṇād eva gāyatryāḥ prajāyate
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.7.1) The fortress of the <s>asuras</s> was enveloped in darkness and had a stone covering. Within it was cattle-wealth. The gods were unable to break it. They said to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>: 'Release these for us!' He dislodged the fortress with the <s>Udbhid</s> (upthrust) and broke it with the <s>Balabhid</s> (strength-breaker). He released them with the <s>Utsedha</s> (elevation) and enclosed them with the <s>Niṣedha</s> (restriction).
(PB 19.7.2) One desiring animals should sacrifice with this.
(PB 19.7.3) When he sacrifices with the <s>Udbhid</s>, he dislodges the fortress for him. When with the <s>Balabhid</s>, he breaks the strength for him.
(PB 19.7.4) The <s>Utsedha</s> and <s>Niṣedha</s> are the <s>Brahma-sāmans</s>. By the <s>Utsedha</s> he raises up animals for him; by the <s>Niṣedha</s> he encloses them.
(PB 19.7.5) '<s>Yajña Indram avardhayat</s>' — the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-offering) pertaining to <s>Brahman</s> is complete in form.
(PB 19.7.6) There are both seven-fold and seventeen-fold <s>stomas</s>. When they praise with seven, the seven domestic animals — thereby he obtains animals. The <s>Śakvarī</s> has seven feet; animals are the <s>Śakvarī</s> — thereby he obtains animals. And when with seventeen, <s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>saptadaśa</s> — thereby he attains <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 19.7.7) It comes to equal the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Brilliance and brahmanical splendor are the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — thereby he obtains brilliance and brahmanical splendor. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; procreation. From <s>prāṇa</s> itself, from the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he is procreated.

body.text:
(PB 19.8.1) athaiṣo 'pacitir apacitikāmo yajetāpacityaivāsmā apacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.8.2) tasya caturviṃśau pavamānau caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī tejasaivāsmai brahmavarcasenāpacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.8.3) ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavata ubhābhyām evāsmai bṛhadrathantarābhyām apacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.8.4) bhargayaśasī bhavato bhargeṇaivāsmai bhargo dadhāti yaśasā yaśaḥ
(PB 19.8.5) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś cobhayair evāsmai stomair apacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.8.6) tad āhur vilomāna stomā īśvarā yajamānaṃ vikṣetor vi hy atiyantīti
(PB 19.8.7) ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomo bhavati pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo 'ntata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.8.1) Now this is the <s>Apaciti</s> (honor-winning rite). One desiring honor should sacrifice. By the <s>Apaciti</s> itself he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.8.2) Its <s>Pavamānas</s> are in the <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-fold). The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables; brilliance and brahmanical splendor are the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. By brilliance and brahmanical splendor he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.8.3) Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are used. By both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.8.4) The <s>Bharga</s> (splendor) and <s>Yaśas</s> (fame) sāmans are used. By splendor he places splendor in him; by fame, fame.
(PB 19.8.5) Both kinds of <s>stomas</s> — even and odd — are used. By both kinds of <s>stomas</s> he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.8.6) They say: 'The <s>stomas</s> in reversed order are liable to harm the sacrificer, for they go in opposite directions.'
(PB 19.8.7) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is in the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold). The <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is indeed firm establishment. At the very end he becomes firmly established in the sacrifice.

body.text:
(PB 19.9.1) athaiṣa sarvastomo 'pacitir apacitikāmo yajeta sarvair evāsmai stomair apacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.9.2) virājaṃ saṃpadyata eṣa vā apacito yo 'nnādo 'nnaṃ virāḍ annādyam evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 19.9.3) ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavato bhargayaśasī bhavata ubhaye stomāś chandomāś ca pṛṣṭhyāś cobhayair evāsmai stomair apacitiṃ vindati
(PB 19.9.4) tasya chandomāḥ pṛṣṭhāni paśavo vai chandomā annaṃ pṛṣṭhāny abhipūrvam evāsminn annādyaṃ paśūn dadhāti yac chandomavāṃs tena dvādaśāhayājinam āpnoti
(PB 19.9.5) tad āhur nānālokāḥ stomāś chandomāś ca pṛṣṭhyāś ca yad ekasmin yajñakratau samavarudhyanta īśvaro [corr. Caland; BI & KSS īśvarā] yajamāno 'pratiṣṭhātor iti
(PB 19.9.6) ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomo bhavati pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhām eva tad abhyāyanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.9.1) Now this is the <s>Sarvastoma</s> (all-<s>stoma</s>) <s>Apaciti</s>. One desiring honor should sacrifice. By all <s>stomas</s> he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.9.2) It comes to equal the <s>Virāj</s>. This is indeed the honored one — he who eats food. Food is <s>Virāj</s>. Thereby he places food-eating in him.
(PB 19.9.3) Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are used; the <s>Bharga</s> and <s>Yaśas</s> are used; both kinds of <s>stomas</s> — meter-measures and <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chants). By both kinds of <s>stomas</s> he wins honor for him.
(PB 19.9.4) Its meter-measures serve as <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants. Animals are the meter-measures; food is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants. He places food-eating and animals in him in due order. Since it has meter-measures, by that he attains the status of a twelve-day sacrificer.
(PB 19.9.5) They say: 'The <s>stomas</s>, meter-measures, and <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> chants belong to different worlds. When they are brought together in a single sacrificial rite, the sacrificer is liable to lose his foundation.'
(PB 19.9.6) The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is in the <s>ekaviṃśa</s>. The <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is indeed firm establishment. They thereby approach firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 19.10.1) pakṣī vā eṣa stomaḥ
(PB 19.10.2) pakṣy eṣa nidhīyate
(PB 19.10.3) na vā apakṣaḥ pakṣiṇam āpnoty atha yad eṣa pakṣy apakṣiṇi nidhīyate tasmāt pakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaiḥ patanti
(PB 19.10.4) pakṣī jyotiṣmān puṇyān lokān saṃcarati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.10.5) trivṛtāv abhito bhavatas tejo brahmavarcasaṃ trivṛt teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
(PB 19.10.6) atha pañcadaśau vīryaṃ vai pañcadaśo vīryam evāvarundhe
(PB 19.10.7) atha saptadaśau paśavo vai saptadaśaḥ paśūn evāvarundhe
(PB 19.10.8) athaikaviṃśau pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo madhyata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 19.10.9) atha triṇavāv ime vai lokās triṇava eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 19.10.10) atha trayastriṃśo varṣma vai trayastriṃśaḥ
(PB 19.10.11) varṣma svānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.10.12) eṣa vāva bradhnasya viṣṭapo yad etau trayastriṃśau madhyataḥ saṃdhīyete tena bradhnasya viṣṭapam ārohati
(PB 19.10.13) madhyato vā agnir variṣṭhas tasmād ete stomā madhyato variṣṭhāḥ kriyante
(PB 19.10.14) trivṛtā praiti trivṛtodeti prāṇo vai trivṛt prāṇenaiva praiti prāṇam abhyudeti
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.10.1) This <s>stoma</s> is indeed winged.
(PB 19.10.2) This winged one is stored up.
(PB 19.10.3) The wingless does not attain the winged. But since this winged one is stored in a wingless form, therefore winged creatures fly with their wings.
(PB 19.10.4) He traverses the auspicious worlds, winged and luminous — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.10.5) <s>Trivṛts</s> (nine-fold) are on both sides. Brilliance and brahmanical splendor are the <s>trivṛt</s> — thereby he obtains brilliance and brahmanical splendor.
(PB 19.10.6) Then <s>pañcadaśas</s> (fifteen-fold). Vigor is the <s>pañcadaśa</s> — thereby he obtains vigor.
(PB 19.10.7) Then <s>saptadaśas</s> (seventeen-fold). Animals are the <s>saptadaśa</s> — thereby he obtains animals.
(PB 19.10.8) Then <s>ekaviṃśas</s> (twenty-one-fold). Firm establishment is the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> — thereby he becomes firmly established in the middle of the sacrifice.
(PB 19.10.9) Then <s>triṇavas</s> (twenty-seven-fold). These worlds are the <s>triṇava</s> — thereby he becomes firmly established in these very worlds.
(PB 19.10.10) Then the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-fold). The <s>trayastriṃśa</s> is indeed height.
(PB 19.10.11) He becomes the tallest among his own — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.10.12) This is indeed the seat of the tawny one (<s>Bradhna</s>, the sun). When these two <s>trayastriṃśas</s> are joined in the middle, by that he ascends to the seat of <s>Bradhna</s>.
(PB 19.10.13) <s>Agni</s> is the greatest in the middle. Therefore these <s>stomas</s> are made greatest in the middle.
(PB 19.10.14) He proceeds with the <s>trivṛt</s>; he rises up with the <s>trivṛt</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>trivṛt</s>. By <s>prāṇa</s> alone he proceeds; he rises up to <s>prāṇa</s>.

body.text:
(PB 19.11.1) athaiṣa jyotiḥ
(PB 19.11.2) tasya trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni caturviṃśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānaḥ saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni
(PB 19.11.3) prāṇo vai trivṛd ātmā pañcadaśaḥ
(PB 19.11.4) mukhaṃ gāyatry annaṃ vai saptadaśo mukhata eva tad annaṃ dhatte
(PB 19.11.5) annam atty annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.11.6) mādhyandinena vai pavamānena devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan yad eṣa caturviṃśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāno bhavati svargasya lokasyākrāntyai caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe prāṇo gāyatrī prajananaṃ prāṇād eva gāyatryāḥ prajāyate
(PB 19.11.7) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tan mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
(PB 19.11.8) pakṣi vā etac chandaḥ pakṣī jyotiṣmān puṇyān lokān saṃcarati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.11.9) madhyato vā agnir variṣṭhas tasmād ete stomā madhyato variṣṭhāḥ kriyante
(PB 19.11.10) ekā saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyata ekākinam evainam annādyasyādhyakṣaṃ karoti
(PB 19.11.11) jyotir vā eṣo 'gniṣṭomo jyotiṣmantaṃ puṇyaṃ lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ vidvān etena yajate
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.11.1) Now this is the <s>Jyotis</s> (light-rite).
(PB 19.11.2) Its <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is in <s>trivṛt</s>; the <s>ājyas</s> are in <s>pañcadaśa</s>; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is in <s>caturviṃśa</s>; the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants are in <s>saptadaśa</s>.
(PB 19.11.3) <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>trivṛt</s>; the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>pañcadaśa</s>.
(PB 19.11.4) The mouth is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; food is the <s>saptadaśa</s>. Thereby he places food at the mouth.
(PB 19.11.5) He eats food; he becomes a food-eater — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.11.6) By the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> the gods went to the heavenly world. Since this midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is in the <s>caturviṃśa</s>, it is for ascending to the heavenly world. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables; brilliance and brahmanical splendor are the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — thereby he obtains brilliance and brahmanical splendor. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; procreation. From <s>prāṇa</s> itself, from the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he is procreated.
(PB 19.11.7) Both kinds of <s>stomas</s> — even and odd. That is a mating pair. From that pair he is procreated.
(PB 19.11.8) This meter is indeed winged. He traverses the auspicious worlds, winged and luminous — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.11.9) <s>Agni</s> is the greatest in the middle. Therefore these <s>stomas</s> are made greatest in the middle.
(PB 19.11.10) One of the collectively praised surpasses the <s>Virāj</s>. He thereby makes him the sole overseer of food-eating.
(PB 19.11.11) This is indeed the <s>Jyotis</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. He wins a luminous, auspicious world — he who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this.

body.text:
(PB 19.12.1) athaiṣa ṛṣabhaḥ
(PB 19.12.2) ṛṣabho vā eṣa stomānām ṛṣabhatāṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.12.3) rājanyaṃ yājayed ṛṣabho vai paśūnām adhipatī rājanyo manuṣyāṇām
(PB 19.12.4) yo vā asti so 'dhipatiḥ
(PB 19.12.5) adhipatiḥ samānānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.12.6) tasya sadoviśīyaṃ mādhyandine pavamāne bhavati viśam evāsmai savanābhyāṃ parigṛhṇāty anapakrāmukāsmād viḍ bhavati
(PB 19.12.7) samantaṃ bhavati samantām evāsmai viśaṃ karoty anapakrāmukāsmād viḍ bhavati
(PB 19.12.8) ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavata iyaṃ vai rathantaraṃ dyaur bṛhadevāsmāl lokād gāyatry evāmuṣmād ubhayor anayor lokayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 19.12.9) anuṣṭubhi bṛhad bhavaty anto vā anuṣṭup chandasām anto bṛhat sāmnām anto rājanyo manuṣyāṇām anta eva tad antaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmād yo rājanyānāṃ hīyate na sa punaragraṃ paryeti
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.12.1) Now this is the <s>Ṛṣabha</s> (bull-rite).
(PB 19.12.2) This is indeed the bull among <s>stomas</s>. He attains bull-hood — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.12.3) One should have a <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior) sacrifice with this. The bull is the lord of animals; the <s>Rājanya</s> is the lord of men.
(PB 19.12.4) Whoever is thus, he is the lord.
(PB 19.12.5) He becomes the lord among his equals — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.12.6) Its <s>Sadoviśīya</s> (sāman pertaining to the assembly of the people) is in the midday <s>Pavamāna</s>. He encloses the common people for him by the two pressings. The common people do not depart from him.
(PB 19.12.7) It is complete. He makes the common people complete for him. The common people do not depart from him.
(PB 19.12.8) Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are used. This world is the <s>Rathantara</s>; heaven is the <s>Bṛhat</s>. From this world by the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and from the yonder world — he becomes firmly established in both of these worlds.
(PB 19.12.9) The <s>Bṛhat</s> is in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the limit of the meters; the <s>Bṛhat</s> is the limit of the <s>sāmans</s>; the <s>Rājanya</s> is the limit of men. He thereby establishes the limit at the limit. Therefore, a <s>Rājanya</s> who is left behind does not come to the front again.

body.text:
(PB 19.13.1) yo vai vājapeyaḥ sa rājasūyo yo rājasūyaḥ sa varūṇasavo 'thaiṣa gosavaḥ svārājyo vā eṣa yajñaḥ
(PB 19.13.2) svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.3) prajāpatir hi svārājyaṃ parameṣṭhī svārājyam
(PB 19.13.4) parameṣṭhitāṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.5) ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavatas tad dhi svārājyaṃ svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.6) ayutaṃ dakṣiṇās tad dhi svārājyaṃ svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.7) pratiduhābhiṣicyate tad dhi svārājyaṃ svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.8) bṛhataḥ stotra pratyabhiṣicyate tad dhi svārājyaṃ svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.13.9) anuddhate dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasyābhiṣicyate 'syām evānantarhite 'dhy abhiṣicyate
(PB 19.13.10) sarvaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśastena gosavaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.13.1) The <s>Vājapeya</s> is indeed the <s>Rājasūya</s>; the <s>Rājasūya</s> is the <s>Vāruṇasava</s> (Varuṇa's pressing). Now this is the <s>Gosava</s> (cow-pressing). This is the sacrifice of self-sovereignty.
(PB 19.13.2) He attains self-sovereignty — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.3) <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed has self-sovereignty; <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme) has self-sovereignty.
(PB 19.13.4) He attains the status of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.5) Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are used. That is self-sovereignty. He attains self-sovereignty — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.6) The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is ten thousand. That is self-sovereignty. He attains self-sovereignty — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.7) He is consecrated with fresh-drawn milk. That is self-sovereignty. He attains self-sovereignty — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.8) He is re-consecrated at the <s>Bṛhat stotra</s> (chant). That is self-sovereignty. He attains self-sovereignty — he who knows thus.
(PB 19.13.9) He is consecrated south of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, without being elevated, on this very ground without interruption.
(PB 19.13.10) The entire rite is thirty-six-fold. By that it is the <s>Gosava</s>.

body.text:
(PB 19.14.1) athaiṣa marutstoma etena vai maruto 'parimitāṃ puṣṭim apuṣyann aparimitāṃ puṣṭiṃ puṣyati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.14.2) yad gaṇaśaḥ stomās tena marutstomo gaṇaśo hi marutaḥ
(PB 19.14.3) etenaiva trīn yājayet
(PB 19.14.4) yat trīṇi trivṛnti stotrāṇi bhavanti nānā brahmavarcase pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 19.14.5) yat trīṇi pañcadaśāni nānā vīrye
(PB 19.14.6) yat trīṇi saptadaśāni nānā paśuṣu
(PB 19.14.7) yat trīṇy ekaviṃśāni nānā pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 19.14.8) pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.14.1) Now this is the <s>Marutstoma</s> (chant pattern of the Maruts). By this the <s>Maruts</s> nourished unlimited prosperity. He who knows thus nourishes unlimited prosperity.
(PB 19.14.2) Because the <s>stomas</s> are in groups, therefore it is the <s>Marutstoma</s>, for the <s>Maruts</s> are in groups.
(PB 19.14.3) With this one should sacrifice for three [sacrificers].
(PB 19.14.4) Because there are three sets of three-fold (<s>Trivṛt</s>) <s>stotras</s>, they become separately established in <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmic splendor).

body.text:
(PB 19.15.1) athaiṣa indrāgnyoḥ kulāyaḥ prajākāmo vā paśukāmo vā yajeta prajā vai kulāyaṃ paśavaḥ kulāyaṃ gṛhāḥ kulāyaṃ kulāyam eva bhavati
(PB 19.15.2) etenaiva dvau yājayet
(PB 19.15.3) yat ṣaṭ trivṛnti stotrāṇi bhavanti nānā brahmavarcase pratitiṣṭhato yat dve pañcadaśe nānā vīrye yat dve saptadaśe nānā paśuṣu yat dve ekaviṃśe nānā pratitiṣṭhataḥ pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.15.1) Now this is the nest (<s>kulāya</s>) of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. One desiring offspring or one desiring cattle should sacrifice. For offspring are a nest, cattle are a nest, a household is a nest. One indeed becomes a nest.
(PB 19.15.2) With this one should sacrifice for two [sacrificers].
(PB 19.15.3) Because there are six three-fold <s>stotras</s>, they become separately established in <s>brahmavarcas</s>. Because there are two fifteen-fold, separately in vigor. Because two seventeen-fold,

body.text:
(PB 19.16.1) athaiṣa pañcadaśa indrastoma ukthyaḥ
(PB 19.16.2) etena vā indro 'ty anyā devatā abhavad aty anyāḥ prajā bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.16.3) rājanyaṃ yājayet
(PB 19.16.4) sarvaḥ pañcadaśo bhavaty ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśa ojasaivainaṃ vīryeṇa samardhayati
(PB 19.16.5) aindrīṣu bhavantīndriyeṇaivainaṃ vīryeṇa samardhayati
(PB 19.16.6) ukthyo bhavati paśavo vā ukthāni viḍ ukthāni viśam evāsmai paśūn anuniyunakty anapakrāmukāsmād viḍ bhavati
(PB 19.16.7) pañcadaśa stotrāṇi pañcadaśāni bhavanty ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśo 'bhipūrvam evāsminn ojo vīryaṃ dadhāti
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.16.1) Now this is the fifteen-fold <s>Indrastoma</s>, an <s>Ukthya</s> [rite].
(PB 19.16.2) By this, <s>Indra</s> surpassed the other deities. He who knows thus surpasses other creatures.
(PB 19.16.3) One should sacrifice for a <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior).
(PB 19.16.4) It is entirely fifteen-fold. Vigor and vitality are in the fifteen-fold. By vigor and vitality one strengthens him.
(PB 19.16.5) They are in <s>Aindrī</s> (Indra-related) [verses] — by the power of <s>Indra</s>.

body.text:
(PB 19.17.1) athaiṣa indrāgnyoḥ stoma etena vā indrāgnī aty anyā devatā abhavatām aty anyāḥ prajā bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.17.2) trivṛt pañcadaśo bhavati
(PB 19.17.3) brahma vai trivṛt kṣatraṃ pañcadaśo brahmaṇa iva cāsya kṣatrasyeva ca prakāśo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.17.4) rājā ca purohitaś ca yajeyātām
(PB 19.17.5) gāyatrīṃ ca jagatīṃ ca saṃpadyate
(PB 19.17.6) tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatryā brāhmaṇo 'varundhe viśaṃ rājā jagatyā praviśati
(PB 19.17.7) purodhākāmo yajeta
(PB 19.17.8) bṛhaspatir akāmayata devānāṃ purodhāṃ gaccheyam iti sa etenāyajata sa devānāṃ purodhām agacchad gacchati purodhāṃ ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.17.1) Now this is the <s>stoma</s> of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. By this, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> surpassed the other deities. He who knows thus surpasses other creatures.
(PB 19.17.2) It becomes three-fold [and] fifteen-fold.
(PB 19.17.3) The three-fold is indeed <s>Brahman</s> (priestly power); the fifteen-fold is <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior power). The brilliance of both his <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Kṣatra</s> comes to he who knows thus.
(PB 19.17.4) A king and a purohita (royal priest)

body.text:
(PB 19.18.1) athaiṣa vighanaḥ
(PB 19.18.2) indro 'kāmayata pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ vihanyām iti sa etaṃ vighanam apaśyat tena pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ vyahan vi pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 19.18.3) yat trivṛd bhavati prāṇāṃs tenāvarundhe yat dvādaśaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ tena yat pañcadaśo vīryaṃ tena yat saptadaśo 'nnādyaṃ tena yad ekaviṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhā tena yan navadaśaḥ prajananaṃ tena yac caturviṃśo brahmavarcasaṃ tena yat triṇavo vajraṃ bhrātṛvyāya praharati
(PB 19.18.4) paśukāmo yajeta bṛhatīṃ saṃpadyate paśavo vai bṛhatī paśūn evāvarundhe
(PB 19.18.5) ṣaḍ etā bṛhatyo bhavanti ṣaḍ ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraṃ paśavo 'nu prajāyante tān evāptvāvarundhe
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.18.1) Now this is the <s>Vighana</s> (the smasher).
(PB 19.18.2) <s>Indra</s> desired: 'Let me smash the sinful rival.' He perceived this <s>Vighana</s>. With it he smashed the sinful rival. He who knows thus smashes the sinful rival.
(PB 19.18.3) Because it is three-fold — by that he secures the vital breaths. Because twelve-fold — by that the year. Because fifteen-fold — by that vigor. Because

body.text:
(PB 19.19.1) indram adevyo māyā ayacanta sa prajāpatim upādhāvavat tasmā etaṃ vighanaṃ prāyacchat tena sarvā mṛdho vyahata yad vyahata tad vighanasya vighanatvam
(PB 19.19.2) sarvā mṛdho vihate ya evaṃ vidvān vighanena yajate yam evaṃ vidvān vighanena yājayati
(PB 19.19.3) paśukāmo yajeta paśavo vai bṛhatī paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 19.19.1) The non-divine <s>māyās</s> (deceptive powers) besought <s>Indra</s>. He ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. [<s>Prajāpati</s>] gave him this <s>Vighana</s>. With it he smashed all enemies. Because he smashed (<s>vyahata</s>), that is the origin of the <s>Vighana's</s> name.
(PB 19.19.2) He who, knowing thus, sacrifices with the <s>Vighana</s> smashes all enemies. He for whom one, knowing thus, sacrifices with the <s>Vighana</s> [likewise smashes all enemies].
(PB 19.19.3) One desiring cattle should sacrifice. Cattle indeed

body.text:
(PB 20.1.1) trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni pañcadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānaḥ saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni saptadaśa ārbhava ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ sokthyaḥ pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.1.2) jyotiṣṭomenātirātreṇarddhikāmo yajetābhikramo vā eṣa stomānām abhikrāntyā abhikrāntena hi yajñasyardhnoti
(PB 20.1.3) eṣo 'gniṣṭoma eṣa ukthya eṣo 'tirātro 'gniṣṭomena vai devā imaṃ lokam abhyajayann ukthyair antarikṣaṃ rātryāmuṃ lokam ajayann ahorātrābhyām abhyavartanta
(PB 20.1.4) parācyo vā anyā vyucchanti pratīcyo 'nyā eṣā vāva pratīcī vyucchati yāśvinena vyucchati pratīcīr evāsmā uṣaso vivāsayati
(PB 20.1.5) dve saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyete eṣā vai stanavatī virāṭ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam etāṃ dugdhe
(PB 20.1.6) trivṛtā praiti trivṛtodeti prāṇo vai trivṛt prāṇenaiva praiti prāṇam abhyudeti
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.1.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is three-fold; the <s>ājyas</s> are fifteen-fold; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is fifteen-fold; the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants] are seventeen-fold; the <s>Ārbhava</s> is seventeen-fold; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is twenty-one-fold with the <s>Ukthya</s>; the night [portion] is fifteen-fold; the joining is three-fold.
(PB 20.1.2) One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra</s>. This is indeed an advance of the <s>stomas</s>. Through advance, one prospers with an advanced sacrifice.

body.text:
(PB 20.2.1) trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāna ekaviṃśāni pṛṣṭhāni triṇava ārbhavas trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamaṃ dve ekaviṃśe saṣoḍaśike pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.2.2) sarvastomenātirātreṇa bubhūṣan yajeta sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvam evaitenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati
(PB 20.2.3) yat trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ bhavati tat trivṛtaṃ stomam āpnoti gāyatrīṃ chando yat pañcadaśāny ājyāni tat pañcadaśaṃ stomam āpnoti triṣṭubhaṃ chando yat saptadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānas tat saptadaśaṃ stomam āpnoti jagatīṃ chando yad ekaviṃśāni pṛṣṭāni tad ekaviṃśaṃ stomam āpnoty anuṣṭubhaṃ chando yat triṇava ārbhavas tat triṇavaṃ stomam āpnoti paṅktiṃ chando yat trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomas tat trayastriṃśaṃ stomam āpnoti virājaṃ chando yad uṣṇikkakubhau kriyete tad uṣṇikkakubhāv āpnoti yad āśvinaṃ śasyate tat sarvam evaitenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati
(PB 20.2.4) prāñcaṃ vai trayastriṃśo yajñaṃ prabhujati tam adhvaryur ekādaśinyā purastāt pratyudyacchaty ekādaśa raśanā ekādaśa paśava ekādaśa yūpā bhavanti tat trayastriṃśe trayastriṃśaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 20.2.5) tayā samudyatayā rātryā yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate taṃ tam abhyaśnute yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate taṃ tam abhyaśnute ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.2.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is three-fold; the <s>ājyas</s> fifteen-fold; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> seventeen-fold; the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> twenty-one-fold; the <s>Ārbhava</s> twenty-seven-fold (<s>Triṇava</s>); the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> thirty-three-fold; the <s>Ukthas</s> descending: the first twenty-seven-fold, two twenty-one-fold with sixteen, the night fifteen-fold, the joining three-fold.
(PB 20.2.2) One wishing to prosper should sacrifice with the <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s>. All the <s>stomas</s>

body.text:
(PB 20.3.1) trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāna ekaviṃśaṃ hotuḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ chandomā itarāṇi triṇava ārbhavas trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamam athaikaviṃśam atha saptadaśam ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhis trivṛt prathamam atiriktastotram atha pañcadaśam atha saptadaśam athaikaviṃśam
(PB 20.3.2) prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tān agniṣṭomena nāpnot tān ukthair nāpnot tān ṣoḍaśinā nāpnot tān rātryā nāpnot tān sandhinā nāpnot tān āśvinena nāpnot tān agnim abravīd imān ma īpseti tān agnis trivṛtā stomena jarābodhīyena sāmnā nāpnot tān indram abravīd imān ma īpseti tān indraḥ pañcadaśena stomena sattrāsāhīyena sāmnā nāpnot tān viśvān devān abravīd imān ma ipsateti tān viśve devāḥ saptadaśena stomena mārgīṃyaveṇa sāmnā nāpnuvaṃs tān viṣṇum abravīd imān ma īpseti tān viṣṇur ekaviṃśena stomenāpnod vāravantīyenāvārayatedaṃ viṣṇur vicakrama iti vyakramata
(PB 20.3.3) yasmāt pra preva paśavo bhraṃśeran sa etena yajeta
(PB 20.3.4) etena vai devā jaitvāni jitvā yaṃ yaṃ kāmam akāmayanta taṃ tam āpnuvan yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam etenāpnoti
(PB 20.3.5) tad aptoryāmno 'ptoryāmatvam
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.3.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold; the <s>Ājya</s> chants are fifteenfold; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is seventeenfold; the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is twenty-onefold; the <s>Chandomā</s> days are the rest; the <s>Ārbhava</s> is twenty-sevenfold; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is thirty-threefold; the <s>Uktha</s> chants descend — twenty-seven first, then twenty-one, then seventeen; the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is twenty-onefold; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> (junction) is threefold; the additional <s>stotra</s> is threefold first, then fifteenfold, then seventeenfold, then twenty-onefold.
(PB 20.3.2) <s>Prajāpati</s> created cattle. Having been created, they ran away from him. He did not obtain them by the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, not by the <s>Uktha</s> chants, not by the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, not by the night rite, not by the <s>Sandhi</s>, not by the <s>Āśvina</s>. He said to <s>Agni</s>: 'Obtain these for me.' <s>Agni</s> did not obtain them with the threefold <s>stoma</s> and the <s>Jarābodhīya Sāman</s>. He said to <s>Indra</s>: 'Obtain these for me.' <s>Indra</s> did not obtain them with the fifteenfold <s>stoma</s> and the <s>Sattrāsāhīya Sāman</s>. He said to the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>: 'Obtain these for me.' The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> did not obtain them with the seventeenfold <s>stoma</s> and the <s>Mārgīyava Sāman</s>. He said to <s>Viṣṇu</s>: 'Obtain these for me.' <s>Viṣṇu</s> obtained them with the twenty-onefold <s>stoma</s>; he barred them with the <s>Vāravantīya</s>; he strode forth with '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode.''
(PB 20.3.3) One from whom cattle run away, as it were — he should sacrifice with this.
(PB 20.3.4) By this the gods, having won what was to be won, whatever desire they desired, they obtained. Whatever desire one desires, one obtains by this.
(PB 20.3.5) That is the <s>Aptoryāma</s>-nature of the <s>Aptoryāma</s>.

body.text:
(PB 20.4.1) trivṛd bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśaṃ hotur ājyaṃ navasaptadaśāni stotrāṇy ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ sokthaḥ pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.4.2) navasaptadaśenātirātreṇa prajākāmo yajeta nava vai prāṇāḥ prajāpatiḥ saptadaśaḥ prāṇebhya eva tad adhi prajāpateḥ prajāḥ prajāyante
(PB 20.4.3) kakubhaṃ prācīm udūhati puruṣo vai kakup garbho vā eṣa madhyato dhīyate
(PB 20.4.4) tasyāṃ sākamaśvam
(PB 20.4.5) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā na prājāyanta sa etat sāmāpaśyat tā aśvo bhūtvābhyajighrat tāḥ prājāyanta prajananaṃ vā etat sāma
(PB 20.4.6) prajāyate bahur bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 20.4.7) dvipadāṃ kakubho loke karoti garbham eva taddhitaṃ madhyataḥ prajanayati
(PB 20.4.8) atirātro bhavaty ahorātre vā anu prajāḥ prajāyante 'horātre evānu prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāyate
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.4.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold; the <s>Ājya</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is fifteenfold; the <s>stotras</s> are nine-by-seventeen; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is twenty-onefold with <s>Uktha</s> chants; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> is threefold.
(PB 20.4.2) One desiring offspring should sacrifice with a nine-by-seventeen <s>Atirātra</s>. There are nine vital breaths; <s>Prajāpati</s> is the seventeenfold. From the vital breaths indeed offspring are born from <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 20.4.3) He raises up the <s>Kakubh</s> (peak verse) forward. Man is the <s>Kakubh</s>. The embryo is placed in the middle.
(PB 20.4.4) On that, the <s>Sākamaśva</s> (Sāman).
(PB 20.4.5) <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. They did not procreate. He perceived this <s>Sāman</s>. Having become a horse, he sniffed them. They procreated. This is the <s>Sāman</s> of procreation.
(PB 20.4.6) He who knows thus procreates and becomes great.
(PB 20.4.7) He places the <s>Kakubh</s> in the world of two-footed creatures. He causes the embryo placed in the middle to procreate.
(PB 20.4.8) It is an <s>Atirātra</s>. Offspring are born following day and night. By day and night he is born with offspring and cattle.

body.text:
(PB 20.5.1) trivṛt bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni pañcadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānaḥ saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni saptadaśa ārbhava ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ saptadaśāny ukthāni pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.5.2) viṣuvatātirātreṇa jyeṣṭhaṃ jyaiṣṭhineyaṃ yājayed viṣuvān vā eṣa stomānāṃ viṣuvān eva bhavati yad eka ekaviṃśo bhavaty ekaviṃśo vā ito 'sāv āditya dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavas traya ime lokā
(PB 20.5.3) asāv āditya ekaviṃśa ādityasyaivainaṃ mātrāṃ gamayati
(PB 20.5.4) eṣa vā udeti na vā enam anyat jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ pratyudeti
(PB 20.5.5) nainam anyaḥ sveṣu pratyudeti ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.5.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold; the <s>Ājya</s> chants are fifteenfold; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is fifteenfold; the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants are seventeenfold; the <s>Ārbhava</s> is seventeenfold; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is twenty-onefold; the <s>Uktha</s> chants are seventeenfold; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> is threefold.
(PB 20.5.2) One should make the eldest son sacrifice with a <s>Viṣuvat Atirātra</s>. This is the equinox of the <s>stomas</s>. He becomes the equinox. Since a single twenty-onefold appears — from here the sun is twenty-onefold: twelve months, five seasons, three worlds.
(PB 20.5.3) That sun is the twenty-onefold. He leads him to the measure of the sun.
(PB 20.5.4) He rises, and no other light rises to oppose him.
(PB 20.5.5) No other rises to oppose him among his own, who knows thus.

body.text: (PB 20.6.1) pañcadaśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ trivṛnty ājyāni saptadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam ekaviṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ sokthaṃ pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhir goṣṭomenātirātreṇa bhrātṛvyavān yajeta gavā vai devā asurān ebhyo lokebhyo 'nudanta rātryānapajayyam ajayann ebhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ praṇudya rātryānapajayyaṃ jayati
body.translated_text: (PB 20.6.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is fifteenfold; the <s>Ājya</s> chants are threefold; the midday pressing is seventeenfold; the third pressing is twenty-onefold, with <s>Uktha</s> chants; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> is threefold. One who has a hostile rival should sacrifice with a <s>Goṣṭoma Atirātra</s>. With the cow the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> from these worlds. By the night they won an unconquerable victory. Having driven the hostile rival from these worlds, he wins an unconquerable victory by the night.

body.text: (PB 20.7.1) trivṛt bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam ekaviṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ sokthaṃ pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhir āyuṣṭomenātirātreṇa svargakāmo yajetordhvāḥ stomā yanty anapabhraṃśāya yad atirātro bhavaty ahorātrābhyām eva svargaṃ lokam eti
body.translated_text: (PB 20.7.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold; the <s>Ājya</s> chants are fifteenfold; the midday pressing is seventeenfold; the third pressing is twenty-onefold, with <s>Uktha</s> chants; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> is threefold. One desiring heaven should sacrifice with an <s>Āyuṣṭoma Atirātra</s>. The <s>stomas</s> go upward — to prevent a fall. Since it is an <s>Atirātra</s>, by day and night he goes to the heavenly world.

body.text: (PB 20.8.1) trivṛt bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśaṃ hotur ājyaṃ saptadaśaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya pañcadaśaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ saptadaśam acchāvākasyaikaviṃśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānaḥ saptadaśaṃ hotuḥ pṛṣṭham ekaviṃśaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya triṇavaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ekaviṃśam acchāvakasya triṇava ārbhavas trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamaṃ dve ekaviṃśe saṣoḍaśike pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhir abhijitātirātreṇa bhrātṛvyavān yajetābhijitā vai devā asurān imān lokān abhyajayat rātryānapajayyam ajayann abhijitaiva bhrātṛvyam imān lokān abhijitya rātryānapajayyaṃ jayati
body.translated_text: (PB 20.8.1) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> is threefold; the <s>Ājya</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is fifteenfold; of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is seventeenfold; of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> is fifteenfold; of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> is seventeenfold; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is twenty-onefold; the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is seventeenfold; of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> twenty-onefold; of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> twenty-sevenfold; of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> twenty-onefold; the <s>Ārbhava</s> is twenty-sevenfold; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is thirty-threefold; the <s>Uktha</s> chants descend — twenty-seven first, then two twenty-one with <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>; the night is fifteenfold; the <s>Sandhi</s> is threefold. One who has a hostile rival should sacrifice with an <s>Abhijit Atirātra</s>. By the <s>Abhijit</s> the gods conquered these worlds from the <s>Asuras</s>. By the night they won an unconquerable victory. By the <s>Abhijit</s> he conquers these worlds from the hostile rival and by the night wins an unconquerable victory.

body.text:
(PB 20.9.1) trivṛt bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśaṃ hotur ājyaṃ saptadaśaṃ maitrāvaruṇasyaikaviṃśaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ pañcadaśam acchāvākasya saptadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāna ekaviṃśaṃ hotuḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ triṇavaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya
(PB 20.9.1) saptadaśaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ekaviṃśam acchāvākasya triṇava ārbhavas trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamaṃ dve ekaviṃśe saṣoḍaśike pañcadaśī rātriḥ trivṛt sandhir viśvajitātirātreṇa paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 20.9.2) reto hi nābhānediṣṭhīyaṃ paśavo vālakhilyā yan nābhānediṣṭhīyaṃ pūrvaṃ śasyata uttarā vālakhilyā retasas tat paśavaḥ prajāyante rūpāṇi vikaroti yad vārṣākapam ṛtuṣu pratitiṣṭhati yad evayāmarut

(PB 20.10.1) trivṛt ātirātreṇa brahmavarcasakāmo yajeta tejo vai trivṛt brahmavarcasaṃ teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe tejasi brahmavarcase pratitiṣṭhati pañcadaśenātirātreṇa vīryakāmo yajetaujo vīryaṃ pañcadaśa oja eva vīryam avarundha ojasi vīrye pratitiṣṭhati saptadaśenātirācreṇānnādyakāmo yajetānnaṃ vai saptadaśo 'nnādyam evāvarundha ekaviṃśenātirātreṇa pratiṣṭhākāmo yajeta pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo yad atirātro bhavaty ahorātrayor eva pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: (PB 20.10.1) One desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge should sacrifice with a threefold <s>Atirātra</s>. The <s>trivṛt</s> is radiance and the splendor of sacred knowledge. He attains radiance and the splendor of sacred knowledge. He becomes established in radiance and the splendor of sacred knowledge. One desiring vigor should sacrifice with a fifteenfold <s>Atirātra</s>. Might and vigor are the <s>pañcadaśa</s>. He attains might and vigor. He becomes established in might and vigor. One desiring food-eating should sacrifice with a seventeenfold <s>Atirātra</s>. Food is the <s>saptadaśa</s>. He attains food-eating. One desiring an establishment should sacrifice with a twenty-onefold <s>Atirātra</s>. Establishment is the <s>ekaviṃśa</s>. Since it is an <s>Atirātra</s>, he becomes established in day and night.

body.text:
(PB 20.11.1) jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātra uttaram
(PB 20.11.2) tasya caturviṃśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ pañadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāna ekaviṃśāni pṛṣṭhāni triṇava ārbhavas trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamam athaikaviṃśam atha saptadaśam ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.11.3) aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs teṣāṃ haviṣmāṃś ca haviṣkṛc cāṅgirasāv ahīyetā tāv āgacchetāṃ yato 'ṅgirasaḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tāv atapyetāṃ tāv ete sāmanī apaśyatāṃ tābhyāṃ dvirātram atanvātāṃ tena svargaṃ lokam aitām
(PB 20.11.4) yaḥ pauṇyo hīna iva syāt sa etena yajetāpnoti pūrveṣāṃ prahām āpnutāṃ hi tāv aṅgirasaḥ
(PB 20.11.5) prajākāmo yajeta dvitīyaṃ hy etad yat prajāḥ
(PB 20.11.6) svargakāmo yajeta dvitīyād dhi lokāt paro loko 'bhiprakramyo durādho dvirātra ity āhur yad agniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavaty ukthyam antaryanti yady ukthyo 'gniṣṭomam
(PB 20.11.7) yaj jyotir ukthyaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavati nāgniṣṭomam antaryanti nokthāni
(PB 20.11.8) tad āhur eṣā vāva yajñasya mātrā yad agniṣṭomo yad agniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavati yajñasya mātrāṃ nātikrāmaty athottarasyāhna ukthebhyo 'dhi rātrim upayanti tenokthāny anantaritāni
(PB 20.11.9) caturviṃśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ bhavaty uttarasyāhnaś caturviṃśaty akṣarā gāyatrī prajananaṃ gāyatrī prajātyai
(PB 20.11.10) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tan mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
(PB 20.11.11) sarvastomo 'tirātro bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvam evaitenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.11.1) The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [has] the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> as the first day and the <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s> as the second.
(PB 20.11.2) Its <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> [has the stoma of] twenty-four; the <s>Ājyas</s> [have the stoma of] fifteen; the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> [has the stoma of] seventeen; the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> [have the stoma of] twenty-one; the <s>Ārbhavas</s> [have the stoma of] thrice-nine; the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [hymn has the stoma of] thirty-three; the <s>Pratyavarohīṇī</s> <s>Uktha</s> hymns [have the stoma of] thrice-nine for the first, then twenty-one, then seventeen; the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> [has the stoma of] twenty-one; the night [has the stoma of] fifteen; the <s>Sandhi</s> (junction) [has the stoma of] thrice-three.
(PB 20.11.3) The <s>Aṅgirasas</s> went to the heavenly world. Of them, <s>Haviṣmān</s> and <s>Haviṣkṛt</s>, two <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, were left behind. They would arrive from where the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> went to the heavenly world. Those two performed austerities. They saw these two <s>Sāmans</s>. With those two they extended the two-day [rite]. By that they went to the heavenly world.
(PB 20.11.4) He who, though meritorious, is as if inferior — let him sacrifice with this. He attains the [same] achievement of his predecessors, for those two <s>Aṅgirasas</s> attained [it].
(PB 20.11.5) One desiring offspring should sacrifice [with this], for offspring is the second [goal].
(PB 20.11.6) One desiring heaven should sacrifice [with this], for from the second [day], the higher world is to be attained. 'Difficult to reach is the two-day [rite],' they say. When the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day, they insert an <s>Ukthya</s>; [but] if the <s>Ukthya</s> [is first], [they insert] an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
(PB 20.11.7) In that <s>Jyotis</s> [form], the <s>Ukthya</s> is the first day — they do not insert an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, nor the <s>Uktha</s> hymns.
(PB 20.11.8) Regarding this they say: 'The measure of the sacrifice is indeed the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. When the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day, one does not transgress the measure of the sacrifice. And on the second day, they go from the <s>Uktha</s> hymns into the night — thus the <s>Uktha</s> hymns are uninterrupted.'
(PB 20.11.9) The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> of the second day has [the stoma of] twenty-four. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is procreation — for the sake of progeny.
(PB 20.11.10) Both types of <s>stomas</s> (praise-modes) are even and odd — that is a pair (<s>mithuna</s>). Therefore, from the pair, [offspring] is produced.
(PB 20.11.11) The <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s> is [employed] for the attainment of all, for the conquest of all. By this one indeed attains all, conquers all.

body.text:
(PB 20.12.1) atha yasya jyotir ukthyaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavaty āyur atirātra uttaram
(PB 20.12.2) tisraḥ pūrvasyāhno virājam atiricyante dvābhyām uttaram ahar virāja ūnam ūnātiriktaṃ vā anuprajāḥ prajāyante
(PB 20.12.3) pra prajayā pra paśubhir jāyate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 20.12.4) ekā saṃstutānāṃ virājam atiricyate ekākinam evainam annādyasyādhyakṣaṃ karoti
(PB 20.12.5) etena vai citrarathaṃ kāpeyā ayājayaṃs tam ekākinam annādyasyādhyakṣam akurvaṃs tasmāc caitrarathīnām ekaḥ kṣatrapatir jāyate 'nulamba iva dvitīyaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.12.1) Now [in that form] where the <s>Jyotis Ukthya</s> is the first day and the <s>Āyus Atirātra</s> the second.
(PB 20.12.2) Three <s>Virāj</s> [hymns] exceed on the first day; by two, the second day is deficient in <s>Virāj</s>. [Through] the deficient and the excessive, offspring is produced without interruption.
(PB 20.12.3) With the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [stomas] they make the second day procreate. What is thus procreated, they take up the next [day]. In wheels, indeed, these are joined —
(PB 20.12.4) — like the hub in the wheel of a chariot, firmly fixed. [In] this two-day [rite], one who knows this is firmly established.
(PB 20.12.5) The <s>Āyus</s> [form of the] <s>Atirātra</s> is the second [day] — the <s>Atirātra</s> is life-force (<s>āyus</s>); verily he places life-force in himself.
(PB 20.12.6) The <s>stomas</s> (praise-modes) should be arrayed in the manner of increasing extension, or in the manner of decreasing extension. The one extending has life-span; the one decreasing has offspring. 'Both indeed should be employed,' — so they say — 'for both purposes are fulfilled.'

body.text:
(PB 20.13.1) atha yasya trivṛt pañcadaśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavaty āyur atirātra uttaram
(PB 20.13.2) mithunābhyāṃ stomābhyām uttaram ahaḥ prajanayanti tat prajātaṃ śva ārabhante cakre vā ete sākaṃvṛtī yat trivṛt pañcadaśau stomau yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam etenābhyaśnute yatra yatra hi cakrīvatā kāmayate tat tad abhyaśnute
(PB 20.13.3) atha yad āyur atirātro bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 20.13.4) etena vai kapivano bhauvāyana iṣṭvārūkṣatām agacchat
(PB 20.13.5) arūkṣo bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān etena yajate
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.13.1) Now [in that form] where the <s>Trivṛt-Pañcadaśa Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day and the <s>Āyus Atirātra</s> the second.
(PB 20.13.2) With the paired <s>stomas</s>, they cause the second day to procreate. What is thus procreated, they take up the next [day]. In wheels, indeed, these are joined — like a chariot. He who knows the chariot [of this rite] is not cut off [from the heavenly world].
(PB 20.13.3) This two-day [rite] is for one who fears being excluded. Verily he joins [himself] with it. By the joined one, he goes to the heavenly world.
(PB 20.13.4) One who has been excluded [from the ritual community] should sacrifice [with this], for re-inclusion. For the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, who had been excluded, went [to heaven] by means of this.
(PB 20.13.5) He whose sacrifice has been interrupted should sacrifice [with this]; for [it is like] hitching [the oxen] again. The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is indeed the beginning of the sacrifice. Having begun again with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, he completes [it] with the <s>Atirātra</s>. The <s>Atirātra</s> is the completion of the sacrifice.
(PB 20.13.6) The <s>Trivṛt</s> is the thunderbolt. With the <s>Trivṛt</s> as a thunderbolt, he strikes down the enemies. The <s>Pañcadaśa</s> is vigor (<s>indriya</s>). He places vigor in himself. The <s>Saptadaśa</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>. From <s>Prajāpati</s>, offspring is produced.

body.text:
(PB 20.14.1) trivṛt prātaḥsavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saptadaśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ saptadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam ekaviṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ soktham ekaviṃśaṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ triṇavaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ trayastriṃśa ārbhavaś catustriṃśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśāny ukthāni saṣoḍaśikāni ṣoḍaśaṃ prathamaṃ rātriṣāma pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 20.14.2) prajāpatir vā idam eka āsīt tasya vāg eva svam āsīd vāg dvitīyā sa aikṣatemām eva vācaṃ visṛjā iyaṃ vā idaṃ sarvaṃ vibhavanty eṣyatīti sa vācaṃ vyasṛjata sedaṃ sarvaṃ vibhavanty ait sordhvodātanod yathāpāṃ dhārā santataivaṃ tasyā eti tṛtīyam acchinat tad bhūmir abhavad abhūd iva vā idam iti tad bhūmer bhūmitvaṃ keti tṛtīyam acchinat tad antarikṣam abhavad antar eva vā idam iti tad antarikṣasyāntarikṣatvaṃ ho iti tṛtīyam ūrdhvam udāsyat tat dyaur abhavad adyutad iva vā iti tad divo divatvam
(PB 20.14.3) eṣā vāva pratyakṣaṃ vāg yaj jihvāgreṇaitad vāco vadati yad eti madhyenaitad vāco vadati yat keti sarvayaitad vāco raso 'dhyūrdhva udvad ati yaddho iti
(PB 20.14.4) yad etāni rūpāṇy anvahaṃ vyajyante mukhata eva tad vācaṃ visṛjante mukhato yajñiyaṃ karma
(PB 20.14.5) prajāpatir vā idam ekākṣarāṃ vācaṃ satīṃ tredhā vyakarot ta ime lokā abhavan rūkṣā anupajīvanāḥ sa aikṣata katham ime lokā loma gṛhṇīyuḥ katham upajīvanīyāḥ syur iti sa etaṃ trirātram apaśyat tam āharat tenemān lokān anvātanot tato vā ime lokā lomāgṛhṇaṃs tata upajīvanīyā abhavaṃs trirātrasya vā idaṃ puṣṭaṃ trirātrasyodaraṇaṃ yad idam eṣu lokeṣv adhi
(PB 20.14.6) gacchati paśūnāṃ bhūmānaṃ dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ya evaṃ veda
(PB 20.14.7) prajāpatir yad vācaṃ vyasṛjata sākṣarad eveti prathamaṃ kṣeti dvitīyaṃ reti tṛtīyaṃ yena yena vai rūpeṇa prajāpatir vācaṃ vyasṛjata tena tena rūpeṇājyāni cārabhyante 'hāni cāpyante
(PB 20.13.8) tad āhur brahmavādino 'kṣarestho vai trirātra ity ekākṣarā vai vāk tryakṣaram akṣaraṃ tryakṣaraḥ puruṣaḥ sa vā enaṃ vedety āhur ya enaṃ puruṣasammitaṃ vedeti
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.14.1) [The stoma is:] <s>Trivṛt</s> for the morning pressing, <s>Pañcadaśa</s> for the midday pressing, <s>Saptadaśa</s> for the third pressing; [alternatively:] <s>Pañcadaśa</s> for the morning pressing, <s>Saptadaśa</s> for the midday pressing, <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> for the third pressing — [thus] with [the addition of] an <s>Uktha</s>; [alternatively:] <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> for the morning pressing, <s>Triṇava</s> for the midday pressing, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> for the third pressing — [thus] with [the addition of] an <s>Uktha</s>.
(PB 20.14.2) In each case one should press [the Soma] in the extended form. For the one who extends has life-span. Whoever, knowing thus, sacrifices with the two-day [rite] goes to the heavenly world.
(PB 20.14.3) He who desires: 'May I be established among my own people' should sacrifice [with this]. For this [rite establishes one]. The <s>Trivṛt</s> is this world; the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> is the atmosphere; the <s>Saptadaśa</s> is the world beyond. Having encompassed these three worlds, he becomes established among his own people.
(PB 20.14.4) <s>Prajāpati</s> created the sacrifice. Having created it, he did not find a completion for it. He saw this <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s>. By that he brought the sacrifice to completion. Hence, whoever concludes [with] the <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s> indeed brings his sacrifice to completion.

body.text:
(PB 20.15.1) etena vai devā eṣu lokeṣv ārdhnuvann etena svargaṃ lokamāyan
(PB 20.15.2) vāg vai trirātro vāco rūpeṇājyāni cāhāni ca vibhajyanta ekākṣarā vai vāk tryakṣaram akṣaram akṣarasya rūpeṇa vibhajyante trayo gandharvās teṣām eṣā bhaktir agneḥ pṛthivī vāyor antarikṣam asāv ādityasya dyaus trayo gharmāsa uṣasaṃ sacante
(PB 20.15.3) agnir uṣasaṃ sacate vāyur uṣasaṃ sacate 'sāv āditya uṣasaṃ sacate
(PB 20.15.4) trīṇi mithunāni tāny eṣaḥ
(PB 20.15.5) mithunaṃ dve sambhavato mithunād yat prajāyate tat tṛtīyam
(PB 20.15.6) indro vṛtrāya vajram udayacchat so 'bravīn mā me praharṣīr asti vā idaṃ mayi vīryaṃ tat te pradāsyāmīti tad asmai prāyacchat tad viṣṇuḥ pratyagṛhṇāt sa dvitīyaṃ sa tṛtīyam udayacchat sa evābravīn mā me prahārṣīr asti vā idaṃ mayi vīryaṃ tat te pradāsyāmīti tad asmai prāyacchat tad viṣṇuḥ pratyagṛhṇād etad vāca tad abhyanūcyate
(PB 20.15.7) ubhau jigyathur na parājayethe na parājigye kataraś ca nainoḥ indraś ca viṣṇo yad apaspṛdhethāṃ tredhā sahasraṃ vitad (?) airayethām iti
(PB 20.15.8) etad vā ābhyāṃ tat sahasraṃ prāyacchat
(PB 20.15.9) tasyaiṣā bhaktir ya ārṣeyo vidvāṃs tasmai prathame 'hani deyaṃ yathā vā iyaṃ evaṃ sa pratiṣṭhiteyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ saḥ
(PB 20.15.10) yo 'nārṣeyo vidvāṃs tasmai dvitīye 'hani deyaṃ yathā vā antarikṣam evaṃ so 'ntarikṣam ity antarikṣaṃ vidur vedaṃ tasya viduḥ
(PB 20.15.11) ya ārṣeyo vidvāṃs tasmai tṛtīye 'hani deyaṃ yathā vai dyaur evaṃ sa dyaur iti divaṃ vidur bandhu tasya viduḥ
(PB 20.15.12) śatāny anvahaṃ dīyante eṣā vāva yajñasya mātrā yac chataṃ saiva sāvicchinnā dīyate daśato 'nvahaṃ dīyante daśākṣarā virāḍ vairājo yajñaḥ saiva sā vicchinnā dīyate
(PB 20.15.13) trayastriṃśac ca trīṇi ca śatāni prathame 'hani deyās tathā dvitīye tathā tṛtīye
(PB 20.15.14) athaiṣā dvidevatyā trirūpā brahmaṇo dve tṛtīye tṛtīyam agnīdhaḥ
(PB 20.15.15) kāmyāsi priyāsi havyāsīḍe rante sarasvati mahi viśruta etāni te 'ghnye nāmāni deveṣu naḥ sukṛto brūtāt
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.15.1) By this indeed the gods prospered in these worlds; by this they went to the heavenly world.
(PB 20.15.2) Speech indeed is the three-night [rite]. By the form of speech, the <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblations) and the days are distributed. Speech is one-syllabled; three-syllabled is the syllable; by the form of the syllable they are distributed. Three are the <s>Gandharvas</s>; this is their share: of <s>Agni</s> — the earth; of <s>Vāyu</s> — the atmosphere; of that <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) — heaven. Three hot-milk vessels (<s>gharma</s>) attend upon <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn).
(PB 20.15.3) <s>Agni</s> attends upon <s>Uṣas</s>; <s>Vāyu</s> attends upon <s>Uṣas</s>; that <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) attends upon <s>Uṣas</s>.
(PB 20.15.4) Three are the pairs — these are they.
(PB 20.15.5) A pair: two come together; what is born from a pair, that is the third.
(PB 20.15.6) <s>Indra</s> raised his thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) against <s>Vṛtra</s>. He [<s>Vṛtra</s>] said: 'Do not strike me! There is indeed this power in me; I shall give it to you.' He gave it to him; <s>Viṣṇu</s> received it. He raised [the thunderbolt] a second time, a third time. He [<s>Vṛtra</s>] said the same: 'Do not strike me! There is indeed this power in me; I shall give it to you.' He gave it to him; <s>Viṣṇu</s> received it. This is recited as a <s>vāca</s> (speech) [formula].
(PB 20.15.7) 'Both of you conquered, neither was defeated; neither of these two was defeated — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when you two contended, you distributed the thousand in three parts.'
(PB 20.15.8) That thousand was given to those two.
(PB 20.15.9) This is its distribution: to one who is of <s>ṛṣi</s>-lineage (<s>ārṣeya</s>) and learned, to him the gift should be given on the first day. Just as this [earth] is, so is he established; this [earth] is established, and so is he.
(PB 20.15.10) To one who is not of <s>ṛṣi</s>-lineage but is learned, to him the gift should be given on the second day. Just as the atmosphere is, so is he; they know him as 'atmosphere'; they know the connection of that [person to the Veda].
(PB 20.15.11) To one who is of <s>ṛṣi</s>-lineage and learned, to him the gift should be given on the third day. Just as heaven is, so is he; they know him as 'heaven'; they know his kinship.
(PB 20.15.12) Hundreds are given each day — this indeed is the measure (<s>mātrā</s>) of the sacrifice, which is a hundred; that same [measure] is given divided. Tens are given each day; the <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; the sacrifice is of the <s>Virāj</s>; that same [measure] is given divided.
(PB 20.15.13) Three hundred and thirty-three should be given on the first day; likewise on the second; likewise on the third.
(PB 20.15.14) Now this [formula] has two deities and three forms: two-thirds belong to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], one-third to the <s>Agnīdh</s> (fire-kindler).
(PB 20.15.15) 'You are desirable, you are dear, you are the oblation-bearer; O <s>Iḍā</s>, O <s>Rantī</s>, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, great and renowned — these are your names, O unslayable one; among the gods, speak well of us, the doers of good deeds.'

body.text:
(PB 20.16.1) idaṃ vāva prathamenāhnā vyakarod yad idam asyām adhyāyat ta mūlam idaṃ dvitīyena yad idaṃ prāṇād ejaty adas tṛtīyena yad varṣati yan nakṣatrāṇi yad amuṃ lokaṃ bheje
(PB 20.16.2) tad āhur brahmavādino mahāvrataṃ vā etad yad eṣa trirātra iti tasyai tad eva mukhaṃ yad eteṣām ahvāṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ ye abhito 'hanī tau pakṣau yan madhyamam ahaḥ sa ātmāgniṣṭomasāmāni puccham
(PB 20.16.3) yad evāsāv udeti tan mukhaṃ ye abhito 'hanī tau pakṣau yan madhyamam ahaḥ sa ātmāgniḥ puccham
(PB 20.16.4) yad evāsāv udeti tan mukhaṃ ye abhito 'hanī tau pakṣau yan madhyamam ahaḥ sa ātmā yad astam eti tat puccham
(PB 20.16.5) etāvān vāva trirātro gāyatraḥ prāṇas traiṣṭubhaṃ cakṣur jāgataṃ śrotraṃ sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda
(PB 20.16.6) tad āhur brahmavādinaḥ kiyāṃs trirātra itīyān iti brūyād iyaddhayetad abhy atho iyān iti brūyād iyaddhayevaitad abhiparā3ṅ arvā3ṅ ity āhuḥ parāṅ iti brūyāt parāṅ hi vadati parāṅ paśyati parāṅ prāṇity ekā3 dvā3 u trayā3 ity āhur eka iti brūyāt samāno hy eṣa yat prāṇo 'pāno vyānas tad yathā vā ado maṇau sūtram otam evam eṣu lokeṣu trirātra otaḥ śobhate 'sya mukhaṃ ya evaṃ veda
(PB 20.16.7) yad vai trirātrasya saloma tad asya viloma yad asya viloma tad asya saloma tad yad etat paraṃ sad ahar avaraṃ kriyate yajamānāyaiva tat paśūn parigṛhṇāti prajananāya na hy amuṣmin loke paśavaḥ prajāyante
(PB 20.16.8) ete vāva chandasāṃ vīryavattame yad gāyatrī ca triṣṭup ca yad ete abhito bhavato madhye jagatī vīryavatībhyām eva tac chandobhyāṃ paśūn parigṛhṇāti prajananāya na hy amuṣmin loke paśavaḥ prajāyante
(PB 20.16.9) asau vāva trirātro yathodety evaṃ prathamam ahar yathā madhyandina evaṃ dvitīyaṃ yathāstam ety evaṃ tṛtīyaṃ gacchaty amuṣyasāyujyaṃ gacchati sāveśyaṃ ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 20.16.1) By the first day he created this [world] — whatever rests upon this [earth]; that is the root. By the second, whatever moves from breath. By the third, whatever rains, whatever the constellations are, whatever attained that [heavenly] world.
(PB 20.16.2) The expounders of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'This three-night [rite] is indeed the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great vow).' Its mouth is the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> (external purification chant) of these days; the two days on either side are the two wings; the middle day is the body (<s>ātman</s>); the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> chants are the tail.
(PB 20.16.3) When that [sun] rises, that is the mouth; the two days on either side are the two wings; the middle day is the body; <s>Agni</s> is the tail.
(PB 20.16.4) When that [sun] rises, that is the mouth; the two days on either side are the two wings; the middle day is the body; when it sets, that is the tail.
(PB 20.16.5) The three-night [rite] is just this much: <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is the eye, <s>Jagatī</s> is the ear. One who knows this attains the full span of life.
(PB 20.16.6) The expounders of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'How great is the three-night [rite]?' One should say 'this much,' for this indeed is this much. Or one should say 'this much,' for this indeed is this much. 'Facing away, facing towards' — they say. One should say 'facing away,' for he speaks facing away, he sees facing away, he breathes facing away. 'One, two, or three' — they say. One should say 'one,' for this is the same — what is <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath), <s>apāna</s> (out-breath), and <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath). Just as a thread is woven into a jewel, so the three-night [rite] is woven into these worlds. His face shines who knows this.
(PB 20.16.7) That which is 'with the hair' of the three-night [rite], that is its 'against the hair'; that which is its 'against the hair,' that is its 'with the hair.' When this further day is made the nearer, that secures cattle for the sacrificer for the sake of procreation, for cattle are not born in the other world.
(PB 20.16.8) These indeed are the most powerful among the meters — the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. When these are on both sides, with the <s>Jagatī</s> in the middle, then by these two most powerful meters he secures cattle for the sake of procreation, for cattle are not born in the other world.
(PB 20.16.9) That [sun] indeed is the three-night [rite]. As it rises, so is the first day; as it is at midday, so is the second; as it sets, so is the third. One who knows this attains union with that [sun], attains co-residence [with it].

body.text:
(PB 21.1.1) indro marutaḥ sahasram ajināt svāṃ viśaṃ somāya rājñe procya tasmād rājñe procya viṃśa jinanti tau yamo 'śṛṇon maruto ha sahasram ajyāśiṣṭām iti sa āgacchat so 'bravīd upa māsmin sahasre hvayethām iti tam upāhvayetāṃ sa yamo 'paśyad ekāṅgāṃ sahasre 'pi sahasrasya payo bibhratīṃ so 'bravīd iyam eva mamāstu sahasraṃ yuvāṃ vikalpayethām iti tāv abrūtāṃ yathā vāva tvam etāṃ paśyasy evam āvam etāṃ paśyāva iti
(PB 21.1.2) tayā vā idaṃ sahasraṃ vikalpayāmahā ity abruvaṃs tām udake prāveśayaṃs te 'bravan na śānāharāmahai yasmai na iyaṃ prathamāyādeṣyati iti te 'ṃśān āharanta somasya prathama aid athendrasyātha yamasya
(PB 21.1.3) te 'bruvan somāya rājña udehi tṛtīyena cātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasa iti sā babhruḥ piṅgākṣy ekavarṣodait tṛtīyena cātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasaḥ sā yā somakrayaṇī saiva sā
(PB 21.1.4) tṛtīyena cāsya tasyā ātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasaḥ somaḥ krīto bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān somaṃ krīṇāti yasmā evaṃ viduṣe somaṃ krīṇanti
(PB 21.1.5) te 'bruvann indrāyodehi tṛtīyena cātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasa iti sā śabalī paṣṭhauhy udait tṛtīyena cātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasaḥ sā %yendriyaiṣyā saiva sā
(PB 21.1.6) tṛtīyena cāsya tasyā ātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasa indriyaiṣyā dattā bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān indriyaiṣyāṃ dadāti yasmā evaṃ viduṣa indriyaiṣyāṃ dadāti
(PB 21.1.7) te 'bruvan yamāyodehi tṛtīyena cātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasa iti sā jaratī kuṣṭhāśṛṅgyad aid dhūmrā vā dityauhīrmato hrasīyasī tṛtīyena cātmanaḥ tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payasaḥ sā yānustaraṇī saiva sā
(PB 21.1.8) tṛtīyena cāsya tasyā ātmanas tṛtīyena ca sahasrasya payaso 'nustaraṇī kṛtā bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān anustaraṇīṃ karoti yasmā evaṃ viduṣe 'nustaraṇīṃ kurvanti nācakṛvān manyate
(PB 21.1.9) tad āhur brahmavādino na vā amuṣmin loke sahasrayāḍ aloko 'stīti tad yāvad itaḥ sahasrasya gaur gavi pratiṣṭhitā tāvad asmāl lokād asau lokaḥ sarasrayājī vā imān lokān vyāpnoty atho yāvat sahasraṃ yojanāny atho sahasram āśvīnān yatho yāvat sahasram ahnayāni tad gavā gavā spṛṇoti samākramaṇāya vā etā dīyante
(PB 21.1.10) sahasraṃ yad asṛjata tasya tārpyaṃ yonir āsīd yat tārpyaṃ pratyasya nayati sayonitvāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.1.1) <s>Indra</s> won a thousand [cows] from the <s>Maruts</s>, having declared them to King <s>Soma</s> for his own people. Therefore, having declared [cows] to a king, they win the people. <s>Yama</s> heard of this: 'The <s>Maruts</s> have had a thousand won from them.' He came and said: 'Invite me to share in this thousand.' They invited him. <s>Yama</s> saw among the thousand [cows] one cow (<s>ekāṅgā</s>) bearing the milk of a thousand. He said: 'Let this one be mine; you two divide the thousand [among yourselves].' They said: 'Just as you see this one, so we too see this one.'
(PB 21.1.2) 'By her let us divide this thousand,' they said. They immersed her in water. They said: 'We shall not bring shares; to whomever she will come first [when she emerges].' They brought shares — <s>Soma's</s> first, then <s>Indra's</s>, then <s>Yama's</s>.
(PB 21.1.3) They said: 'Rise up for King <s>Soma</s>, with a third of yourself and a third of the milk of the thousand.' She rose up — tawny, yellow-eyed, one year old — with a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand. She who is the cow for purchasing <s>Soma</s> (<s>somakrayaṇī</s>) — she is that one.
(PB 21.1.4) With a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand, <s>Soma</s> is bought. One who, knowing this, buys <s>Soma</s>, or for whom, knowing this, they buy <s>Soma</s> —
(PB 21.1.5) They said: 'Rise up for <s>Indra</s>, with a third of yourself and a third of the milk of the thousand.' She rose up — speckled, with humps on her back — with a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand. She who is the [cow] for seeking <s>Indra's</s> power (<s>indriyaiṣyā</s>) — she is that one.
(PB 21.1.6) With a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand, the [cow] for seeking <s>Indra's</s> power is given. One who, knowing this, gives the cow for seeking <s>Indra's</s> power, or to whom, knowing this, they give the cow for seeking <s>Indra's</s> power —
(PB 21.1.7) They said: 'Rise up for <s>Yama</s>, with a third of yourself and a third of the milk of the thousand.' She rose up — old, with broken horns, smoky-colored, or a piebald cow, shorter [than the others] — with a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand.
