She who is the cow for covering [the dead] (<s>anustaraṇī</s>) — she is that one.
(PB 21.1.8) With a third of herself and a third of the milk of the thousand, the covering-cow is made. One who, knowing this, makes the covering-cow, or for whom, knowing this, they make the covering-cow — he does not think [he has committed an offense].
(PB 21.1.9) The expounders of <s>Brahman</s> say: 'In the other world there is no abode for one who performs the thousand-[cow sacrifice].' But as far as from here a cow of the thousand is established upon cow, so far is the other world from this world. The performer of the thousand-[cow sacrifice] pervades these worlds. Also, as far as a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, also a thousand horse-stages, and as far as a thousand day-journeys — that he spans cow by cow. For [cows] are given for the purpose of crossing over.
(PB 21.1.10) When he created the thousand, its source was <s>Tārpya</s>. When he brings back the <s>Tārpya</s>, it is for the sake of [returning to] the source.

body.text:
(PB 21.2.1) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā asmāt sṛṣṭāḥ parācya āyan natsyati na iti bibhyatyaḥ so 'bravīd upa mā vartadhvaṃ tathā vai vo 'tsyāmi yathādyamānā bhūyasyaḥ prajaniṣyatha iti tābhyo vainaṃ ṛtaṃ brūhīty abruvaṃs tābhya ṛtanidhanenartam abravīd īnidhanenāvayat triṇidhanena prājanayad etair ha vā idaṃ sāmabhir mṛtyuḥ prajā atti ca prajanayati
(PB 21.2.2) adyamānasya bhūyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.2.3) jyeṣṭhasāmāni vā etāni śreṣṭhasāmāni prajāpatisāmāni
(PB 21.2.4) gacchati jyaiṣṭhayaṃ śraiṣṭhayaṃ ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.2.5) etair vai sāmabhiḥ prajāpatir imān lokān sarvān kāmān dugdhe yad ācyā dugdhe tad ācyā dohānām ācyā dohatvam
(PB 21.2.6) sarvān imān lokān kāmān dugdhe ya evaṃ vidvān etais sāmabhiḥ stute
(PB 21.2.7) ime vai lokā etāni sāmāny ayam evartanidhanam antarikṣam īnidhanaṃ dyaus triṇidhanam
(PB 21.2.8) yathā kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrāṇy anusañcaraty evam imān lokān anusañcarati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.2.9) agner vā etāni vaiśvānarasya sāmāni yatra vā etair aśāntaiḥ stuvanti tat prajā devo ghātuko bhavaty agnim upanidhāya stuvate svāyā eva tad devatāyāḥ sāmyekṣāya namaskṛtyodgāyati śāntais stuvanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.2.1) <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Once created, they went away from him, fearing 'He will eat us, he will eat us.' He said: 'Come back to me. I will eat you in such a way that, being eaten, you will become more and procreate.' They said: 'Tell us the truth about this.' He told them the truth with the <s>ṛta</s>-ending (truth-ending); he ate them with the <s>ī</s>-ending; he made them procreate with the <s>triṇi</s>-ending. With these <s>sāmans</s> indeed, Death eats creatures and makes them procreate.
(PB 21.2.2) He who is eaten becomes more, who knows thus.
(PB 21.2.3) These are the eldest <s>sāmans</s>, the best <s>sāmans</s>, the <s>sāmans</s> of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 21.2.4) He attains seniority and excellence who knows thus.
(PB 21.2.5) With these <s>sāmans</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> milks all desires from these worlds. What he milks by milking — that is the milking-nature of the <s>ācyā</s> (milking) chants.
(PB 21.2.6) He milks all desires from these worlds who, knowing thus, has these <s>sāmans</s> praised.
(PB 21.2.7) These worlds are these <s>sāmans</s>: this world is the <s>ṛta</s>-ending, the atmosphere is the <s>ī</s>-ending, heaven is the <s>triṇi</s>-ending.
(PB 21.2.8) Just as a field-knower traverses his fields, so he traverses these worlds who knows thus.
(PB 21.2.9) These are the <s>sāmans</s> of <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>. Where they praise with these unpacified, there the divine one becomes a slayer of creatures. They praise having placed fire nearby — for the sake of being in harmony with one's own deity. He chants having made obeisance. They praise with the pacified forms.

body.text:
(PB 21.3.1) vāg vai śabalī tasyās trirātro vatsas trirātro vā etāṃ pradāpayati
(PB 21.3.2) tad ya evaṃ veda tasmā eṣā prattā dugdhe
(PB 21.3.3) yo 'lam annādyāya sann athānnaṃ nādyāt
(PB 21.3.4) barāsīṃ paridhāya taptaṃ piban dvādaśa rātrīr adhaḥ śayīta
(PB 21.3.5) yā dvādaśī syāt tasyā upavyuṣaṃ śabalīhomaṃ hutvā purā vāgbhyaḥ sampravaditor yatra grāmyasya paśor nāśṛṇuyāt tad araṇyaṃ paretya darbhastambam ālabhya śabali śabalīti trir āhvayed yad anyac chunaś ca gardabhāc ca prativāśyate sā samṛddhā
(PB 21.3.6) yadi na prativāśyeta saṃvatsare punar āhvayeta
(PB 21.3.7) śabali samudro 'si viśvavyacā brahma devānāṃ prathamajā ṛtasyānnam asi śukram asi tejo 'sy amṛtam asi tāṃ tvā vidma śabali dīdyānāṃ tasyāste pṛthivī pādo 'ntarikṣaṃ pādo dyauḥ pādaḥ samudraḥ pāda eṣāsi śabali tāṃ tvā vidma sā na iṣam ūrjaṃ dhukṣva vasordhārāṃ śabali prajānāṃ śaciṣṭhā vratam anugeṣaṃ svāhā
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.3.1) Speech is indeed the speckled cow (<s>Śabalī</s>). The three-night rite is her calf. The three-night rite makes her yield milk.
(PB 21.3.2) He who knows thus — for him she, when given, yields milk.
(PB 21.3.3) He who, though capable of eating food, does not eat food:
(PB 21.3.4) He should put on a rough garment, drink hot liquid, and sleep on the ground for twelve nights.
(PB 21.3.5) On the twelfth night, before dawn, having offered the <s>Śabalī</s> oblation, before voices begin to speak, where one does not hear domestic animals — having gone to such a wilderness, grasping a clump of <s>darbha</s> grass, he should call three times: '<s>Śabalī</s>! <s>Śabalī</s>!' If anything other than a dog or a donkey calls back, it is accomplished.
(PB 21.3.6) If nothing calls back, he should call again after a year.
(PB 21.3.7) '<s>Śabalī</s>, you are the ocean, all-pervading, the first-born of <s>Brahman</s> among the <s>devas</s>, of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order). You are food, you are brightness, you are brilliance, you are immortality. We know you, <s>Śabalī</s>, the shining one. The earth is your one foot, the atmosphere your one foot, heaven your one foot, the ocean your one foot. You are this, <s>Śabalī</s>. We know you. Yield us nourishment and vigor, the stream of wealth, O <s>Śabalī</s>, most powerful among creatures. I follow the vow. <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text:
(PB 21.4.1) catuṣṭomo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśa ukthyaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 21.4.2) prajāpater vā akṣy aśvat tat parāpatat tad aśvo 'bhavat tad aśvasyāśvatvaṃ tad devā aśvamedhena pratyadadhur eṣa vāva prajāpatiṃ sarvaṃ karoti yo 'śvamedhena yajate
(PB 21.4.3) eṣa vāva saśarīraḥ sambhavaty amuṣmai lokāyayo 'śvamedhī
(PB 21.4.4) saraghā vā aśvasya sakthy āvṛhat tad devāś catuṣṭomena pratyadadhur yac catuṣṭomo bhavaty aśvasya sarvatvāya
(PB 21.4.5) yat tisro 'nuṣṭubhaś catasro gāyatrīḥ karoti tasmāt tribhis tiṣṭhan pratitiṣṭhati sarvān palāyamānaḥ pratidadhāti
(PB 21.4.6) anto vā aśvaḥ paśūnām anto 'nuṣṭup chandasām anto viṣṇur devatānām antaś catuṣṭomas stomānām antas trirātro yajñānāṃ yad vaiplavyo 'nuṣṭubhaḥ pratipado bhavanti catuṣṭoma stomas trirātro yajño 'nta eva tadantaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
(PB 21.4.7) ekaviṃśam ahar bhavati yasminn aśva ālabhyata ekaviṃśo vā ito 'sāv ādityo dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavas traya ime lokā asāv āditya ekaviṃśa ādityasyaivainaṃ mātrāṃ gamayati
(PB 21.4.8) tasya mahānāmnyaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavanti
(PB 21.4.9) anyad-anyad vā etāś chando 'nyonya ete paśava ālabhyanta etā vā etaṃ samāpnuvanti yan mahānāmnyaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavanty aśvasya sarvatvāya
(PB 21.4.10) pārthuraśmaṃ brahmasāma bhavati
(PB 21.4.11) īśvaro vā eṣo 'yato 'dhṛtaḥ parāṃ parāvatam eto raśminā vā aśvo dhṛto yat pārthuraśmaṃ brahmasāma bhavaty aśvasyaiva yatyai
(PB 21.4.12) sarvastomo 'tirātro bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvam evaitenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati
(PB 21.4.13) ekayūpo vaikādaśinī vānyeṣāṃ yajñānāṃ bhavaty ekaviṃśiny aśvamedhasya khādiro vā bailvo vā pārṇo vā 'nyeṣāṃ yajñānāṃ bhavati naicudāra ekaviṃśatyaratnir aśvamedhasya nānyeṣāṃ paśūnāṃ tejanyā avadyanty avadyanty aśvamedhasya dakṣiṇato 'nyeṣāṃ paśūnām avadyanty uttarato 'śvamedhasya plakṣaśākhāsv anyeṣāṃ paśūnām avadyanti vetasaśākhāsv aśvamedhasya yūpe grāmyān paśūn niyuñjanty ārokeṣv āraṇyān dhārayanty ā grāmyān paśūn labhante prāraṇyān sṛjanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.4.1) A four-<s>stoma</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a twenty-one-fold <s>ukthya</s>, and an all-<s>stoma</s> <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite).
(PB 21.4.2) <s>Prajāpati</s>'s eye fell out. Having fallen, it became a horse. That is the horse-nature of the horse. The <s>devas</s> restored it with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice). He who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> indeed makes <s>Prajāpati</s> whole.
(PB 21.4.3) He who performs the <s>Aśvamedha</s> goes to the other world with his body intact.
(PB 21.4.4) <s>Saraghā</s> tore out the horse's thigh. The <s>devas</s> restored it with the four-<s>stoma</s> rite. The four-<s>stoma</s> rite is for making the horse whole.
(PB 21.4.5) Because he makes three <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s> and four <s>Gāyatrīs</s>, therefore one standing on three legs stands firm and restores all that flee.
(PB 21.4.6) The horse is the end of cattle, the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the end of meters, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the end of deities, the four-<s>stoma</s> is the end of <s>stomas</s>, the three-night rite is the end of sacrifices. When the <s>Vaiplavya</s> opening verses are in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, the four-<s>stoma</s> is the <s>stoma</s>, the three-night rite is the sacrifice — thereby one establishes the end at the end.
(PB 21.4.7) The day on which the horse is immolated is the twenty-one-fold. The twenty-one-fold is the sun counted from here: twelve months, five seasons, three worlds, and yonder sun — twenty-one. Thereby one brings him to the measure of the sun.
(PB 21.4.8) The <s>Mahānāmnī</s> chants are its <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
(PB 21.4.9) Various meters, various animals are immolated. The <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> encompass all of this. When the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> are the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, it is for making the horse whole.
(PB 21.4.10) The <s>Pārthuraśma</s> is the <s>Brahma Sāman</s>.
(PB 21.4.11) The horse is liable to go loose to the farthest distance. The horse is held by a rein. When the <s>Pārthuraśma</s> is the <s>Brahma Sāman</s>, it is for restraining the horse.
(PB 21.4.12) The <s>Atirātra</s> is all-<s>stoma</s>, for obtaining all, for conquering all. With it one obtains all, conquers all.
(PB 21.4.13) Other sacrifices have one post or eleven, but the <s>Aśvamedha</s> has twenty-one. Other sacrifices use <s>Khadira</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, or <s>Pārṇa</s> wood, but the <s>Aśvamedha</s> uses <s>Naicudāra</s> (deodar) wood, twenty-one cubits for the <s>Aśvamedha</s>. Other animals' slaughtering posts have no pointed blades, but the <s>Aśvamedha</s>'s does. Other animals are slaughtered to the south, but the <s>Aśvamedha</s>'s to the north. Other animals are slaughtered on fig-tree branches, but the <s>Aśvamedha</s>'s on willow branches. At the <s>Aśvamedha</s> post they yoke domestic animals; in the wilderness they hold wild animals. They seize the domestic animals; they release the wild ones.

body.text:
(PB 21.5.1) trayas trivṛto 'tirātrāḥ sarve ṣoḍaśimantaḥ
(PB 21.5.2) yo rājya āśaṃseta sa etena yajeta
(PB 21.5.3) rājā vā eṣa stomānāṃ rājyam evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 21.5.4) yadākṣārāṇi prathamam ahar bhajanta ekākṣarā vai vāg vāco 'nativādāya
(PB 21.5.5) atha yat dvyakṣaraṇidhanam ājyadohaṃ bhavaty uttarayor ahor abhisantatyā anvaham ājyadohāni bhavanty anvaham evainaṃ paśubhiḥ samardhayanti
(PB 21.5.6) sarve ṣoḍaśimanto bhavantīndriyaṃ vīryaṃ ṣoḍaśīndriyeṇaivainān vīryeṇa samardhayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.5.1) Three nine-fold <s>Atirātra</s> rites, all with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.
(PB 21.5.2) He who aspires to kingship should sacrifice with this.
(PB 21.5.3) The nine-fold is the king of the <s>stomas</s>. Thereby one places kingship in him.
(PB 21.5.4) When one-syllable endings are distributed on the first day — speech has one syllable — it is for not surpassing speech.
(PB 21.5.5) When two-syllable endings with <s>ājyadoha</s> (ghee-milking) chants are used on the latter two days for continuity — the <s>ājyadoha</s> chants are used each day — thereby one enriches him with cattle each day.
(PB 21.5.6) All have the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. <s>Indra</s>'s power and vigor is the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. With <s>Indra</s>'s power and vigor one enriches them.

body.text:
(PB 21.6.1) caturviṃśāḥ pavamānās trivṛnty ājyāni pañcadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomaś catuścatvāriṃśāḥ pavamānāḥ pañcadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāny ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ soktho 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśāḥ pavamānā ekaviṃśāny ājyāni triṇavāni pṛṣṭhāni trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśāny ukthāni saṣoḍaśikāni pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiś chandomapavamānaḥ
(PB 21.6.2) paśukāmo yajet
(PB 21.6.3) paśavo vai chandomā yac chandomāḥ pavamānā bhavanti paśūnevāvarūndhe
(PB 21.6.4) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tat mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.6.1) Twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamānas</s>, nine-fold <s>ājya</s> chants, fifteen-fold <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants, seventeen-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; forty-four-fold <s>Pavamānas</s>, fifteen-fold <s>ājya</s> chants, seventeen-fold <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants, twenty-one-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> with <s>uktha</s>; forty-eight-fold <s>Pavamānas</s>, twenty-one-fold <s>ājya</s> chants, twenty-seven-fold (<s>triṇava</s>) <s>pṛṣṭha</s> chants, thirty-three-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, twenty-one-fold <s>ukthas</s> with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>; fifteen-fold night rite, nine-fold junction, <s>chandomā</s> <s>Pavamāna</s>.
(PB 21.6.2) One desiring cattle should sacrifice.
(PB 21.6.3) Cattle are the <s>chandomā</s> days. When the <s>chandomā</s> <s>Pavamānas</s> are used, one obtains cattle.
(PB 21.6.4) Both types of <s>stomas</s> — even and odd — are used. That is a pair; from the pair one procreates.

body.text:
(PB 21.7.1) trivṛt prātassavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saptadaśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ caturviṃśaṃ prātassavanaṃ catuścatvāriṃśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam aṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ soktham ekaviṃśaṃ prātassavanan triṇavaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ trayastriṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ soktham ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhir antarvasuḥ
(PB 21.7.2) ime lokās trirātraḥ
(PB 21.7.3) astīva vā ayaṃ loko 'stīvāsau chidram ivāntarikṣam
(PB 21.7.4) astīva trirātrasya prathamam ahar astīvottamaṃ chidram iva madhyataḥ
(PB 21.7.5) paśavo vai chandomā yac chandomā madhyato bhavanty apihityā evācchidratāyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.7.1) Nine-fold morning pressing, fifteen-fold midday pressing, seventeen-fold third pressing; twenty-four-fold morning pressing, forty-four-fold midday pressing, forty-eight-fold third pressing with <s>uktha</s>; twenty-one-fold morning pressing, twenty-seven-fold (<s>triṇava</s>) midday pressing, thirty-three-fold third pressing with <s>uktha</s>; twenty-one-fold <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, fifteen-fold night rite, nine-fold junction, <s>Antarvasuḥ</s>.
(PB 21.7.2) These worlds are the three-night rite.
(PB 21.7.3) This world is as if solid, that world is as if solid; the atmosphere is as if perforated.
(PB 21.7.4) The first day of the three-night rite is as if solid, the last is as if solid; the middle is as if perforated.
(PB 21.7.5) Cattle are the <s>chandomā</s> days. When <s>chandomā</s> days are in the middle, it is for blocking up, for imperforability.

body.text:
(PB 21.8.1) trivṛt prātassavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saptadaśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ ekaviṃśaṃ prātassavanaṃ triṇavaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ trayastriṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ sokthaṃ caturviṃśaṃ prātassavanaṃ catuścatvāriṃśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam aṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ soktham ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ parākaḥ
(PB 21.8.2) parākeṇa vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokamāyan svargakāmo yajeta parāṅ evaitena svargaṃ lokam ākramate
(PB 21.8.3) yad vā etasyākaṃ tad asya parāk tat parākasya parākatvam
(PB 21.8.4) na vai tatra jagmuṣe kiñcanā'kam
(PB 21.8.5) nāsmā akaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.8.6) prajāyās tv akḷptaḥ parāṅ hy evaitena svargaṃ lokam ākramate tad yad ekaviṃśaḥ ṣoḍaśī bhavati pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhis tenāsmin loke pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 21.9.1) caturviṃśāḥ pavamānās trivṛnty ājyāni pañcadaśāni pṛṣṭhāni saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomaś caturviṃśāḥ pavamānāḥ pañcadaśāny ājyāni saptadaśāni pṛṣṭhāny ekaviṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ sokthaś caturviṃśāḥ pavamānāḥ saptadaśāny ājyāny ekaviṃśani pṛṣṭhāni triṇavo 'gniṣṭomaḥ sokthaś caturviṃśāḥ pavamānā ekaviṃśāny ājyāni triṇavāni pṛṣṭhāni trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśāny ukthāni saṣoḍaśikāni pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhi
(PB 21.9.2) atrir akāmayata catvāro me vīrā ājāyerann iti sa etam apaśyat tasya catvāro vīrā ājāyantāsya catvāro vīrā jāyante ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.9.3) ekaṃ stomam utsṛjyaikam abhyārabhate vīrajananaṃ vai stomo vīram evāsmai tat prajanayati
(PB 21.9.4) caturviṃśāḥ pavamānā bhavanti caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī prajananaṃ gāyatrī prajātyai
(PB 21.9.5) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tan mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
(PB 21.9.6) agniṣṭomaḥ prathamam ahar ūktho dvitīyaṃ ṣoḍaśī tṛtīyam atirātraś caturthaṃ nānāvīryatāyai
(PB 21.9.7) nānāvīryāṇy ahāni karoti
(PB 21.9.8) gāyatraṃ vai prathamam ahas traiṣṭubhaṃ dvitīyaṃ jāgataṃ tṛtīyam ānuṣṭubhaṃ caturtham
(PB 21.9.9) tad āhur yat tṛtīye 'hani ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhṇīyus tṛtīyenāhnānuṣṭubham āpnuyur acchandaś caturtham ahaḥ syād ānuṣṭubho vai ṣoḍaśīti
(PB 21.9.10) caturthe 'hani ṣoḍaśī grahītavyaḥ sva āyatane ṣoḍaśī gṛhyate
(PB 21.9.11) chandobhir ahāni nānāvīryāṇi karoti
(PB 21.9.12) naudhasaṃ prathamasyāhno brahmasāma śyaitaṃ dvitīyasya śrāyantīyaṃ tṛtīyasya traiśokaṃ caturthasya
(PB 21.9.13) tad āhur apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yat jyāyasaḥ chandaso 'dhi kanīyaś chanda upaitīti
(PB 21.9.14) tadyadeṣā caturthe'hanyatijagatī kriyate'napabhraṃśāya
(PB 21.9.15) kāleyaṃ prathamasyāho 'cchāvākasāma mādhucchandasaṃ dvitīyasya rauravaṃ tṛtīyasya samantaṃ caturthasya nānāvīryatāyai nānāvīryāṇy ahāni karoti
(PB 21.9.16) ''abhitvā vṛṣabhā suta'' iti tṛtīyasyāhno rathantaraṃ ''kastam indra tvā vasava'' iti vāmadevyaṃ ''yajñā yathā apūrva'' iti caturthasyāhno bṛhat ''ed u madhor madintaram'' iti vāmadevyaṃ chandasāṃ nānāvīryatāyai nānāvīryāṇy ahāni kāroti
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.8.1) Threefold morning pressing, fifteenfold midday pressing, seventeenfold third pressing; twenty-one-fold morning pressing, <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold) midday pressing, thirty-three-fold third pressing with <s>Uktha</s>; twenty-four-fold morning pressing, forty-four-fold midday pressing, forty-eight-fold third pressing with <s>Uktha</s>; twenty-one-fold <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, fifteenfold night rite, threefold junction. This is the <s>Parāka</s> (far-going rite).
(PB 21.8.2) With the <s>Parāka</s> the gods went to the heavenly world. One desiring heaven should sacrifice with it. He directly ascends to the heavenly world with this.
(PB 21.8.3) That which is 'near' (<s>āka</s>) to it is its 'far' (<s>parāk</s>). That is the nature of the <s>Parāka</s> as 'far-going.'
(PB 21.8.4) For him who has gone there, nothing is near.
(PB 21.8.5) Nothing near exists for him who knows this.
(PB 21.8.6) But for offspring he is not prepared, for he ascends directly to the heavenly world with this. Therefore the twenty-one-fold <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, the fifteenfold night rite, and the threefold junction — with these he becomes established in this world.
(PB 21.9.1) Twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamāna</s> chants, threefold <s>Ājya</s> libations, fifteenfold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, seventeenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamāna</s> chants, fifteenfold <s>Ājya</s> libations, seventeenfold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, twenty-one-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> with <s>Uktha</s>; twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamāna</s> chants, seventeenfold <s>Ājya</s> libations, twenty-one-fold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, <s>Triṇava</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> with <s>Uktha</s>; twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamāna</s> chants, twenty-one-fold <s>Ājya</s> libations, <s>Triṇava</s> <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, thirty-three-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; twenty-one-fold <s>Uktha</s> recitations with <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, fifteenfold night rite, threefold junction.
(PB 21.9.2) <s>Atri</s> desired: 'May four heroes be born to me.' He perceived this. Four heroes were born to him. Four heroes are born to him who knows this.
(PB 21.9.3) Releasing one <s>stoma</s> and taking hold of another — the <s>stoma</s> is the generator of heroes. He generates a hero for him.
(PB 21.9.4) The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants are twenty-four-fold. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is procreation — for begetting.
(PB 21.9.5) Both kinds of <s>stomas</s> are present — even and odd. That is a pair. From that pairing he procreates.
(PB 21.9.6) <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day, <s>Uktha</s> the second, <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> the third, <s>Atirātra</s> the fourth — for the diversity of vigor.
(PB 21.9.7) He makes the days diverse in vigor.
(PB 21.9.8) The first day belongs to the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the second to the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the third to the <s>Jagatī</s>, the fourth to the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 21.9.9) On this they say: 'If they take the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> cup on the third day, they would attain the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> with the third day; the fourth day would be without meter, for the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> belongs to the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.'
(PB 21.9.10) The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> cup should be taken on the fourth day. The <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> is taken in its own place.
(PB 21.9.11) He makes the days diverse in vigor through the meters.
(PB 21.9.12) The <s>Naudhasa</s> is the <s>Brahma-Sāman</s> of the first day, the <s>Śyaita</s> of the second, the <s>Śrāyantīya</s> of the third, the <s>Traiśoka</s> of the fourth.
(PB 21.9.13) On this they say: 'This seems like a falling away — that from a greater meter one descends to a lesser meter.'
(PB 21.9.14) Therefore when on the fourth day the <s>atijagatī</s> (beyond-<s>Jagatī</s>) is made — that is to prevent falling away.
(PB 21.9.15) The <s>Kāleya</s> is the <s>Acchāvāka-Sāman</s> of the first day, the <s>Mādhucchandasa</s> of the second, the <s>Raurava</s> of the third, the <s>Samanta</s> of the fourth — for the diversity of vigor. He makes the days diverse in vigor.
(PB 21.9.16) 'This bull has been pressed for you' — the <s>Rathantara</s> of the third day. 'Who, O <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>' — the <s>Vāmadevya</s>. 'The sacrifices as in ancient times' — the <s>Bṛhat</s> of the fourth day. 'This sweetest of the sweet' — the <s>Vāmadevya</s>. For the diversity of vigor through the meters. He makes the days diverse in vigor.

body.text:
(PB 21.10.1) trivṛt pañcadaśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ prathamam ahaḥ
(PB 21.10.2) athottarasyāhnoś caturviṃśaṃ vahiṣpavamānaṃ pañcadaśāni trīṇy ājyāni saptadaśam acchāvākasyaikaviṃśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamānaḥ saptadaśe dve pṛṣṭhe ekaviṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃṃ soktham
(PB 21.10.3) tṛtīyasyāhna ekaviṃśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ trīṇi cājyāni pañcadaśam acchāvākasya caturviṃśo mādhyandinaḥ pavamāna ekaviṃśāni pṛṣṭhāni triṇavaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ dve cokthe ekaviṃśam acchāvākasya
(PB 21.10.4) caturthasyāhnaś caturviśāḥ pavamānāḥ pañcadaśaṃ hotur ājyaṃ saptadaśāni trīṇy ekaviṃśāni pṛṣṭhāni trayastriṃśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśāny ukthāni saṣoḍaśikāni pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 21.10.5) jamadagniḥ puṣṭikāma etam āharat sa imān poṣān apuṣyat
(PB 21.10.6) yad idam āhur navā ūrvau palitau sañjānāte iti
(PB 21.10.7) tat sarvān evaitena poṣān puṣyati
(PB 21.10.8) jagatī chandobhiḥ sampadyate
(PB 21.10.9) jagatī vai chandasāṃ paramaṃ poṣaṃ puṣṭā paramam evaite poṣaṃ puṣyati
(PB 21.10.10) puroḍāśinya upasado bhavanti paśavo vai puroḍāśāḥ paśuṣveva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 21.10.11) agne ver hotra ver adhvaram āpitaraṃ vaiśvānaram avase 'kar indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.12) devāv aśvinau madhukaśayādyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya mimikṣatam indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.13) deva viṣṇa urv adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyādhi vikramasvendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.14) deva soma retodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhīndrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.15) deva savitaḥ susāvitram adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāsuvasvendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.16) deva dhātaḥ sudhātādyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhīndrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.17) devā grāvāṇo madhumatīm adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya vācaṃ vadatendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.18) devy anumate 'nvadyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya manyasvendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.19) devy adite svādityām adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasvendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.20) devya āpo nannamyadhvam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyendrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.21) sadassadaḥ prajāvān ṛbhur juṣāṇa indrāya devebhyo juhutā havis svāhā
(PB 21.10.22) deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhīndrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā
(PB 21.10.23) āgneya ekakapāla āśvino dvikapālo vaiṣṇavas trikapālaḥ saumyaś catuṣkapālaḥ sāvitraḥ pañcakapālo dhātraḥ ṣaṭkapālo mārūtaḥ saptakapālo bārhaspatyo 'ṣṭākapālo maitro navakapālo vārūṇo daśakapāla aindra ekādaśakapālo vaiśvadevo dvādaśakapālaḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.10.1) Threefold, fifteenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the first day.
(PB 21.10.2) Of the second day: twenty-four-fold <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (external purification chant), three fifteenfold <s>Ājya</s> libations, seventeenfold <s>Acchāvāka</s>, twenty-one-fold midday <s>Pavamāna</s>, two seventeenfold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, twenty-one-fold third pressing with <s>Uktha</s>.
(PB 21.10.3) Of the third day: twenty-one-fold <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> and three <s>Ājya</s> libations, fifteenfold <s>Acchāvāka</s>, twenty-four-fold midday <s>Pavamāna</s>, twenty-one-fold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, <s>Triṇava</s> third pressing, two <s>Uktha</s> recitations, twenty-one-fold <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
(PB 21.10.4) Of the fourth day: twenty-four-fold <s>Pavamāna</s> chants, fifteenfold <s>Hotṛ</s>'s <s>Ājya</s>, three seventeenfold, twenty-one-fold <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants, thirty-three-fold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, twenty-one-fold <s>Uktha</s> recitations with <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s>, fifteenfold night rite, threefold junction.
(PB 21.10.5) <s>Jamadagni</s>, desiring nourishment, brought this forth. He nourished these nourishments.
(PB 21.10.6) Regarding what they say: 'The new are recognized along with the gray-haired' —
(PB 21.10.7) He nourishes all nourishments with this.
(PB 21.10.8) It corresponds to the <s>Jagatī</s> among the meters.
(PB 21.10.9) The <s>Jagatī</s> is the supreme nourishment among the meters. He who is nourished thus nourishes the supreme nourishment.
(PB 21.10.10) The approach-offerings (<s>upasad</s>) are with <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cakes). Cattle are the <s>puroḍāśas</s>. He becomes established in cattle.
(PB 21.10.11) 'O <s>Agni</s>, O active <s>Hotṛ</s>, the active sacrifice, the enriching <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, for our aid — make! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.12) 'O divine <s>Aśvins</s>, from the honey-whip, gratify this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.13) 'O divine <s>Viṣṇu</s>, stride widely today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer, with your own! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.14) 'O divine <s>Soma</s>, bestower of seed, kindle today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.15) 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, with good impulsion, impel today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.16) 'O divine <s>Dhātṛ</s>, with good establishment, kindle today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.17) 'O divine pressing stones, speak a honey-sweet word today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.18) 'O divine <s>Anumati</s> (Approval), approve today this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.19) 'O divine <s>Aditi</s>, with good <s>Āditya</s>-ship, impel today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.20) 'O divine Waters, bow down today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.21) 'O <s>Ṛbhu</s>, rich in offspring, seated in the seat of seats, being pleased — offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.22) 'O divine <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, bestower of good seed, kindle today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Offer oblation to <s>Indra</s> and the gods, <s>svāhā</s>!'
(PB 21.10.23) An offering to <s>Agni</s> on one dish, to the <s>Aśvins</s> on two dishes, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> on three dishes, to <s>Soma</s> on four dishes, to <s>Savitṛ</s> on five dishes, to <s>Dhātṛ</s> on six dishes, to the <s>Maruts</s> on seven dishes, to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> on eight dishes, to <s>Mitra</s> on nine dishes, to <s>Varuṇa</s> on ten dishes, to <s>Indra</s> on eleven dishes, to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> on twelve dishes.

body.text:
(PB 21.11.1) trivṛta prātassavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ saptadaśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ pañcadaśaṃ prātassavanaṃ saptadaśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanam ekaviṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ sokthaṃ saptadaśaṃ prātassavanam ekaviṃśaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ triṇavaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ soktham ekaviṃśaṃ prātassavanaṃ triṇavaṃ mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ trayastriṃśaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamaṃ dve ekaviṃśe saṣoḍaśike pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 21.11.2) vasiṣṭhaḥ putrahato hīna ivāmanyata sa etam apaśyat so 'graṃ paryaid yo hīna iva manyeta sa etena yajeta
(PB 21.11.3) yat stomāt stomam abhisaṃkrāmaty agrād evāgraṃ rohati vasiṣṭhasya janitre bhavataḥ prajātyai
(PB 21.11.4) pratyavarohīṇy uttamasyāhna ukthāni bhavanti pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.11.1) The morning pressing in <s>trivṛt</s> (nine-fold), the midday pressing in <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold), the third pressing in <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold); the morning pressing in <s>pañcadaśa</s>, the midday pressing in <s>saptadaśa</s>, the third pressing in <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) with <s>uktha</s>; the morning pressing in <s>saptadaśa</s>, the midday pressing in <s>ekaviṃśa</s>, the third pressing in <s>triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold) with <s>uktha</s>; the morning pressing in <s>ekaviṃśa</s>, the midday pressing in <s>triṇava</s>, the third pressing in <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-fold). The <s>ukthas</s> are in descending order. The first in <s>triṇava</s>; two in <s>ekaviṃśa</s> with <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteen-fold addendum); the night in <s>pañcadaśa</s>; the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) in <s>trivṛt</s>.
(PB 21.11.2) <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, having lost his son, felt as if diminished. He perceived this rite. He returned to the front. One who feels diminished should sacrifice with this.
(PB 21.11.3) Since he crosses from <s>stoma</s> to <s>stoma</s>, he ascends from summit to summit. There are two <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> birth-songs — for procreation.
(PB 21.11.4) The <s>ukthas</s> of the last day are in descending order — for firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 21.12.1) trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthaḥ saptadaśa uktha ekaviṃśo 'tirātro viśvāmitrasya sañjayaḥ
(PB 21.12.2) jahnuvṛcīvanto rāṣṭra āhiṃsanta sa viśvāmitro jāhnavo rājaitam apaśyat sa rāṣṭram abhavad arāṣṭram itare
(PB 21.12.3) bhrātṛvyavān yajeta
(PB 21.12.4) bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.12.5) jyotir vā eṣa vihṛtaḥ
(PB 21.12.6) jyotiḥ prajānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.12.7) catuṣṭomo vā eṣa catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 21.12.8) ekaviṃśaṃ stomā nātiyanti pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo 'ntata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhati
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.12.1) <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>pañcadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>saptadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>ekaviṃśa</s> <s>Atirātra</s>. This is the <s>Sañjaya</s> of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
(PB 21.12.2) The <s>Jahnu</s> and <s>Vṛcīvat</s> clans were harming his kingdom. <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the <s>Jāhnava</s> king, perceived this. He gained the kingdom; the others lost theirs.
(PB 21.12.3) One who has a rival should sacrifice with this.
(PB 21.12.4) By his own self his rival is defeated — he who knows thus.
(PB 21.12.5) This is the <s>Jyotis</s> (light) spread out.
(PB 21.12.6) He becomes the light of his people — he who knows thus.
(PB 21.12.7) This has four <s>stomas</s>. Animals are four-footed — thereby he becomes firmly established in animals.
(PB 21.12.8) The <s>stomas</s> do not exceed <s>ekaviṃśa</s>. The <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is firm establishment. At the very end he becomes firmly established in the sacrifice.

body.text:
(PB 21.13.1) dve trivṛtī savane pañcadaśam ekaṃ dve pañcadaśe savane saptadaśam ekaṃ dve saptadaśe savane ekaviṃśam ekaṃ dve ekaviṃśe savane triṇavam ekaṃ dve triṇave savane trayastriṃśam ekaṃ pratyavarohīṇy ukthāni triṇavaṃ prathamaṃ dve ekaviṃśe saṣoḍaśike pañcadaśī rātris trivṛt sandhiḥ
(PB 21.13.2) devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta te na vyajayanta te 'bruvan vāco mithunena vijayāmahai yatare no vāco mithunaṃ na prativindāṃs te parā bhavān iti te devā eka ity abruvann ekety asurā vāco mithunaṃ pratyavindan dvāv iti devā abruvan dve ity asurā vāco mithunaṃ pratyavindanaṃs traya iti devā abruvaṃs tisra ity asurā vāco mithunaṃ pratyavindaṃś catvāra iti devā abruvaṃś catastra ity asurā vāco mithunaṃ pratyavindan pañceti devā abruvan nāsurā avindaṃs tato devā abhavan parāsurāḥ
(PB 21.13.3) bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.13.4) saṃvatsaraṃ vā eṣāṃ tad vīryam annādyam avṛñjata
(PB 21.13.5) saṃvatsaraṃ vīryam annādyaṃ bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte ya evaṃ veda
(PB 21.13.6) pañcarātro vā eṣa pāṅktaḥ purūṣaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavas tena purūṣaṃ ca paśūṃś cāpnoti
(PB 21.13.7) āstharir vā eṣa santato yajño dvau dvau hi stomāv ahar vahato yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam etenābhyaśnute
(PB 21.13.8) yatra yatra hy asthūriṇā kāmayate tat tad abhyaśnute
(PB 21.13.9) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho bhavati santatyai
(PB 21.13.10) pratyavarohīṇy uttamasyāhna ukthāni bhavanti pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.13.1) Two pressings in <s>trivṛt</s>, one in <s>pañcadaśa</s>; two pressings in <s>pañcadaśa</s>, one in <s>saptadaśa</s>; two pressings in <s>saptadaśa</s>, one in <s>ekaviṃśa</s>; two pressings in <s>ekaviṃśa</s>, one in <s>triṇava</s>; two pressings in <s>triṇava</s>, one in <s>trayastriṃśa</s>. The <s>ukthas</s> are descending. The first in <s>triṇava</s>; two in <s>ekaviṃśa</s> with <s>ṣoḍaśin</s>; the night in <s>pañcadaśa</s>; the <s>sandhi</s> in <s>trivṛt</s>.
(PB 21.13.2) The gods and <s>asuras</s> contended. They could not prevail. They said: 'Let us prevail by the pairing of speech. Those of us who cannot find the pair of speech shall be defeated.' The gods said 'one' (<s>ekaḥ</s>); the <s>asuras</s> said 'one' (<s>ekā</s>) — they found the speech-pair. The gods said 'two' (<s>dvau</s>); the <s>asuras</s> said 'two' (<s>dve</s>) — they found the speech-pair. The gods said 'three' (<s>trayaḥ</s>); the <s>asuras</s> said 'three' (<s>tisraḥ</s>) — they found the speech-pair. The gods said 'four' (<s>catvāraḥ</s>); the <s>asuras</s> said 'four' (<s>catasraḥ</s>) — they found the speech-pair. The gods said 'five' (<s>pañca</s>); the <s>asuras</s> could not find it. Thereupon the gods prevailed; the <s>asuras</s> were defeated.
(PB 21.13.3) By his own self his rival is defeated — he who knows thus.
(PB 21.13.4) They wrested vigor and food-eating from them for a year.
(PB 21.13.5) He wrests vigor and food-eating from his rival for a year — he who knows thus.
(PB 21.13.6) This is indeed a five-night rite. The person belongs to the group of five; animals belong to the group of five. Thereby he attains both persons and animals.
(PB 21.13.7) This is a spread-out, continuous sacrifice, for two <s>stomas</s> bear each day. Whatever desire he desires, he attains it by this.
(PB 21.13.8) Wherever one desires with the spread-out rite, that he attains.
(PB 21.13.9) The five-day rite becomes connected — for continuation.
(PB 21.13.10) The <s>ukthas</s> of the last day are descending — for firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 21.14.1) trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthaḥ saptadaśa ukthaḥ pañcadaśa ukthaḥ saptadaśo 'tirātraḥ pañcaśāradīyo marutāṃ stomaḥ
(PB 21.14.2) yaḥ kāmayeta bahu syām iti sa etena yajeta
(PB 21.14.3) marūto vai devānāṃ bhūyiṣṭhā bahur eva bhavati
(PB 21.14.4) saptadaśaṃ stomā nātiyanti prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajāpatim evāpnoti
(PB 21.14.5) agastyo vai marūdbhya ukṣṇaḥ praukṣat tān indrāyābadhnāt te vajram ādāyābhyapatan sa etat kayāśubhīyam apaśyat tenāśamayat
(PB 21.14.6) yat kayāśubhīyaṃ śasyate śāntyā eva
(PB 21.14.7) saptadaśa pṛśnīn ukṣṇaḥ pañcavarṣān saptadaśa pṛśnīs trivatsā apravītās tān paryagnikṛtān prokṣitānetarā labhante pretarān sṛjanti
(PB 21.14.8) tataḥ saṃvatsare navanītapṛśnīr arūṇā ānayanti tāṃś caivokṣṇas tān paryagnikṛtān prokṣitān etarā labhante pretarān sṛjanti tataḥ saṃvatsare rājīvā ānayanti tāṃś caivokṣṇas tān paryagnikṛtān prokṣitān etarā labhante pretarān sṛjanti tataḥ saṃvatsare piśaṅgīr ānayanti tāṃś caivokṣṇas tān paryagnikṛtān prokṣitān etarā labhante pretarān sṛjanti tataḥ saṃvatsare sāraṅgīr ānayanti tāṃś caivokṣṇas tān paryagnikṛtān pokṣitān etarā labhante pretarān sṛjanti
(PB 21.14.9) tataḥ saṃvatsare somā bhavanti
(PB 21.14.10) trīṃs trīn anvaham ālabhante pañcottame 'hani
(PB 21.14.11) ajo 'gnīṣomīyaḥ
(PB 21.14.12) aindrā mārūto ukṣāṇo mārūtyo vatsataryaḥ
(PB 21.14.13) yadi rūdro 'bhimanyotāgnaye rūdravate puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.14) yadi saṃśīryaita bhaumam ekakapālaṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.15) yady avasīder nairṛtaṃ caruṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta yady apsu mriyetāponaptrīyaṃ caruṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta yady andhasyāt sauryaṃ caruṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.16) yadi ślavaṇo vā kuṭo vā syād bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nipyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.17) yadi palāyeta vāyavyaṃ caruṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.18) yadi prāsahājayeyur indrāya prasahvana ekādaśakapālaṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.19) yady anyena mṛtyunā mriyeta prājāpatyaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirūpyāthānyam ālabheta
(PB 21.14.20) etena vā ekayāvā gāndamo vetasvatīṣṭvā sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot
(PB 21.14.21) sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.14.1) <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>pañcadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>saptadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>pañcadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>saptadaśa</s> <s>Atirātra</s>. This is the five-year <s>stoma</s> of the <s>Maruts</s>.
(PB 21.14.2) One who desires: 'May I become many' should sacrifice with this.
(PB 21.14.3) The <s>Maruts</s> are indeed the most numerous among the gods. He becomes numerous indeed.
(PB 21.14.4) The <s>stomas</s> do not exceed <s>saptadaśa</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>saptadaśa</s>. He attains <s>Prajāpati</s> himself.
(PB 21.14.5) <s>Agastya</s> sprinkled bulls for the <s>Maruts</s> and bound them for <s>Indra</s>. They, seizing the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), rushed upon him. He perceived this <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> (sāman). By it he pacified them.
(PB 21.14.6) Since the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> is recited, it is for peace.
(PB 21.14.7) Seventeen dappled five-year-old bulls, seventeen dappled three-year-old unbred cows — these, having been encircled by fire and sprinkled, the former ones are sacrificed and the latter are released.
(PB 21.14.8) Then after a year they bring butter-colored, reddish cows and likewise bulls — encircled by fire and sprinkled, the former sacrificed, the latter released. Then after a year they bring streaked ones and likewise bulls — encircled by fire, the former sacrificed, the latter released. Then after a year they bring tawny ones and likewise bulls — encircled by fire, the former sacrificed, the latter released. Then after a year they bring spotted ones and likewise bulls — encircled by fire, the former sacrificed, the latter released.
(PB 21.14.9) Then after a year the <s>Soma</s> pressings take place.
(PB 21.14.10) Three animals are sacrificed each day; five on the last day.
(PB 21.14.11) The goat is for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>.
(PB 21.14.12) The bulls are for <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>; the heifer-calves are for the <s>Maruts</s>.
(PB 21.14.13) If <s>Rudra</s> becomes angry, having offered an eight-kapāla cake to <s>Agni Rudravat</s>, then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.14) If the animal crumbles, having offered a one-kapāla cake to <s>Bhūmi</s> (Earth), then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.15) If the animal sinks down, having offered a porridge to <s>Nirṛti</s>, then one should sacrifice another. If it dies in the water, having offered a porridge to the Water Offspring, then one should sacrifice another. If it becomes blind, having offered a porridge to <s>Sūrya</s>, then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.16) If it becomes lame or hunchbacked, having offered a porridge to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.17) If it runs away, having offered a porridge to <s>Vāyu</s>, then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.18) If enemies conquer by force, having offered an eleven-kapāla cake to <s>Indra Prasahvan</s> (Indra the Overpowerer), then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.19) If the animal dies by some other death, having offered a twelve-kapāla cake to <s>Prajāpati</s>, then one should sacrifice another.
(PB 21.14.20) By this, <s>Gāndama</s> of the <s>Ekayāvā</s> clan, having sacrificed at the <s>Vetasvatī</s> river, attained all prosperity.
(PB 21.14.21) He attains all prosperity — he who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 21.15.1) jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo gaur ukthyo mahāvrataṃ gaur ukthya āyur atirātraḥ
(PB 21.15.2) saṃvatsaro vai vrataṃ tasya vasanta ṛtur mukhaṃ grīṣmaś ca varṣāś ca pakṣau śaran madhyaṃ hemantaḥ puccham
(PB 21.15.3) tasmāc charadam oṣadhayo 'bhisampacyante śarad dhi madhyaṃ saṃvatsarasya
(PB 21.15.4) akṛtaṃ vā ete kurvanti ye purā saṃvatsarāt vratam upayanti
(PB 21.15.5) etad vai vratam āptaṃ yat pañcarātre pañca hy ṛtavaḥ
(PB 21.15.6) āptena vratena stute sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 21.15.1) <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Gaur</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>, <s>Gaur</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Āyus</s> <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 21.15.2) The year is indeed the observance. Spring is its mouth; summer and the rains are its two wings; autumn is its middle; winter is its tail.
(PB 21.15.3) Therefore herbs ripen in autumn, for autumn is the middle of the year.
(PB 21.15.4) Those who undertake the observance before the year is complete do something unaccomplished.
(PB 21.15.5) This observance is accomplished when it is a five-night rite, for there are five seasons.
(PB 21.15.6) Having praised with an accomplished observance, he lives his full lifespan — he who knows thus.

body.text:
(PB 22.1.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ
(PB 22.1.2) ṛtavo na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta etena pratyatiṣṭhan pratiṣṭhākāmo yajeta praty eva tiṣṭhati
(PB 22.1.3) ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtuṣv evaitena pratitiṣṭhati pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho bhavati pratyakṣam ṛdhyai
(PB 22.1.4) pratyakṣaṃ hy etenartava ārdhnuvann ṛdhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.1.1) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite.
(PB 22.1.2) The seasons were not firmly established. By this they became firmly established. One desiring firm establishment should sacrifice. He becomes firmly established indeed.
(PB 22.1.3) There are six seasons. By this he becomes firmly established in the seasons. The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite is for manifest prosperity.
(PB 22.1.4) For by this the seasons manifestly prospered — for prosperity indeed.

body.text:
(PB 22.2.1) trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyo jyotir gaur āyur atirātraḥ
(PB 22.2.2) yaḥ kāmayeta sarvam āyur iyām iti sa etena yajeta
(PB 22.2.3) yat tryahaḥ purastād bhavati trayaḥ prāṇāpānavyānās ta eva tat saṃdhīyante
(PB 22.2.4) atha yat jyotir gaur āyur atirātro bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.2.1) <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>pañcadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>saptadaśa</s> <s>Ukthya</s>; <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s> <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.2.2) One who desires: 'May I live my full lifespan' should sacrifice with this.
(PB 22.2.3) Since there is a three-day rite first, the three vital breaths — <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s> — are thereby joined.
(PB 22.2.4) Then the <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s> <s>Atirātra</s> follows — for firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 22.3.1) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho viśvajid atirātraḥ
(PB 22.3.2) anyasmai vai kāmāya sattram anyasmai yajño na tatsatreṇāpnoti yasmaikaṃ yajño na tad yajñenāpnoti yasmaikaṃ sattram
(PB 22.3.3) sattram iva vā etad yad anulomaṃ pṛṣṭhāni yad ekadhā pṛṣṭhāni bhavanty ekadhaivāsmiṃs tad ojo vīryaṃ dadhāti
(PB 22.3.4) annaṃ pṛṣṭhāny annādyam evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 22.3.5) paśavaḥ pṛṣṭhāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.3.6) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho bhavati santatyai
(PB 22.3.7) viśvajid atirātro bhavati viśvasyābhijityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.3.1) An <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> (approaching) five-day rite, an all-conquering (<s>Viśvajit</s>) <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.3.2) A <s>sattra</s> (communal sacrifice) serves one purpose, an individual sacrifice another. What one does not obtain by a <s>sattra</s>, one obtains by a sacrifice; what one does not obtain by a sacrifice, one obtains by a <s>sattra</s>.
(PB 22.3.3) This is like a <s>sattra</s>, in that the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants] are in regular order. When the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants are uniform, one thereby places vigor and vitality uniformly.

body.text:
(PB 22.4.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho mahāvratam atirātraḥ
(PB 22.4.2) sapta ṛṣaya etenārdhnuvaṃs tenarddhis tasmād etena yajanta ṛddhyā eva
(PB 22.4.3) sapta śirasi prāṇāḥ prāṇā indriyāṇīndriyāṇy evaitenāpnoti
(PB 22.4.4) sapta grāmyāḥ paśavas tān etenāpnoti
(PB 22.4.5) vrataṃ saptamasyāhnaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati tad dhy anāptam annaṃ vai vratam annādyam evaitenāpnoti
(PB 22.4.6) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho bhavati pratyakṣam ṛdhyai
(PB 22.4.7) pratyakṣaṃ hy etena sapta ṛṣaya ārdhnuvann ṛdhyā eva
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.4.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.4.2) The Seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> (Sages) prospered by this. Therefore prosperity comes from sacrificing with this — for the sake of prosperity indeed.
(PB 22.4.3) There are seven vital breaths in the head. The vital breaths are the sense faculties. By this one obtains the sense faculties.
(PB 22.4.4) There are seven domestic animals. By this one obtains them.
(PB 22.4.5) The observance (<s>vrata</s>) of the seventh day becomes the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chant].

body.text:
(PB 22.5.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ saptadaśaṃ mahāvratam atirātraḥ
(PB 22.5.2) tasya trivṛc chiraḥ pañcadaśau pakṣau saptadaśa ātmaikaviṃśaṃ puccham
(PB 22.5.3) etena vai prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata
(PB 22.5.4) pra prajayā pra paśubhir jāyate ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.5.5) saptadaśo vai prajāpatir yat saptadaśaṃ vrataṃ bhavati prajāpatim evāpnoti
(PB 22.5.6) yat trivṛc chiro bhavati nava prāṇāḥ prāṇeṣv eva prati tiṣṭhati
(PB 22.5.7) yat pañcadaśau pakṣau savīvadhatvāya
(PB 22.5.8) saptadaśa ātmā bhavati prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajā patim evāpnoti
(PB 22.5.9) ekaviṃśaṃ puccha bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.5.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], a seventeen-fold <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.5.2) Its head is three-fold, its two wings are fifteen-fold, its body is seventeen-fold, and its tail is twenty-one-fold.
(PB 22.5.3) By this, <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring.
(PB 22.5.4) He who knows thus prospers with offspring and with cattle.
(PB 22.5.5) <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the seventeen-fold. Because the <s>Mahāvrata</s> is seventeen-fold,

body.text:
(PB 22.6.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahaś chandomapavamānaṃ mahāvratam atirātraḥ
(PB 22.6.2) paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 22.6.3) paśavo vai chandāmāḥ
(PB 22.6.4) yac chadomāḥ pavamānā mahāvratasya bhavanti paśūnevāvarūndhe
(PB 22.6.5) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tan mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.6.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], with <s>Chandoma</s> (meter-variant) <s>Pavamāna</s> [chants], a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.6.2) One desiring cattle should sacrifice.
(PB 22.6.3) The <s>Chandomas</s> are indeed cattle.
(PB 22.6.4) Because the <s>Chandoma Pavamānas</s> belong to the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, one secures cattle.
(PB 22.6.5) Both kinds of <s>stomas</s>, even and odd, form a pair (<s>mithuna</s>). From that pairing, offspring are born.

body.text:
(PB 22.7.1) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho 'tha trayastriṃśām ahas tasya catustriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ saptadaśaṃ mahāvratam atirātras tasya caturviṃśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ trivṛc chiraḥ pañcadaśau pakṣau saptadaśa ātmaikaviṃśaṃ puccham
(PB 22.7.2) etena vai jamadagniḥ sarvān poṣān apuṣyat sarvān evaitena poṣān puṣyati
(PB 22.7.3) yad abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāhaḥ purastād bhavati santatyā eva
(PB 22.7.4) athaitat trayastriṃśam ahas trayastriṃśad devatā devatā evāpnoti
(PB 22.7.5) tasya catustriṃśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ prajāpatiś catustriṃśo devatānāṃ prajāpatim evāpnoti
(PB 22.7.6) caturviṃśaṃ bahiṣpavamānaṃ bhavati mahāvratasya caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī prajananaṃ gāyatrī prajātyai
(PB 22.7.7) ubhaye stomā yugmantaś cāyujaś ca tan mithunaṃ tasmān mithunāt prajāyate
(PB 22.7.8) yat trivṛc chiro bhavati nava prāṇāḥ prāṇeṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati yat pañcadaśau pakṣau savīvadhatvāya saptadaśa ātmā bhavati prajāpatir vai saptadaśaḥ prajāpatim evāpnoty ekaviṃśaṃ pucchaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.7.1) An <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> five-day rite, then a thirty-three-fold day, its <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is thirty-four-fold; a seventeen-fold <s>Mahāvrata</s>; an <s>Atirātra</s> with a twenty-four-fold <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>; its head is three-fold, its wings fifteen-fold, its body seventeen-fold, its tail twenty-one-fold.
(PB 22.7.2) By this, <s>Jamadagni</s> nourished all forms of prosperity. By this indeed one nourishes all forms of prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 22.8.1) jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo gaur ukthya āyur ukthyo 'bhijid agniṣṭomo viśvajid agniṣṭomaḥ sarvajid agniṣṭomaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 22.8.2) etena vā indro 'ty ānyā devatā abhavad aty anyā prajā bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.8.3) yat jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ purastād bhavati prajñātān stomānupaitīmān eva lokān eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.8.4) athābhijid abhijitā vai devā imān lokān abhyajayan viśvajitā viśvam ajayan sarvajitā sarvam ajayan
(PB 22.8.5) sarvastomātirātro bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvam evaitenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.8.1) A <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Gaus Ukthya</s>, an <s>Āyus Ukthya</s>, an <s>Abhijit Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma</s>, and a <s>Sarvastoma Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.8.2) By this, <s>Indra</s> surpassed the other deities. He who knows thus surpasses other creatures.
(PB 22.8.3) Because the three-day sequence of <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaus</s>, and <s>Āyus</s> comes first, one approaches the known <s>stomas</s>; [one is established] in these very worlds.

body.text:
(PB 22.9.1) catvāri trivṛnty ahāny agniṣṭomamukhāni viśvajin mahāvrataṃ jyotiṣṭomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 22.9.2) etena vai prajāpatiḥ purūṣam asṛjata sa sarvasyānnādyasyādhipatyam agacchat
(PB 22.9.3) sarvasyānnādyasyādhipatyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.9.4) śiro vā agre sambhavataḥ sambhavati caturdhā vihitaṃ vai śiraḥ prāṇaś cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vāgātmā vai pṛṣṭhāni yat pṛṣṭhāny upaiti śira evātmānam anusandadhāti
(PB 22.9.5) etad vai purūṣam akas tasmā annam eva vratam apidadhāti
(PB 22.9.6) atha yat jyotiṣṭomo 'tirātro bhavaty akḷptasya kḷptyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.9.1) Four three-fold days with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> openings, an all-conquering (<s>Viśvajit</s>) <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and a <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.9.2) By this, <s>Prajāpati</s> created man. He attained lordship over all food.
(PB 22.9.3) He who knows thus attains lordship over all food.
(PB 22.9.4) The head indeed comes into being first. He comes into being four-fold.

body.text:
(PB 22.10.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ stomaḥ ṣaḍaho viśvajid atirātraḥ
(PB 22.10.2) anyasmai vai kāmāya sattram anyasmai yajño na tat sattreṇāpnoti yasmaikaṃ yajño na tad yajñenāpnoti yasmaikaṃ sattraṃ sattram iva vā etad yad anulomaṃ pṛṣṭhāni yadaikadhā pṛṣṭhāni bhavaty ekadhaivāsmiṃs tejo vīryaṃ dadhāty annaṃ pṛṣṭhāny annādyam evāsmin dadhāti paśavaḥ pṛṣṭhāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.10.3) yad vai manuṣyāṇāṃ pratyakṣaṃ taddevānāṃ parokṣamatha yanma manuṣyāṇāṃ parokṣaṃ taddevānāṃ pratyakṣam
(PB 22.10.4) etad vai parokṣaṃ vrataṃ yad viśvajit pratyakṣam evaitenānnādyam avarundhe
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.10.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> <s>stoma</s> and an all-conquering (<s>Viśvajit</s>) <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.10.2) A <s>sattra</s> serves one purpose, a sacrifice another. What one does not obtain by a <s>sattra</s>, one obtains by a sacrifice; what one does not obtain by a sacrifice, one obtains by a <s>sattra</s>. This is like a <s>sattra</s>, in that the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> are in regular order. When the <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> are uniform, one thereby places radiance and vigor uniformly. Food is the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>.

body.text:
(PB 22.11.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho mahāvrataṃ jyotiṣṭomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 22.11.2) etena vai devā devatvam agacchan
(PB 22.11.3) devatvaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.11.4) etad vai vratam āptaṃ yad aṣṭarātre 'gniṣṭomo hi vrataṃ sampadyate
(PB 22.11.5) atha yat jyotiṣṭhomo 'tirātro bhavaty akḷptasya kḷptyai
(PB 22.11.6) aṣṭarātreṇa vai devāḥ sarvam āśnuvata
(PB 22.11.7) sarvam aśnute ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.11.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and a <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.11.2) By this the gods attained divine status.
(PB 22.11.3) He who knows thus attains divine status.
(PB 22.11.4) This observance is indeed fulfilled in the eight-night rite, for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> constitutes the observance.
(PB 22.11.5) And because the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Atirātra</s> occurs — for the accomplishment of what has not been accomplished.

body.text:
(PB 22.12.1) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho jyotir gaur āyur atirātro devā vai mṛtyor abibhayus te prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etena navarātreṇāmṛtatvaṃ prāyacchat
(PB 22.12.2) etad vāva manuṣyasyāmṛtatvaṃ yat sarvam āyur eti vasīyān bhavati
(PB 22.12.3) sarvam āyur eti vasīyān bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.12.4) navarātro vā eṣa nava prāṇāḥ prāṇeṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.12.5) pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho bhavati pratyakṣam ṛddhayā atha yat jyotir gaur āyur atirātro bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.12.1) A six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants]; <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaus</s>, <s>Āyus</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. The gods feared death. They ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. He bestowed immortality upon them through this nine-night rite.
(PB 22.12.2) This indeed is the immortality of a human: that one lives a full lifespan and becomes prosperous.
(PB 22.12.3) He who knows thus lives a full lifespan and becomes prosperous.
(PB 22.12.4)

body.text:
(PB 22.13.1) jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭhomo gaur ukthya āyur ukthyo 'bhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho viśvajid atirātraḥ paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 22.13.2) yat jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ purastād bhavati prajñātān stomānupaitīmān eva lokān eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.13.3) atha yad abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho madhyato bhavati pāṅktaḥ purūṣaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavas tena purūṣaṃ ca paśūṃś cāpnoti
(PB 22.13.4) viśvajid atirātro bhavati viśvasyābhijityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.13.1) A <s>Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Gaus Ukthya</s>, an <s>Āyus Ukthya</s>, an <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> five-day rite, and an all-conquering (<s>Viśvajit</s>) <s>Atirātra</s>. One desiring cattle should sacrifice.
(PB 22.13.2) Because the three-day sequence of <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaus</s>, and <s>Āyus</s> comes first, one approaches the known <s>stomas</s> — these very worlds — and becomes established in them.
(PB 22.13.3) And because the <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> five-day rite is in the middle,

body.text:
(PB 22.14.1) trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyas trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomas triṇavo 'gniṣṭomas trayastriṃśa ukthyas triṇavo 'gniṣṭomo viśvajid atirātraḥ
(PB 22.14.2) indro 'surān hatvākāryaṃ cakṛvāṃ amanyata taṃ devā etena stomenāyājayan sa pāpmano nairdaśyam agacchat
(PB 22.14.3) tasmād iṣuhato vā daṇḍahato vā daśamīṃ nairdaśyaṃ gacchati
(PB 22.14.4) daśa daśinī vā eṣā virāḍ annaṃ virāḍ annādyam evāsmin dadhāti
(PB 22.14.5) agniṣṭomena vai devā asurān nigṛhya madhyata ukthaiḥ prajayā paśubhiḥ prājāyantāgniṣṭomenaiva bhrātṛvyaṃ nigṛhya madhyata ukthyaiḥ prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāyate
(PB 22.14.6) trikakub vā eṣa yajñaḥ
(PB 22.14.7) trikakup samānānāṃ ca prajānāṃ ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.15.1) trayastrivṛto 'gniṣṭomās trayaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyās trayaḥ saptadaśa ukthyā ekaviṃśo 'tirātraḥ kusuruvindadaśarātraḥ
(PB 22.15.2) yaḥ kāmayeta bahu syām iti sa etena yajeta
(PB 22.15.3) yad gaṇaśaḥ stomo bahur eva bhavati
(PB 22.15.4) saha trivṛta saha pañcadaśāḥ saha saptadaśāḥ
(PB 22.15.5) ekaviṃśo 'tirātro bhavati pratiṣṭhityai
(PB 22.15.6) jyotir vā eṣa vihṛtaḥ
(PB 22.15.7) jyotiṣ prajānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.15.8) catuṣṭomo vā eṣa catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhati
(PB 22.15.9) ekaviṃśaṃ stomā nātiyanti pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśaḥ praty eva tiṣṭhati
(PB 22.15.10) etena vai kusurūvinda auddālakir iṣṭvā bhūmānam āśnuta
(PB 22.15.11) bhūmānam aśnute ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.14.1) A threefold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a fifteenfold <s>Ukthya</s>, a threefold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a seventeenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a twenty-onefold <s>Ukthya</s>, a seventeenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a twenty-sevenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a thirty-threefold <s>Ukthya</s>, a twenty-sevenfold <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.14.2) <s>Indra</s>, having slain the <s>Asuras</s>, thought he had done an evil deed. The gods made him sacrifice with this <s>stoma</s>. He reached freedom from evil on the tenth day.
(PB 22.14.3) Therefore one struck by an arrow or a stick reaches freedom from evil on the tenth day.
(PB 22.14.4) This ten-day period is a <s>Virāj</s> of ten. Food is the <s>Virāj</s>. He places food-eating in him.
(PB 22.14.5) By the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> the gods suppressed the <s>Asuras</s>; in between, by the <s>Ukthya</s> days, they procreated with offspring and cattle. By the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> he suppresses the hostile rival; in between, by the <s>Ukthya</s> days, he procreates with offspring and cattle.
(PB 22.14.6) This sacrifice has three peaks.
(PB 22.14.7) He who knows thus becomes three-peaked among his equals and his offspring.
(PB 22.15.1) Three threefold <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>, three fifteenfold <s>Ukthyas</s>, three seventeenfold <s>Ukthyas</s>, a twenty-onefold <s>Atirātra</s>. This is the <s>Kusuruvinda</s> ten-night rite.
(PB 22.15.2) One who desires: 'May I be abundant' — he should sacrifice with this.
(PB 22.15.3) Since the <s>stoma</s> is in groups, he becomes abundant indeed.
(PB 22.15.4) Three of the threefold together, three of the fifteenfold together, three of the seventeenfold together.
(PB 22.15.5) The <s>Atirātra</s> is twenty-onefold — for establishment.
(PB 22.15.6) This is light distributed.
(PB 22.15.7) He who knows thus becomes the light of his offspring.
(PB 22.15.8) This has four <s>stomas</s>. Cattle are four-footed. He becomes established among cattle.
(PB 22.15.9) The <s>stomas</s> do not exceed twenty-one. The twenty-one is establishment. He becomes firmly established.
(PB 22.15.10) Having sacrificed with this, <s>Kusuruvinda Auddālaki</s> attained abundance.
(PB 22.15.11) He who knows thus attains abundance.

body.text:
(PB 22.16.1) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāhaś catvāraś chandomaḥ viśvajid atirātraḥ paśukāmo yajeta
(PB 22.16.2) yad abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāhaḥ purastād bhavati pāṅktaḥ puruṣaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavas tena purūṣaṃ ca paśūṃś cāpnoti
(PB 22.16.3) chandomā madhyato bhavanti paśavo vai chandomāḥ paśūnām avarudhyai
(PB 22.16.4) viśvajid atirātro bhavati viśvasyābhijityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.16.1) A five-day <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> rite, four <s>Chandomā</s> days, a <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s>. One desiring cattle should sacrifice.
(PB 22.16.2) Since the five-day <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> rite is in front — man is fivefold, cattle are fivefold — by it he obtains both man and cattle.
(PB 22.16.3) The <s>Chandomā</s> days are in the middle. Cattle are the <s>Chandomā</s> days — for the attainment of cattle.
(PB 22.16.4) The <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s> is at the end — for the conquest of all.

body.text:
(PB 22.17.1) triṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo jyotir ukthyas triṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo gaurukthyo 'bhijid agniṣṭomo gaur ukthyo viśvajid agniṣṭoma āyur ukthyo viśvajid agniṣṭomasya sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 22.17.2) devā vā asurair hanyamānās te prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etāṃ devapuraṃ prāyacchat tāṃ prāviśan
(PB 22.17.3) abhicāryamāṇaṃ yājayed etām eva devapuraṃ praviśaty asṛtyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.17.1) A three-<s>stoma</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Jyotis Ukthya</s>, a three-<s>stoma</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Gau Ukthya</s>, an <s>Abhijit Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Gau Ukthya</s>, a <s>Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma</s>, an <s>Āyus Ukthya</s>, a <s>Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma</s>, a complete-<s>stoma</s> <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.17.2) The gods, being slain by the <s>Asuras</s>, ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. He gave them this divine fortress. They entered it.
(PB 22.17.3) One who is being attacked by sorcery should be made to sacrifice. He enters this divine fortress — for safety.

body.text:
(PB 22.18.1) abhyāsaṅgyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayaś chandomāś catuṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo viśvajid atirātraḥ
(PB 22.18.2) svārājyo vā eṣa yajñaḥ
(PB 22.18.3) svārājyaṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.18.4) prajāpatir hi svārājyaṃ parameṣṭhī svārājyam
(PB 22.18.5) parameṣṭhitāṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.18.6) ubhe bṛhadrathantare bhavatas tad dhi svārājyam ayutaṃ dakṣiṇās tad dhi svārājyaṃ ṣaḍviṃśastomo bhavati sa hi svārājyaṃ catuṣṭomastomaḥ sa hy anto 'nte śriyā gacchati ya evaṃ veda
(PB 22.18.7) etena vai kṣema dhṛtvā pauṇḍarīkaṃ iṣṭvā sudāmnas tīra uttare
(PB 22.18.8) sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot sarvāmṛddhim ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text:
(PB 22.18.1) A six-day <s>Abhyāsaṅgya</s> rite, three <s>Chandomā</s> days, a four-<s>stoma</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s>.
(PB 22.18.2) This is the sacrifice of self-sovereignty.
(PB 22.18.3) He who knows thus attains self-sovereignty.
(PB 22.18.4) <s>Prajāpati</s> has self-sovereignty; <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme One) has self-sovereignty.
(PB 22.18.5) He who knows thus attains the status of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
(PB 22.18.6) Both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are used — for that is self-sovereignty. Ten thousand are the gifts — for that is self-sovereignty. The <s>stoma</s> is twenty-sixfold — for that is self-sovereignty. The four-<s>stoma</s> day is the limit. He who knows thus reaches <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) at the end.
(PB 22.18.7) By this, <s>Kṣema Dhṛtva</s>, having sacrificed with the <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s>, at <s>Sudāman</s>'s bank in the north —
(PB 22.18.8) He attained all prosperity. He who knows thus attains all prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 23.1.1) atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraś catvāraś chandomā atirātraḥ
(PB 23.1.2) eṣa vā āpto dvādaśāho yat trayodaśarātraḥ
(PB 23.1.3) samāno hy eṣa yat prayaṇīyaś codayanīyaś cātirātrau kāmaṃ kāmayante tam etābhir abhyaśnuvate
(PB 23.1.4) gṛhapates tu vāg upadāsukā bhavati tad yan madhye sarvastomo 'tirātro bhavati tena gṛhapater vāg anupadāsukā bhavati
(PB 23.1.5) etā vā aryalagṛhapataya ārūṇihotāraḥ subhagāsūpayanti te sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.1.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, a complete-<s>stoma</s> <s>Atirātra</s>, four <s>Chandomā</s> days, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.1.2) This is the completed twelve-day rite as a thirteen-night session.
(PB 23.1.3) This is the same, since the departure and concluding <s>Atirātras</s> are one. Whatever desire they desire, they attain it by these.
(PB 23.1.4) But the speech of the householder tends to falter. Since the complete-<s>stoma</s> <s>Atirātra</s> is in the middle, thereby the speech of the householder does not falter.
(PB 23.1.5) Those Āryala-householders, the <s>Āruṇihotars</s>, practice these with the Fortunate Ones. They attained all prosperity. They who practice these attain all prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 23.2.1) atirātro dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 23.2.2) vāg vā eṣā pratāyate yad eṣa dvādaśāhas tāṃ vicchindyur yan madhye 'tirātraṃ kuryuḥ
(PB 23.2.3) yad upariṣṭād vratam upayanti na vācaṃ vicchindanty āpnuvanti trayodaśaṃ māsam
(PB 23.2.4) etā vai pratiṣṭhitās trayodaśa rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.2.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, and the <s>Mahāvrata</s> and <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.2.2) Speech is stretched out in this twelve-day rite. They would cut it off if they were to place an <s>Atirātra</s> in the middle.
(PB 23.2.3) Since they practice the observance at the end, they do not cut off speech. They attain the thirteenth month.
(PB 23.2.4) These thirteen nights are established. They who practice these become established.

body.text:
(PB 23.3.1) atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 23.3.2) kāmasanayo vā etā rātrayaḥ
(PB 23.3.3) virāḍh ḍhi daśātmaikādaśī prajā dvādaśī paśavas trayodaśī kāmāya caturdaśī
(PB 23.3.4) sarvān evaitābhiḥ kāmān avarūndhate
(PB 23.3.5) etā vāva bradhnasya viṣṭapo yad etau trayastriṃśau madhyataḥ saṃdhīyete tena bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ rohanti
(PB 23.3.6) dviḥ pṛṣṭhāny upayanty abhipūrvam evaitābhir annādyaṃ dadhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.3.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, a thirty-three-initial <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.3.2) These nights fulfill desires.
(PB 23.3.3) The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; the self is the eleventh; offspring the twelfth; cattle the thirteenth; desire the fourteenth.
(PB 23.3.4) By these they attain all desires.
(PB 23.3.5) These are the footsteps of the Ruddy One (<s>Bradhna</s>, the Sun). When these two thirty-three-day periods are joined in the middle, by that they ascend to the abode of the Ruddy One.
(PB 23.3.6) They practice the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> days twice. By these they place food-eating in succession.

body.text:
(PB 23.4.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha āyur gaur jyotir atirātraḥ
(PB 23.4.2) yāṃs talpe vodake vā vivāhe vā mīmāṃseraṃs ta etā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.4.3) yat jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ prajñātāṃ stomān upayanti
(PB 23.4.4) imān eva lokān eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhānti
(PB 23.4.5) atha yat pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho madhyato bhavaty eṣu vāva devatalpo devatalpam eva tad ārohanti talpyā bhavanti
(PB 23.4.6) pravasīyasas talpam āpnuvanti
(PB 23.4.7) atha yad āyur gaur jyotir atirātro yeneto yanti tena punar āyanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.4.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Jyotis</s>-<s>Gau</s>-<s>Āyus</s> three-day rite, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, an <s>Āyus</s>-<s>Gau</s>-<s>Jyotis</s> <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.4.2) Those whom they would examine at the bed, at the water, or at the marriage — they should practice these.
(PB 23.4.3) When the <s>Jyotis</s>-<s>Gau</s>-<s>Āyus</s> three-day rite uses recognized <s>stomas</s>, they practice them.
(PB 23.4.4) They become established in these very worlds.
(PB 23.4.5) When the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite is in the middle — this is the divine bed; they ascend the divine bed. They become bedworthy.
(PB 23.4.6) They attain the excellent bed.
(PB 23.4.7) When the <s>Āyus</s>-<s>Gau</s>-<s>Jyotis</s> <s>Atirātra</s> — by the same way they went, they return.

body.text:
(PB 23.5.1) atirātro gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.5.2) yad gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī bhavato mithunau stomāv upayanti prajātyai
(PB 23.5.3) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 23.5.4) etā vai pratiṣṭhitāś caturdaśa rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.5.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the <s>Gau</s> and <s>Āyus</s> as two days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.5.2) Since the <s>Gau</s> and <s>Āyus</s> are two days, they practice paired <s>stomas</s> — for procreation.
(PB 23.5.3) The ten days of the twelve-day rite — they practice unbroken speech — for procreation.
(PB 23.5.4) These fourteen nights are established. They who practice these become established.

body.text:
(PB 23.6.1) atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho mahāvrataṃ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 23.6.2) etābhir vai devā devatvam agacchan devatvaṃ gacchanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.6.3) etad vai devānāṃ sattraṃ tad adyāpi devāḥ sattram āsate
(PB 23.6.4) paurṇamāsy atirātro 'tha yāni ṣaḍ ahāni sa pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaha ekāṣṭakā mahāvratam atha yāni ṣaḍ ahāni sa pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho 'māvāsyātirātraḥ
(PB 23.6.5) tasmāt tarhi manuṣyāṇāṃ na suto devānāṃ hi tarhi sutaḥ pratyakṣam evaitābhir devatā abhyārohanti
(PB 23.6.6) pratinodāt tu bhayyam itaram anupakṣo dīkṣerann apratinodāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.6.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite, a thirty-three-initial <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.6.2) By these the gods attained divinity. They who practice these attain divinity.
(PB 23.6.3) This is the <s>sattra</s> (session) of the gods. Even now the gods sit in session.
(PB 23.6.4) The full-moon <s>Atirātra</s>; then the six days — that is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> is the <s>Mahāvrata</s>; then the six days — that is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; the new-moon <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.6.5) Therefore at that time there is no pressing of <s>Soma</s> among humans, for at that time it is the gods' pressing. By these they ascend directly to the gods.
(PB 23.6.6) But there is fear of repulsion. Therefore they should consecrate the next period without repulsion.

body.text:
(PB 23.7.1) atirātras trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomo jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaha āyur gaur jyotir atirātraḥ
(PB 23.7.2) kṣatraṃ vā etā rātrayo 'bhinirvadanti
(PB 23.7.3) brahmavarcasakāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.7.4) yat trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomo bhavati brahma tad yaśasārdhayati
(PB 23.7.5) brahma vai trivṛt
(PB 23.7.6) yat jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ prajñātān stomān upayantīmān eva lokān eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanty atha yat pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho madhyato bhavaty annaṃ vai pṛṣṭāny annam eva tan madhyato dhīyate tasmān madhye sad annaṃ dhinoty atha yad āyur gaur jyotir atirātro yeneto yanti tena punar āyanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.7.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a three-fold <s>Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus</s> three-day rite, a six-day rite with <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], an <s>Āyus-Gaus-Jyotis</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.7.2) These nights indeed declare the <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior power).
(PB 23.7.3) Those desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmic splendor) should undertake this.
(PB 23.7.4) Because there is a three-fold <s>Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma</s>, thereby one prospers in <s>Brahman</s> and glory.
(PB 23.7.5) <s>Brahman</s> indeed

body.text:
(PB 23.8.1) trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomo jyotir gaur āyus tryaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.8.2) anyasmai vai kāmāya sattram anyasmai yajño na tat sattreṇāpnoti yasmaikaṃ yajño na tad yajñenāpnoti yasmaikaṃ sattram
(PB 23.8.3) yad anyato 'tirātrās tena yajño 'tha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni tena sattram
(PB 23.8.4) ubhāv evaitābhiḥ kāmāv avarūndhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.8.1) A three-fold <s>Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus</s> three-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.8.2) A <s>sattra</s> serves one purpose, a sacrifice another. What one does not obtain by a <s>sattra</s>, one obtains by a sacrifice; what one does not obtain by a sacrifice, one obtains by a <s>sattra</s>.
(PB 23.8.3) Because there are <s>Atirātras</s> on either side, thereby it is a sacrifice. And because there are the ten days of the twelve-day rite,

body.text:
(PB 23.9.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ prajākāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.9.2) etābhir vai prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata pra prajayā pra paśubhir jāyante ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.9.3) yat jyotir gaur āyus tryahaḥ prajātān stomān upayantīmān eva lokān eṣv eva lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 23.9.4) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 23.9.5) etā vai pratiṣṭhitāḥ pañcadaśa rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.9.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus</s> three-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring offspring should undertake this.
(PB 23.9.2) By these, <s>Prajāpati</s> created offspring. Those who undertake these prosper with offspring and with cattle.
(PB 23.9.3) Because there is a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus</s> three-day rite, one approaches the established <s>stomas</s> — these very worlds — and becomes established in them.

body.text:
(PB 23.10.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ
(PB 23.10.2) etābhir vā indraḥ paramāṃ vijitiṃ vyajayata paramām evaitābhir vijitiṃ vijayante
(PB 23.10.3) pañcadaśo vai vajro na vā agṛhītena vajreṇa vīryaṃ karoti yā ṣoḍaśy ārambhaṇam eva tad gṛhītena vajreṇa vīryaṃ karoti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.10.1) These same [rites] include the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
(PB 23.10.2) By these, <s>Indra</s> won the supreme conquest. By these they win the supreme conquest.
(PB 23.10.3) The fifteen-fold is indeed the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>). One does not accomplish valor with an ungrasped thunderbolt. The sixteenth [verse] serves as the grasping. With the grasped thunderbolt one accomplishes valor.

body.text:
(PB 23.11.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyur gaur āyuḥ pañcāho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.11.2) etābhir vai prajāpatir anantāṃ śriyam ajayad anantā vā etā yat pañcāhavidhāḥ
(PB 23.11.3) yat pañcāho 'nantād eva prajāyante
(PB 23.11.4) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 23.11.5) etā vai pratiṣṭhitāḥ saptadaśa rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.11.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus-Gaus-Āyus</s> five-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.11.2) By these, <s>Prajāpati</s> won unlimited glory. These are indeed unlimited, being five-day configurations.
(PB 23.11.3) Because there is a five-day rite, they are born from the unlimited.
(PB 23.11.4) And because there are the ten days of the twelve-day rite, one approaches uninterrupted speech.

body.text:
(PB 23.12.1) atirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.12.2) devā vai mṛtyor abibhayus te prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etenāṣṭādaśarātreṇāmṛtatvaṃ prāyacchat
(PB 23.12.3) etad vāva manuṣyasyāmṛtatvaṃ yat sarvam āyur eti vasīyān bhavati
(PB 23.12.4) sarvam āyur yanti vasīyāṃso bhavanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.12.5) dvir vā etā nava nava prāṇā abhipūrvam evaitābhir āyur dadhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.12.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.12.2) The gods feared death. They ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. He bestowed immortality upon them through this eighteen-night rite.
(PB 23.12.3) This indeed is the immortality of a human: that one lives a full lifespan and becomes prosperous.
(PB 23.12.4) They live a full lifespan and become prosperous,

body.text:
(PB 23.13.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ
(PB 23.13.2) etābhir vai vāyur āraṇyānāṃ paśunām ādhipatyaṃ gacchanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.13.3) mṛgasatraṃ vā etat
(PB 23.13.4) etābhir vā āraṇyāḥ paśavo nākṛtāḥ prajāyante
(PB 23.13.5) anākṛtam eṣāṃ prajāyate ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.13.1) These same [rites] include the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
(PB 23.13.2) By these, <s>Vāyu</s> attained lordship over the wild animals. Those who undertake these attain [the same].
(PB 23.13.3) This is indeed the <s>Mṛgasattra</s> (hunt-session).
(PB 23.13.4) By these the wild animals are born without being shaped.
(PB 23.13.5) The unshaped is born for those who undertake these.

body.text:
(PB 23.14.1) atrirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'bhijic ca viśvajic ca dve ahanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.14.2) purūṣakāmā upeyur etābhir vai prajāpatiḥ purūṣam asṛjata
(PB 23.14.3) sa sarvasyānnādyasyādhipatyam agacchat sarvasyānnādyasyādhipatyaṃ gacchanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.14.4) purūṣasatraṃ vā etat
(PB 23.14.5) viṃśo vai purūṣo daśa hi hastyā aṅgulyo daśa pādyāḥ
(PB 23.14.6) yad etā viṃśatī rātrayo bhavanty eṣv evaitābhir lokeṣu purūṣaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayanti
(PB 23.14.7) etā vai pratiṣṭhitā viṃśatī rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.14.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, an <s>Abhijit</s> and <s>Viśvajit</s> as two days, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.14.2) Those desiring a man (<s>puruṣa</s>) should undertake this. By these, <s>Prajāpati</s> created man.
(PB 23.14.3) He attained lordship over all food. Those who undertake these attain lordship over all food.
(PB 23.14.4) Man

body.text:
(PB 23.15.1) atirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ paśukāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.15.2) etābhir vā ādityāḥ sapta grāmyān paśūn udasṛjanta paśūn evaitābhir utsṛjanti (utsṛjante)
(PB 23.15.3) trir vai sapta saptādityāḥ
(PB 23.15.4) paśava ādityāḥ
(PB 23.15.5) ādityā asmiṃl loke ṛddhā ādityā amuṣmin
(PB 23.15.6) paśavo 'smin ṛtavo 'muṣmin
(PB 23.15.7) ubhayor anayor lokayor ṛdhnuvanti devaloke ca manuṣyaloke ca ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.15.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring cattle should undertake this.
(PB 23.15.2) By these, the <s>Ādityas</s> released the seven domestic animals. By these they release cattle.
(PB 23.15.3) Three times seven — seven are the <s>Ādityas</s>.
(PB 23.15.4) Cattle are the <s>Ādityas</s>.
(PB 23.15.5) The <s>Ādityas</s>

body.text:
(PB 23.16.1) atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahas trayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmānaḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇo 'tirātro brahmavarcasakāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.16.2) svarbhānur vā āsuraḥ sūryaṃ tamasāvidhyat tasmai devāḥ prāyaścittim aicchaṃs ta etā avindaṃs tābhir asmāt tamo 'pāghnan
(PB 23.16.3) apa tamo ghnate ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.16.4) saumāpauṣaṃ paśum upālabhyam ālabheran
(PB 23.16.5) somo vai brāhmaṇaḥ paśavaḥ pūṣā svām eva tad devatāṃ paśubhir baṃhayante tvacam evākrata
(PB 23.16.6) manor ṛcaḥ sāmidhenyo bhavanti
(PB 23.16.7) manur vai yat kiṃ cāvadat tad bheṣajaṃ bheṣajatāyai
(PB 23.16.8) naidādhīya upeyuḥ
(PB 23.16.9) tad dhy eṣa prati tejiṣṭhaṃ tapati
(PB 23.16.10) kilāsatvāt tu bhayam ati hy ebhyo 'pahanti
(PB 23.16.11) etā vā ugradevo rājanir upait sa kilāso 'bhavat
(PB 23.16.12) akilāso bhavati ya evaṃ vidvānetā upaiti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.16.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day rite, three days with <s>Svarasāman</s> (tonal chant), the <s>Divākīrtya</s> (day-celebrating) day, three days with <s>Svarasāman</s>, a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day rite, with a thirty-three-fold opening, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (brahmic splendor) should undertake this.
(PB 23.16.2) <s>Svarbhānu</s>, the <s>Asura</s>, pierced the sun with darkness. The gods sought an expiation for that. They found these [rites]. By them they drove away the darkness from it.

body.text:
(PB 23.17.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryaho 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś cānnādyakāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.17.2) pañcartavo dvādaśa māsās traya ime lokā asāv āditya ekaviṃśo 'nnaṃ dvāviṃśam ebhyo lokebhyaḥ saṃvatsarād amuṣmād ādityād annādyam avarundhate ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.17.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus</s> three-day rite, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring food-sovereignty should undertake this.
