(PB 23.17.2) Five seasons, twelve months, three worlds, yonder sun — [that makes] twenty-one. Food is the twenty-second. From these worlds, from the year, from yonder sun, those who undertake these obtain food-sovereignty.

body.text:
(PB 23.18.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyur gaur āyuḥ pañcāho 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ pratiṣṭhākāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.18.2) etābhir vai prajāpatir eṣu lokeṣu pratyatiṣṭhat
(PB 23.18.3) yad etās trayoviṃśatī rātrayo bhavanti traya ime lokā eṣv evaitābhir lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 23.18.4) etā vai pratiṣṭhitās trayoviṃśatī rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.18.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a <s>Jyotis-Gaus-Āyus-Gaus-Āyus</s> five-day rite, an <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite, the ten days of a twelve-day rite, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring firm establishment should undertake this.
(PB 23.18.2) By these, <s>Prajāpati</s> became firmly established in these worlds.
(PB 23.18.3) Because these amount to twenty-three nights — these worlds are three — by these one becomes firmly established in these very worlds.

body.text:
(PB 23.19.1) atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ stomaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśam ahar aniruktam upahavyasya tantre kḷpta tasya kaṇvarathantaraṃ madhyandine 'tha trayastriṃśa niruktaṃ triṇavaṃ dve ekaviṃśe triṇavaṃ trayastriṃśam ahar niruktaṃ trayastriṃśam ahar aniruktam pṛṣṭhayaḥ stomaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pratyaṅ trivṛd ahar aniruktaṃ jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo 'tirātraḥ
(PB 23.19.2) etābhir vai devāḥ svarge loke samasīdan svarge loke sīdāmety etāḥ
(PB 23.19.3) etā vāva bradhnasya viṣṭapo yad ete trayastiṃśā madhyataḥ saṃdhīyante tena bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ rohanti
(PB 23.19.4) madhyataḥ pṛṣṭhāny upayanty annaṃ vai pṛṣṭhāny annam eva tan madhyato dhīyate tasmān madhye sad annaṃ dhinoti
(PB 23.19.5) saptāhā vā ete
(PB 23.19.6) ato vai prajāḥ prajāyante
(PB 23.19.7) pra prajayā pra paśubhirjāyante ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.19.8) apaśavyaṃ vā etat sattraṃ yad acchandomaṃ yat saptāhās tena chandomavatyas tena paśavyāḥ
(PB 23.19.9) trayastriṃśas trayastriṃśam anveti trivṛt trivṛtam agrād agraṃ rohanti yat trayastriṃśas trayastriṃśam anveti prāṇāt prāṇeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 23.19.10) yat trivṛt trivṛtam
(PB 23.19.11) vilomāno vā etā rātrayo yat jyotir agniṣṭoma utthānīyam ahar bhavaty akḷptasya kḷptyai
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.19.1) <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite), <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>-<s>stoma</s> six-day period, thirty-three-fold undefined day, arranged in the framework of <s>Upahavya</s>; its <s>Kaṇva-Rathantara</s> is at midday. Then: thirty-three-fold defined day, <s>Triṇava</s>, two twenty-one-fold, <s>Triṇava</s>, thirty-three-fold defined day, thirty-three-fold undefined day. <s>Pṛṣṭha</s>-<s>stoma</s> six-day period reversed. Threefold undefined day. <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.19.2) With these the gods sat in the heavenly world. 'Let us sit in the heavenly world' — such are these.
(PB 23.19.3) These are indeed the abode of <s>Bradhna</s> (the sun). When these thirty-three-fold days are joined in the middle, by that they ascend to the abode of <s>Bradhna</s>.
(PB 23.19.4) The <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants approach from the middle. Food is the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> chants. Food is placed in the middle. Therefore one sitting in the middle shakes out food.
(PB 23.19.5) These are indeed seven-day periods.
(PB 23.19.6) From these, offspring are born.
(PB 23.19.7) They prosper with offspring and with cattle, those who adopt these.
(PB 23.19.8) This <s>sattra</s> would be without cattle if it were without <s>chandomas</s> (metrical days). Because of the seven-day periods, they have <s>chandomas</s>. Therefore they have cattle.
(PB 23.19.9) Thirty-three follows thirty-three, threefold follows threefold — from tip to tip they ascend. When thirty-three follows thirty-three, they become established in breath after breath.
(PB 23.19.10) When threefold follows threefold —
(PB 23.19.11) These nights go against the grain. When the <s>Jyotis</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the concluding day — that is for the arrangement of the unarranged.

body.text:
(PB 23.20.1) atirātro dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ prajākāmā vā paśukāmā vopeyuḥ
(PB 23.20.2) kḷptādvai yoneḥ prajāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante yat kḷptau ṣaḍahāv upayanti kḷptādeva yoneḥ prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāyante
(PB 23.20.3) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 23.20.4) etā vai pratiṣṭhitāś caturviṃśatī rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.20.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring offspring or those desiring cattle should adopt these.
(PB 23.20.2) From a well-arranged womb, offspring and cattle are born. When they adopt well-arranged six-day periods, they are born from a well-arranged womb with offspring and cattle.
(PB 23.20.3) And the ten days of the twelve-day rite — they adopt uninterrupted speech, for procreation.
(PB 23.20.4) These are indeed twenty-four established nights. They become firmly established, those who adopt these.

body.text:
(PB 23.21.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ
(PB 23.21.2) etābhir vai prajāpatiḥ sarvam annādyam avārūndha
(PB 23.21.3) caturviṃśatiḥ saṃvatsarasyārdhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ pañcaviṃśo 'nnaṃ vrataṃ saṃvatsarād etābhir annādyam avarūndhate ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.21.1) These same with the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great vow).
(PB 23.21.2) With these <s>Prajāpati</s> secured all food.
(PB 23.21.3) Twenty-four are the half-months of the year. The year is the twenty-fifth. Food is the vow. With these they secure food from the year, those who adopt these.

body.text:
(PB 23.22.1) atirātro gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍāhau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.22.2) ṛtavo na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta etābhiḥ pratyatiṣṭhan pratiṣṭhākāmā upeyuḥ praty eva tiṣṭhanti
(PB 23.22.3) ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtuṣv evaitābhiḥ pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 23.22.4) yad gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī bhavato mithunau stomāv upayanti prajātyai
(PB 23.22.5) yat kḷptau ṣaḍahāv upayanti kḷptyā eva
(PB 23.22.6) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 23.22.7) etā vai pratiṣṭhitā ṣaḍviṃśatī rātrayaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.23.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryaho dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātra ṛddhikāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.23.2) etābhir vai nakṣatrāṇi sarvāmṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 23.23.3) yad etā saptaviṃśatī rātrayo bhavanti saptaviṃśatir nakṣatrāṇi nakṣatrasammitā vā etā rātrayo nakṣatrāṇām evardhim ṛdhnuvanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.22.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Gaus</s> (cow) and <s>Āyus</s> (life) — two days, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.22.2) The seasons were not firmly established. With these they became established. Those desiring firm establishment should adopt them. They indeed become established.
(PB 23.22.3) There are six seasons. With these they become established in the seasons.
(PB 23.22.4) When <s>Gaus</s> and <s>Āyus</s> are two days, they adopt paired <s>stomas</s> — for procreation.
(PB 23.22.5) When they adopt well-arranged six-day periods — for the sake of arrangement.
(PB 23.22.6) And the ten days of the twelve-day rite — they adopt uninterrupted speech, for procreation.
(PB 23.22.7) These are indeed twenty-six established nights. They become firmly established, those who adopt these.
(PB 23.23.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Jyotis</s> (light), <s>Gaus</s>, <s>Āyus</s> — a three-day period, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring prosperity should adopt these.
(PB 23.23.2) With these the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) attained all prosperity. They attain all prosperity, those who adopt these.
(PB 23.23.3) When these are twenty-seven nights — twenty-seven are the <s>nakṣatras</s>. These nights are measured by the <s>nakṣatras</s>. They attain the prosperity of the <s>nakṣatras</s>.

body.text: (PB 23.24.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ paśukāmā upeyur yad etā aṣṭāviṃśatī rātrayo bhavanty aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśa evaitābhiḥ paśūn avarūndhate
body.translated_text: (PB 23.24.1) These same with the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. Those desiring cattle should adopt them. When these are twenty-eight nights — cattle have eight hooves — they secure cattle hoof by hoof with these nights.

body.text:
(PB 23.25.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyur gaur āyuḥ pañcāho dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 23.25.2) etābhir vai prajāpatir anantāṃ śriyam ajayat
(PB 23.25.3) anantā vā etā yā ekayānatriṃśann eti vai vāco 'nantam
(PB 23.25.4) yad etā ekayānatriṃśad rātrayo bhavanty anantām evaitābhiḥ śriyaṃ jayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.25.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaus</s>, <s>Āyus</s>, <s>Gaus</s>, <s>Āyus</s> — a five-day period, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 23.25.2) With these <s>Prajāpati</s> conquered infinite glory.
(PB 23.25.3) These are infinite, being thirty-one. The infinite extends beyond speech.
(PB 23.25.4) When these are thirty-one nights, they conquer infinite glory with these.

body.text:
(PB 23.26.1) atirātras trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātro 'nnādyakāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.26.2) parokṣam anyāni sattrāṇi virājaṃ sampadyante pratyakṣam etā virājaṃ sampannāḥ
(PB 23.26.3) pratyakṣam etābhir annādyam avarūndhate ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.26.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring food should adopt these.
(PB 23.26.2) Other <s>sattras</s> achieve the <s>Virāj</s> indirectly. These achieve the <s>Virāj</s> directly.
(PB 23.26.3) They directly secure food with these, those who adopt them.

body.text:
(PB 23.27.1) etā eva samahāvratā etābhir vai prajāpatir abhipūrvam annādyam avārūndha
(PB 23.27.2) annaṃ virāḍ annaṃ vratam
(PB 23.27.3) abhipūrvam evaitābhir annādyam avarūndhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.27.1) These same with the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. With these <s>Prajāpati</s> secured food in succession.
(PB 23.27.2) Food is the <s>Virāj</s>. Food is the vow.
(PB 23.27.3) They secure food in succession with these.

body.text:
(PB 23.28.1) atirātro gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ paśukāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 23.28.2) anuṣṭub vā etā rātrayaḥ
(PB 23.28.3) dvātriṃśad akṣarānuṣṭup
(PB 23.28.4) vāg anuṣṭup
(PB 23.28.5) catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ
(PB 23.28.6) vācā paśūn dādhāra
(PB 23.28.7) etābhī rātrībhiḥ
(PB 23.28.8) tasmāt te vācā siddhā vācāhūtā ā yanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 23.28.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Gaus</s> and <s>Āyus</s> — two days, three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring cattle should adopt these.
(PB 23.28.2) These nights are of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter.
(PB 23.28.3) The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> has thirty-two syllables.
(PB 23.28.4) Speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.
(PB 23.28.5) Cattle are four-footed.
(PB 23.28.6) With speech he upheld the cattle.
(PB 23.28.7) With these nights.
(PB 23.28.8) Therefore they, perfected by speech and called by speech, come.

body.text:
(PB 24.1.1) atirātras trayaḥ pañcāhā viśvajid atirātra ekaḥ pañcāho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 24.1.2) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs tā etābhiḥ pratyatiṣṭhann ime lokā na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta etābhiḥ pratyatiṣṭhan pratyatiṣṭhan pratiṣṭhākāmā upeyuḥ praty eva tiṣṭhanti
(PB 24.1.3) arūpeṇa vā etāḥ sarūpā arūpeṇa prajāḥ sarūpā arūpeṇeme lokāḥ sarūpā yad rathantarasya lokaṃ bṛhad āpadyate bṛhato rathantaram arūpeṇaivaibhyas tat sarūpaṃ prajanayanti
(PB 24.1.4) lupyate vā etat ṣaṣṭham ahar yat pañcāhān upayanti nartavaḥ kalpanteḥ yat pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍahas tena ṣaṣṭham ahar na lupyate tenartavaḥ kalpante
(PB 24.1.5) atha yāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni tena pañcāhebhyo na yanti
(PB 24.1.6) ūdhar vā antarikṣaṃ stanāv abhito 'nena vā eṣa devebhyo dugdhe 'munā prajābhyaḥ
(PB 24.1.7) idaṃ vā antarikṣaṃ viyad imau stanāv abhitaḥ
(PB 24.1.8) tad abhyanūktā
(PB 24.1.9) triṃśati trayaḥ paro ye devā barhir āsata vyann aha dvitā taneti
(PB 24.1.10) ūdhar vai madhyamo 'tirātraḥ stanāv abhitaḥ
(PB 24.1.11) yad eṣo 'natirātraḥ syād ūdhaḥ pratiharet
(PB 24.1.12) tasmād atirātraḥ kārya ūdhaso 'pratihārāya
(PB 24.1.13) trayastriṃśad devatā etābhir ārdhnuvaṃs tenardhis tasmād etābhir yajanta ṛdhyā eva
(PB 24.1.14) nānā brahmasāmāny upayanty ahnā nānā vīryatāyai nānaiva vīryāṇy avarūndhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.1.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, three five-day periods, <s>Viśvajit</s> <s>Atirātra</s>, one five-day period, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.1.2) <s>Prajāpati</s> created beings. They were not firmly established. With these they became established. These worlds were not established. With these they became established. Those desiring establishment should adopt them. They indeed become established.
(PB 24.1.3) With a dissimilar form these become similar. With a dissimilar form beings become similar. With a dissimilar form these worlds become similar. When the <s>Rathantara</s>'s place is obtained by the <s>Bṛhat</s>, and the <s>Bṛhat</s>'s by the <s>Rathantara</s> — with dissimilar form they generate similarity for them.
(PB 24.1.4) The sixth day is lost when they adopt five-day periods. The seasons do not fit. When the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day period is adopted, the sixth day is not lost and the seasons fit.
(PB 24.1.5) And the ten days of the twelve-day rite — by that they do not depart from the five-day periods.
(PB 24.1.6) The atmosphere is the udder; the two teats are on either side. With this one he milks for the gods, with that one for beings.
(PB 24.1.7) This atmosphere is the space between. These two teats are on either side.
(PB 24.1.8) That has been declared in verse:
(PB 24.1.9) 'Thirty and three beyond — those gods who sat upon the sacred grass — stretched the body twofold.'
(PB 24.1.10) The middle <s>Atirātra</s> is the udder; the teats are on either side.
(PB 24.1.11) If this were not an <s>Atirātra</s>, it would strike back the udder.
(PB 24.1.12) Therefore an <s>Atirātra</s> should be performed, to prevent the striking back of the udder.
(PB 24.1.13) There are thirty-three deities. With these they prospered. Therefore that is prosperity. Those who sacrifice with these prosper.
(PB 24.1.14) They adopt different <s>Brahma-Sāmans</s> day by day — for the diversity of vigor. They secure diverse vigors.

body.text:
(PB 24.2.1) atirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirāś ca
(PB 24.2.2) ādityāś cāṅgirasaś caitat sattraṃ samadadhatādityānām ekaviṃśatir aṅgirasāṃ dvādaśāha ādityā asmiṃl loka ṛddhā ādityā amuṣminn aṅgiraso 'sminn aṅgiraso 'muṣmin dvayaṃ sattraṃ yāvad dvayena sattreṇardhnuvanti tāvaty etāsām ṛddhiḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.2.1) <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day period, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day period, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day period, ten days of the twelve-day rite, <s>Mahāvrata</s> and <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.2.2) The <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s> established this <s>sattra</s> together. The <s>Ādityas</s> contributed twenty-one days, the <s>Aṅgirases</s> the twelve-day rite. The <s>Ādityas</s> prospered in this world, the <s>Ādityas</s> in that world; the <s>Aṅgirases</s> in this world, the <s>Aṅgirases</s> in that world. The <s>sattra</s> is twofold. As much as they prosper with the twofold <s>sattra</s>, that much is the prosperity of these.

body.text:
(PB 24.3.1) atirātras trayaḥ pañcāhā viśvajid atirātras trayaḥ pañcāhā atirātraḥ
(PB 24.3.2) apaśavyaṃ vā etat sattraṃ yad acchandomaṃ yadviśvajiti chandomān upayanti tena chandomavatyas tena paśavyāḥ
(PB 24.3.3) pakṣiṇyo vā etā rātrayo yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayante tam etābhir abhyaśnuvate yatra yatra hi pakṣī kāmayate tat tad abhyaśnute
(PB 24.3.4) trivṛtā prayanti trivṛtodyanti prāṇā vai trivṛt stomānāṃ prāṇair eva prayanti prāṇeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.3.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, three five-day periods, a <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering), an <s>Atirātra</s>, three five-day periods, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.3.2) This <s>sattra</s> is without cattle-producing power when it lacks <s>chandomā</s> days. When they reach the <s>chandomā</s> days in the <s>Viśvajit</s>, thereby they become possessed of <s>chandomā</s>, thereby they become cattle-producing.
(PB 24.3.3) These nights are winged. Whatever desire they desire, they achieve it with these. For wherever a winged creature desires to go, it reaches there.
(PB 24.3.4) They set forth with the nine-fold and rise up with the nine-fold. Breath is the nine-fold among <s>stomas</s>. With breaths they set forth, in breaths they are established.

body.text:
(PB 24.4.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryahas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś cardhikāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 24.4.2) etābhir vai prajāpatiḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.4.3) yad etāś catustriṃśad rātrayo bhavanti trayastriṃśad devatāḥ prajāpatiś catustriṃśo devatānāṃ prajāpater evardhim ṛdhnuvanti
(PB 24.5.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyuḥ pañcāhas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ paśukāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 24.5.2) yad etāḥ pañcātriṃśad rātrayo bhavanti pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśūn evaitābhir avarundhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.4.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the <s>Jyotis</s> (light), the <s>Gau</s> (cow), and the <s>Āyus</s> (life) three-day period, three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring prosperity should undertake these.
(PB 24.4.2) With these, <s>Prajāpati</s> attained all prosperity. Those who undertake these attain all prosperity.
(PB 24.4.3) Because these are thirty-four nights, and there are thirty-three deities with <s>Prajāpati</s> as the thirty-fourth — they attain the prosperity of the deities and of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 24.5.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the <s>Jyotis</s>, the <s>Gau</s>, and the <s>Āyus</s> five-day period, three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring cattle should undertake these.
(PB 24.5.2) Because these are thirty-five nights, and cattle are five-fold (<s>pāṅkta</s>) — with these they obtain cattle.

body.text:
(PB 24.6.1) atirātraś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ paśukāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 24.6.2) etābhir vai devā ādityam astabhnuvann ādityalokaṃ jayanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.6.3) bṛhatī vā etā rātrayaḥ svārājyaṃ chandasāṃ bṛhatī yo vai paśūnāṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchati sa svārājyaṃ gacchati pra svārājyam āpnuvanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.6.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring cattle should undertake these.
(PB 24.6.2) With these the <s>devas</s> propped up the sun. Those who undertake these win the world of the sun.
(PB 24.6.3) These nights are of the <s>Bṛhatī</s> type. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> is the sovereign splendor of the meters. He who attains the abundance of cattle attains sovereign splendor. Those who undertake these attain sovereign splendor.

body.text:
(PB 24.7.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ
(PB 24.7.2) etābhir vai prajāpatir ubhau kāmāv avārūndhānnaṃ vrataṃ paśavo bṛhaty ubhāv evaitābhiḥ kāmāv avarūndhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.7.1) The same, with the <s>Mahāvrata</s> added.
(PB 24.7.2) With these, <s>Prajāpati</s> obtained both desires — food and vow, cattle and the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. With these one obtains both desires.

body.text:
(PB 24.8.1) atirātro gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ paśukāmā upeyuḥ spaṣṭo 'rthaḥ
(PB 24.8.2) yad etā aṣṭātriṃśad rātrayo bhavanty aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśa evaitābhiḥ paśun avarūndhate
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.8.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the <s>Gau</s> and <s>Āyus</s> as two days, four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>. Those desiring cattle should undertake these. The meaning is clear.
(PB 24.8.2) Because these are thirty-eight nights, and cattle have eight hooves — by hooves they obtain cattle with these.

body.text:
(PB 24.9.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryahaś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 24.9.2) etābhir vai prajāpatir anantā śriyam ajayad anantā vā etā yā ekayānacatvāriṃśan neti vai vāco 'nantam
(PB 24.9.3) yad etā ekayānacatvāriṃśad rātrayo bhavanty anantām evaitābhiḥ śriyaṃ jayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.9.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, the <s>Jyotis</s>, the <s>Gau</s>, and the <s>Āyus</s> three-day period, four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.9.2) With these, <s>Prajāpati</s> won infinite glory. These are infinite, being forty-one. 'Not' (<s>na</s>) is the infinite of speech.
(PB 24.9.3) Because these are forty-one nights, with these they win infinite glory.

body.text:
(PB 24.10.1) etā eva samahāvratāḥ
(PB 24.10.2) sarvā vā etā virājo daśinī prathamā viṃśinī dvitīyā triṃśinī tṛtīyaiṣā vai paramā virāṭ yac catvāriṃśad rātrayaḥ paṅktir vai paramā virāṭ
(PB 24.10.3) paramāyām eva virāji pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.10.1) The same, with the <s>Mahāvrata</s> added.
(PB 24.10.2) All these are <s>Virājs</s> (sovereign meters): the first has ten, the second twenty, the third thirty. The supreme <s>Virāj</s> has forty nights. The <s>Paṅkti</s> (five-fold) is the supreme <s>Virāj</s>.
(PB 24.10.3) They are established in the supreme <s>Virāj</s>.

body.text:
(PB 24.11.1) atirātras trīṇi trivṛnty ahāny agniṣṭomamukhāny atirātro daśa pañcadaśā ukthyāḥ ṣoḍaśimad daśamam ahar atirātro dvādaśa saptadaśā ukthyā atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhayaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro dvādaśaikaviṃśā ukthyā atirātraḥ
(PB 24.11.2) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā avidhṛtā asañjānānā anyonyām ādaṃs tena prajāpatir aśocat sa etā apaśyat tato vā idaṃ vyāvartata gāvo 'bhavann aśvā aśvāḥ purūṣāḥ purūṣā mṛgā mṛgāḥ
(PB 24.11.3) vi pāpmanā vartante ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.11.4) yad atirātrā antarā vidhṛtyai tasmān netara itarasmin reto dadhāti
(PB 24.11.5) yat pṛṣṭhyāḥ stomāḥ sa sṛṣṭās tasmād ajāvayaḥ paśūnāṃ saha caranti tasmād u gardabho vaḍavāyā reto dadhāti
(PB 24.11.6) apaśavyaṃ vā etat sattraṃ yad acchandomaṃ yat sandhiṣāmasu chandāṃsy upayanti tena chandomavatyas tena paśavyāḥ
(PB 24.11.7) gāyatrīṣu jarābodhīyam uṣṇikṣu śrudhyam anuṣṭupsu nānadaṃ bṛhatīṣu rathantaraṃ paṅktiṣu rāyovājīyaṃ triṣṭupsv auśanaṃ jagatīṣu kāvam
(PB 24.11.8) ūrdhvāni chandāṃsy upayanty anapabhraṃśāya
(PB 24.11.9) prāṇo vai svaro yat svarāv antato bhavatas tasmāt dvāv antataḥ prāṇau
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.11.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, three nine-fold days with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> beginnings, an <s>Atirātra</s>; ten fifteen-fold <s>ukthya</s> days with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> on the tenth day, an <s>Atirātra</s>; twelve seventeen-fold <s>ukthya</s> days, an <s>Atirātra</s>; a <s>pṛṣṭha</s> six-day period, an <s>Atirātra</s>; twelve twenty-one-fold <s>ukthya</s> days, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.11.2) <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Being undifferentiated and not recognizing each other, they ate one another. <s>Prajāpati</s> grieved at this. He beheld these rites. From that, differentiation arose: cows became cows, horses horses, humans humans, deer deer.
(PB 24.11.3) Those who undertake these are freed from evil.
(PB 24.11.4) Because <s>Atirātras</s> are placed between, for differentiation — therefore one species does not place its seed in another.
(PB 24.11.5) Because the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> <s>stomas</s> are released — therefore goats and sheep live together among cattle, and therefore a donkey places its seed in a mare.
(PB 24.11.6) This <s>sattra</s> is without cattle-producing power when it lacks <s>chandomā</s> days. When they approach meters in the junction <s>sāmans</s>, thereby they become possessed of <s>chandomā</s>, thereby they become cattle-producing.
(PB 24.11.7) In <s>Gāyatrīs</s> the <s>Jarābodhīya</s>, in <s>Uṣṇihs</s> the <s>Śrudhya</s>, in <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s> the <s>Nānada</s>, in <s>Bṛhatīs</s> the <s>Rathantara</s>, in <s>Paṅktis</s> the <s>Rāyovājīya</s>, in <s>Triṣṭubhs</s> the <s>Auśana</s>, in <s>Jagatīs</s> the <s>Kāva</s>.
(PB 24.11.8) They approach the meters in ascending order, to prevent falling away.
(PB 24.11.9) Breath is the <s>svara</s> (melodic accent). Because two <s>svaras</s> are at the end, there are two breaths at the end.

body.text:
(PB 24.12.1) atirātrau dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau gauś cāyuś cātirātrau dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahāv abhijic ca viśvajic catirātrāv eko 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ sarvastomaś ca nava saptadaśaś cātirātro dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 24.12.2) ādityānāṃ yamātirātrāḥ
(PB 24.12.3) yamevaiṣā śrīr bhavati ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.12.4) etābhir vā ādityā dvandvam ārdhnuvan mitraś ca varūṇaś ca dhātā cāryamā cāṃśaś ca bhagaś cendraś ca vivasvāś caitāsām eva devatānām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.12.5) tad abhyanūktā
(PB 24.12.6) aṣṭau putrāso aditer ye jātās tanvaṃ pari devā upaprait saptabhiḥ parā mārtāṇḍam āsyad iti
(PB 24.12.7) ādityā asmiṃl loka ṛddhā ādityā amuṣminn ubhayor anayor lokayor ṛdhnuvanti devaloke ca manuṣyaloke ca ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.13.1) atirātraś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ sarvastomo 'tirātro dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 24.13.2) prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa rūkṣo 'bhavat taṃ rūkṣaṃ nājanan sa ā cāṅktābhi cāṅkta
(PB 24.13.3) ya ātmānaṃ neva jānīraṃs ta etā upeyur yadā cāñjate 'bhi cāñjate śubham evātman dadhate jānanty enān
(PB 24.13.4) gauggulavena prātassavane saugandhikena mādhyandine savane paitudāraveṇa tṛtīyasavane
(PB 24.13.5) agnir vai devānāṃ hautram upaiṣyañ charīram adhūnuta tasya yanmāṃ samāsīt tad guggulv abhavadyat snāva tat sugandhitejanaṃ yad asthi tat potudārv etāni vai devasurabhīṇi devasurabhibhir eva tad abhyañjate
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.12.1) Two <s>Atirātras</s>, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, the <s>Gau</s> and <s>Āyus</s>, two <s>Atirātras</s>, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, the <s>Abhijit</s> and <s>Viśvajit</s>, two <s>Atirātras</s>, one <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day period, the all-<s>stoma</s> and nine seventeen-fold, an <s>Atirātra</s>, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.12.2) These are the paired <s>Atirātras</s> of the <s>Ādityas</s>.
(PB 24.12.3) The same glory of the <s>Ādityas</s> comes to those who undertake these.
(PB 24.12.4) With these the <s>Ādityas</s> attained prosperity in pairs: <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Aṃśa</s> and <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vivasvān</s>. Those who undertake these attain the prosperity of these very deities.
(PB 24.12.5) This has been proclaimed:
(PB 24.12.6) 'Eight are the sons of <s>Aditi</s>, who were born from her body. With seven she went among the <s>devas</s>; she cast away <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>.'
(PB 24.12.7) The <s>Ādityas</s> prosper in this world, the <s>Ādityas</s> in that world. Those who undertake these prosper in both worlds — the world of the <s>devas</s> and the world of humans.
(PB 24.13.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, an all-<s>stoma</s> <s>Atirātra</s>, two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods constituting the ten days of the twelve-day rite, an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.13.2) <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. He became rough. Being rough, they did not recognize him. He anointed himself thoroughly.
(PB 24.13.3) Those whom people do not recognize should undertake these. When they anoint and adorn themselves, they place beauty in themselves, and people recognize them.
(PB 24.13.4) With <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) resin at the morning pressing, with <s>sugandhika</s> (fragrant substance) at the midday pressing, with <s>potudāra</s> (deodar) at the third pressing.
(PB 24.13.5) When <s>Agni</s> was about to undertake the role of <s>Hotṛ</s> among the <s>devas</s>, he shook his body. What was his flesh became <s>guggulu</s>; what was sinew became fragrant tinder; what was bone became deodar wood. These are the divine fragrances; with divine fragrances they anoint themselves.

body.text:
(PB 24.14.1) atirātraś caturviṃśaṃ prāyaṇīyam ahas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā abhijit trayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajid eko 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaha āyuś ca gauś ca dve āhanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca saṃvatsarasam mitā yāvatī saṃvatsarasyarddhis tāvaty etāsām ṛddhiḥ
(PB 24.14.2) tad āhur yac caturviṃśam ahaḥ prayaṇīyaṃ kuryuḥ saṃvatsaram ārabhya na samāpayeyur iti trivṛd eva kāryaṃ prāṇā vai trivṛt prāṇān evopayanti
(PB 24.14.3) atho khalv āhuś caturviṃśam eva kāryaṃ samṛdhyai
(PB 24.14.4) athaite svarasāmānaḥ śiro vai divākīrtyaṃ prāṇāḥ svarasāmāno yad divākīrtyam abhitaḥ svarasāmāno bhavanti śirasyeva tat prāṇā dhīyante
(PB 24.14.5) atha yāvantyau prāṇau tau viśvajid abhijitāv athaite goāyuṣī mithunau stomāv upayanti prajātyai
(PB 24.14.6) athaitāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāya
(PB 24.14.7) athaitad vratam annaṃ vai vrata na vā anyatra mukhād annaṃ dhinoti yad upariṣṭād vratam upayanti mukhata eva tad annādyaṃ dhīyate tasmān mukhe sad annaṃ dhinoti
(PB 24.14.8) athaitau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.14.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>, a twenty-four-fold opening day, three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day periods, the <s>Abhijit</s>, three melodic-accent days, a <s>Divākīrtya</s> day, three melodic-accent days, a <s>Viśvajit</s>, one <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day period, the <s>Āyus</s> and <s>Gau</s> as two days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, a <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and an <s>Atirātra</s>. This is measured equal to a year; as great as the prosperity of the year, so great is the prosperity of these.
(PB 24.14.2) They say: 'If one makes the opening day twenty-four-fold, one would begin the year without completing it.' The nine-fold should be used. Breath is the nine-fold; with breath they set forth.
(PB 24.14.3) But they also say: 'The twenty-four-fold should indeed be used, for the sake of prosperity.'
(PB 24.14.4) Now these melodic-accent days: the <s>Divākīrtya</s> is the head; the breaths are the melodic-accent days. When melodic-accent days are on both sides of the <s>Divākīrtya</s>, it is as if breaths are placed in the head.
(PB 24.14.5) The two breaths are the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s>. The <s>Gau</s> and <s>Āyus</s> are paired <s>stomas</s> — for procreation.
(PB 24.14.6) The ten days of the twelve-day rite — they approach unbroken speech, for procreation.
(PB 24.14.7) The <s>vrata</s> (observance) is food. Food is not placed anywhere except from the mouth. When the <s>vrata</s> is approached at the top, food is placed from the mouth. Therefore, being in the mouth, it provides food.
(PB 24.14.8) The opening and closing <s>Atirātras</s>: with the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up.

body.text:
(PB 24.15.1) atirātro nava trivṛnty ahāny agniṣṭomamukhaṣ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāni trīṇy ahāny agniṣṭomāv abhita ukthyaṃ madhyato nava pañcadaśāny ahāny agniṣṭomam ukhaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāni trīṇy ahāny agniṣṭomāv abhita ukthyaṃ madhyato nava saptadaśāny ahāny agniṣṭomamukhaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāni trīṇy ahāny agniṣṭomāv abhita ukthyaṃ madhyato navaikaviṃśāny ahāny agniṣṭomamukhaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāni trīṇy ahāny agniṣṭomāv abhita ukthyaṃ madhyato dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 24.15.2) etābhir vai savitā sarvasya prasavam agacchat
(PB 24.15.3) sarvasya prasavaṃ gacchanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.15.4) yad gaṇaśaḥ stomā bahava eva bhavanti saha trivṛtaḥ saha pañcadaśāḥ saha saptadaśāḥ sahaikaviṃśāḥ savitur vā etāḥ kakubhaḥ
(PB 24.15.5) kakubhaḥ samānānāṃ ca prajānāṃ ca bhavanti ya etā upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.15.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; nine <s>trivṛt</s> days, a six-day rite beginning with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, of which the three days have <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> on both sides and <s>Ukthya</s> in the middle; nine <s>pañcadaśa</s> days, a six-day rite beginning with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, of which the three days have <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> on both sides and <s>Ukthya</s> in the middle; nine <s>saptadaśa</s> days, a six-day rite beginning with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, of which the three days have <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> on both sides and <s>Ukthya</s> in the middle; nine <s>ekaviṃśa</s> days, a six-day rite beginning with <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, of which the three days have <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> on both sides and <s>Ukthya</s> in the middle; the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and the <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.15.2) By these <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Impeller) attained the impulsion of all.
(PB 24.15.3) They attain the impulsion of all — those who undertake these.
(PB 24.15.4) Since the <s>stomas</s> come in groups and are numerous — the <s>trivṛts</s> together, the <s>pañcadaśas</s> together, the <s>saptadaśas</s> together, the <s>ekaviṃśas</s> together — these are the peaks of <s>Savitṛ</s>.
(PB 24.15.5) They become the peaks among their equals and their offspring — those who undertake these.

body.text:
(PB 24.16.1) atirātraś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā mahāvrataṃ dvāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny atirātraḥ
(PB 24.16.2) ṛtavo na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta etābhiḥ pratyatiṣṭhan pratiṣṭhākāmā upeyuḥ
(PB 24.16.3) praty eva tiṣṭhanti ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtuṣv evaitābhiḥ pratitiṣṭhanti yat kḷptān ṣaḍahān upayanti kḷptyā eva
(PB 24.16.4) athaitad vratam annaṃ vai vrataṃ na vā anyatra madhyād annaṃ dhinoti yad vrataṃ madhyata upayanti madhyata eva tad annādyaṃ dhīyate tasmān madhye sad annaṃ dhinoti
(PB 24.16.5) yat kḷptau ṣaḍahāv upayanti kḷptyā eva
(PB 24.16.6) athaitāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāyāthaitau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.16.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Mahāvrata</s>; two <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; the ten days of the twelve-day rite; <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.16.2) The seasons were not firmly established. By these they became firmly established. Those desiring firm establishment should undertake them.
(PB 24.16.3) They become firmly established indeed. There are six seasons. By these they become firmly established in the seasons. Since they undertake properly arranged six-day rites, it is for proper arrangement.
(PB 24.16.4) Now this is the observance. Food is indeed the observance. Nowhere but from the middle does food flow. Since they undertake the observance in the middle, food-eating is thereby placed in the middle. Therefore, one seated in the middle has food flowing to him.
(PB 24.16.5) Since they undertake properly arranged six-day rites, it is for proper arrangement.
(PB 24.16.6) Now these are the ten days of the twelve-day rite. They approach with unbroken speech — for procreation. And these are the opening and closing <s>Atirātras</s>. By whatever vital breath they proceed, by that they rise up.

body.text:
(PB 24.17.1) atirātraḥ ṣaḍabhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 24.17.2) etābhir vā indrāgnī atyanyā devatā abhavatām atyanyāḥ prajā bhavanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.17.3) indrāgnī vai devānām ojiṣṭhā ojiṣṭhā bhavanti ya etā upayanti
(PB 24.17.4) yat kḷptān ṣaḍahān upayanti kḷptyā evāthaitāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vācam avicchinnām upayanti prajananāyāthaitad vratam athaitau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.17.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; six <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and the <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.17.2) By these <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> surpassed the other deities. Those who undertake these surpass other peoples.
(PB 24.17.3) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are the most powerful of the gods. Those who undertake these become the most powerful.
(PB 24.17.4) Since they undertake properly arranged six-day rites, it is for proper arrangement. Now these are the ten days of the twelve-day rite. They approach with unbroken speech — for procreation. Now this is the observance. And these are the opening and closing <s>Atirātras</s>. By whatever vital breath they proceed, by that they rise up.

body.text:
(PB 24.18.1) atirātraś caturviṃśaṃ prāyaṇīyam ahas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'bhijit trayassvarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajit pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇa eko 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaha āyuś ca gauś ca dve ahanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataś cātirātraś ca tad etad ekaṣaṣṭirātraṃ daivānāṃ vrātyānām
(PB 24.18.2) daivā vai vrātyāḥ sattram āsata budhena sthapatinā te ha vā aniryācya varuṇaṃ rājānaṃ devayajanaṃ didīkṣus tān ha vā varūṇo rājānu vyājahārāntar emi vo yajñiyād bhāgadheyān na devayānaṃ panthānaṃ prajñāsyatheti tasmāt tebhyo na havir gṛhṇanti na graham
(PB 24.18.3) atha ha vai tarhi nauṣadhīṣu paya āsīn na kṣīre sarpir na māṃse medo na tvaci lomāni na vanaspatiṣu palāśāni tad yata etad ekaṣaṣṭirātraṃ daivā vrātyā upāyaṃs tato vai tāni bhutāny etair vīryaiḥ samasṛjyanta tejasvanty evāsan payasvanti
(PB 24.18.4) tad eṣa śloko 'bhyanūcyate
(PB 24.18.5) kim akarteti yat putrān muhur daivāṃ apṛcchata mahī budhasyāsīd dīkṣā sa kṣīre sarpir āharat
(PB 24.18.6) mahīṃ dīkṣāṃ saumāyano budho yad udayacchadanandat sarvam āpnon manmāṃse medo 'dhā iti
(PB 24.18.7) daridrā āsan paśavaḥ kṛśāḥ santo vyasthakāḥ saumāyanasya dīkṣāyāṃ samasṛjyanta medaseti
(PB 24.18.8) tad ya etad ekaṣaṣṭirātram upeyus te devayajanam adhyavasāya gārhapatya āhutiṃ juhayur deva varuṇa devayajanaṃ no dehi svāheti te datte devajane yajante
(PB 24.18.9) te sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.18.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>caturviṃśa</s> opening day; three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; <s>Abhijit</s>; three <s>Svarasāman</s> days; <s>Divākīrtya</s> day; three <s>Svarasāman</s> days; <s>Viśvajit</s>; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; <s>trayastriṃśa</s> commencement; one <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite; <s>Āyus</s> and <s>Gaur</s>, two days; the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Atirātra</s>. This is the sixty-one-night rite of the divine <s>Vrātyas</s>.
(PB 24.18.2) The divine <s>Vrātyas</s> sat in a sacrificial session with <s>Budha</s> as their chief. They wished to consecrate themselves at the divine sacrificial ground without having properly solicited king <s>Varuṇa</s>. King <s>Varuṇa</s> spoke to them: 'I shall intervene in your sacrificial portion. You shall not know the path to the gods.' Therefore for them no oblation is taken nor is a cup drawn.
(PB 24.18.3) At that time there was no milk in the herbs, no butter in the milk, no fat in the flesh, no hair on the skin, no leaves on the trees. But when the divine <s>Vrātyas</s> undertook this sixty-one-night rite, then these beings were joined with these powers — they became radiant, full of milk.
(PB 24.18.4) On this a verse is recited:
(PB 24.18.5) 'What have we done?' — when the sons repeatedly asked the divine ones. Great was the consecration of <s>Budha</s>; he placed butter in the milk.
(PB 24.18.6) When <s>Budha</s> the <s>Saumāyana</s> raised up the great consecration, everything rejoiced and was obtained — 'He has placed fat in the flesh.'
(PB 24.18.7) 'The animals were poor, thin, and bony. By the consecration of the <s>Saumāyana</s>, they were joined with fat.'
(PB 24.18.8) Those who undertake this sixty-one-night rite, having resolved upon the divine sacrificial ground, offer an oblation in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire: 'O god <s>Varuṇa</s>, give us the divine sacrificial ground, <s>svāhā</s>!' Having been given the divine ground, they sacrifice.
(PB 24.18.9) They attained all prosperity. Those who undertake this attain all prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 24.19.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryahaś caturdaśābhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 24.19.2) devā vai mṛtyor abibhayus te prajāpatim upādhāvaṃs tebhya etena śatarātreṇāmṛtatvaṃ prāyacchad etad vāva manuṣyasyāmṛtatvaṃ yat sarvam āyur eti vasīyān bhavati sarvam āyur yanti vasīyāṃso bhavanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 24.19.3) abhiprayāyam abhiṣuṇvanty abhikrāntyai samānatrābhiṣuṇvanti pratiṣṭhityai
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.19.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s> three-day rite; fourteen <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.19.2) The gods feared death. They ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>. He gave them immortality by this hundred-night rite. This is indeed the immortality of a human — that he lives his full lifespan and becomes more prosperous. They live their full lifespan and become more prosperous — those who undertake this.
(PB 24.19.3) They press Soma going forward — for progression. They press Soma in the same place — for firm establishment.

body.text:
(PB 24.20.1) atirātraś caturviṃśaṃ prāyaṇīyam ahaś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturthaḥ sa pañcamas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'bhijit trayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajit pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇaś catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturthas trayo 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā āyuś ca gauś ca dve ahanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrañcātirātraś ca
(PB 24.20.2) saṃvatsarabrāhmaṇaṃ brāhmaṇam
body.translated_text:
(PB 24.20.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>caturviṃśa</s> opening day; four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite — that is one month. A second, a third, a fourth, a fifth. Three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; <s>Abhijit</s>; three <s>Svarasāman</s> days; <s>Divākīrtya</s> day; three <s>Svarasāman</s> days; <s>Viśvajit</s>; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; <s>trayastriṃśa</s> commencement; three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; <s>trayastriṃśa</s> commencement; four <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites — that is one month. A second, a third, a fourth. Three <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; <s>Āyus</s> and <s>Gaur</s>, two days; the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 24.20.2) This is the year-long <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (explanatory text).

body.text:
(PB 25.1.1) atirātraś caturviṃśaṃ prāyaṇīyam ahar dvau trivṛt pañcadaśau ṣaḍahau pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho dvau trivṛt pañcadaśau ṣaḍahau sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturthaḥ sa pañcamas trayas trivṛt pañcadaśāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trivṛd bṛhaspatistomas trayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmānaḥ pañcadaśa indrastoma ukthyaḥ pṛṣṭyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇa ekaḥ pañcadaśas trivṛt ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vyūḍhā agniṣṭomās trivṛta udbhic ca balabhic ca dve ahanī dvau pañcadaśatrivṛtau ṣaḍahau pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho dvau pañcadaśatribṛtau ṣaḍahau sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturthaḥ pañcadaśatrivṛt ṣaḍahaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pañcadaśatrivṛt ṣaḍaho gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī chandomadaśāho 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ prathamam ahar atha catuścatvāriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ triṃśaṃ dve aṣṭāviṃśe pañcaviṃśaṃ caturviṃśaṃ mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 25.1.2) ādityānām madhye pṛṣṭhyam
(PB 25.1.3) madhye pṛṣṭhyena vā ādityāḥ svargaṃ lokam ākramanta yan madhye pṛṣṭhāny upayanti svargasya lokasyākrāntyai
(PB 25.1.4) annaṃ vai pṛṣṭhāny annam eva tan madhyato dhīyate tasmān madhye sad annaṃ dhinoti
(PB 25.1.5) paśavaḥ pṛṣṭhāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 25.1.6) cakre vā ete sākaṃvṛtīyat trivṛt pañcadaśau stomau yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayante tam etenābhyaśnuvate yatra yatra hi cakrīvatā kāmayate tat tad abhyaśnute
(PB 25.1.7) athaiṣa trivṛd bṛhaspatistoma etena vai bṛhaspatir devānāṃ purodhām agacchat purodhakāmā upeyur gacchanti purodhāṃ pura enān dadhate
(PB 25.1.8) athaite svarasāmānaḥ śiro vai divākīrtyaṃ prāṇāḥ svarasāmāno yad divākīrtyam abhitaḥ svarasāmāno bhavanti śivasyeva tat prāṇā dhīyante
(PB 25.1.9) athaiṣa pañcadaśa indrastoma ukthya etena vā indro 'tyanyā devatā abhavad atyanyāḥ prajā bhavanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.1.10) athaitāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vyūḍhā agniṣṭomās trivṛto madhyataḥ pāpmano mucyanta eṣa vāva devatalpo devatalpam eva tad ārohanti talpyā bhavanti pravasīyasas talpam āpnuvanti
(PB 25.1.11) athaitāv udbhidbalabhidāv etābhyāṃ vai bṛhaspatir devebhyaḥ paśūn udasṛjat paśūn evaitābhyām utsṛjante
(PB 25.1.12) athaite go āyuṣī mithunau stomāv upayanti prajātyai
(PB 25.1.13) athaiṣa chandomadaśāhaś chandasāṃ doho 'rvāñci chandāṃsy upayanti tasmād arvāñco bhuñjantaḥ paśava upatiṣṭhante
(PB 25.1.14) athaid vratam annaṃ vai vrataṃ na vā anyatra mukhād annaṃ dhinoti yad upariṣṭād vratam upayanti mukhata eva tad annādyaṃ dhīyate tasmān mukhe sad annaṃ dhinoti
(PB 25.1.15) athaitau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
body.translated_text: (PB 25.1.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>; a twenty-four-fold introductory day; two three-fold-and-fifteen-fold six-day rites; a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day rite; two three-fold-and-fifteen-fold six-day rites — that constitutes a month. The second [month], the third, the fourth, the fifth [are the same]. (PB 25.2.1) atirātraś caturviṃśaṃ prāyaṇīyam ahaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaś catvāras trivṛto 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturthaḥ sa pañcamas trayas trivṛto 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trivṛd bṛhaspatistomas trayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyam ahas trayaḥ svarasāmānaḥ pañcadaśa indrastoma ukthyaḥ pṛṣṭyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastriṃśārambhaṇa ekas trivṛd abhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni vyūḍhā agniṣṭomās trivṛta udbhic ca balabhic ca dve ahanī catvāras trivṛto 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahāḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahau sa māsaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīyaḥ sa caturtho dvau trivṛtāv abhiplavau ṣaḍahau pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha āyuś ca gauś ca dve ahanī chandomadaśāhaś caturviṃśaṃ prathamam ahar dve aṣṭāviṃśe triṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ catuścatvāriṃśam aṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ caturviṃśaṃ mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś cāṅgirasāṃ purastāt pṛṣṭhyam
(PB 25.2.2) purastāt pṛṣṭhyena vā aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃ lokam ākramanta yat purastāt pṛṣṭhāny upayanti svargasya lokasyākrāntyai
(PB 25.2.3) annaṃ vai pṛṣṭhāny annam eva tan mukhato dhīyate tasmān mukhe sad annaṃ dhinoti paśavaḥ pṛṣṭhāni paśuṣv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 25.2.4) yad anyac cakrābhyāṃ sākavṛdbhyāṃ tatsamānam ā chandomadaśāhāt
(PB 25.2.5) athaiṣa chandomadaśāhaś chandasāṃ doha ūrdhvāni chandāṃsy upayanty anapabhraṃśāyaiṣa vāva devayānaḥ panthāḥ pra devayānaṃ panthānam āpnuvanti ya etad upayanty athaitad vratam
(PB 25.2.6) athaitau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau yenaiṣa prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
body.translated_text: (PB 25.2.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>; a twenty-four-fold introductory day; a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day rite; four three-fold <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites — that constitutes a month. The second [month], the third, the fourth, the fifth [are the same]. Three three-fold <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rites; a <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> six-day rite; a three-fold <s>Bṛhaspatistoma</s>; three days with <s>Svarasāman</s>; the <s>Divākīrtya</s> day; three days with <s>Svarasāman</s>; a fifteen-fold

body.text:
(PB 25.3.1) atirātras trivṛtā māsaṃ pañcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsam ekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsaṃ trayastriṃśena māsaṃ mahāvrataṃ trayastriṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsam ekaviṃśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsaṃ pañcadaśena māsaṃ trivṛtā māsam atirātraḥ
(PB 25.3.2) ṛtavo na pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta etena pratyatiṣṭhan pratiṣṭhākāmā upeyuḥ praty eva tiṣṭhanti ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtuṣv evaitena pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 25.3.3) yad gataṃ madhyata upayanti madhyata eva tad annādyaṃ dhīyate tasmān madhye dhinoti
(PB 25.3.4) pakṣi vā etat sattrāyaṇaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayante tam etenābhyaśnuvate yatra yatra hi pakṣī kāmayate tat tad abhyaśnute
(PB 25.3.5) trivṛtā prayanti trivṛtodyanti prāṇā vai trivṛt stomānāṃ prāṇair eva prayanti prāṇeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 25.3.6) etad vai dṛtivātavantau khāṇdava upeto viṣuvati vātavān uttiṣṭhati samāpayati dṛtis tasmāt tanīyāṃso vātavatā bhūyāṃso dārteyāḥ
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.3.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>; a month with the three-fold [stoma]; a month with the fifteen-fold; a month with the seventeen-fold; a month with the twenty-one-fold; a month with the twenty-seven-fold (<s>Triṇava</s>); a month with the thirty-three-fold; a <s>Mahāvrata</s>; a month with the thirty-three-fold; a month with the twenty-seven-fold; a month with the twenty-one-fold; a month with the seventeen-fold; a month with the fifteen-fold; a month with the three-fold; and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 25.3.2) The seasons did not become firmly established. By this they became firmly established.

body.text:
(PB 25.4.1) māsaṃ dīkṣitā bhavanti te māsi somaṃ krīṇanti teṣāṃ dvādaśopasada upasadbhiś caritvā somam upanahya māsam agnihotraṃ juhvati māsaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajante māsaṃ vaiśvadevena māsaṃ varuṇapraghāsair māsaṃ sākamedhair māsaṃ śunāsīryeṇa trivṛtā māsaṃ pañcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsam ekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsam aṣṭādaśa trayastriṃśāny ahāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvrataṃ cātirātraś ca
(PB 25.4.2) agnihotraṃ daśahotā darśapūrṇamāsau caturhotā cāturmāsyāni pañcahotā saumyo 'dhvaraḥ saptahotā
(PB 25.4.3) ete vāva sarveṇa yajñena yajante ya etad upayanti sarva eva bhavanti
(PB 25.4.4) te sarve kuṇḍapāyino 'tsarukaiś camasair bhakṣayanti
(PB 25.4.5) yo hotā so 'dhvaryuḥ sa potā ya udgātā sa neṣṭā so 'cchāvāko yo maitrāvaruṇaḥ sa brahmā sa pratihartāyaḥ prastotā sa brāhmaṇācchaṃsī sa grāvastut yaḥ pratiprasthātā so 'gnīt sa unnetā gṛhapatir gṛhapatiḥ subrahmaṇyassubrahmaṇyaḥ
body.translated_text: (PB 25.4.1) For a month they remain consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>). In the [second] month they purchase <s>Soma</s>. Having observed twelve <s>Upasads</s> (preparatory rites), having bound the <s>Soma</s>, for a month they offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>; for a month they sacrifice with the new-and-full-moon rites (<s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>); for a month with the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; for a month with the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s>; for a month with the <s>Sākamedha</s>; for a month with the <s>Śunāsīrya</s>; a month with the three-fold; a month with the fifteen-fold; a month with the seventeen-fold; a month with the

body.text:
(PB 25.5.1) saṃvatsaraṃ dīkṣitā bhavanti saṃvatsaram upasadbhiś caranti saṃvatsaraṃ prasuto bhavati
(PB 25.5.2) tat saṃvatsaraṃ dīkṣitā bhavanti tapa eva tena tapyante yat saṃvatsaram upasadbhiś caranti punata eva tena yat saṃvatsaraṃ prasuto bhavati devalokam eva tenāpi yanti
(PB 25.5.3) etena vai tapaścito devāḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.5.1) They remain consecrated for a year; they observe the <s>upasad</s> (approach-offerings) for a year; the Soma pressing continues for a year.
(PB 25.5.2) During the year they remain consecrated — thereby they perform <s>tapas</s> (austerity). During the year they observe the <s>upasads</s> — thereby they purify themselves. During the year the Soma is pressed — thereby they go to the world of the gods.
(PB 25.5.3) By this the gods, rich in <s>tapas</s>, attained all prosperity. Those who undertake this attain all prosperity.

body.text:
(PB 25.6.1) trayastrivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarās trayaḥ pañcadaśās trayaḥ saptadaśās traya ekaviṃśāḥ prajāpater dvādaśasaṃvatsaram
(PB 25.6.2) etena vai prajāpatiḥ sarvasya prasavam agacchat sarvasya prasavaṃ gacchanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.6.3) yat trayas trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā bhavanti tejo brāhmavarcasaṃ trivṛt teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhate yat trayaḥ pañca daśā ojo vīryaṃ pañcadaśa oja eva vīryam avarundhate yat trayaḥ saptadaśā annaṃ vai saptadaśo 'nnādyam evāvarundhate yat traya ekaviṃśāḥ pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo 'ntata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhanti
(PB 25.6.4) etena vai naimiśīyāḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.6.5) te ha saptadaśebhya evādhyuttasthus ta u hocur yo naḥ prajāyām ṛdhyātai sa etat sattraṃ samāpayād iti tad etat samīpsanto brāhmaṇās sattram āsate
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.6.1) Three <s>trivṛt</s> years, three <s>pañcadaśa</s> years, three <s>saptadaśa</s> years, three <s>ekaviṃśa</s> years — this is <s>Prajāpati</s>'s twelve-year session.
(PB 25.6.2) By this <s>Prajāpati</s> attained the impulsion of all. They attain the impulsion of all — those who undertake this.
(PB 25.6.3) Since there are three <s>trivṛt</s> years, brilliance and brahmanical splendor are the <s>trivṛt</s> — thereby they obtain brilliance and brahmanical splendor. Since there are three <s>pañcadaśa</s>, power and vigor are the <s>pañcadaśa</s> — thereby they obtain power and vigor. Since there are three <s>saptadaśa</s>, food is the <s>saptadaśa</s> — thereby they obtain food-eating. Since there are three <s>ekaviṃśa</s>, firm establishment is the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> — at the very end they become firmly established in the sacrifice.
(PB 25.6.4) By this the people of <s>Naimiśa</s> attained all prosperity. Those who undertake this attain all prosperity.
(PB 25.6.5) They rose up from the seventeenth year itself. And they said: 'Whoever among our offspring prospers, let him complete this sacrificial session.' Desiring that, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> sit in the sacrificial session.

body.text:
(PB 25.7.1) nava trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā nava pañcadaśā nava saptadaśā navaikaviṃśāḥ śāktyānāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśat saṃvatsaram
(PB 25.7.2) etena vai gaurīvitiḥ śāktas tarasapuroḍāśo yavyāvatyāṃ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.7.3) bṛhatī vā etat sattrāyaṇaṃ svārājyaṃ chandasāṃ bṛhatī pra svārājyam āpnuvanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.7.4) tad etac chāktyānāṃ daśavīram eṣāṃ daśa vīrā jāyante ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.7.1) Nine <s>trivṛt</s> years, nine <s>pañcadaśa</s>, nine <s>saptadaśa</s>, nine <s>ekaviṃśa</s> — this is the thirty-six-year session of the <s>Śāktyas</s>.
(PB 25.7.2) By this <s>Gaurīviti Śāktya</s>, with a <s>tarasa</s> (swift) offering-cake, at the <s>Yavyāvatī</s> river attained all prosperity. Those who undertake this attain all prosperity.
(PB 25.7.3) This sacrificial journey is in the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. Self-sovereignty belongs to the <s>Bṛhatī</s> among meters. They attain self-sovereignty — those who undertake this.
(PB 25.7.4) This is the 'ten-hero' session of the <s>Śāktyas</s>. Ten heroes are born to those who undertake this.

body.text:
(PB 25.8.1) pañcaviṃśatis trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ pañcadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ saptadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatir ekaviṃśāḥ sādhyānāṃ śatasaṃvatsaram
(PB 25.8.2) sādhyā vai nāma devebhyo devāḥ pūrva āsaṃs ta etat sattrāyaṇam upāyaṃs tenārdhnuvaṃs te sagavaḥ sapuruṣāḥ sarva eva saha svargaṃ lokam āyann evaṃ vāva te saha svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.8.3) āyur vā etat sattrāyaṇaṃ śatāyuḥ puruṣo yāvad evāyus tad avarundhate na hy atyāyuṣaṃ sattram asti
(PB 25.8.4) tad abhyanūktā tānīd ahāni bahulāny āsan yā prācīnam uditā sūryasya yataḥ pari jāra ivācaranty ūṣā (?) dādṛśe na punar yatīveti
(PB 25.8.5) jyotiṣṭomasyāyanena yanti jyotir eva bhavanti
(PB 25.8.6) ekaviṃśo 'ntataḥ stomānāṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo 'ntataḥ stomānāṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhā vā ekaviṃśo 'ntata eva yajñasya pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.8.1) Twenty-five <s>trivṛt</s> years, twenty-five <s>pañcadaśa</s>, twenty-five <s>saptadaśa</s>, twenty-five <s>ekaviṃśa</s> — this is the hundred-year session of the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
(PB 25.8.2) The <s>Sādhyas</s> were gods even before the gods. They undertook this sacrificial journey. By it they prospered. Together with their cattle and men, all of them went to the heavenly world together. Thus indeed they all go to the heavenly world together — those who undertake this.
(PB 25.8.3) This sacrificial journey is the lifespan. A man lives a hundred years. He obtains as much lifespan as there is. For there is no <s>sattra</s> that exceeds the lifespan.
(PB 25.8.4) On this a verse is recited: 'Those days were many that were before the rising of the sun, from which <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), going about like a lover, was seen — she who does not return.'
(PB 25.8.5) They go by the path of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>. They become light itself.
(PB 25.8.6) The <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is the final among the <s>stomas</s>. Firm establishment is the <s>ekaviṃśa</s>. At the very end they become firmly established in the sacrifice.

body.text:
(PB 25.9.1) atirātraḥ sahasram ahāny atirātro 'gneḥ sahasrasāvyam
(PB 25.9.2) etena vā agniḥ savasya prasavam agacchat sarvasya prasavaṃ gacchanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.9.3) agner vai sarvam ādyaṃ sarvam eṣām ādyaṃ bhavati ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.9.4) atha yat sahasrasāvyaṃ bhavati sahasrākṣarā vai paramā virāṭ paramāyām eva virāji pratitiṣṭhanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.9.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; a thousand days; <s>Atirātra</s>. This is <s>Agni</s>'s thousand-pressing session.
(PB 25.9.2) By this <s>Agni</s> attained the impulsion of all. They attain the impulsion of all — those who undertake this.
(PB 25.9.3) Everything is food for <s>Agni</s>. Everything becomes food for those who undertake this.
(PB 25.9.4) Since it is the thousand-pressing, the supreme <s>Virāj</s> has a thousand syllables. They become firmly established in the supreme <s>Virāj</s>.

body.text:
(PB 25.10.1) sarasvatyā vinaśane dīkṣante
(PB 25.10.2) teṣāṃ dvādaśa dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ
(PB 25.10.3) yad ahar atirātro bhavati tad ahar vatsān apākurvanti saṃsthite 'tirātre sānnāyyena yajante
(PB 25.10.4) sānnāyyeneṣṭvādhvaryuḥ śamyāṃ parāsyati sā yatra nipatati tad gārhapatyas tataḥ ṣaṭtriṃśataṃ prakramān prakramati tad āhavanīyaḥ
(PB 25.10.5) cakrīvat sadaś cakrīvad dhavirdhānaṃ cakrīvad āgnīdhram ulūkhalabudhno yūpaḥ prakṛṣya upopta eva noparavān khananti
(PB 25.10.6) te tam āpūryamāṇam āvāsyena yanti
(PB 25.10.7) teṣāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ goṣṭomastomo bhavaty ukthyo bṛhatsāmā
(PB 25.10.8) saṃsthite goṣṭome paurṇamāsaṃ nirvapante te tam apakṣīyamāṇaṃ paurṇamāsena yanti teṣām amāvāsyāyām āyuṣṭomastomo bhavaty ukthyo rathantarasāmā
(PB 25.10.9) mitrāvaruṇayor ayanam
(PB 25.10.10) etena vai mitrāvaruṇāv imān lokān ājayatām ahorātrau vai mitrāvaruṇāv ahar mitro rātrir varuṇo 'rdhamāsau vai mitrāvaruṇau ya āpūryate sa mitro yo 'pakṣīyate sa varuṇaḥ sa eṣa mitro varuṇe retaḥ siñcati
(PB 25.10.11) sarasvatyā vai devā ādityam astabhnuvan sā nāyacchat sābhyavlīyata tasmāt sā kubjimatīva taṃ bṛhatyāstabhnuvan sāyacchat tasmād bṛhatī chandasāṃ vīryavattamādityaṃ hi tayāstabhnuvan
(PB 25.10.12) pratīpaṃ yanti na hy anvīpam aṣṭa vai pūrveṇa pakṣasā yanti
(PB 25.10.13) tad dhi praty ekāpyeti
(PB 25.10.14) dṛṣadvaty eva
(PB 25.10.15) dṛṣadvatyā apyaye 'ponaptrīyaṃ caruṃ nirupyāthātiyanti
(PB 25.10.16) catuścatvāriṃśad āśvīnāni sarasvatyā vinaśanāt plakṣaḥ prāsravaṇas tāvad itaḥ svargo lokaḥ sarasvatīsammitenādhvanā svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti
(PB 25.10.17) etena vai namī sāpyo vaideho rājāñjasā svargaṃ lokam aid añjasāgāmeti tad añjaskīyānām añjaskīyatvam
(PB 25.10.18) sa etad avabhṛtham abhyavaid ya eṣa uttareṇa sthūlārmaṃ hradas tad dhāsya śataṃ gāvaḥ sahasraṃ sampeduḥ
(PB 25.10.19) śate goṣv ṛṣabham apy ṛjanti(?) tā yadā sahasraṃ sampadyante 'thotthānam
(PB 25.10.20) yadā sarvajyāniṃ jīyante 'thotthānaṃ yadā gṛhapatir mriyate 'thotthānam
(PB 25.10.21) yadā plakṣaṃ prāsravaṇam āgacchanty athotthānam
(PB 25.10.22) plakṣaṃ prāsravaṇam āgamyāgnaye kāmāyeṣṭiṃ nirvapante tasyām aśvāṃ ca puruṣīṃ ca dhenuke datvā
(PB 25.10.23) kārapacavaṃ prati yamunām avabhṛtham abhyavayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.10.1) They are consecrated at the disappearance of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> river.
(PB 25.10.2) Their consecration lasts twelve days; the <s>upasads</s> last twelve days.
(PB 25.10.3) On the day of the <s>Atirātra</s>, they separate the calves. When the <s>Atirātra</s> is completed, they sacrifice with the <s>Sānnāyya</s> (cooked milk offering).
(PB 25.10.4) Having sacrificed with the <s>Sānnāyya</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> casts the measuring-peg. Where it falls, there is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire. From there he steps thirty-six paces — there is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
(PB 25.10.5) The assembly hall is on wheels; the <s>Havirdhāna</s> shed is on wheels; the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> shed is on wheels. The sacrificial post has a mortar for its base. Having plowed, they sow in the plowed ground and do not dig nearby.
(PB 25.10.6) They go with the waxing moon until the new-moon day.
(PB 25.10.7) On the full moon, there is the <s>Goṣṭoma</s> (cow-praise) rite — an <s>Ukthya</s> with the <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>sāman</s>.
(PB 25.10.8) When the <s>Goṣṭoma</s> is completed, they prepare the full-moon offering. They go with the waning moon by the full-moon offering. On the new-moon day there is the <s>Āyuṣṭoma</s> (life-praise) rite — an <s>Ukthya</s> with the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>sāman</s>.
(PB 25.10.9) This is the journey of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 25.10.10) By this <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> conquered these worlds. Day and night are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> — day is <s>Mitra</s>, night is <s>Varuṇa</s>. The two fortnights are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> — the waxing is <s>Mitra</s>, the waning is <s>Varuṇa</s>. This <s>Mitra</s> casts seed into <s>Varuṇa</s>.
(PB 25.10.11) By the <s>Sarasvatī</s> the gods propped up the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). She could not hold him. She collapsed — therefore she flows as if hunchbacked. They propped him up with the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. She held him. Therefore the <s>Bṛhatī</s> is the most powerful of meters, for they propped up the sun with her.
(PB 25.10.12) They go upstream, for one cannot go downstream. They go by the northern bank.
(PB 25.10.13) For one who goes this way comes back.
(PB 25.10.14) It is at the <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s> river indeed.
(PB 25.10.15) At the confluence of the <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>, having prepared a porridge for the Water Offspring, they cross over.
(PB 25.10.16) There are forty-four <s>Āśvina</s> stations from the disappearance of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> to the <s>Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa</s> (the fig tree at the spring). That far from here is the heavenly world. By a path measured by the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, they go to the heavenly world.
(PB 25.10.17) By this <s>Nami Sāpya</s>, the king of <s>Videha</s>, went directly to the heavenly world. 'He went directly' — that is the <s>Añjaskīya</s>-nature of the <s>Añjaskīyas</s>.
(PB 25.10.18) He came upon this concluding bath at the pool north of <s>Sthūlārman</s>. There a hundred cows, then a thousand, gathered for him.
(PB 25.10.19) Among every hundred cows they acquire a bull. When they reach a thousand, then the rising.
(PB 25.10.20) When they lose everything, then the rising. When the householder dies, then the rising.
(PB 25.10.21) When they reach <s>Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa</s>, then the rising.
(PB 25.10.22) Having reached <s>Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa</s>, they prepare an offering to <s>Agni Kāma</s> (the fire of desire), giving a mare and a human female as the <s>dhenukā</s> (milch-cow equivalents) at that offering.
(PB 25.10.23) They go for the concluding bath to the <s>Yamunā</s> river at <s>Kārapacava</s>.

body.text:
(PB 25.11.1) atirātras trivṛt pañcadaśam indrāgnyor ayanaṃ goāyuṣī indrakukṣī atirātraḥ
(PB 25.11.2) etena vā indrāgnī atyanyā devatā abhavatām atyanyāḥ prajā bhavanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.11.3) indrāgnī vai devānām ojiṣṭhā ojiṣṭhā bhavanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.11.4) atha yat trivṛt pañcadaśam indrāgnyor ayanaṃ goāyuṣī indrakukṣī bhavato 'saṃvyāthāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.11.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>trivṛt</s> <s>pañcadaśa</s> journey of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>; <s>Go</s> and <s>Āyus</s>, the two flanks of <s>Indra</s>; <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 25.11.2) By this <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> surpassed the other deities. Those who undertake this surpass other peoples.
(PB 25.11.3) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are the most powerful of the gods. Those who undertake this become the most powerful.
(PB 25.11.4) Since it has the <s>trivṛt</s> <s>pañcadaśa</s> journey of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Go</s> and <s>Āyus</s> as the flanks of <s>Indra</s> — it is to prevent scattering.

body.text:
(PB 25.12.1) atirātro jyotir gaur āyus tryaho viśvajid abhijitāv indrakukṣī atirātraḥ
(PB 25.12.2) etena vāryamaitaṃ lokam ajayat
(PB 25.12.3) yad āhur aryamṇaḥ panthā ity eṣa vāva devayānaḥ panthāḥ
(PB 25.12.4) pra devayānaṃ panthānam āpnuvanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.12.5) tasmād eṣo 'ruṇatama iva diva upadadṛśe 'ruṇatama iva hi panthāḥ
(PB 25.12.6) atha yat jyotir gaur āyus tryaho viśvajid abhijitāv indrakukṣī bhavato 'saṃvyāthāya
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.12.1) <s>Atirātra</s>; <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s> three-day rite; <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s>, the two flanks of <s>Indra</s>; <s>Atirātra</s>.
(PB 25.12.2) By this <s>Aryaman</s> conquered this world.
(PB 25.12.3) What they call 'the path of <s>Aryaman</s>' — this is indeed the path to the gods.
(PB 25.12.4) They attain the path to the gods — those who undertake this.
(PB 25.12.5) Therefore this path appears most reddish in the sky, for the path is most reddish.
(PB 25.12.6) Since the <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s> three-day rite, <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s> serve as the flanks of <s>Indra</s> — it is to prevent scattering.

body.text:
(PB 25.13.1) saṃvatsaraṃ brāhmaṇasya gā rakṣet saṃvatsaraṃ vyarṇe naitandhave 'gnim indhīta saṃvatsare parīṇahy agnīn ādadhīta
(PB 25.13.2) sa dakṣiṇena tīreṇa dṛṣadvatyā āgneyenāṣṭākapālena śamyāparāsīyāt
(PB 25.13.3) indraś ca ruśamā cāṃśaṃ prāsyetāṃ yataro nau pūrvo bhūmiṃ paryeti sa jayatīti bhūmim indraḥ paryait kurukṣetraṃ ruśamā so 'bravīd ajaiṣaṃ tv ety aham eva tvām ajaiṣam itīndro 'bravīt tau deveṣv apṛcchetāṃ te devā abruvann etāvatī vāva prajāpater vedir yāvat kurukṣetram iti tau na vyajayetām
(PB 25.13.4) sa ya āgneyenāṣṭākapālena dakṣiṇena tīreṇa dṛṣadvatyāḥ śamyāparāsyeti triplakṣān prati yamunām avabhṛtham abhyavaiti tad eva manuṣyebhyas tiro bhavati
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.13.1) For a year one should guard the cows of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. For a year, in the desert place of an <s>Naitandhava</s>, one should kindle the fire. At the year's end, having brought fires around, one should establish the fires.
(PB 25.13.2) On the southern bank of the <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s> [river], one should remove [the fault] with an eight-dish offering to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Śamyā</s> ritual.
(PB 25.13.3) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Ruśamā</s> cast lots: 'Whichever of us first circumambulates the earth, he shall be the victor.' The earth

body.text:
(PB 25.14.1) āgneyo 'ṣṭākāpāla aindra ekādaśakapālo vaiśvadevaś caruḥ
(PB 25.14.2) adīkṣitaḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ pratimuñcate yad adīkṣitaḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ pratimuñcate yo mānuṣy ṛddhis tāṃ tenardhnoti
(PB 25.14.3) atha yat tapas tapyate yā daivī tāṃ tena
(PB 25.14.4) yad āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo bhavaty agnimukhā vai devatā mukhata eva tad devatā ṛdhnoty atho prātassavanam eva tenāpnoty atha yad aindra ekādaśakapālo bhavaty aindraṃ vai mādhyandinaṃ savaṇaṃ mādhyandinam eva savanaṃ tenāpnoty atha yad vaiśvadevaś carur bhavati vaiśvadevaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam eva tenāpnoti
(PB 25.14.5) etena vai puro devamuniḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti ya etad upaiti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.14.1) An eight-dish offering to <s>Agni</s>, an eleven-dish offering to <s>Indra</s>, and a <s>caru</s> (porridge) to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-Gods).
(PB 25.14.2) One who is unconsecrated puts on a black antelope skin. Because one who is unconsecrated puts on a black antelope skin, whatever human prosperity there is, one prospers in that.
(PB 25.14.3) And because one performs austerity (<s>tapas</s>), whatever divine [prosperity there is], by that.
(PB 25.14.4) Because the eight-dish offering belongs to <s>Agni</s> — for <s>Agni</s> is indeed the mouth of the gods.

body.text:
(PB 25.15.1) atirātrāv abhito 'gniṣṭomā madhye sarvo daśadaśī saṃvatsaro dvādaśo viṣuvān sarpasāmāni viṣuvati kriyante
(PB 25.15.2) etena vai sarpā eṣu lokeṣu pratyatiṣṭhann eṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.15.3) jarvaro gṛhapatiḥ dhṛtarāṣṭra airāvato brahmā pṛthuśvarā daureśravasa udgātā glāvaś cājagāvaś ca prastotṛpratihartārau dattastāpaso hotā śitipṛṣṭho maitrāvaruṇaḥ takṣako vaiśāleyo brāhmaṇācchaṃsī śikhānuśikhau neṣṭāpotārau aruṇa āṭocchāvākaḥ timirgho daureśruto 'gnīt kautastāv adhvaryū arimejayaś ca janamejayaś cārbudo grāvas tu dajiraḥ subrahmaṇyaḥ cakkapiśaṅgāv unnetārau ṣaṇḍakuṣaṇḍāv abhigarāpagarau
(PB 25.15.4) etena vai sarpā apamṛtyum ajayann apamṛtyuṃ jayanti ya etad upayanti tasmāt te hitvā jīrṇāṃ tvacam atisarpanty apa hi te mṛtyum ajayan sarpā vā ādityā ādityānām ivaiṣāṃ prakāśo bhavati ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.15.1) <s>Atirātras</s> on both sides, <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> in the middle — the entire year consists of groups of ten. The twelfth [month] is the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice). The <s>Sarpasāman</s> (Serpent-chant) melodies are performed at the <s>Viṣuvat</s>.
(PB 25.15.2) By this the serpents became firmly established in these worlds. Those who undertake this become established in these worlds.
(PB 25.15.3) <s>Jarvara</s> is the householder, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra Airāvata</s> is the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], <s>Pṛthuśvarā Daureśravasa</s>

body.text:
(PB 25.16.1) gavām ayanaṃ prathamaḥ saṃvatsaro 'thādityānām athāṅgirasām
(PB 25.16.2) etena vai gāvaḥ prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchan prajāyante bahavo bhavanti ya etad upayanty etena vā ādityā eṣu lokeṣu pratyatiṣṭhan pratitiṣṭhanti ya etad upayanty etena vā aṅgirasaḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.16.3) para āhṇāras trasadasyuḥ paurukutso vītahavyaḥ śrāyasaḥ kakṣīvān auśijas ta etat prajātikāmāḥ sattrāyaṇam upāyaṃs te sahasraṃ sahasraṃ putrān apuṣyann evaṃ vāva te sahasraṃ sahasraṃ putrān puṣyanti ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.16.1) The <s>Gavāmayana</s> (Path of the Cows) is the first year; then that of the <s>Ādityas</s>; then that of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.
(PB 25.16.2) By this the cows attained procreation and abundance. Those who undertake this procreate and become many. By this the <s>Ādityas</s> became firmly established in these worlds. Those who undertake this become established. By this the <s>Aṅgirases</s> went to the heavenly world. Those who undertake this go to the heavenly world.

body.text:
(PB 25.17.1) atirātraḥ sahasraṃ trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā atirātraḥ prajāpateḥ sahasrasaṃvatsaram
(PB 25.17.2) etena vai prajāpatiḥ sarvasya prasavam agacchat sarvasya prasavaṃ gacchanti ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.17.3) etad vai prajāpatir jīryā mūra upait tena jarām apāhatāpa jarāṃ ghnate ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.17.4) tad etat prajāpateḥ sahasrasaṃvatsaram etena vai prajāpatiḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.17.1) An <s>Atirātra</s>; a thousand three-fold years; an <s>Atirātra</s>. This is the thousand-year [rite] of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(PB 25.17.2) By this, <s>Prajāpati</s> attained sovereignty over all creation. Those who undertake this attain sovereignty over all creation.
(PB 25.17.3) <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed undertook this when aged and foolish. By it he drove away old age. Those who undertake this drive away old age.

body.text:
(PB 25.18.1) pañca pañcāśatas trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañca pañcāśataḥ pañcadaśā pañca pañcāśataḥ saptadaśāḥ pañca pañcāśata ekaviṃśā viśvasṛjāṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram
(PB 25.18.2) etena vai viśvasṛja idaṃ viśvam asṛjanta yad viśvam asṛjanta tasmāt viśvasṛjaḥ
(PB 25.18.3) viśvam enān anu prajāyate ya etad upayanti
(PB 25.18.4) tapo gṛhapatir brahma brahmerā patny amṛtam udgātā bhūtaṃ prastotā bhaviṣyat pratihartartava upagātāra ārtavāḥ sadasyāḥ satyaṃ hotartaṃ maitrāvaruṇa ojo brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tviṣiś cāpacitiś ca neṣṭāpotārau yaśo 'cchāvāko 'gnir evāgnīd bhago grāvastud ūrg unnetā vāk subrahmaṇyaḥ prāṇo 'dhvaryur apānaḥ pratiprasthātā diṣṭir viśāstā balaṃ dhruvagopam āśā haviṣyeṣy ahorātrāv idhmavāhau mṛtyuḥ śamitaite dīkṣante
(PB 25.18.5) tad eṣa śloko viśvasṛjaḥ prathame sattram āsata sahasrasamaṃ prasutena yantas te ha yajñe bhuvanasya gopā hiraṇmayaḥ śakuno brahmanām eti
(PB 25.18.6) brahmaṇaḥ salokatāṃ sārṣṭitāṃ sāyujyaṃ gacchanti ya etad upayanti tad etad viśvasṛjāṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram etena vai viśvasṛjaḥ sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnuvan sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuvanti ya etad upayanti
body.translated_text:
(PB 25.18.1) Five sets of fifty three-fold years; five sets of fifty fifteen-fold; five sets of fifty seventeen-fold; five sets of fifty twenty-one-fold. This is the thousand-year [rite] of the <s>Viśvasṛjs</s> (world-creators).
(PB 25.18.2) By this the <s>Viśvasṛjs</s> created this entire universe. Because they created the universe, therefore [they are called] <s>Viśvasṛjs</s>.
(PB 25.18.3) Everything is reproduced for those who undertake this.
